Jeremiyah Love Headlines Official Cardinals-Rams Injury Report
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams have unveiled their first official injury reports for Week 6.
The list is headlined by rookie running back Jeremiyah Love , who continues to deal with ankle injuries despite not missing a regular season game.
Official Wednesday updates from both teams:
Sweat, Baker and Seumalo were on their typical rest days.
The main story out of Arizona is Love, who will have heavy eyes on his practice participation over the next few days.
"We all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday," LaFleur said of Love's ankle injury, which is different than his preseason one.
Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur, who spent the last few years in Los Angeles  before taking the head coaching gig in Arizona, dove deep into Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford and his impressive process:
"Well, it starts with his process. His process is the most consistent I've ever been around in my life. It's daily, and I won't even take you through it because it'd take me an hour. But it was fascinating to watch him go through it. Monday putting a game to bed, giving himself some time on a Tuesday. It was kind of cool, he'd bring his wife and kids in, get some breakfast and stuff like that. So I'd always get to see the kids on Tuesday morning. Then he'd go do what he needed to do after he dropped them off. He's a great father too, as I'm kind of saying that. And then he clears his mind on Tuesday as much as a quarterback can, and then get right back in on Wednesday.
"He was in there when the coffee machines were starting. By the time you got to install, he already kind of heard it three or four times. When I would be installing, I'd be kind of looking at him, and you could tell when he's listening, and then you could also tell when he's memorizing all the playcalls. And so you didn't want to ask him a question, if you will, or ask him to speak, because you kind of had that vibe, like you know where he was at. He's getting these plays, he's visualizing it. And then it just goes on to practice and all those kind of things. So, ultimate professional, better person, obviously MVP/Hall of Fame quarterback, and I look forward to going against that challenge. When I took this, I told him how grateful I am for him. But at the same time, when it's time to go on Sunday, let's go. And I'm excited to watch our guys go compete."
The Cardinals and Rams will practice twice more this week (Thursday and Friday) before revealing game statuses such as questionable, doubtful or out.

title: Cardinals Fans Won't Like Latest Carson Beck Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals won't be making a change at quarterback this week.
Not their starter, or their backup.
Rookie third-round pick Carson Beck will not have his role changed, according to head coach Mike LaFleur .
"Nothing new for this week, no," he told reporters on Wednesday. The Cardinals' head coach was previously asked about Beck's role changing on Monday with those discussions occuring on Tuesday.
Those discussions, if there were any, went nowhere. Arizona will continue to start Jacoby Brissett with Gardner Minshew behind him, likely making Beck inactive on game day as the team's emergency quarterback.
The Cardinals (1-4) are on the road to face the Los Angeles Rams (2-3) this week.
LaFleur did mention Beck is looking good behind the scenes and is working extensively with quarterbacks coach Matt Schaub during practice.
"You guys don't get to see it. No, he's doing a good job. He's out there. Obviously, from a look squad standpoint, what you try to tell all these guys, let alone the quarterback is, 'Yes, you're getting the starting defense prepared, but you still got to play your game. Like, don't be forcing stuff just because you're trying to give those guys production. Continue to work on your timing. Continue to work on your accuracy and continue to work on your game.'" he said.
"And so you don't just throw them out there and look at a [play]card. It's like, okay, how can the card be somewhat of our offense, if not our offense? And then on the same side of it is you know Shauby [Matt Schaub] is with him every single play. So when we get done, and I'm kind of roaming, being with the defense a little bit, [Nathaniel] Hackett's talking to Jacoby and then Shauby's with Carson and Gardner making sure that we're just obviously coaching."
The Cardinals are expected to see Beck under center at some point in 2026, though recent reports suggest that won't come until later in the season.
However, LaFleur did say the Miami product was improving.
"Yeah, I have. I've seen a lot of these guys improve. I particularly think over the last few weeks he's continued to get better, and he's enjoying his process of of improving," said LaFleur.
"Sometimes the best learning you can do is watching what's going on on Sundays. The smart ones can can pick up on stuff, and he's certainly one of them. He's very smart."

title: Jeremiyah Love Gets Concerning Injury Update Ahead of Cardinals-Rams
full_text:
TEMPE — The Arizona Cardinals are holding star rookie running back Jeremiyah Love out of practice on Wednesday as Week 6 preperations for the Los Angeles Rams ramp up.
"Take him one day at a time. You know, we want to get this ankle right and do it the right way," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Wednesday.
Love has been nursing an ankle injury through the opening stages of his rookie season after suffering a different ankle injury during preseason. While he hasn't missed any regular season action, Love's participation and impact has been slightly hindered.
There's been some talks about potentially shutting Love down to allow the ankle to heal, though LaFleur didn't seem willing to do that. Arizona is just 1-4 and is again favored to lose in Los Angeles.
"Listen, I'm going to try to be as candid as possible with also knowing that everyone's listening to this too, right? But he's a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. I mean, imagine being a running back in the NFL trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you know that you're capable of," LaFleur said.
"And so we all are in agreeance — as much as you know he wants to battle through — we're all in agreeance right now, it's just hey, give [the injury] a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on, what that'll entail for Sunday."
Love, the No. 3 overall pick, has 67 carries for 245 yards and one touchdown on the ground while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and a score through the air.
"I think early at his career [he battled injuries], but you had the right [ankle] early, and then now you got the left one. So now you're just kind of — it's just double dipping. The right side, the preseason one's fine. It's the other one right now that's the lingering issue. They're ankles, you know, it's an ankle. I'm not a doctor, and each body's a little bit different," LaFleur continued.
"Like the way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable, like he doesn't even feel it. But this one is the one that happened kind of when the regular season started, and it just lingered."
Has Love lost any of his explosiveness?
"You'd have to ask him that," LaFleur added. "I know how explosive he is. I know how explosive he wants to be. So I mean I think that's a fair assessment in some aspects. Again, I don't think it's an overall hindrance, but again the the rest for him is going to be vital."

title: 5 More Cardinals Trade Candidates After Marvin Harrison Jr. Deal
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' trade involving Marvin Harrison Jr. and the Houston Texans is officially in the rearview mirror, but there could be more moves to come.
There's ample time between now and the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline for the 1-4 Cardinals to facilitate more deals. Noise around the organization will only grow with each loss that piles up.
Harrison's gone — but who else could Arizona trade away?
Five candidates that make sense, ranked in no order:
Brissett was awarded $15 million more on his contract this summer after a lengthy contract holdout, one the Cardinals hope would be justified by steady play under center. While Brissett's not exactly losing games for Arizona, his inability to push the ball downfield and low/safe ceiling as a quarterback hasn't been close to par.
The Cardinals could easily trade him to a team looking to bolster their quarterback room ahead of a potential playoff push.
Minshew makes sense as a trade candidate as a middle man between Brissett and rookie Carson Beck, who the Cardinals absolutely need to see before the end of the season. Minshew signed in the offseason as a veteran backup and hasn't played in 2026.
That could be alluring for similar reasons for Brissett, though Minshew's on a cheap one-year deal and is a buy-low candidate for other teams around the league. For the Cardinals, this would clear the path for Beck to gain valuable playing time in the desert.
The veteran running back hasn't played in over a calendar year since injuring his foot/ankle in Week 3 of 2025. Conner practiced in individual drills during training camp but is currently on injured reserve.
There's not room for Conner to have anything close to a sizable role in Arizona thanks to Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier's presence. If Conner isn't flat-out cut by the Cardinals, he's a great experienced locker room piece for other teams to target with solid rotational snaps available.
Sweat's dissatisfaction with the Cardinals isn't exactly a secret, and Arizona's star pass rusher simply doesn't look like himself in 2026. Is it injury? Is it Sweat making his feelings known to the organization? Perhaps even both?
Sweat's had trade rumors swirl around him all offseason and those aren't going away. If the compensation is right, this absolutely makes sense for Arizona given their start to the season.
This would sting, as Baker's been a glue guy for the Cardinals since landing in the desert ten years ago. However, Baker's play has slowly dipped over the last few years. He's serviceable to say the least, though he's on the downswing of his career.
Perhaps more than anything, this would be to free Baker from the perennial losing this franchise has suffered in recent years. Baker's a stand-up person who can still make contributions to a winning football team. Unfortunately, that's not in Arizona.

title: Week 6 Consensus NFL Power Rankings: Cardinals Sink to Bottom
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals, to perhaps no surprise, are near the bottom of several NFL power rankings as we move into Week 6.
As the Cardinals prepare for the Los Angeles Rams, here's where they sit among various NFL power rankings:
Mike Florio : "The Week 1 win over the Chargers becomes less impressive by the week."
Our take : Very fair assessment, though in the moment Arizona's Week 1 victory was very impressive. The Cardinals weren't far away from stacking a couple more wins to their record, either.
Conor Orr : "As Kyle Odegard noted, we now have a full season sample size of Jacoby Brissett as the Cardinals’ starter, albeit between two different head coaches. The result? 2–15 record, 35th in total EPA among qualifying quarterbacks. But, as Mike LaFleur said after Sunday’s loss, I truly don’t think he’s the problem. When the Lions can simply double your best wideouts and wreak havoc, there are larger issues afoot."
Our take : While Brissett may not be the problem, he's also not the solution, either. Also, we as a society need to decide if wins are going to be a quarterback stat or not.
Pete Prisco : "The defense is a mess right now and they don't do enough on offense. At some point, they have to play rookie Carson Beck at quarterback."
Our take : They will have to play Beck at some point, though there also remains a strong possibility Gardner Minshew enters action before Beck does.
Josh Kendall/Chad Graff : "That season-opening win feels like ancient history. They’ve lost four straight games and surrendered 30 or more points in all four of them. At least they got a second-round pick back for Marvin Harrison Jr."
Our take : The return for Harrison was about as good as it was going to get for Arizona. They did well to get a second for a receiver who had just five receptions this season.
Josh Weinfuss : "Arizona is giving up a league-high 32.4 points per game and has the second-worst point differential in the NFL (minus-54). But the core of the Cardinals' defensive issues are coming against the pass. Arizona is giving up a league-worst 8.5 net yards per attempt and 236.8 passing yards per game (25th in the NFL). And when it comes time to stop touchdown passes, the Cardinals continue to struggle, with opposing quarterbacks completing 10.1% of their passes for touchdowns (the highest rate in the NFL)."
Our take : The Cardinals' defense has been so bad, people were legitimately surprised Arizona has retained defensive coordinator Nick Rallis for another week. Arizona's allowed 30+ points in four straight weeks and there's no clear signs of a turnaround coming soon.
Nick Shook : "In the first few weeks of this season, the Cardinals ostensibly proved they could score enough to keep up with most teams, even if their defense couldn’t do its part. That seemed to position them well against a Lions team that dragged a porous defense through the opening month, but that just wasn't the case on Sunday in the desert. Arizona scored once, then went completely quiet, reducing its offense to a chuck-and-pray approach on third-and-long and completely eliminating Jeremiyah Love from the game plan because of the score difference. With all due respect to Jacoby Brissett, you’re not going to win many games when he’s averaging 40 throws per outing."
Our take : This was the largest tumble for the Cardinals, falling five spots after last week. Shook is right, however: Arizona had a golden opportunity to take advantage of a poor Lions defense and they simply couldn't.
Frank Schwab : "Trading Marvin Harrison Jr. was best for everyone involved, but let's not celebrate the Cardinals too much for getting a second-round pick back in a trade with the Texans. Arizona got very little out of the fourth overall pick in a loaded 2024 NFL Draft. That's horrendous, even if the Cardinals recouped some value. As Bob McManaman of the Arizona Republic pointed out , the Cardinals have already moved on from four of the last six players they drafted in the top 10 overall: Josh Rosen, Kyler Murray , Isaiah Simmons and Harrison."
Our take : Moving on from Harrison was indeed the right decision, and as we stated above, a second-round pick was the best they were going to get — all things considered. Disappointing? Massively, especially given the expectations he had entering the league. However, the Cardinals and Harrison both get a much-needed fresh start.

title: Ranking Arizona Cardinals’ Biggest Draft Busts Under Monti Ossenfort
full_text:
General manager Monti Ossenfort's seat is red-hot for the Arizona Cardinals, and many believe that he should have been fired along with former head coach Jonathan Gannon early in the 2026 offseason.
Owner Michael Bidwill decided to give Ossenfort another chance, and it has proven to be a costly move at best. A future in Arizona beyond 2026 feels incredibly unlikely for Ossenfort with each day that passes.
There's been no shortage of failures, missteps, and more for Ossenfort, but his NFL Draft record stands out like a sore thumb. The jury is out on 2026, but his three previous draft classes are a mess.
The 2023 class gave some decent returns, while the 2024 class was nothing short of horrendous. The 2025 class already appears to be quite concerning, too, which makes us understandably nervous for the 2026 class.
I took a look at Ossenfort's draft classes and ranked his biggest blunders. Sorting a top five was difficult, and many picks came from the aforementioned 2024 class. 2026 picks are not being included considering we've had five games to evaluate, but we can make a note that Jeremiyah Love's slow start to the year hasn't been great (though a lot of his struggles come from the offensive line in front of him).
Before we get to the top five, let's go through a chunk of honorable, or perhaps dishonorable, mentions:
There's still time for Darius Robinson to turn his fortunes around. He's looked good in a part-time role for the Cardinals, though that's still disappointing considering he was a first-round pick. If Robinson doesn't put everything together in year three, then he will skyrocket up this list; I'm giving him the benefit of the doubt for the time being.
It isn't fair to call Will Johnson a bust, but the talented Michigan corner was expected to be a first-round pick in 2025 before teams learned of potential long-term injury concerns. Johnson looked solid as a rookie for Arizona, but he is on injured reserve with a neck injury and will miss the rest of the year. If the long-term injury concerns prove to be true, then this was a massive gamble that didn't work out.
I don't think including a fifth-round pick should count as one of the "biggest busts" under Ossenfort, but it certainly was a wasted pick by him on the Houston quarterback. There were plenty of questions about whether Clayton Tune was even good enough for the NFL, let alone play, but Ossenfort took that ill-advised shot anyway.
One of many cornerbacks drafted under Ossenfort, Elijah Jones has become an almost obscure player to casual Cardinals fans. Jones has appeared in just ten games and recorded three assisted tackles. That's a horrific return on a third-round pick.
We know that Tip Reiman was always intended to be a backup tight end for the Cardinals, but he's made next to no impact regardless of when he's seen the field. Reiman has appeared in just 21 career games, none this year (PUP list), and recorded nine receptions for 55 yards and zero touchdowns.
Regardless of the supposed versatility that Reiman provides, there has been no production to back up that claim. Reiman hasn't been able to carve out a consistent role with Arizona, and that speaks to the front office's misevaluation of the Illinois product.
This isn't to say that Max Melton has been terrible; he's a fine player who would be much better in a reserve role than as a starter. Melton hasn't recorded an interception in 32 games and 16 starts, and has broken up just 14 passes. However, Melton makes the top five because of the situation that the Cardinals found themselves in.
Arizona decided to trade down and draft Melton with several cornerbacks on the board. Those cornerbacks? Cooper DeJean, Kool-Aid McKinstry, and Kamari Lassiter. Those three are light-years better than Melton and would be big-time difference-makers for this defense.
After the Cardinals passed on Will Anderson Jr. in the first round following their trade-down, the team drafted BJ Ojulari out of LSU. It felt like a pretty solid consolation prize, and he posted 40 tackles and four sacks as a rookie contributor. The sky was seemingly the limit before one of the worst knee injuries possible derailed everything.
Ojulari would miss the entire 2024 season and appear in just eight games in 2025, making nine tackles and recording a single sack. He was released in the 2026 offseason with his future with the Cardinals bleak. Injuries robbed Ojulari of what could've been a great career in Arizona, but we'll never know.
There was a belief at the time of this pick that Trey Benson was the future of the Cardinals' run game. James Conner had been terrific for the team, but he was getting up there in age, prompting Arizona to begin searching for his heir apparent. They thought Benson was the guy, and the pick received applause at the time, but things couldn't have worked out any worse than they did.
Benson lasted just two seasons with the team before the Cardinals decided to move on. He appeared in just 17 games and started two games, rushing for 451 yards and a single touchdown. His tenure in the desert ended the moment the team spent the third overall pick this year on Jeremiyah Love.
The undisputed number one bust on Monti Ossenfort's track record is also among the biggest busts in Cardinals franchise history. The Ohio State standout and legacy pick Marvin Harrison Jr. was hailed as a generational can't-miss prospect, making him one of the easiest selections the Cardinals have ever made.
Despite an underwhelming rookie season, which felt inevitable given his sky-high expectations, Harrison declined substantially and was quickly forgotten about on an offense known for garbage-time yards and scores.
Effort appeared to be an issue going into the season, and his drops were becoming alarming. Arizona ultimately pulled the plug and dealt him to the Houston Texans for seemingly good draft compensation. Still, there's not much the Cardinals can draft with the compensation to make up for such a devastating bust.
Marvin Harrison Jr. is one of the greatest failures in the history of the Cardinals dating back to their days in Chicago and St. Louis. It's hard to blame Ossenfort for Harrison's failure with what most believed was the safest pick possible, but it will hang on his resume forever.

title: Cardinals-Texans Trade for Marvin Harrison Jr. Brewed Quietly For Weeks
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Houston Texans' deal for receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. made waves through the NFL world over the weekend in one of the more surprising trades made in quite some time.
Harrison's departure from Arizona isn't at all surprising — things clearly weren't working with the former No. 4 overall pick and he had previously hired agents to help navigate a deal earlier in the week.
However, the timing threw practically everybody off. A big-name player such as Harrison was offloaded, at least in public eyes, quickly. The Cardinals made Harrison inactive on Saturday morning, and by time their Week 5 contest kicked off, Harrison was on the move to Houston.
SI.com's Albert Breer added the trade process began weeks ago.
"The Cardinals asked around for a second-round pick plus a sweetener. Houston, over the 24 hours leading into kickoff Sunday, wound up coming around on that, ending an interesting process that ended Harrison’s two-plus years in Arizona," he wrote.
"It actually began weeks ago, with the No. 4 pick from the 2024 draft deciding to hire an agent to handle his situation, bringing in veterans Todd France and Tory Dandy of Athletes First.
"Quietly, the groundwork was laid for Harrison’s exit, starting then. The writing had been on the wall with the team’s decision to extend another young receiver, Michael Wilson, to pair long-term with big-money tight end Trey McBride. It had to stay that way for Arizona to get the type of return that would motivate the team to move Harrison. And things heated up over the course of the weekend, with the Texans’ effort to reunite Harrison with Stroud, his teammate at Ohio State."
Harrison, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur and general manager Monti Ossenfort did a strong job of collectively downplaying the noise while the workings of the trade were happening. All three parties, to varying extents, shot down trade rumors through the last few weeks.
Even after the deal was complete, figures such as LaFleur and Ossenfort didn't dive deep into the reasons for a trade.
“Decisions like this are never easy,” said Ossenfort in a statement after terms became final.
“Ultimately, we have to do what is best for our football team and that will always be the driving factor. We are extremely grateful to Marvin for what he has contributed to our organization and wish him the very best as he moves forward in his career.”
LaFleur, speaking after the loss to the Lions, added, "I'm not going to totally get into that right now. I really like Marvin Harrison.  He's a good person. I wish him well. We did what we thought was in the best interest of the Cardinals. Any guy that does not play to the level that I feel like they're capable of, I'm always going to put that on me and  coaching in general."

title: Cardinals Eying Free Agent Help to Upgrade OL
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' offensive line needs help, and the team is looking to upgrade their trenches with a potential addition via free agency.
The Cardinals are hosting Jamaree Salyer for a visit, according to ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler. Salyer is healthy after recovering from a knee issue and has versatility to play either guard or tackle:
Free agent OL Jamaree Salyer is visiting the Arizona Cardinals today, per source. Salyer had his knee scoped in August and is healthy now, will likely sign in coming weeks. Salyer can play tackle or guard, has 40 career starts. pic.twitter.com/3wVu0OJMQP
The Cardinals recently lost Paris Johnson Jr. for the season and Isaiah Adams to injured reserve last week, missing two of Arizona's starting five offensive lineman. Second-round pick Chase Bisontis was also lost in preseason play.
The Cardinals rolled out seventh-round rookie Jayden Williams at left tackle and Jon Gaines at right guard in their Week 5 loss to the Detroit Lions. Mike LaFleur highlighted the Cardinals' inability to run the ball as their biggest area of concern.
“Not bad. Against a pretty good front. We were mixing and matching where 97 (Lions Edge Aidan Hutchinson) was trying to get some ribs and licks and trying to help those guys, but I thought for the most part they did a fairly good job. Obviously, we threw the ball way too much because of how that game got out of hand and trying to establish a run game. If you guys want me to be candid, that’s really where I want to see us improve more," he said.
"That was going to be a hard game running the football, but we’re better than that. There were more yards out there than what was had. Some of it was them swimming our blocks and our double teams, but other times there was some space and we just weren’t taking up that space. We have to put them in better positions, but there’s more to be had in the run game.”
LaFleur was also less than impressed with their pass protection, which required more running back help to chip as opposed to Jeremiyah Love running routes as a receiver.
“Just helping out with those edges and stuff like that. I mean they have a pretty premier player so even if we’re in a six-man protection with the back, if they’re not bringing a linebacker, we still work at what you’d call a shave technique on their edge guys where you’re helping those tackles," he added.
"That’s not just our tackles; that’s all the tackles I’ve ever been a part of. You don’t want to put those guys on islands anywhere I’ve ever been too often.”
Salyer was initially believed to be lost for the season after signing with the Miami Dolphins this summer, though he was released and now appears to be healthy.

title: Cardinals' Mike LaFleur Highlights Arizona's Biggest Problem
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a run game problem, and Mike LaFleur knows it.
Through five weeks, the Cardinals rank in the bottom ten of NFL teams in terms of rushing yards per game (91.6) while they're averaging under four yards per carry at 3.8.
That's created a massive imbalance in the Cardinals' offense, one that has LaFleur digging for answers after the team's Week 5 thrashing to the Detroit Lions.
“Obviously, we threw the ball way too much because of how that game got out of hand and trying to establish a run game. If you guys want me to be candid, that’s really where I want to see us improve more," said LaFleur.
"That was going to be a hard game running the football, but we’re better than that. There were more yards out there than what was had. Some of it was them swimming our blocks and our double teams, but other times there was some space and we just weren’t taking up that space. We have to put them in better positions, but there’s more to be had in the run game.”
The Cardinals now move forward into the foreseeable future with Paris Johnson Jr. out for the season and Isaiah Adams on injured reserve for at least the next three weeks. Arizona's down two of their starters along the offensive line — a unit that was already viewed as average before the season began.
Their running back corps also isn't finding success. Jeremiyah Love is nursing an ankle injury and is averaging 3.7 yards per carry while backfield mate Tyler Allgeier is at 3.4. Arizona runners are averaging just 1.0 yards before contact, which ranks in the bottom half of the league.
Trading away Marvin Harrison Jr. only makes life easier for defenses to prepare for Arizona's rushing attack. So does the stagnant play of Jacoby Brissett at quarterback, and the Cardinals' inability to stop opposing offenses only dwindles their opportunity to have a balanced offense.
Arizona's inability to run the ball at high levels isn't talked about in the likes of making changes at quarterback — or defensive coordinator — though it very much is one of the larger problems for LaFleur to solve after such a struggling start.
With injuries piled up in the desert, it's tough to imagine the Cardinals can really turn things around unless a massive shift in philosophy upfront occurs.

title: State of the Arizona Cardinals, Part 1: How We Got Here
full_text:
It has certainly been an eventful first quarter of the 2026 season for the Arizona Cardinals.
The team started with an electric upset in Week One over the Los Angeles Chargers on the road and have slowly been falling back to Earth ever since. Competitive first halves against division foes Seattle and San Francisco turned into fiascos and the past two weeks against the Giants and Lions have been nothing short of disastrous.
Unfortunately, it is a narrative all too common for the Cardinals fan. A glimmer of hope for the future quickly blotted out by the harsh realities of the NFL.
Things seems bad right now, that would be hard for anyone to deny. So let us take a minute today to review the past five weeks and see where the team really is. We will review the results, check in on the state of the roster, and try to see where the team might go from here.
So whether you have been following the team closely this season or are just tuning in to see what your team is up to in yet another "rebuilding year" hopefully this will provide something for you.
The Cardinals successfully surprised the majority of the NFL world with a convincing win on the road to open the 2026 season. Their 26-14 victory felt complete with a great effort from quarterback Jacoby Brissett and the offense paired with a strong showing from a defense that came into the season with several question marks.
Week Two brought Arizona back to down to reality. They were competitive in the first half against the defending champion Seattle Seahawks finishing the period tied 7-7, but the wheels came off in the second half on the way to a 31-7 loss.
The schedule did not get any easier the following week back on the road to Santa Clara to face off against another division foe, the San Francisco 49ers. The Cardinals had it within 2 points late in the fourth quarter, but the defense couldn't stop George Kittle from finding the end zone with under two minutes left and a failed onside kick gave the team its second loss of the year, 36-30.
Week Four against the New York Giants started with as good of an offensive performance as could be expected, the Cardinals scoring on their first two offensive drives. The quick start quickly fell apart with the offense stagnating and the defense struggled to get a stop, allowing the Giants to score 17 unanswered points and take the lead. Arizona had a chance to score with seconds left but Brissett ended the game with a 98-yard pick-six.
Most recently, the Cardinals faced the Detroit Lions and former offensive coordinator Drew Petzing at home in Week Five and were thoroughly trounced. Once again scoring on their first drive, Arizona rapidly lost control of this game. Jahmyr Gibbs had over 200 yards from scrimmage and the defense surrended a season high 45 points, the most since a similar beatdown in Week 14 of the 2025 season against the Los Angeles Rams.
Injuries are a well-known and accepted part of the NFL season and the Cardinals have certainly had their fair share of them already this season.
The team is tied for the 10th most injured in the league after five weeks of play. There are currently five players with injury designations that should return at some points this season, but in addition there are already ten players who have hit the Injured Reserve list that are done for the year.
The IR list includes some of the biggest pieces of this roster, including starting LT Paris Johnson, Jr. and CB1 Will Johnson. Starting RG Isaiah Adams was recently added to the list and two key pieces of the 2026 Draft class hit the list before the season even started, second round pick G Chase Bisontis and fourth rounder DL Kaleb Proctor.
The loss of Johnson and Adams means that the Cardinals offensive line is down to 3/5 of their original starters. The secondary has also been decimated. Will Johnson is the biggest loss but of the fifteen total players with some sort of injury designation at the moment, four of them are safeties, a position lacking a true pair with Budda Baker after the loss of Jalen Thompson to free agency this offseason.
One of the big narratives of this season from the first week centered around the production and value of the No. 4 overall selection of the 2024 draft, Marvin Harrison, Jr.
With the high draft selection and the Hall of Fame pedigree, Harrison, Jr. was considered by most at the time to be a can't miss, generational wide receiver prospect after a stellar collegiate outing at Ohio State.
His rookie season in 2024, was good but not spectacular and questions began to pop up surrounding Harrison. His sophomore season had a rocky start, concerns about his catching and lack of effort starting to be raised among some but the year was cut short due to injury.
Harrison's 2026 did not get off on a stellar note, either. There were a few highlight catches but he still was not a featured part of the Cardinals offense and questions from fans and the national media reached a fever pitch in the past few weeks.
This all leads to the news that broke last Friday that the Cardinals had negotiated a trade for Harrison, but the details were initially kept close to the vest. On Sunday, we received the official news that he and a 7th round pick would be traded to the Houston Texans for a 2027 2nd and 6th.
Harrison now becomes the first former Top 5 wide receiver selection since Ahmad Rashad to be traded within the first three years of his career. interestingly, it was also the Cardinals that traded Rashad in 1974 to the Buffalo Bills for quarterback Dennis Shaw.
Harrison's trade means one big thing for the Cardinals going forward this season. The role of Michael Wilson as WR1 is now undisputed and the team will have to search through their wide receiver room to find some additional production alongside him and Kendrick Bourne, who has been a decent addition so far.
Part Two of this piece will address what I think has gone wrong with the Cardinals so far and where the team can go from here.

title: Falcons Provide Encouraging Michael Penix Jr. Injury Update Ahead of Bears
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons received an encouraging update on quarterback Michael Penix Jr. ahead of Sunday’s matchup against the Chicago Bears .
Kevin Stefanski indicated the young signal caller is trending toward playing.
Penix suffered a rib injury during the fourth quarter of Atlanta’s 30- 23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football. The quarterback went down after taking a sack and returned for just one play before missing the team's last drive and overtime. Another injury that raised immediate questions about his availability for the Falcons’ upcoming matchup.
Stefanski offered optimism Wednesday when asked about Penix’s status for Sunday’s contest against Chicago.
“As long as everything goes accordingly,” Stefanski said. “I am not going to get into specifics, but he’s feeling better.”
Stefanski’s comments provide a positive sign for Atlanta, although Penix’s availability will depend on how his recovery progresses throughout the remainder of the week. The coach’s qualification suggests the Falcons are encouraged by the quarterback’s progress but are not ready to consider his status completely settled.
Penix’s injury came at an unfortunate time for Atlanta, who had seen their eight-point lead evaporate, but there was still time to drive for a game-winning field goal before the end of regulation. Backup quarterback Tua Tagovailoa came in for one play and completed a screen to Bijan Robinson for a 14-yard gain.
Penix returned and threw and incompletion that ended regulation in a 23-23 time. The Ravens won the toss and kept the ball for an eight minute touchdown drive. Penix indicated that time was not good for his ribs as he tightened up and the adrenaline wore off.
Tagovailoa completed a 20-yard pass to Drake London, but his second was intercepted to end the game.
Now, the focus shifts to whether Penix can recover in time to lead the offense against Chicago. His potential return would provide Atlanta with continuity at quarterback as it looks to bounce back from Sunday’s disappointing result.
The Falcons will also need to improve their offensive execution after failing to capitalize on several scoring opportunities against the Ravens. Finishing drives and making the most of possessions will be crucial as Atlanta attempts to get back into the win column.
If Penix cannot play, the Falcons would turn to Tagovailoa for his first start of the season.
For a team looking to respond after a difficult loss, getting Penix back under center would be a significant development heading into Week 6.

title: Falcons Could Be Facing Bears Down Two Prominent Starters
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons failed to capitalize on an undermanned Baltimore Ravens in Week 5, but they may get another chance in Week 6 as the Chicago Bears come to town. One week after dropping an overtime home game to a Lamar Jackson- and Trey Hendrickson-less Ravens squad, the Bears could come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium missing two prominent players.
Quarterback Caleb Williams is suffering from a lingering hamstring injury that has held him out of the Bears’ last three games, while defensive end Montez Sweat has been suspended by the NFL for the use of performance-enhancing drugs.
The defender has totaled seven tackles, four quarterback hits, and two sacks over the Bears’ first five weeks of the season, but the former Pro Bowl pass rusher led the team with 10 sacks last season. He has missed just one game over his last four seasons, but this suspension comes at a bad time for the Bears.
Sweat’s suspension comes days after the Bears lost defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo with a quad injury. His game status for Sunday is unknown, but he is second among Chicago defenders in sacks (three) and ranks third in tackles for loss (three).
The Bears, 3-2, are coming off their worst defensive performance of the season, surrendering 31 points and 428 total yards to the Packers. If Michael Penix Jr. is ready to play , the Falcons will look to find some similar success.
Williams, meanwhile, could return this week. Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Sunday that his quarterback is “close” to being available. He returned to practice last Friday but was limited and inactive Sunday.
With Williams out, the Bears turned to backup quarterbacks Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum. The pair of reserves went 2-1, throwing for 762 yards, four touchdowns, and two interceptions, but struggled against Green Bay in Week 5.
Bagent couldn't push the ball downfield, going 2-for-8 for 24 yards and two interceptions on throws of more than five air yards, and was benched for Keenum, who finished with 108 yards and an interception in relief.
The Falcons’ defense faltered down the stretch against a backup quarterback on Sunday. Tyler Huntley went 11-for-11 for 80 yards and two total touchdowns (one rushing) in the final two drives of the Ravens’ comeback effort, and Atlanta will look for redemption in Week 6.

title: Falcons Host former Denver Broncos Safety for Tryout
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons have battled through injury, especially on the defensive side of the ball, since training camp, and they're always on the lookout for players who can contribute.
On Tuesday, the Falcons hosted former Denver Broncos safety Delarrin Turner-Yell for a tryout. Turner-Yell was originally a fifth-round pick by the Broncos in the 2022 NFL Draft out of Oklahoma.
He measured 5'10 and 197 pounds and the NFL Combine that year, with an impressive 4.47 forty.
"Turner-Yell's fluidity in space is the first thing that jumps off the tape whether he's in coverage or in pursuit as a run defender," NFL Network's Lance Zierlein wrote of him as a prospect . "Anticipation and decisiveness help speed up his pace of play, but his playmaking demeanor also hurts his coverage discipline at times.
He saw extensive action for the Broncos his first two seasons. As a rookie, he was a special teams contributor. But in 2023, he saw action in 16 games with two starts and had 34 tackles, a quarterback hit, and a pass defended on 210 defensive snaps.
After a promising second season, Turner-Yell suffered an ACL injury before the 2024 season and missed the entire year. He was activated in Dember of 2025 by the Broncos, only to suffer another knee injury his first game back .
If the Falcons were to sign Turner-Yell, it would likely be to the practice squad. Their starting safety duo of Jessie Bates III and Xavier Watts is one of the best in the NFL. Sydney Brown has played well in his role at safety and nickel at times. DeMarcco Hellams has also been effective in a backup role.
It's hard to picture the Falcons taking a risk on him on their active roster, considering the depth at safety and Turner-Yell's injury history. However, if he looked fully rececovered at his tryout, the Falcons might be able to find a spot for him on their practice squad.
In other news, former Falcons undrafted free agent cornerback Cobee Bryant worked out with the Miami Dolphins on Tuesday. Bryant was a favorite of former head coach Raheem Morris , but failed to make the initial 53-man roster out of training camp in either 2025 or this year.
Next up for the Falcons will be the Chicago Bears on Sunday at 1 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

title: Falcons See Surprising Movement in Power Rankings Despite OT Loss to Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons let the Baltimore Ravens claw back into Sunday’s primetime showdown, surrendering 15 unanswered points in an overtime loss. As a result, the Falcons dropped to 2-3 and face another tough test against the Chicago Bears in Atlanta.
Michael Penix Jr.’s health will be at the center of discussions again this week after the Falcons’ quarterback suffered another injury that puts his availability in question.
Elsewhere in the division, the Panthers sat out this week, the Buccaneers stunned the Cowboys Thursday night, and the Saints continued their downward trajectory with a third straight loss. Falcons OnSI pulled the results from those sites and put them all in one place for fans. See below where the Falcons land compared with their division rivals.
The Falcons continued climbing Conor Orr’s power rankings despite losing to the Ravens in overtime, moving into the top spot in the NFC South. He cited Michael Penix Jr.'s presence as the biggest boon to the team and sent good vibes into the universe that the rib injury isn't serious.
Elsewhere in the South, SI ranks the Panthers No. 20 (down six spots), the Saints No. 25 (even), and the Buccaneers No. 27 (up three spots). Orr has the Bears (Atlanta’s Week 6 opponent) at No. 13.
Pete Prisco docked the Falcons for their loss to the Lamar Jackson-less Ravens and added Penix's lingering injury concerns to their drop.
Elsewhere in the South, CBS ranks the Panthers No. 20 (down two spots), the Saints No. 26 (down three spots), and the Buccaneers No. 29 (up one spot). Prisco has the Bears at No. 15.
Nick Shook still believes in what the Falcons can do, keeping them at No. 15 in his rankings. He said they're becoming an “imposing offensive force” with a “sneaky-good” defense. The hope is that Penix stays in the mix, which is why he sees the Falcons’ ceiling.
Elsewhere in the South, NFL.com ranks the Panthers No. 14 (even), the Saints No. 27 (down seven spots), and the Buccaneers No. 23 (up seven spots). Shook has the Bears at No. 13.
One week after ranking them near the bottom of the NFL, ESPN moved the Falcons up a few spots after the Ravens' loss. Marc Raimondi highlighted improvements in run defense and pass rush (despite the loss of James Pearce Jr. and Jalon Walker), but injuries in the secondary are becoming increasingly concerning.
Elsewhere in the South, ESPN ranks the Panthers No. 18 (even), the Saints No. 26 (down five spots), and the Buccaneers No. 27 (up three spots). ESPN has the Bears at No. 13.

title: Where Do Atlanta Falcons Stand in NFC South after 5 Games?
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons suffered a tough 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football, ending their two-game winning streak. Despite entering the matchup as one of the hottest teams in the NFL, Atlanta could not capitalize on several opportunities to secure a victory.
The Falcons had chances to put Baltimore away but struggled to finish drives and allowed the Ravens to complete a fourth quarter comeback. The defeat leaves Atlanta searching for answers as it looks to regain momentum in the NFC South race.
With Week 5 in the books, here is where the Falcons stand in the division.
Atlanta currently holds second place in the NFC South with a 2-3 record, sitting half a game behind the Carolina Panthers, who are 2-2 after taking their bye week in Week 5.
Carolina's position at the top gives the Panthers an early advantage in the division, but the Falcons remain within striking distance. Atlanta has shown flashes of being a competitive team this season, and a strong performance in Week 6 could help the team close the gap.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and New Orleans Saints are tied behind Atlanta, with both teams holding 1-4 records. Neither team has found consistent success early in the season, leaving Carolina and Atlanta currently occupying the top two spots in the division.
For the Falcons, Sunday's loss was a missed opportunity to improve their record and put pressure on the Panthers. Instead, Atlanta must regroup and focus on getting back into the win column.
The Falcons will face the Chicago Bears in Week 6, giving them an opportunity to respond after their disappointing loss to Baltimore.
Carolina will travel to Philadelphia to take on the Eagles, while the Saints head to MetLife Stadium to face the New York Giants. The Buccaneers will host the Pittsburgh Steelers.
These matchups could have a direct impact on the NFC South standings. If Atlanta takes care of business against Chicago while Carolina struggles against Philadelphia, the Falcons would move into a tie with the Panthers for the division lead, but the Panthers would hold the head-to-head tiebreaker.
The NFC South has often featured competitive division races in recent seasons, and the current standings suggest another battle could develop between Atlanta and Carolina.
Although the Falcons are coming off a frustrating loss, they remain just half a game behind the division leader. The Buccaneers and Saints also have time to improve their positions, but both teams need to start stringing together victories.
Atlanta's immediate focus is getting back on track against Chicago. With the division still tightly contested, the Falcons have an opportunity to regain momentum and challenge Carolina for the top spot as the season progresses.

title: Divine Deablo Takes Ownership of Falcons Run Defense Struggles vs. Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered Sunday night's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens with the NFL's top-ranked run defense, but they struggled to contain Derrick Henry and Baltimore's rushing attack.
The Ravens finished with 208 rushing yards on 35 carries, including 102 yards on 24 attempts from Henry, exposing weaknesses in a defense that had allowed just 48.3 rushing yards per game entering the contest.
Following the loss, linebacker Divine Deablo took responsibility for the disappointing performance, acknowledging that Atlanta must improve both individually and collectively.
"Defensively, we just got to do better job of stopping the run. Clearly, they had 200. I'll put that on me for real. For real. We got to be better as a whole, but I definitely got to be better myself," Deablo said.
Deablo reflected on the frustration of a defense that had established itself as one of Atlanta's biggest strengths early in the season.
Deablo pointed to one area that needs improvement from him.
"Sometimes trying to make a play. Getting out of my gap. I got to stay in my gap, make sure I do my job plus one," Deablo said.
Against a physical rushing attack like Baltimore's, maintaining gap integrity is critical. When defenders leave their assigned areas, it can create openings for offensive linemen to exploit and give running backs additional room to operate.
Deablo also explained the challenges of Atlanta's defensive scheme, which requires players to remain disciplined when defensive linemen move across the formation.
"We got, you know, we do different things sometimes. Sometimes we have movement. So, I'm imagining this guy is going to be here, but he might not make it over there. So, I just got to make sure I secure that gap before I make the move I want to make," Deablo said. "You secure your gap first and then go make a play."
That responsibility becomes especially important when offensive linemen climb to the second level and attempt to block linebackers. With defensive linemen focused on their individual gaps, linebackers must react quickly while maintaining their own assignments.
"Oh yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Somebody's definitely climbing. So we got to, you know, secure our gap off of that climb and then still try to get to the ball. So, a little more challenging," Deablo said.
Deablo also evaluated Atlanta's efforts to contain Derrick Henry.
"For the most part, we did a great job [forcing Derrick Henry back inside]. We had a few mishaps where he got to our corner. But overall pretty good," Deablo said.
Despite those challenges, Deablo emphasized that execution remains the most important factor.
"We had plenty of opportunities to make a play and we just didn't. So, at the end of the day, we just got to do our job," Deablo said.
Atlanta's performance against Baltimore was a significant setback for a defense that had been effective at limiting opposing rushing attacks. Moving forward, the Falcons must improve their gap discipline, execute their assignments and take advantage of opportunities to bring down ball carriers.
It won't take long to see if their corrections work, because they face the Chicago Bears and their No. 1-ranked rushing offense on Sunday .

title: Drake London has Massive Numbers with Michael Penix Jr. at QB, and He Doesn't Care
full_text:
This offseason, Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London signed a massive contract extension that made him the third-highest-paid wide receiver in the NFL on a per-year basis at $35.3 million.
Like the rest of the team, London had trouble getting out of first gear during the first two weeks of the season with Cooper Rush at quarterback. He had 6 catches for 70 yards in the two losses.
Michael Penix Jr. returned at quarterback for Week 3 against the Green Bay Packers, and London had 21 catches for 408 yards in the next three games, including 118 on Sunday night against the Ravens.
This isn't anything new for London and Penix. The Athletic's Josh Kendall asked London how aware he was that his numbers improved dramatically with Penix as his on-again, off-again quarterback the last three seasons.
"I mean, I'm a little bit aware that they go up, but nothing too crazy right now. I'm just worried about W's at the moment," London answered.
They don't just go up; they skyrocket. 15 starts for Penix, and London has 103 catches and 1,570 yards in those games, not all of which Penix finished. Extrapolated across 17 games, London would have 117 catches and 1,779 yards.
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba was the NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2025 with 119 catches, 1,793 yards, and 10 touchdowns. London's production is almost identical.
Rams wide receiver Pika Nacua was second in receiving yards with 1,715. No one else had more than 1,429.
When asked if the numbers themselves surprised him, London remained humble.
"I mean a little bit," London answered.
"I just try to go out there and catch the ball if it comes my way," London said. "If I get opportunities and stuff, I try to make the best of them and do whatever is best for the team. The numbers, that's just like a cherry on top type of situation.
"Nothing really changes. We're going in there, and we're striving for greatness. We're striving to get better every day, every hour, and just come out there and be ready for Sunday's game against a very, very good Chicago team."
Penix is day-to-day this week after suffering a rib injury against the Ravens. Falcons fans and London fantasy football owners hope it's Penix behind center on Sunday against the Chicago Bears.
Lost in the numbers is London's blocking ability. Not only is he one of the most productive receivers in the NFL, he's one of the best blockers at his position.
Many around the league who ignore the playoff-less Falcons questioned the big contract extension to London, but few who watch him play every day had those concerns.

title: Chicago Bears Offense Could Provide Even Bigger Challenge to Falcons Than Ravens
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons entered their matchup against the Baltimore Ravens with the NFL’s No. 1 run defense, allowing just 48.3 rushing yards per game.
However, Baltimore exposed weaknesses in Atlanta’s defensive front, rushing for 208 yards on 35 carries and averaging 5.9 yards per attempt.
Derrick Henry led the way with 102 rushing yards and added a receiving touchdown on a screen pass, helping Baltimore control the line of scrimmage and win in Atlanta. For a Falcons defense that had been dominant against the run entering Sunday night, it was a significant step backward.
Atlanta’s struggles were particularly evident during Baltimore’s overtime drive. The Ravens ran for 45 yards on the ground during the possession, wearing down the Falcons’ defensive front as they moved down the field. After spending much of the game trying to contain Henry and Baltimore’s rushing attack, Atlanta struggled to get the necessary stops when it mattered most.
Falcons defensive lineman Gervon Dexter acknowledged that improving against the run is essential.
“We got to stop the run to get the pass rush, so we want to get more of those opportunities. We got to do a better job at stopping the run,” Dexter said.
Baltimore’s success on early downs made it hard for Atlanta to dictate the game's terms defensively. The Ravens consistently gained positive yardage, keeping the Falcons from focusing on pressuring the quarterback and adding strain to the defensive front as the game progressed.
Dexter also recognized the challenge of containing Henry, whose ability to finish runs can make him especially dangerous late in games.
“Obviously, he’s a good player. You got to stop his feet, get him behind the line of scrimmage, and make a play on him. He’s one of those players in a long time where he can, like you say, finish those games. So we knew we had to try to get him down there,” Dexter said.
The challenge does not get any easier for Atlanta over the next two weeks. The Falcons’ next two opponents, the Chicago Bears and San Francisco 49ers, both rank among the NFL’s top 10 rushing offenses.
Chicago leads the league with 173.2 rushing yards per game, while San Francisco ranks eighth with 128 yards per game. Both teams will test an Atlanta defense that must improve its tackling, gap discipline, and ability to withstand physical rushing attacks.
The performance exposed an area that needs immediate attention, especially with two productive rushing offenses coming up on the schedule.
Atlanta has already shown it can be one of the league’s best run defenses. Now, after Henry and the Ravens wore them down, the Falcons must return to that standard before their upcoming opponents exploit the same weaknesses.

title: Michael Penix Jr. Injury Update: Adam Schefter Provides Latest on Falcons QB
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. had a rough start and finish to the team's 30-23 loss to the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday Night Football.
He started the game 0-5 and took until midway through the second quarter to complete his first pass. He finished with a towel over his head as he watched Tua Tagovailoa take the field in overtime after suffering a rib injury on a hit in the backfield.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday afternoon that the rib injury isn't considered to be a problem for Penix long-term, but that doesn't mean he'll be suiting up against the Chicago Bears on Sunday.
"Michael Penix’s rib injury is not considered serious, per sources. Penix might be able to return for Sunday’s game vs. the Bears, but the team wants to be cautious and see him practice this week before it knows whether he will be able to play in Week 6," Schefter reported on X .
Bookending the start and finish of the Ravens game was a fantastic performance from Penix. The Ravens had sold out to stop Bijan Robinson and the Falcons' rushing attack, and Penix made them pay.
On Atlanta's first offensive touchdown drive, Penix went 5 of 5 passing and finished it with a touchdown pass to Kyle Pitts Sr. He finished the game 19 of 32 passing for 240 yards and a touchdown.
Along the way, Penix showed off the howitzer of a left arm that made him the No. 8 overall pick in 2024. On four separate occasions, he converted third-and-10 or more yards with long passes, and Drake London was his favorite target.
London finished the game with seven catches for 118 yards, his third straight 100-yard game with Penix as the starting quarterback.
If there was a chink in his armor, other than another injury, Penix struggled on bootleg passes that required a touch pass over a defender. One such occasion cost the Falcons a touchdown, and while offensive tackle Jake Matthews will feel he probably should have made the catch, Penix would probably say he could have made it easier with better placement and touch.
Another occasion saw Bijan Robinson open in the backfield, but Penix left it short with a defender pressuring him. Robinson had a lot of green turf in front of him had the pass been on target.
That said, there's no question Penix put the team on his back for more than two quarters as Atlanta couldn't find a running game en route to a 23-15 lead. The Falcons hope he will be healthy enough to start on Sunday against the Chicago Bears.
If not, Tua Tagovailoa could get the start he was scheduled to make in Week 1 after injuring an oblique three days before the opener in Pittsburgh.

title: Why the Falcons’ OT Loss to Ravens Could Be Wake-Up Call They Need
full_text:
For two weeks, the Atlanta Falcons were riding high on back-to-back wins over the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints .
The team was playing some inspired football behind the Week 3 return of starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr. , a reimagined offense after a disastrous first two weeks of the season, alongside a shutdown defense that earned high statistical marks across the NFL.
But the inevitable happened – the Falcons took a loss.
And it may be for the better.
“It’s heartbreaking to an extent,” said Atlanta cornerback Billy Bowman Jr.
“I know this team is going to bounce back, and the feeling in the building is getting back to work, focus on next week, and overcome this lesson.”
On Sunday Night Football, Atlanta (2-3) suffered a rare primetime game loss to the Baltimore Ravens (4-1). Baltimore visited Atlanta and left with a 30-23 Week 5 overtime win .
The Falcons led 17-9 midway through the third quarter, but were outscored 21-6 for the rest of the night. Backup quarterback Tyler ‘Snoop’ Huntley, replacing the injured Lamar Jackson , scored a one-yard sneak to take the overtime lead after nearly eight minutes of the 10-minute overtime period.
With Penix out of the game with a rib injury sustained from a hit by Ravens outside linebacker Tavius Robinson as time expired in regulation, Tua Tagovailoa came in to take it home.
That he did, after a 20-yard gain to wide receiver Drake London . Then, Tagovailoa in fact did take it home by tossing a game-sealing interception to Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton.
“Obviously, we didn’t do enough to win that game. Really missed opportunities,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski recapped the loss. “When you’re playing a good football team, and these margins are razor-thin, we’ve got to come through on some of those plays. We can be better in those moments. Disappointing, frustrating,  but we will learn from it.”
A culprit in the Falcons’ loss was struggling to stop the Baltimore rushing attack, as running back Derrick Henry led with 102 rushing yards, contributing to a 208-yard effort on the ground. The Falcons entered the game with the NFL’s top run defense .
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson eclipsed 100 scrimmage yards but was fairly neutralized.
“It’s just one game. It doesn’t define us,” Falcons tight end Kyle Pitts Sr. said. “We’ll get back to the drawing board and get these details right for next week.”
A Sunday positive was Atlanta’s ability to lean on Penix without its fine-tuned run game. The quarterback went 19-for-32 for 240 yards and threw a touchdown pass. London and Pitts were heavily involved in the offense.
Defensively, the defense showed it can get on the scoreboard as safety Jesse Bates III returned a 30-yard fumble recovery after safety Sydney Brown punched the football out of the hands of Ravens tight end Mark Andrews.
“We’re going to be good. It’s one game,” Penix reacted to the Falcons’ loss to the Ravens. “Obviously, it’s a game we felt like we could’ve won – we should’ve won. Whenever you get a chance to close out a game with a good team like that, you’ve got to do it. But we’re good with where we’re at. The loss sucks, but we’ve got to be ready for next week.”
So, in the loss, Atlanta has some building blocks moving forward in the season.
And now the Falcons are humbled entering another home game against the Chicago Bears in the potential return of quarterback Caleb Williams, who’s been out since Week 1 with a grade two right hamstring strain.
And the best thing about it is that Atlanta is still in play for the NFC South, holding on to the No. 2 spot behind the Carolina Panthers and ahead of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Saints.

title: How Hard Are Ravens Pushing Derrick Henry? The Data Is Alarming
full_text:
Ravens rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle would not back away from the potential for Derrick Henry to carry the ball 300 times or more this season, despite him being 32-years-old and despite him having never hit that mark in three straight seasons in his Hall of Fame.
Turns out, there was every reason to take him at his word.
Henry is being asked to do, already, things no running back his age has done since the NFL/AFL merger through five weeks of a season, and there is not reason to expect that to change much anytime soon. The Ravens have had to navigate through a new offensive line every week and huge issues at center (including moving rookie guard Vega Ioane there ), and they could very well be without two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson again this week, and it’s been a tough slow on the ground this season in ways Henry never experienced previously in Baltimore, but he is nothing if not a workhorse.
And despite this unprecedented load – as we will detail below – Henry still appeared to be one of the freshest and more impactful players Sunday night as the Ravens produced a game-winning, seven-minute drive in overtime, with backup Snoop Huntley at QB, during which Henry went over 100 yards and had the ball in his hands 25 more times and was at his best putting the game away.
“Obviously, we wanted to score, but I think having that drive was great for us to be able to keep the momentum going, keep the drive going, letting the clock run down, and just keeping that energy,” Henry said after the gutsy win. “I feel like guys were just focused on another level, and  great execution by every single body on offense. The O-line - hell of a job. They did a great job in the run game."
Henry is not having his most explosive season, and he is getting hit behind the line of scrimmage more than ever before as a Raven as part of the experimentation up front, but he remains as integral as ever to this offense and to keep a defense suffering from its share of issues off the field . And no Ravens coach has ever ridden him harder through the first five weeks of a season. And perhaps he could use more help from a blocking standpoint , too).
What he’s taking on already is simply historic.
Henry’s 113 carries through the first five games are the most in NFL history by a running back in his age 32 season. The great Walter Payton is second at 110, Curtis Martin has 105 at this point in that season and Otis Anderson (98) and Emmitt Smith (87) are the only others to carry the ball more than 80 times at that age at this point in the season.
Henry leads them with seven touchdowns through five weeks, while his 4.2 yards/carry is basically league average (Payton was at 4.6 at this point, while Ricky Williams, the only age 32 back since the merger to average over. 4.5/carry in that season, had run just 61 times through Week 5 (but at a robust 5.2/carry). We studied 55 years of age 32 running back data this offseason and the general portrait it painted was quite bleak – but Henry has long been a unicorn and if he gets more consistent run blocking there is reason to believe some of his efficiencies could spike.
Henry’s 476 yards are 30 behind “Sweetness” – the Bears legend who proved incredibly durable and consistent – for the most ever by an age 32 RB through five weeks. When Doyle refused to back away from lofty projection in terms of touches for Henry, he was not foolin around .
“He is a special talent,” Doyle said of Henry this summer. “There are not many guys in the league who can do what he does. The vision for him in the offense is an immense role. Obviously, I don't want to put a number on the amount of [carries], because obviously, as you look at every single week, every week is different. You want to be able to deploy things in different ways, and at the same point in time, he's going to have a pretty large workload.”
Only once previously in his career has Henry run the ball this much through the first five games, and that was in 2001 in Tennessee (142). Think about how the Titans ran their offense through him, and only once did he eclipse this 113 carry mark this soon.
Last year, Henry had just 64 rushes at this point in the season, and the year before he had 95. He’s essentially played one more game to this point than either of those two years at mid-October. In those seasons he was averaging 5.0 and 6.0 per carry to this point, so the yards have been tougher to come by now (0.99 yards before contact this season, 1.77 at this point last year and 2.66 in 2024).
Henry also already has eight catches for 62 yards and a touchdown; he’s never had more than 15 catches in a season as a Raven.
So, um, what exactly would it look like if Henry maintained this pace for the full season? Well, it would be painful, that’s for sure.
He is averaging 22.6 rushes per game, with would yield 384 carries if he kept it up. I did mention he’s never run 300 times in three straight years didn’t I? The 384 carries would surpass anything he’s ever done before. That 2021 season – the only time with more carries through five weeks – was cut short due to injury and he only played eight games.
Henry’s never carried more than 325 in a season in Baltimore and 378 is his career high (2000), the year he went over 2000 rushing yards. Perhaps that will truly be put to the test.

title: Lamar Jackson's Ankle Injury Is Still A Problem In Week 6
full_text:
The possibility that Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss another game with his ankle injury looms after the two-time MVP was unable to practice again on Wednesday. This week always presented a tricky challenge with Jackson’s health paramount and the team also juggling yet another unusual situation at center.
Head coach Jesse Minter spoke at the time of Jackson’s injury in Week 4 as if he may have had  chance to re-enter the game – that was never happening, by the way – which may have skewed the way some fans view the injury. But ankle issues can he difficult for running quarterbacks and while the team has called this “day-to-day” at times the reality was it was always “week-to-week” with a real chance he does not return until Week 7 as we have been pointing out.
Minter again couched the injury as “day-to-day,” but it also seems less than ideal that Jackson would likely only practice limited Thursday (him coming back from this long out and practicing fully right away would be a surprise) and then go into a walkthrough Friday and play. Minter reiterated that Jackson can play without practicing, but given where this injury is on his body, and how the Ravens have been handling injuries in general early this season , that may end up being empty rhetoric to try to plant doubt with the Browns as to who is playing.
“It’s definitely day-to-day,” Minter said, and alluding to his original description of the timetable added, “I think a lot of times those things, right when they happen, you’re not sure … When he’s able to be out there, he will.”
Back-up Snoop Huntley was excellent in the fourth quarter and overtime of a comeback win at Atlanta on Sunday. If Huntley gets the bulk of the reps with another totally new center – recent trade acquisition Cam Jurgens – and then Jackson gets the start, that would be a little odd.
Jurgens was never going to be able to practice fully right away as he was acquired – for a desperately steep price – from the Eagles last week after just entering the concussion protocol. He must continue to get cleared for more work with doctors and if he is unable to still practice fully on Thursday it further cuts into the timeframe to work with the quarterbacks.
It also remains to be seen if Jurgens is actually an upgrade of rookie guard Vega Ioane, who was doing an exception job all things considered.
Minter essentially confirmed that top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson is getting fully cleared to return after having a procedure on his injured finger two weeks ago. “I expect him to be able to play,” the coach said, adding he is “super excited to get him back.” The Ravens badly need a more consistent edge push on third down, with their secondary getting picked apart on that money down and the cornerbacks the biggest underachievers on this roster by a wide margin.
Receiver Rashod Bateman has been limited but Minter implied he will be good to go and the Ravens are hopeful that rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane will be returning from Injured Reserve as well. Rookie tight end Matthew Hibner – who should be in line for way more snaps with starting end Mark Andrews fading fast – is dealing with a hand injury but he was able to return on Sunday night and play the second half after suffering the setback.

title: Ravens Week 5 Rookie Report: Vega Ioane Shines In Primetime
full_text:
Several members of the Baltimore Ravens' 2026 rookie class saw extended action in Sunday's overtime thriller of a 30-23 road win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 5. They are in an AFC North division in which every team's record is above .500, and at 4-1, they sit alone atop the standings heading into next week.
Drafted and undrafted first-year players saw extensive playing time in all three phases. The only rookies who were healthy scratches were fourth-round wide receiver Elijah Sarratt and undrafted quarterback Joe Fagnano, who still suited up as an emergency No. 3 option. Fifth-round running back Adam Randall wasn't activated from short-term injured reserve in his first week of eligibility, while third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane is now eligible to be activated from the list. Seventh-round defensive tackle Rayshaun Benny is on the practice squad and has yet to be elevated.
Here’s an overview of how these rookies performed in their late taste of NFL regular-season action.
The first-round interior offensive lineman made his second straight and final start at center before sliding back over to right guard and was superb once again. While some of his non-under-center snaps weren't on point all night, his blocking performance was, as he didn't allow a single pressure on 38 pass-blocking reps and his 71.9 run-blocking grade from Pro Football Focus was the highest on the team. Ioane was leading the way on several of the Ravens' biggest and most important plays, whether it was Zay Flowers' 13-yard run on the first play from scrimmage of the game, Derrick Henry's 18-yard touchdown on a screen play and Tyler Huntley's quarterback sneaks that included the game-winning score.
"For him to be able to do what he has done, play the way that he has played, [it is] pretty remarkable, I would say," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I do not know who votes for Rookie of the Year and all that stuff, and it is really, really early in the season, but he is a very impactful rookie for our team that has done things that I do not know that any rookies have ever done. Having to play those two positions [and] get shifted over to center in a game where you have to go on a drive to try to win the game, then to play the way that he has played in these big moments, [it is] pretty cool to see."
The second-rounder was one of several players for whom this game served as a homecoming, as he wasn't just born and raised in Georgia; Atlanta is his hometown, where he played at Westlake High School. He played a season-high 40.6% of the Ravens' total defensive snaps, set a strong edge on early downs against the run and finished with a pair of total tackles, including a solo takedown of Falcons star running back Bijan Robinson for a minimal gain of three yards in the first quarter.
Young had his first career tackle for a loss negated on the Ravens' huge fourth-down stop in the third quarter after official review ruled that the completion to tight end Charlie Woerner , whom he tackled two yards behind the line of scrimmage, was incomplete. Either way, he was at the right place at the right time to prevent a successful conversion.

The fourth-rounder made his second straight start, and the only reason he saw a slight reduction in his playing time instead of another increase was that he left the game on a cart at one point due to a hand injury. However, he'd eventually not only return to action but make a key block on one of the biggest plays of the game, where he helped spring Henry into the end zone on the game-tying two
Derrick Henry's game-tying 2 Pt conversion run looks like an option "read", but really isn't. With the Ravens going up against a run-centric offense, the fifth-round nickel saw his fewest snaps on defense in the four games he's played in, with 19, but he did play a season-high 15 snaps on special teams. He recorded a pair of solo tackles, struggled at times in coverage and had a bad whiff on a missed tackle that came on third-and-long and allowed Falcons rookie wide receiver Zachariah Branch to pick up a first down on a career-long 23.

The sixth-round specialist had back-to-back stellar performances, with a game that saw him be a field-flipping weapon once again, as a key to helping the Ravens win the battle of field position. He pinned the Falcons' offense inside their 20-yard line three times on his four punts, averaged 44.3 yards per punt with a long of 54 and didn't have a single punt returned against him for the second time this season.
With four-time Pro Bowl veteran edge rusher Trey Hendrickson out recovering from finger surgery a second straight week, the undrafted free agent played double-digit snaps on defense again after playing exclusively on special teams through the first three weeks. During his 17 snaps, Burke recorded a career-high three total tackles, including a solo takedown of Robinson for a minimal gain of four yards in the second quarter.
Although he wasn't credited with a pass defensed, he was responsible for forcing an incompletion to Falcons wide receiver Drake London on a flat route on a play where he dropped into underneath coverage instead of rushing.
