title: Ravens 3 Biggest Needs 1 Month Before Trade Deadline
full_text:
The Ravens already made their biggest swing at the trade deadline, giving quite a haul to the Eagles to find out if Cam Jurgens can still play center.
It was a massive pay in terms of draft-pick compensation including a future second-round pick, and it was a steep price in terms of taking on $15M fully guaranteed next year on top of a $16.5M salary this season for a player who may or may not have been getting benched in Philadelphia who carries extreme injury risk. So there’s that.
Ravens general manager Eric DeCosta has swung big heading into the deadline – which comes in early November, many years in his long reign and he’s only stuck impact once, landing Roquan Smith from Chicago to try to fix the defense in 2023; then he overpaid Smith with a hasty contract extension has felt the sting of that since. So thinking he will navigate this crucial time of the roster landscape expertly demand hopes and prayers, and with a team-record payroll and after the Jurgens trade I wouldn’t expect much.
That doesn’t mean more needs won’t develop between now and the deadline. And it certainly doesn’t mean they won’t do anything to address them.  As it stands now, the Ravens are in expert health from a long-term standpoint and the roster is in good shape overall, especially if the 10 rookies on the roster can increase their timeshare as the season goes on.
These are the areas that still warrant the closest inspection:
It’s a “Zay And Pray” downfield passing game until proven otherwise, with Zay Flowers having a monster season but now one else providing much in terms of explosives or YAC, and certainly no one else when it comes to catching balls that travel 20 or yards downfield. Their alleged No. 1 move tight end, Mark Andrews, has been cooked since late in the 2024 season , though rookie Matthew Hibner should start cutting into his route volume ASAP.
Tall slot receiver Ja’Kobi Lane barely got a target on the NFL before he broke his wrist and that sapped the momentum he established in the summer. At 6-4 and slithery with a flair for acrobatic catches, he could provide a spark immediately in the slot and in the redzone . But, alas, Rashod Bateman is erratic and Devontez Walker might be a more of a tease than a real thing, and this skillset has been an obvious cause for concern for years now.
Marlon Humphrey is not a $19M corner and it ain’t even close . Would he be best inside playing the slot? Probably but they don’t have much they like on the boundary and there is an abundance of options and body types in the slot including hybrid defensive back Kyle Hamilton and rookie Chandler Rivers and youngster Keyon Martin. So um, this is it.
Top wideouts are tearing this defense up pretty good and a better pass rush with the return of Trey Hendrickson from injury could help that cause . But this staff seems very reticent to lean into veteran Chidobe Awuzie nearly as much as last year’s staff and something is giving them trepidation.
Humphrey on No. 1 receivers won’t work and Nate Wiggins had issues Sunday with Drake London and larger targets will do that to him. Baltimore is playing more dime than anyone in the NFL and ranks 20th in opposing passer rating with six DBs on the field, allowing 66% completions. Oh and their corners do not have an INT all season. Here’s what No. 1 receivers have done since Week 2 (and the real challenges from better QBs are still to come).
The corners are allowing a combined passer rating of 101 and 11 yards per completion and they aren't impacting the football (four total pass breakups to go with the zero interceptions. They are the biggest underperformers on this football team and it isn't close .
Drake London (ATL): 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Carnell Tate (TEN): 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Chris Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
With the Bengals looming and the Jaguars and the Bills, and even the new-look Panthers, we'll know plenty about if this group is good enough to go deep in the playoffs by their early December bye.
I thought Lucas Scott did enough in the preseason to merit a practice squad spot as a young fullback; with Durham Smythe able to fill a “Joker” role , turns out they didn’t need him, but with Smythe out for the year he’s back. Not sure Nick Vannett is athletic enough to do what Smythe did and the need for a traditional fullback could emerge and it could be Scott isn’t there in his development yet.
Smythe was adding serious impact to the run game and the pass game and Hibner and fellow rookie tight end Josh Cuevas weren’t expected to have to contribute heavily in that regard at the line of scrimmage. Overall, tight end has always looked like a problem area and a body short of where you would like with a QB in Lamar Jackson, still dealing with an ankle injury , getting more deadly the more TEs are on the field.

title: Ravens Most Underperforming Position Group Entering Week 6 Will Shock You
full_text:
The Ravens offense was was brand new. The Ravens defense was supposed to be stout Week 1.
The offense had all the new coaches who had no ties to this organization and a totally foreign system and a coordinator who had never called a play before . They had a totally reconstructed interior offensive line and need a host of rookies to make an impact on that side of the ball.  The offense was going to need time to adjust and adapt and there would be a lot of penalties along the way … and despite those infractions the offense has still been by far the strength of this football team. By far.
And that’s despite the only real winning downfield option, Zay Flowers, missing about half the season to this point and another starting receiver, rookie Ja’Kobi Lane, playing only a few snaps before he headed to IR and with two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson missing a game and iffy to play Sunday and with four players already handling center duties through five weeks.
So color me surprised and give major kudos to that 30-year-old coordinator , Declan Doyle, for managing this transition expertly. But, um, also color me shocked that this secondary hasn’t been much more impactful and specifically the corners and the free safety. Head coach Jesse Minter was already a proven defensive play caller and all the money and resources were in the secondary and this system is a “cousin” of what Mike Macdonald ran to perfection here (as Kyle Hamilton dubbed it).
And all of the corners are back from last season and the only new addition of note to the entire secondary was a veteran box safety and the group has been almost entirely healthy.  They just haven’t been nearly good enough.
Given that Minter’s superpower is coverage and the back end, and given that he is flooding the field with defensive backs more than almost anyone in the NFL (second at 32% - NFL average is 8%) and ranks 20th in opposer QB rating and completion percentage out of dime, we got problems. And considering their late-game third-down issues are coming in dime, and they have only faced one above average QB all season (Dak Prescott) it’s fair to say the corners especially have a long way to go, and the secondary as a whole.
“I don't think we played well, for real,” Hamilton said after Sunday’s comeback win in Atlanta. “We still – the third-down stuff was crazy … Third down, we have to do better. But it obviously feels a lot better fixing those mistakes with a win. I might be a little too cynical or critical, but we can be better."
Nah, he’s just being honest. Here’s where they need to get better, fast.
Hamilton just alluded to another rough night on third down, with Atlanta’s suspect QB Michael Penix, just back from a third ACL surgery, going 7/12 throwing on third down against the Ravens’s dime packages, including three conversions on third and 10 and one on third-and-11 and another on third-and-15. Can’t happen.
On the season opponents are converting 45% of their third downs in the second half of games against the Ravens when they throw the ball; Baltimore ranks just 27th in that metric. Yikes. Better pass rush would help but these are all highly paid guys and/or first-round picks back there with a premier schemer and play caller … unless maybe some of them aren’t quite as good as the GM thinks?
One of the great things about Minter’s scheme with the Chargers is it put everyone in position to make plays on the ball and he had a bunch of mid-round picks at corner and they got off the field with interceptions. They were third in the NFL in INT% in two years under Minter and entering mid-October the Ravens corners have combined for … wait for it … no picks.
Baltimore has three picks all season and they were all on very shallow passes to the middle of the field and all were essentially picked off underneath by linebackers – middle linebacker Roquan Smith and Hamilton in a linebacker role. The corners have played 485 total pass rush reps, combined, by the way, without that INT.
The Ravens have built up many big leads this season and made teams one-handed, and it’s been obvious that suspect QB for the most part would be forced to chuck the ball around and they also have faced many teams with an absolute funnel on where the ball was going – Drake London on Sunday in Atlanta and Carnell Tate with the Titans and Chris Olave with the Saints.
Yet, um, dudes are not making plays on the ball. At all. Even with high volume from weak QBs who are making turnover-worthy throws. Here’s how the Ravens corners have fared in coverage. Hint – it sucks:
Opposing QBs : 49/74 (66%), 537 yards (11 yds/comp), 3 TDs – 0 INTs, 101.0 rating 6 Passes 20+, 31 1st Downs, 2 DPI, 4 pass break ups
Now hold your nose, because here are the numbers for corners + free safeties:
Opposing QBs : 70/100 (70%), 836 yards (11.9/comp), 5 TDs – 0 INTs, 111.9 rating 13 passes 20+, 41 1st downs, 3 DPI, 4 PBUs
=Let’s see what Joe Burrow and Trevor Lawrence and Josh Allen have in store if this doesn’t get cleaned up real quick.
The Ravens were lucky that Daniel Jones was on a wonky Achilles Week 1 and Alec Pierce was never right with the ankle problem and couldn’t even function as a pretend downfield decoy. Since then, here’s how things have been going:
London (ATL) : 7/11, 118 yards, 7 1st D
Tate (TEN) : 9/12, 145 yds, 6 1st D
CeeDee Lamb (DAL): 7/8, 112 yds 5 1st D
George Pickens (DAL): 7/11, 82 yds, 4 1st D
Olave (NO): 8/10, 86 yds, TD, 6 1st D
Yeah, better get to work back there, now.

title: Calais Campbell Made History And Honored Late Mother With Ravens In Week 5
full_text:
The last time Ravens defensive end Calais Campbell was in the state of Georgia before the team's Week 5 game against the Atlanta Falcons was in the wake of unspeakable tragedy for him and his family.
In late June, about a month before the six-time Pro Bowler was slated to report to his 19th and what he believes will have been the final training camp of his illustrious Hall of Fame-worthy career, his mother, Nateal Campbell, was found slain at her Buckhead townhouse in Atlanta during a welfare check.
To make matters even worse, his older brother, Ciarre Campbell, was arrested at the scene and charged with murder after police found him in possession of a knife.
Sunday would've been the former matriarch of the family's 72nd birthday. Instead of being celebrated on the same day her son was slated to pass NFL legend Jim Marshall for the record for most games ever played by a defensive lineman from a suite or somewhere in the stands at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, she was watching over him from further above. Yet, he still felt her presence as the battle-tested Ravens rallied to beat his former team 30-23 in overtime .
"I just wanted to play my heart out for my mom today." Calais Campbell talked about honoring his mother in last night's victory. 💜 pic.twitter.com/Z2yKgSKyPS
"It felt really good. I just wanted to play my heart out for my mom today [and] honor her," Campbell said. "I felt like I achieved that goal. I left it all on the field today."
Before the game, he wore a memorial shirt in her honor with pictures of her on it, and with his siblings in attendance.
Calais Campbell with a loving pregame tribute to his late mother, Nateal: “She would’ve been here, celebrating loud as can be. … I’m just grateful that I had a wonderful mother.” Calais will set the NFL record for games played by a DL tonight, breaking a tie with Jim Marshall… pic.twitter.com/REKLY1wIna
"She would've been here celebrating loud as can be, getting hype, telling me to go out there and make some plays," Campbell said in a video tribute on Instagram. "I'm just grateful that I had a wonderful mother for all the years I had her."
The 40-year-old expressed even greater gratitude after the game when his teammates came through on what was a very special yet still somber day for him and the whole Campbell family.
"I feel really good to honor my mom today and I am really happy that we got a win," Campbell said. "I know a lot of the guys were trying to get a win because they knew how much this meant to me, and I am very grateful."
It's one thing to hang in and bounce around the league for a decade plus, but to do what Campbell has been able to pull off in his late 30s and officially his 40s as of Sept. 1, is nothing short of spectacular.
Despite nearly two decades on the job, he continued to show he is still one of the best interior disruptors in the game in  Week 5 against the Falcons, the team he signed with after his first stint with the Ravens ended.
"I really did not make a whole lot of plays, but I felt like I was playing some of my best football of my career, in spurts," Campbell said.
Humility is another one of the honorable traits that the team captain and former Walter Payton Man Of The Year award recipient possesses. However, he sold himself short when recalling the plays and significant contributions he made to the best performance by the Ravens' revamped defense of the season in his 283rd career game.
Atop the record books. Calais Campbell has now played more games than any defensive lineman in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/JzO3AmaEwh
Campbell played 50% or more of the Ravens' total defensive snaps in a game for the third time this season and helped fellow multi-time Pro Bowler and his former mentee, Nnadmdi Madubuike lead the charge in stifling what had been a juggernaut of a Falcons' rushing attack the previous two weeks. He recorded a pair of total tackles, both of which were solos, including one that went for a loss. His overall grade of 85.1 was the highest given to a Ravens player on either side of the ball.
Calais Campbell is still a dawg in his 283rd career NFL game. pic.twitter.com/QwXOk1ZAAy
"It is hard to even explain just the work that [Campbell] puts in, how he goes about his business, the pro that he is, how he makes everybody around him better," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I know he was dealing with some, obviously, emotional thoughts and things, playing in Atlanta [on] his mom's birthday.
"I mean, [it is] pretty amazing. It was really cool to see the guys have his back, I would say, and know that that meant a lot to him without him having to say anything about it. [I] just feel very blessed to be around Calais and have him on our team, and him be the leader that he is and impacting our team the way that he is, both on the field, obviously, and in the locker room."

title: Ravens Head Coach's Words And Actions Indicate This About Lamar Jackson's Status
full_text:
The Ravens have one of the best records in the NFL while having to workshop around a multitude of personnel and injury issues and face a significant upgrade in level of competition starting in Week 7.
This week presents another unique challenge for rookie head coach Jesse Minter as he prepares for his first AFC North game, on the road at Cleveland, with his offensive line likely to be reshuffled for the sixth-straight week and with quarterback Lamar Jackson’s status in limbo with an ankle injury and his practice time almost surely to be compromised. Now is not the time to deviate from the overarching medical approach that has served Baltimore well during its 4-1 start, and backup Snoop Huntley was excellent in the clutch Sunday night.
There is a strong case to be made for taking no risks with Jackson unless he is able to practice fully at least by Thursday, and a multitude of sound reasons why erring on the side of caution at this point in the season – for a team in Super Bowl or bust mode – makes all the sense in the world. And Minter seems to understand as much. The Ravens have taken the longview with other star players and even in the way the coach spoke Monday about his two-time MVP quarterback it was clear to the discerning ear that he is going out of his way not to raise expectations to the level where his return is anything close to guaranteed.
“Definitely doing better,” Minter said of his superstar QB. “Wednesday, I am not sure about exactly how that practice will look, but again, to Lamar's credit, he is doing everything he can to get back out there. I thought he was awesome (on sidelines Sunday night). There are a lot of cool pictures and clips of him on the sideline in between series talking to Snoop' and hyping guys up.
“What a wonderful teammate and leader that he is, even when he was not playing. So, I am very, very proud of Lamar for handling himself like that, and again he is doing everything he can. I think we will know more definitely by the middle of the week.”
Here’s why we wouldn’t be surprised at all is Jackson came back Week 7 against the Bengals:
The fact Minter made Wednesday sound that murky tells me Jackson isn’t practicing fully to open the week and if Huntley looks good in practice and if Jackson is likely to be limited on Thursday, then should we just devote all the snaps to Snoop and let Lamar take over the following week? With all the offensive line shake-ups are we going to throw multiple QBs into the mix?
Minter leaving things that open ended, and the fact that Jackson was ruled out last Friday and there was no real emphasis put on his pre-game training and work, tends to point to a multi-week absence. This is a team that was very cautious with Zay Flowers early this season and waiting longer with Nnamdi Madubuike’s return from neck surgery than they might have to try to get him back to close to normal, every-snap form before activating him. They brought in a new sports science team headed by former New Zealand rugby trainer Dr. Nic Gill in the offseason to try to rethink their approach to some of this stuff.
Even the call to have newly-signed, $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson get a procedure on his finger that would take him out at least two weeks spoke to them taking a long-term view with potential lingering issues for key players in September/October given how this franchise’s success is measured in January.
The Ravens appear to be in quite the hurry to try someone else at center now – this will be center No. 4 since the start of the regular season – after paying a very steep price to land offensive lineman Cam Jurgens from the Eagles last week in a very risky acquisition . But he was in the concussion protocol when they landed him and was never going to practice last week or play in Week 5.
A player returning to play must go through a battery of sessions off the field and then full work off the side and then come through that okay and be cleared to eventually return to full practices. How will all of this sync up with Jackson also being able to practice anything close to full enough to actually get to practice with this new center before he can play? The idea that Jackson could do nothing all week and then get cleared after a glorified walk-thru and play a game Sunday with a center he has literally never worked with before is quite a stretch.
Remember it’s not like Jurgens has been here for practices and training camps and OTAs before. He just got here. Now, don’t get me wrong, I am more than fine with sticking with Vega Ioane at center – and I am far from convinced that Jurgens is some big immediate upgrade from how that rookie was performing brand new to the center position – but we know how it works and they got Jurgens to impact them right away (it wreaked of a level of desperation likely not warranted ).
But these timelines might not align with also making a late QB switch over the weekend.
Jackson in general needs to feel very good about his body and how fine tuned he is to play at the genius levels where he operates. And while the Browns have very good talent in key defensive spots, the Ravens play a top-five schedule from here on out in terms of quality of opponent defense.
From Week 7 on, the Ravens play six straight teams that went to the playoffs in 2025 ahead of their bye the first week of December. Their season is going to come down to the final four games, invaribly – all AFC North contests – and for all that Huntley brings, having to try to get into the playoffs with him in the dead of winter unable to push the ball downfield isn’t going to work … like it didn’t work last season.
It would make sense for Jackson to truly test himself in practice on mutliple occasionsl before I’d play him this week, and the Ravens are already sending signals that might not be how the work week plays out.

title: Three Ways Ravens Rookie WR Ja'Kobi Lane Can Boost Ravens Offense
full_text:
The Ravens should be getting rookie receiver Ja’Kobi Lane back at the perfect time.
They could certainly use him.
The “Zay And Pray” offense remains very real for the Ravens , with top receiver Zay Flowers continuing to carry an extremely heavy load in the pass game and even being asked to chip in more now in the run game with backup Snoop Huntley in for Lamar Jackson last week and the offensive line constantly reshuffled due to injury and ineffectiveness.
Baltimore could badly use a new element to be folded into the passing attack no matter who the quarterback is Sunday at Cleveland, and there is reason to believe Lane could return soon enough as he is eligible to leave Injured Reserve with the four-week minimum absence now complete. The wrist surgery did not preclude him from getting in cardio and trying to keep his conditioning base, though it remains to be seen if he requires more than a week of practice to be cleared to play.
Lane played only one half of the Week 1 game at the Colts before suffering the injury, curbing the momentum he took into the season after a dominant summer in training camp and the preseason games. The Ravens released veteran receiver Chris Moore on Tuesday - he'll sign to the practice squad soon enough - creating a spot on the active roster for Lane.
“Ja'Kobi has done a really good job,” Minter said. “I would say sometimes, when you are going through an injury and you are on IR, how much can you do physically to be ready to play, to your point, that first week back?
“I think he is in a really good place from a conditioning standpoint, from what he has been able to do with the training room and the rehab standpoint. So, we will see how that shakes out on Wednesday.”
There are some immediate ways Lane can contribute.
Flowers has been an absolute beast in the slot, but the guy getting the second-most run there, tight end Mark Andrews, can’t move or separate and is looking each week more like a sunk cost . Flowers has 318 receiving yards in the slot and a gaudy 16 yards/catch. The rest of the team have combined for 248 yards in the slot on 12.4/catch.
Lane was doing a lot of his damage in the preseason in the slot , especially on crossers and working the middle of the field, where at 6-4 he is a great compliment to Flowers, who is smaller and shiftier. And having the big target in the slot who can separate and capitalize on a large catch radius is even more important as the field gets constricted in the …
This was a major area of concern a year ago, with Baltimore 27th in redzone passing. So far this season Jackson has been an expert in this part of the field and he and Huntley have found six different pass catchers on redzone TDs (all with one each(.
Lane’s body type is a natural to do damage and he is slithery and can leave his feet to make a play. Jackson had a lot of success throwing to former move tight Isaiah Likely in this areas the last few years and no doubt the Ravens had replacing some of that stuff when they took Lane in the third round.
There really isn’t anyone doing anything on this team in this regard except for Flowers. Lane and fellow rookie Matthew Hibner are their best chances to start changing that.
Flowers is first on the team with 182 yards after the catch; running back Derrick Henry is second at 97, astoundingly for a guy who rarely gets targeted. Flowers has done that in basically playing the equivalent of three games considering injury absences. Rashod Bateman is second on the team in YAC among receivers with a paltry 52 in five games.
Lane should be able to offset that wide divide even if his opportunities are fairly limited as he works back into the offense. Jackson loves big targets and has his highest passer rating throwing to tight end and Lane can certainly work a lot of areas on the field that Andrews did before he fell off.

title: Unsung Heroes From The Ravens’ Week 5 Win Over Falcons
full_text:
In Week 5, the Baltimore Ravens came out on top in their first primetime game of the season with a 30-23 overtime victory over the previously surging Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football. While they were one of three AFC North teams to emerge victorious this past week, since the Cleveland Browns were the only ones who didn't, they now sit alone atop the division standings at 4-1.
In a game where they came in not favored to win with their star quarterback and pass rusher out , the Ravens never led at any point during regulation and mounted an impressive late rally to earn their third straight win.
The Ravens were able to secure the victory thanks to some underrated yet impactful performances from a handful of well-known starters and some of their less-heralded players making plays in all three phases of the game.
Going up against the top-ranked defense in the league in terms of applying pressure and stopping the run, this unit held up in pass protection when it mattered most and imposed its will when it came to run-blocking. The Falcons went from allowing 193 rushing yards in their first four games combined to letting the Ravens rack up a season-high 208 yards in one night, and the big boys in the trenches deserve just as much, if not even more, credit as the stars of the game such as backup quarterback Tyler Huntley and running back Derrick Henry.
Two players who deserve special recognition for their performance and grit are rookie interior lineman Olaivavega Ioane and third-year right tackle Roger Rosengarten. The first-round offensive guard was stellar in his second straight start at center, aside from a couple of off-target snaps, and Rosengarten showed some excellent situational awareness after briefly leaving the game when he wisely leapt out of his stance when a Falcons defensive player jumped into the neutral zone before the snap. In doing so, he drew five-yard penalties on two separate occasions, and while that might not sound like a big deal, when mounting a comeback while short-handed on the road, every inch and yard counts and can be the difference between being on the outskirts or just within comfortable field goal range.
On the other side of the ball, the Ravens faced another tall task with a second-ranked rushing attack through four weeks and one of the best pass-protecting offensive lines in the league. After a shaky start to the season, in which this unit was still getting healthy and gelling, it played its best game to date under a national spotlight. The collective effort it took to bottle up arguably the most explosive running back in the game, Bijan Robinson, to 86 yards on 17 carries began with how the Ravens played up front in the trenches along the interior.
The combination and rotation of Pro Bowlers Nnamdi Madubuike and Calais Campbell, with fellow starter Travis Jones and a handful of snaps from John Jenkins and Broderick Washington, not only led the charge to stuff the run but also applied some nice interior pressure as well. Madubuike was getting constant penetration into the backfield, registering a quarterback hit and nearly had a couple of sacks. Campbell had his best game of the season in his second stint with the team, recording a pair of tackles, both of which were solos, and one went for a loss as he received the highest overall grade of any player on either side of the ball from Pro Football Focus with an 85.1 .
Calais Campbell is still a dawg in his 283rd career NFL game. pic.twitter.com/QwXOk1ZAAy
While the third-year pro didn't see a single snap on offense for the fifth week in a row as Henry and fellow veteran Justice Hill split backfield duties, he still made his presence felt in a noticeable way as one of the Ravens' most active and impactful special teams players. Ali's 17 snaps in the third phase of the game tied veteran safety K'Von Wallace for the fourth-most on the team; he led all players in special teams tackles with both a season and career single-game high of three total, including a pair of solos.
After battling through a hamstring and calf injury that caused him to leave last week's game early and limited him during the week of preparation, the four-time Pro Bowler was not only one of three players who played 100% of the Ravens' defensive snaps, but he also made some key plays. While he was one of several defensive backs who got picked on at times and gave up some conversions in coverage, he was highly impactful when sent on well-timed blitzes.
Humphrey recorded a quarterback hit and applied quick pressure on a huge fourth-and-short stop in the third quarter that resulted in a completion to a diving tight end who was tackled short of the line to gain by rookie outside linebacker Zion Young. He finished with four total tackles, including two solos, and was the Ravens' fifth-highest-graded defender with an overall grade of 67.
The @Ravens defense gets the stop on 4th down! @BALvsATL on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/0UrbWMHtd4
All Pro safety Kyle Hamilton was far from the only Georgia native on the team who had an impact and made their presence felt in this game. On a day in which long-snapping was under a microscope around the league after botched and high snaps led to disaster, the seventh-year veteran was on point all game for the Ravens, delivering accurate snaps to rookie punter Ryan Eckley to boot away and get in place for second-year kicker Tyler Loop to drill through the uprights. Moore's most notable play of the night was the physical solo tackle me made on the Ravens' second punt of the game in the second quarter for his second of the season in his first time playing in the 2018 SEC Championship as a senior at the University of Georgia.

title: Nnamdi Madubuike's Impact On Ravens Defense Can Already Be Felt In These 3 Ways
full_text:
Nnamdi Madubuike is getting better by the week.
Progress won’t always be linear, especially with the former All-Pro defensive tackle coming off neck surgery in the spring, and assignments vary from week to week based on the prowess of the opponent, but there is no doubt that this lineman is back to being a disruptive force, it’s hard to imagine the Ravens would have had nearly as much success neutralizing Atlanta’s vaunted rushing attack without him, and the best is still to come with just three games under his belt.
Especially with the Ravens having to play without $30M/year pass rusher Trey Hendrickson the last two weeks, Madubuike’s presence has been vital and he is making a major impact across the board already. His mere ability to log more playing time, and impactful playing time, has allowed everyone else in their defensive line rotation to perform on at a less-demanding rate (and 40-year-old Calais Campbell is coming in right at the pitch count talked about this summer) .
Here’s how Madubuike, 28, is already making everyone else better by being in the middle of this defense:
Madubuike has played 140 snaps over three games, which has settled everything else down. He is sixth on the team in reps in that span, but only middle linebacker Roquan Smith and the regulars in the secondary have played more. By comparison, Travis Jones – a Robin who has to be Batman when Madubuike is out – is second on the team in snaps on the defensive line over the last three weeks with just 107.
It’s like Madubuike has played one more game than the rest of this group since he’s come back. That’s a tall ask and the Ravens did quite well to take the approach they did with his return , not activating him until they believed he could take on a significant role rather than a very gradual ramp up.
Guess who leads the Ravens in pressures over the last three weeks?
Yup, Madubuike with 11. He’s playing a heavy load, as noted above, and still getting a 13% pressure rate and that’s despite there not being a proven disruptor off the edge and him facing some stout offensive lines in that span.
Madubuike is second on the team in QB hits since he came back and tied for first with six QB hurries. He’s seeing the double teams again and extra attention and also had to deal with a trip to Brazil for his first game back in over a year, so he’s only really getting into the flow of a normal schedule now.
It’s only a matter of time before the sacks start coming and getting the chance to play some games up from with Hendrickson should help in that regard. The Ravens need to get the edge pressure rates cranking.
If you recall, a Dallas team that can’t run on anyone ran all over the Ravens in Brazil. That was Madubuike’s first game back, it was essentially his preseason all in one afternoon and he was just getting back used to rotations and playing with this defensive line. And, uh, the run defense the last two weeks has been excellent
Tennessee’s Tony Pollard entered Week 4 on a tear for two weeks averaging round 5.5 yards per carry on under center runs; those went nowhere against the Ravens with Madubuike anchoring. Pollard ran 16 times for 48 yards (3.0/carry).
Atlanta’s Bijan Robinson came into Week 5 the best back in the NFL, averaging 7.4/carry on outside zone and with the Falcons rolling up 477 rushing yards in the past two games. Robinson ran 17 times with just three rushes of five yards or more against the Ravens; he had one carry for 38 yards and 16 for 48.
If this defense becomes the top five unit many believed it could be in Jesse Minter’s first season as head coach, Madubuike will have everything to do with it. So far, so very good.

title: Three Buffalo Bills With Most to Prove Entering Week 6
full_text:
Week 5 was full of highs and lows for the Buffalo Bills as they knocked off the Los Angeles Rams in overtime .
It was a thrilling game that seemed to be going in the Rams’ favor, until Greg Rousseau blocked a field goal in overtime . That allowed Buffalo to drive down the field for a game-winning field goal of their own.
That win means they’re now 4-1 and in control of the AFC East . The Bills don’t have time to celebrate, however, as they’re preparing to take on the Las Vegas Raiders on the road in Week 6. Buffalo will be favored in this one, but they can’t take the Raiders lightly. They also have multiple players entering Week 6 with a lot to prove, including the following three Bills.
Dalton Kincaid got off to a hot start this season, hauling in 14 passes for 225 yards and a touchdown over the first two weeks. Since then, his production has dropped significantly. He had three receptions for 38 yards in Week 3 but has just two catches for seven yards in each of the past two games.
When Kincaid is at his best, this offense is nearly unstoppable. When he disappears, everything seems much more difficult. That’s why they need him to turn things around as they get ready to play the Raiders on Sunday.
Monday night was not the best showing for safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson. According to PFF, he allowed five receptions on seven targets for 63 yards and a touchdown. In addition to his struggles in coverage, Gardner-Johnson was penalized for unnecessary roughness on second-and-16, giving the Rams a fresh set of downs and 15 penalty yards.
Gardner-Johnson was added this offseason in an attempt to shore up the back end of the Buffalo secondary. He’s had some great moments, including an interception against the Los Angeles Chargers, but hasn’t been getting it done in coverage over the past couple of weeks.
James Cook is one of the more dynamic running backs in the NFL. After five games, he has 532 rushing yards and five touchdowns while averaging 5.6 yards per attempt. He also has a serious fumbling problem.
Cook already has four fumbles on the season, including a critical lost fumble that nearly cost them the game against the Rams, if not for Rousseau’s blocked field goal. Cook’s fumbling problem has been a hot topic, even leading to Joe Brady making it clear that it has to stop . All eyes will be on Cook, who is still one of the best players on the roster, but is feeling the pressure following his ball security concerns.

title: Bills' WR Week 6 Injury Outlook: When Will DJ Moore, Josh Palmer Return to Action?
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' receiving corps faced the Los Angeles Rams without the services of veterans DJ Moore and Josh Palmer , and their absences were more than noticeable.
In the 37-34 overtime road win , Bills' wide receivers combined for 87 yards on four receptions.
Khalil Shakir's three catches for 80 yards and Keon Coleman's seven-yard touchdown grab accounted for the position group's only production on Monday Night Football in Week 5. Fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell was unsuccessfully targeted twice while Trent Sherfield and Khalil Shakir got no looks.
To say the offense will be better off once both veterans, especially Moore, return is quite the understatement. As for when that will happen, no real hints emerged on Wednesday at the Bills practiced at UC Irvine.
Buffalo held a walkthrough, meaning all practice participation statuses on the official injury report are only estimations. Moore was a non-participant while Palmer was deemed limited.
"We're going through a walkthrough today, so it's really not gonna be able to tell us much. We'll kinda see how it looks tomorrow," said Brady on Wednesday.
Although Brady was specifically answering a question about starting right tackle Spencer Brown, who left Monday's win after 16 snaps , the statement also applies to Moore and Palmer.
Moore has been dealing with an AC joint sprain since Week 2 when he landed hard on his shoulder while diving for a pass in the end zone late during the second quarter against the Detroit Lions.
Fighting through what mainly appeared to be a pain tolerance issue, Moore suited up in Weeks 3 and 4 despite being limited during practice. He reaggravated the injury in the first half against the New England Patriots on October 4, and missed the remainder of the 29-26 loss.
Moore was a non-participant at the first two practices in Week 5. After getting on the field in a limited capacity on Saturday, he was officially questionable for the Monday road game.
Apparently unable to go, Moore was scratched prior to kickoff, ending his 91-game consecutive appearance streak. Even with the bye week looming, one has to think more wants to get bqck out there as soon as possible.
"No one's gonna be 100 percent healthy right now. We just played a Monday night game. We're five weeks into the season. It's part of the growing. If guys can be out there, the anticipation is for them to be out there," said Brady prior to Wednesday's
When asked how Moore handled sitting out in Week 5, Brady took a long pause before simply saying "yeah," and moving onto the next question.
After plagued by a lingering knee/ankle throughout much of a disappointing 2025 campaign, Palmer was healthy as the Bills kicked off 2026.
Unfortunately, his availability streak ended at four games due to a shoulder injury that he picked up during last Friday's practice. After initially appearing on the injury report as limited , Palmer missed Saturday's practice and was ruled out for the game .
"He got kind of twisted up yesterday in practice. We're still kinda going through some of the testing and whatnot," said Brady on Saturday.
The fact that Palmer was estimated as limited, as opposed to a non-participant, on Wednesday is a positive sign. Practice participation, however, has not necessarily been a factor in determining whether the injured player will be available on game day.
"There's going to be guys that aren't going to be out there today that still have a chance at playing, and probably are going to play this weekend," said Brady earlier this month.
The Bills will practice again on Thursday in Irvine as they prepare to visit the Las Vegas Raiders on October 18.

title: Analyst Blasts Buffalo Bills For Having ‘Not a Sustainable Winning Model'
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills are 4-1 and are coming off a wild win over the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night, so everything is just peachy keen, right?
Well, not exactly. The Bills have a lot of stuff to clean up in order to put themselves in the best position possible to accomplish their ultimate goal.
Former SportsCenter anchor and analyst Trey Wingo recently took to X to point out just how much the Bills are lacking on defense, and with turnovers and penalties.
And, Wingo believes that what the Bills are doing right now just isn't sustainable.
Yes (the Buffalo Bills are) 4-1," Wingo began . "But look a little deeper: they’re 30th in total defense, 28th in points per game, have a -4 turnover differential and are a top 10 most penalized team… this is not a sustainable winning model. Lots to clean up here."
The Bills have coughed up the football nine times this season and only four teams have more. What's worse is James Cook and Josh Allen have combined for seven of those, with Cook having two lost fumble and Allen having four picks and one lost fumble. In all, the two Bills stars have combined for eight fumbles, losing three in total.
That's a major problem in and of itself and things have gotten so bad with Cook that head coach Joe Brady even threateneed to take carries away from him , something the offense can't afford.
When it comes to takeaways, Buffalo only has five and just six teams in the NFL have fewer. The Bills could better cover for their poor defense by taking the ball away more often, but they have not been able to do so in 2026.
The Bills sport the second-worst pass defense in the NFL, but they have actually been decent against the run, ranking 15th.
Last but not least, we have penalties, with Buffalo notching 43 thus far, good enough for the sixth-most in the league, per NFLPenalties.com .
Now, again, the Bills can have these issues and make the playoffs, especially when they're scoring the amount of points they have been. Buffalo leads the NFL with 32.8 points per game.
But this is the Buffalo Bills we're talking about here. Simply going to the postseason is not enough. This team has to win a Super Bowl or it's a total disappointment, plain and simple.
Once the competition gets tougher in January, these issues will become more glaring and much more difficult to overcome.
Then, you're depending on perfect play from Josh Allen, which we know doesn't always happen, especially in the playoffs.
All of that adds up to an increased chance the Bills will do what they always do in the postseason, which is hit a wall and get eliminated.
Thankfully for Buffalo, it has ample time to clean all of this up, but whether or not they'll actually be able to do that remains to be seen.

title: Bills' QB Josh Allen 'Fighting Some Stuff' as Eli Manning Sees Major Area to Improve
full_text:
Outside of either outside linebacker Gregory Rousseau or kicker Tyler Bass, quarterback Josh Allen was undoubtedly the most important player on the field for the Buffalo Bills to end Week 5 in the National Football League.
The team’s prized gunslinger almost single-handedly willed the Bills to a win against the Los Angeles Rams under the primetime lights of SoFi Stadium on Monday Night Football .
The ninth-year veteran’s performance, in every sense of the word , was simply electric from the quarterback spot.
However, despite what his positional title might imply, it was Allen’s legs—not his “golden” arm—that was the difference-maker during Buffalo’s seemingly improbable road victory in Inglewood, California.
In comparison to his counterpart on the Rams’ sideline, Matthew Stafford, who completed 74.1% of his passes on 54 attempts for 383 yards, three passing touchdowns, and no interceptions in the losing effort, Allen completed just 12 of his 19 throws—which was good for a completion rate of 63%—for only 210 passing yards, one passing touchdown, and one interception.
On the ground, however, the former 2018 first-rounder, who stands at 6-foot-5 and weighs 237 pounds according to the team’s official roster, accounted for more than half of Buffalo’s total rushing output (234 yds) for the night as he registered an astonishing 121 rushing yards and one touchdown on only 10 carries against Los Angeles.
And, considering the glaring fact that the Bills’ only had two wide receivers—Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman —record a reception during their most recent win, it’s a good thing that Allen was able to have such a big day in the running department.
Of course, that’s not all that unusual.
The former University of Wyoming playmaker has made quite a habit of being a thorn in the sides of his opponents when using his legs in the past ever since first entering the league nearly a decade ago, but right now it seems like more of a necessity than ever.
Well, not only is Buffalo experiencing issues with injuries to wideouts D.J. Moore and Joshua Palmer at the current moment, but the 30-year-old franchise superstar admitted after Monday’s game that he’s struggling with some of the finer points of playing the position right now.
It’s frustrating, but the Firebaugh, California, native is pushing through the adversity . . . just like the Bills collectively did as a team against the Rams when their backs were against the wall.
Right now, Allen leads the league in total touchdowns with a mark of 15, but he’s tied for only 16th in the NFL in passing touchdowns with seven and is sitting at 10th in passing yards with 1,249 yards on just 91 completions.
And, given running back James Cook’s struggles with putting the ball on the ground right now, it’ll be prudent for Buffalo’s aerial attack to start picking up steam a little more as the season progresses, regardless if there are injuries at wide receiver or not.
Doing so this week against the Las Vegas Raiders would be a good start.
“It’s football. You can be down and out one play, and the next play you’re on top of the world. And, again, that’s just how it rolled for us today. A lot of things to clean up. Early on, (I) just didn’t feel like I was in a rhythm, (and I) wasn’t taking some of the underneath stuff.
“(I’m) fighting—mechanically—some stuff right now that I’m working on. But, I felt like in that second half I got into a rhythm, (and) guys made some plays,” Bills’ quarterback Josh Allen said following the overtime thriller out West on Monday night.
“(We’ve) gotta’ be better in the pass game . . . we understand that, but we’ll take a win no matter what. It’s just kind of the way the game rolled. It’s a really good secondary, (and) it’s a really good defense. . . . Just (keep working on) ball position. You know, it coming out of my hand, I want it to feel as good as possible.
“And, that second half, I just said, ‘You know what? Turn off the mind, and throw the dang ball.’ And, that’s kind of what I did, and (it) felt pretty good.”
While the split differentials between the first half to the second half weren’t drastically different for Allen, they were slightly better as he was just 4-of-7 passing for 60 yards and an interception in the first 30 minutes of game action before finishing the final 30 minutes of regulation by going 8-of-11 on his passing attempts for 93 yards and one touchdown.
In overtime, in addition to his two carries for 32 rushing yards, the veteran completed his only registered pass attempt for 57 yards, which went to wide receiver Khalil Shakir after his first attempt of the extra period was negated by a penalty thanks to a hold by rookie wide receiver Skyler Bell .
So, with that in mind, the statistics did seem to improve for Buffalo’s quarterback through the air as the game progressed, which is exactly what he referred to in his postgame press conference.
The yardage gained on the passing play in overtime, however, is a bit misleading. But, that’s not necessarily a bad thing.
Well, when provided further context that Shakir caught the ball just five yards past the line of scrimmage on the explosive play before proceeding to run free for the remaining 52 yards, it proves that Allen doesn’t need to be putting several air yards under his passes in order to make an impact with his arm.
Yes, he might have the strongest arm out of any of the other quarterbacks in the NFL, but in back-to-back games he’s thrown questionable interceptions on deep passes that seemingly had no business being put in harm's way in the first place.
If Allen would just take what the defense is presenting him, then maybe the offense would be able to operate even more effectively, which would certainly be a scary proposition for opposing defenses considering that Buffalo is currently averaging 32.8 points per game—the highest in the NFL through five weeks of the 2026 season—while scoring on 54.7% of their drives, which would be the highest rate in the history of the league if it were to stay that way for the remaining 12 games. Right now, the 2007 New England Patriots hold the record with a points-per-drive rate of 52.7%.
First-year head coach Joe Brady has already stated earlier this fall that he believes Allen has a new level to reach in his career . And, apparently he’s not the only observer who feels that way.
During a segment on ESPN2 ’s ManningCast during Monday Night Football between the Bills and Rams, two-time Super Bowl MVP quarterback Eli Manning said that Buffalo’s franchise leader isn’t always living up to the standard of what it takes to be a successful passer in the NFL.
While nobody seems to question his lack of intimidating weapons at wide receiver, especially with the previously mentioned Moore and Palmer currently sidelined, there are moments when Allen gets way too greedy in Manning’s opinion.
The film shows that there are options available to him, but Allen—for whatever reason—is simply choosing not to throw it . . . which is obviously a concern.
“Sometimes, Josh—he has guys open—he doesn’t always throw it. . . . He kind of has the quick out right here to the right to Coleman. You know, it’s 3rd-and-7, you can throw that, and he can turn it up and get the first (down),” former New York Giants’ quarterback Eli Manning said on Monday as he was pointing out a particular play where Allen was sacked by Rams’ EDGE defender Josaiah Stewart on the opening drive of the first quarter.
“Sometimes, because he has such (an) ability to scramble and make plays, he kind of won’t always take the open guy. You know, sometimes it’s, ‘Hey, let’s take it. It’s 3rd-and-7, we called a quick out, (so) throw the quick out.’ Take some of these completions. Just because you have the ability to scramble, we can still get the ball out on time a little bit more.”
While Brady and the offensive staff certainly won’t want to handcuff Allen by taking away his ability to scramble, there’s no denying that capitalizing on the easy “gimmes” would make…

title: Buffalo Bills' Highest And Lowest Graded Players in Week 5
full_text:
It was a full team effort on Monday Night Football as the Buffalo Bills defeated the Los Angeles Rams 37-34 in overtime.
As expected, this proved to be a battle of heavyweights as both teams had more than their share of explosive plays. That included a couple of huge swings in overtime. The Rams thought they had it won following a fumble by James Cook but a blocked field goal by Greg Rousseau ended that.
Buffalo capitalized by hitting a field goal of their own, courtesy of Tyler Bass, which gave them the win. With the dust settled on that showdown, let’s look at which Bills’ players earned the top grades from PFF, as well as those who earned the lowest.
Kaleb Elarms-Orr didn’t get many snaps, but he did his job well when he was on the field. With Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams not living up to expectations, it will be interesting to see if the rookie gets more time after his performance. The only other defender in the top five was fellow rookie T.J. Parker, who was fourth with a 78.9 . Parker had three tackles while Elarms-Orr had one, while also recording one pass deflection.
Offensively, Dion Dawkins and Alec Anderson were at their best , which kept Aaron Donald from ruining the game plan. They finished second and third, respectively. Third-down back Ty Johnson had his best game of the year, recording 72 yards on four receptions. He was the fifth-highest rated player but in all honesty, Buffalo may not have won if not for some of his clutch receptions.
Maxwell Hairston’s rocky sophomore campaign continues as he finished with a team-low grade of 28.6. Hairston had just 17 snaps, which is his least of the season, but gave up 32 yards while surrendering a reception both times he was targeted. C.J. Gardner-Johnson followed Hairston after giving up multiple big plays, including a touchdown. The third defender on the list was linebacker Terrel Bernard, who hasn’t seemed comfortable in the new defensive scheme.
On offense, Tylan Grable struggled mightily once he went in for an injured Spencer Brown. Also landing in the bottom five was Skyler Bell, who had no receptions on two targets in his debut game.

title: Bills and Eagles Connected as Possible Trade Partners Ahead of NFL Deadline
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have an issue at the cornerback position and one analyst thinks a trade with the Philadelphia Eagles should be in order.
The Bills' cornerback play has not been up to snuff through five games. Not only has Christian Benford struggled, but so have the two guys playing opposite him, second-year corner Maxwell Hairston and rookie Davison Igbinosun.
Igbinosun is allowing a passer rating of 104.0 when targeted and has given up a pair of touchdowns. Hairston has also given up two scores, but his completion rate and passer rating allowed are 60% and 79.2, which aren't terrible. However, clearly the Bills aren't thrilled with him after he lost his starting job in Week 5 .
In all, only one team in the NFL is giving up more passing yards per game than the Bills and that just cannot continue.
With their issues at cornerback, Bleacher Report's Alex Kay thinks the Bills should trade for Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Kelee Ringo.
"With Ringo playing out the final year of his rookie deal and unlikely to stick around the City of Brotherly Love beyond this trying season, dealing him outside of the NFC for a late-round pick would be a shrewd move for a reeling Eagles side that is falling out of contention," Kay wrote. "The 6'2", 207-pound corner could benefit from a change of scenery and would get every opportunity to reach his ceiling in a Buffalo secondary that has become downright desperate for capable defenders."
After having a fairly regular role with the Eagles last season, Ringo has completely fallen off the map on defense. Over five games, he has not played a single defensive snap and is instead only contributing on special teams (113 snaps).
That puts Ringo on the map to be traded, as does his expiring contract.
We couldn't say for sure, but for a late-round pick, it's worth it to see if he can.
In 2025, Ringo only played 311 snaps in 17 games, but he did make three starts. He also showed flashes of being an effective cornerback with a 56% completion rate allowed and a passer rating permitted of 83.7 on 25 targets thrown his way.
Again, there's no guarantee Ringo would even make a dent, but at the very least he can provide more depth and competition for the Bills' cornerbacks room, two things the team could certainly use. Ringo's special teams prowess would be an added benefit if he doesn't ever secure a regular role on defense.
We project Ringo costing about a sixth- or seventh-round pick, and it may only take a swap of late-round picks to get a trade done.
For that cheap price, general manager Brandon Beane would be wise to take a swing on the former fourth-round pick.

title: Bills' Week 5 Snap Count Takeaways: Maxwell Hairston Benching, Ray Davis Revival
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills increased opportunities for two important second-stringers during their Monday Night Football road win over the Los Angeles Rams.
Backup running back Ray Davis and second-round rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun each saw season-high snap counts in Week 5.
In all, the Bills' offense was on the field for 64 snaps while the defense saw 82 snaps during the overtime affair.
Quarterback Josh Allen along with offensive lineman Dion Dawkins, Alec Anderson, Connor McGovern and O'Cyrus Torrence did not come off the field on offense. Meanwhile, safety Cole Bishop was the lone player deployed for all of the defense's reps.
Here are the top takeaways from the Bills' snap counts during the 37-34 road win over the Rams on October 12.
Bills' Official Week 5 Snap Counts at Rams [ @NFL345 ] pic.twitter.com/cH002du1jn
Although Maxwell Hairston, a 2025 first-round draft pick, struggled mightily against the New England Patriots in Week 4, head coach Joe Brady confirmed his starting status heading into the Monday night matchup.
When the Bills took the field for their first defensive series against the Rams, however, veteran Christian Benford and second-round rookie Davison Igbinosun were the starting outside cornerbacks.
It wasn't until the second quarter that Hairston saw his first snaps of the night. He finished with only 17 reps at cornerback (a 21 percent snap share). Meanwhile, Igbinosun saw a season-high 69 snaps (84 percent).
It's also notable that the undermanned Bills' defense chose to deploy practice squad defensive back Anthony Kendall for 31 snaps as the slot cornerback instead of using Hairston as a fill-in there.
Still, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard claimed the decision on playing time had more to do with Igbinosun's hot hand than a performance-based reflection on Hairston .
"The intent was not to limit his snaps as much as we did. We thought IGB was playing well yesterday and kind of rolled with him on the outside," said Leonhard on Tuesday .
Igbinosun, who appears stronger against the run than Hairston, totaled seven tackles and one pass break-up against the Rams' high-powered attack. There are signs that the Bills are considering at least 50-50 platoon moving forward.
According to Brady, earlier this month, the plan is to find more chances for Davis to contribute on offense.
"But the running back right now, I got to get Ray playing more," said Brady in the wake of  the Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
Davis averaged only six offensive snaps over the season's first four weeks, but his saw an uptick on Monday night. After bringing the heat on the opening kickoff, returning the ball 70 yards to the Rams' 26, Davis proceeded to see 10 offensive snaps. He touched the ball three times on offense, twice as a rusher and once on a 31-yard catch-and-run.
While the Bills gradually upped Davis's playing time, bellcow starter James Cook fumbled twice during the game . The second miscue turned the ball over to the Rams in overtime.
"Some point, there has to be consequences when we're putting negative stuff out there. And so it's the conversations that we're having on going. James knows it's important to him, but that can't happen. And it's going to cost us football games. It almost cost us one. ... So, it's got to improve, or the carries are going to decrease," said Brady.
It's not out of the question for the Bills to move closer to their approach from 2024 when Cook played only 50 percent of snaps with Davis seeing a 24 percent share.
Once tabbed as a potential training camp cut candidate , defensive lineman DeWayne Carter has become a key piece in the rotation thus far this season.
Carter totaled 37 snaps against the Rams. It was the fourth game in a row where he was on the field at least 45 percent of the time.
"DeWayne has been very consistent. He's physical. We need him to be physical. We need him to change the math in the run game at times, and he's doing a great job of that," said Leonhard.
Carter, a 2024 third-round draft pick, missed the entire 2025 campaign after tearing his Achilles prior to the opener.
"Anytime you see a guy coming off an injury like that, he's continued to grow in his confidence and his physicality on the field," said Leonhard.
Defensive lineman TJ Sanders had yet to see live game action this season due to a minor knee issue and a subsequent unrelated appendectomy.
Debuting against the Rams, the 2025 second-round selection logged 51 snaps. He made five tackles in addition to a consequential stop on a two-point conversion attempt.
"TJ was great. He was like a little kid out there, man. He was really excited to get back on the field and show what he can do. And it wasn't perfect by any stretch, but he fought. He battled," said Leonhard.
There were three noteworthy moments when players were forced to exit due to in-game injuries on Monday night.
Atop the list, starting right tackle Spencer Brown left after 16 snaps and did not return. Called into duty, Tylan Grable subbed in at right tackle for the ensuing 48 snaps.
Benford, who missed the Week 4 loss due to a toe injury, initially appeared to reaggravate his foot issue while tackling Puka Nacua. He was cleared to return after missing five snaps.
Safety Chauncey Gardner-Johnson, who played 78 of 82 reps, went down due to a potential knee problem . He was briefly examined before returning.
Backup safety Damar Hamlin was in action for 26 snaps.

title: Bills' Roster Gymnastics: Re-sign 2x Super Bowl Champ 24 Hours After Releasing Him
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills needed game day insurance at three different positions to face the Los Angeles Rams on October 12, but each team is permitted to make only two practice squad elevations per week.
As a result of the limitation, the Bills had to exercise some roster gymnastics that included temporarily releasing veteran edge rusher Mike Danna.
Needing to make room for practice squad defensive back Anthony Kendall , Buffalo cut its sixth outside linebacker.
Danna, a two-time Super Bowl champion who joined the Bills in the offseason , was in line to be a healthy scratch on Monday night. Therefore, it made sense to move him off the roster in order to sign Kendall, who proceeded to play 31 defensive snaps in the 37-34 overtime road win.
On Tuesday, the Bills officially brought Danna back onto the 53-man roster, releasing Kendall in a corresponding move.
With Danna's veteran status exempting him from waivers, Buffalo apparently planned to subsequently re-sign him all along. The Bills are reportedly bringing Kendall back to the practice squad provided he clears waivers.
The Bills were forced to scratch two wide receivers , two interior defensive linemen and their starting slot cornerback in Week 5 due to injuries.
With DJ Moore fighting through an AC joint sprain that was reaggravated in Week 4, and Josh Palmer injuring his shoulder during Friday's practice, Buffalo elevated wide receiver Trent Sherfield, who also brings value to special teams. Sherfield played seven offensive snaps and took 17 reps on specials against the Rams.
After both tweaking a knee against the Patriots, defensive linemen Ed Oliver and Landon Jackson were unavailable for Monday Night Football. The Bills called up Phidarian Mathis as a substitute. He was in the field for 18 percent of the defense's snaps.
It was an ankle injury to starting slot cornerback Dee Alford that necessitated the Kendall move. With back nickel cornerback Jordan Hancock already on Injured Reserve, Buffalo was undermanned in the defensive backfield.
The 28-year-old Danna spent his first six NFL seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs. The 2020 fifth-round draft pick made 87 regular season appearances, including 49 starts, before the Chiefs cut him loose this past February.
The Bills signed Danna in June, and he showed enough to earn a roster spot in a crowded edge rusher room headlined by Greg Rousseau and Bradley Chubb. With Buffalo needing only five edge rushers on game days, Danna was a healthy scratch three of the first four weeks.
Danna, who has 21.5 career sacks, made his Bills' debut in Week 2 when Oliver injured himself during pregame warmups. He saw eight defensive snaps in the September 17 victory over the Detroit Lions.

title: Lead NFL Announcer Highlights Career Parallels Between Josh Allen And Peyton Manning
full_text:
Sometimes, Buffalo Bills’ franchise quarterback Josh Allen seems otherworldly .
A player once thought by many outside observers to be a walking joke when first entering the NFL in 2018 out of the University of Wyoming is now literally rewriting the record books of professional football.
In fact, the running joke within Bills Mafia has become that Allen is seemingly always “the first player in history to” . . .  fill in the blank.
And, ultimately, the joke isn’t far off from reality, as just the other night against the Los Angeles Rams the former Wyoming gunslinger became the first player in league history to record a rushing touchdown in five straight games to start a season, while also becoming the only player in history to ever record over 200 passing yards on fewer than 20 attempts and over 100 rushing yards on 10 or fewer attempts in the same game.
It was an impressive performance .
And, in the end, Allen—who finished the game 12-of-19 passing for 210 yards and one touchdown through the air in addition to tallying 121 rushing yards and one touchdown on just 10 carries— willed the Bills to victory over the Rams under the primetime lights of Monday Night Football at SoFi Stadium.
Following back-to-back performances against the Los Angeles Chargers and New England Patriots that were seemingly subpar by Allen’s standards , the dazzling display from Buffalo’s unquestioned leader out West was exactly what fans were hoping to see to end Week 5.
But, is the superstar’s current statistical pace —which has actually only been seen twice before in the NFL—something that is sustainable moving forward? Furthermore, is it a recipe for Super Bowl success later on in February for first-year head coach Joe Brady and Co.?
Well, according to legendary broadcaster Jim Nantz, who is the lead play-by-play annoucncer for NFL on CBS, not only does he see the current output as sustainable, but Allen’s legacy is beginning to shape up in a similar fashion to that of another walking football legend: former Indianapolis Colts’ and Denver Broncos’ quarterback Peyton Manning.
Manning, who recorded over 50 total touchdowns in 2013—a trajectory Allen is still on track for after last night’s road win over the Rams—appeared in four Super Bowls ( SB XLI, SB XLIV, SB XLVIII, and SB 50 ) during his 18-year career. However, he didn’t reach and win his first Super Bowl until 2009 . . . his ninth season in the NFL with the Colts.
Coincidentally, Allen is also now in Year Nine with Buffalo.
“I wish (Josh) could enjoy the ride, but—until he gets there—it’s going to always be with him. It’s never going to leave him. And, I believe just like you (Peyton), that when it breaks through—and maybe this is the year—there are going to be multiple trips (to the Super Bowl) afterward.
"His career really does parallel yours Peyton." Jim Nantz thinks Josh Allen will have a path similar to Peyton Manning 👀 pic.twitter.com/PGZmk5x2mP
“It’s a story that you see (every so often) in sports, and it’s a great story to tell, you know, if you go back through the years,” longtime broadcaster Jim Nantz said while on ESPN2 ’s ManningCast during Buffalo’s victory over Los Angeles on Monday Night Football .
“Phil Mickelson—in golf—could never, supposedly, win the big one, and he got asked that question forever. (Peyton), you got asked that question forever. . . . (It’s about) just defying the odds and silencing the critics, and what’s better than that?
“I mean, really, truly? You know . . . I think his career does, in many ways, parallel yours, Peyton. I really do.”
While some fans may question that sentiment from Nantz, especially considering how shaky things are on the defensive side for the Bills at this point in time, there’s no denying that Allen appears to be on a bit of a rampage this season to right all the wrongs of his past.
It hasn’t exactly been pretty each week so far, but the results speak for themselves. After already finding a way to win on the road at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas, in Week 1 for the first time in his career, Allen’s overtime victory against Los Angeles on Monday evening was also the first of his NFL tenure.
Might there be another first in his future later this February? I mean, he’s already gotten himself acquainted with SoFi Stadium this season, so who knows?
The Bills just might be making a return visit in a few short months if Allen keeps up his do-it-all, Superman mentality moving forward.
At this juncture, it’s Buffalo’s best shot at a championship run .

title: Joe Brady Puts James Cook on Notice as Bills RB's Fumbling Issues Continue
full_text:
Buffalo Bills running back James Cook has an issue with fumbles that once again reared its ugly head on Monday night.
During the Week 5 game against the Los Angeles Rams, Cook had a pair of fumbles and lost one of them . And that lost fumble came at a crucial time, as Cook coughed up the rock in the overtime period and nearly cost his team the game.
Thankfully for the Bills, Greg Rousseau blocked Harrison Mevis' field goal on the next drive, which saved Cook and the Bills and allowed Buffalo to drive down the field and win the game.
On Tuesday afternoon, head coach Joe Brady didn't mince words about Cook's fumbling issues and even said that Cook could lose carries if the problems persist.
"I have all the confidence in him, that's why I put him right back out there," he said of Cook . "But, obviously, at some point there has to be consequences to when we're putting negative stuff out there."
"That can't happen and at some point it's going to cost us football games, and it almost cost us one," Brady added. "And so, it's got to improve or the carries are going to decrease."
That's a bold statement from Brady, who is threatening to take carries away from last year's rushing champion.
That said, Cook's fumbling issues have gotten so bad that it's necessary to put him on notice in the hopes it will lead to the veteran running back fixing his major problem.
Cook has a whopping four fumbles in five games this season.
Of course, this is not a new issue for Cook, who has struggled to hold on to the football throughout his career. Cook had six fumbles last season, and he had four in 2023.
According to Pro Football Focus , Cook's 10 fumbles since last season are the most in the NFL among running backs. The next closest player is Atlanta Falcons superstar Bijan Robinson, who has seven in that span. So, that goes to show you Cook isn't the only elite running back to have this issue.
Considering the fact that we're just five contests into this season and he is already two shy of his career-high puts an extra bright spotlight on the problem that has plagued Cook for far too long.
The problem with lessening Cook's carries is that it will hurt the offense. Ty Johnson and Ray Davis are solid backs, but they do not have the game-changing ability Cook has.
However if Cook is hurting the team and costing it games, like he nearly did on Monday night, his advantage in ability over the other two doesn't mean as much.

title: It's Time to Ask the Question Panthers Fans Didn't Expect This Soon
full_text:
Maybe Panthers fans are finally starting to believe in this offense.
During a recent discussion on the Carolina Panthers subreddit , one fan asked a pretty simple question: “Maybe the offense we have here is legit?”
After watching the first four games, it's a fair question.
The Panthers have scored more than 30 points in three of their first four games and have 121 points on the season. That's the most points Carolina has ever scored through the first four games of a season, which is kind of crazy when you think about some of the offenses we've watched around here the last few years.
Carolina put up 37 against Chicago, followed that with 34 against Atlanta and then scored 32 against Detroit before the bye. Cleveland is the only team so far that has kept the Panthers under 30.
Detroit was the game that really made me start thinking about this differently. Young threw for 329 yards, Tetairoa McMillan had 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns, and Carolina kept finding ways to move the football.
At some point, three games like that can't just be brushed off as a couple of good Sundays.
The other thing I like is that it doesn't feel like one guy has to do everything. McMillan has obviously been a huge part of what Carolina is doing, but Jalen Coker has made plays, Chuba Hubbard is still a big piece of the offense, and Young has more places to go with the football.
That's a much different feeling from what we've seen in Carolina lately. There have been plenty of Sundays when getting to 20 points felt like pulling teeth. Now the Panthers have gone over 30 three times in four games.
I'm not going to sit here after four games and say Carolina suddenly has one of the best offenses in football. That's getting a little ahead of ourselves, and there are going to be games when it doesn't look this good.
But I'm also done acting like what we've seen so far doesn't mean anything.
Maybe Panthers fans are still getting used to that part. We've watched enough bad offense over the last few years that it's probably natural to see Carolina putting up points and immediately wonder when it's going to stop.
We aren't even a quarter of the way through the season, so there's a long way to go. But three games with more than 30 points are enough for me to at least start looking at this offense a little differently.
That fan on Reddit asked a pretty good question.
Maybe this offense really is legit.
