title: 4 Bold Panthers Predictions That Could Turn Week 6 Upside Down
full_text:
If you had asked me after the Chicago game if the Panthers could go into Philadelphia and beat the Eagles, I probably would've laughed. Now? I think they can.
I'm not saying Carolina suddenly has everything figured out because they beat Detroit. I watched the Bears put 59 points on this team in Week 1, and I'm definitely not forgetting that. But I've also watched the Panthers look like a completely different team since then.
Philadelphia isn't exactly rolling right now, either. The Eagles have lost three straight after falling 19-17 to Jacksonville on Sunday, while Carolina got a week off after beating Detroit 32-26. I don't know if the Panthers are suddenly better than Philadelphia, but I'm not looking at this game the same way I was a month ago.
Maybe I'm buying in a little too much. We'll find out Sunday, but here are four predictions I'm willing to put out there.
I'm finally starting to trust Bryce Young, and it's taken me a while to get here. We've done this before with Young. He'll play well, everybody starts talking about how he's turned the corner, and I'm usually sitting there thinking, “OK, show me again.”
I don't think that's unfair after everything we've watched during his first few years in Carolina. Young threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, and he now has 1,268 passing yards and nine touchdowns through four games. He's only thrown two interceptions, and Carolina isn't asking him to just stay out of the way anymore.
They're putting the ball in his hands and letting him go win games.
I expect Philadelphia to come after him on Sunday. I'd also expect the Eagles to make stopping Chuba Hubbard a priority after he ran for 122 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. If they load up against Hubbard and basically tell Young, “Go beat us,” I'm interested to see what happens.
A month ago, I would've said that's exactly what Philadelphia should do. I'm not so sure anymore.
Prediction: Young throws for 315 yards and two touchdowns.
OK, this one might get me in trouble. Tetairoa McMillan just caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit, and now I'm asking him to go into Philadelphia and score twice again.
I'm not predicting another 192 yards because that would be getting a little ridiculous. If he does that again, we're going to have to start having a much different conversation about just how good McMillan already is. But I can't get away from how much Young trusts him.
When Carolina needs a play, everybody watching knows where Young wants to go with the football. The defense knows it too, and lately it hasn't mattered. Philadelphia is obviously going to have a plan for McMillan after watching what he did to Detroit, and I wouldn't be surprised if he sees extra attention, especially around the red zone.
I'm still taking him. Maybe I'm asking for too much here, but McMillan has reached the point where I'm done trying to figure out what his ceiling is every week.
Prediction: McMillan goes over 100 receiving yards and catches two touchdowns.
I don't know what to do with this Panthers defense anymore. I just wrote an entire article trying to figure them out, and I'm still not sure I did. They give up too many yards, they don't get nearly enough pressure, and there are drives where I'm sitting there wondering how they're ever going to get off the field.
Then somebody makes a play.
Carolina has eight takeaways through four games. At first, I kept wondering how long that could continue, but we're getting to the point where maybe I need to stop asking that question. Maybe this is just what this defense is.
I'm not predicting Carolina shuts down Jalen Hurts because I don't believe that's happening. Hurts is going to make plays, Philadelphia is going to move the football, and there will probably be a couple of drives where this Panthers defense drives me crazy. But if Carolina can give Young two extra possessions, that could completely change this game.
And I've got a feeling one of them comes late.
Prediction: Hurts turns it over twice, including once in the fourth quarter.
This was one of those games I looked at before the season and pretty much put in the loss column. Carolina going into Philadelphia and winning? I would've needed to see a whole lot before I was willing to make that pick, and I think I've seen enough.
That doesn't mean I'm sitting here telling you Carolina is better than Philadelphia. I'm not. But the Panthers don't have to be the better team for the entire season. They just have to be better for three hours Sunday, and right now I'm not sure Philadelphia is playing better football than Carolina.
The Eagles have lost three straight, while the Panthers went into the bye after beating a Detroit team that I wasn't sure they were ready to beat. Young is playing the best football we've seen from him, McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, and Hubbard just ran for 122 yards against Detroit. Then there's that defense I still can't figure out, but somehow it keeps getting the ball back.
Maybe this completely blows up in my face. Philadelphia could come out angry after losing three straight, score a couple of quick touchdowns, and have me regretting every word of this by halftime. That's part of making a bold prediction.
A month ago, there's no chance I pick Carolina here.

title: The Panthers Are Making Bryce Young's Job Nearly Impossible. He's Doing It Anyway
full_text:
I'm starting to run out of things to question about Bryce Young , and I didn't think I'd be saying that four games into this season.
I've been hard on Young. I don't think I've been unfair, but I've definitely been one of those people who wanted to see more before I started believing he had finally turned the corner. One good game wasn't going to do it for me, and honestly, two probably weren't either.
How often NFL quarterbacks have been under pressure and how they've fared in 2026 Bryce Young has been terrific despite a shakier #Panthers OL pic.twitter.com/qD73ja5vWT
Then I saw this chart from PFF's Bradley Locker, and it made me look at what Young is doing a little differently. I knew Carolina's offensive line had struggled. You don't watch these games and miss how often Young has somebody coming after him, but I didn't realize it was happening this much.
Young has been pressured on roughly 47% of his dropbacks. That's almost half. Look at Locker's chart, and Young is sitting way over on the right, almost by himself, while still carrying a passing grade under pressure of around 64.
I looked at it and thought, how in the world is he playing this well?
For most of Young's career, I've wondered what he would look like if Carolina could just give him some help. Get him a legitimate receiver. Give him a running game. Protect him. Put something around the guy, and let's find out whether he can actually play.
Carolina has finally done some of that. Tetairoa McMillan looks like a legitimate No. 1 receiver, Chuba Hubbard has been really good, and the offense looks nothing like some of the messes we've watched the last few years.
The protection is where things haven't gone nearly as well.
There are reasons for that. Taylor Moton has been out, Monroe Freeling has had to move to right tackle after playing almost exclusively on the left side at Georgia, and Damien Lewis missed the Detroit game. Corey Bullock had to step in at left guard, so Carolina hasn't exactly had the luxury of putting the same five guys out there every week and forgetting about it.
I get all of that, but 47% is still 47%. At some point, I stopped looking at that chart and thinking about the offensive line and started thinking about Young. Because if we're going to criticize him when he doesn't play well — and I certainly have — then I think we have to give him some credit for what he's doing right now.
Young has thrown for 1,268 yards, nine touchdowns, and only two interceptions through four games. He just threw for 329 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit in a game I wasn't sure Carolina could win. And he's doing all of this while getting pressured on almost half of his dropbacks.
Maybe I've been looking at Young the wrong way.
I spent a lot of time wondering whether he could be good enough if Carolina finally put the right pieces around him. Now I'm starting to wonder how good he could be if the Panthers actually kept him clean. That's a much different conversation than the ones we've been having about Young for the last few years.
I'm still not ready to go crazy after four games. There's a lot of football left, and Philadelphia coming out of the bye is going to tell us even more about where Young and this offense really are. Ask me again in a couple of weeks, and maybe I'll feel completely different.
But I'm also not going to keep moving the goalposts every time Young answers another question. I wanted to see him do it more than once, and he has. I wanted to see what happened when things weren't perfect around him, and I think getting pressured on nearly half of his dropbacks answers that one pretty well.
Now, for the love of God, can somebody block for him?

title: Chargers Projected to Make Blockbuster Trade Soon & Panthers Must Be on Receiving End
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers entered this season with one unit most in need of improvement: the pass rush. Carolina's pass rush was the worst in the NFL in 2025, making it the focal point of free agency .
Carolina's splash signing of Jaelan Phillips showed how desperate the Panthers were to improve the pass rush, and while it has improved thus far, the room lacks depth.
The Panthers already started the season down a pass rusher, as second-year EDGE Nic Scourton tore his ACL on the first day of training camp. Now, Jaelan Phillips is hurt . It's not nearly as serious, but his status for Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles is in question.
Phillips hurt his hamstring in Carolina's Week 4 victory over the Detroit Lions, and there's been no confirmation that he'll be ready to roll this week and return to where he played last season in Philadelphia.
This isn't just a Week 6 concern either. Hamstring injuries are notoriously prone to lingering and can be easily aggravated or just last longer than expected.
With that said, Carolina should be looking at the trade market , and one veteran could welcome a change of scenery this season.
CBS Sports' Carter Bahns released his list of NFL trade-deadline candidates on Monday. With the deadline is just less than a month away, veterans across the league could head to new teams where they can contribute to winning and fill a need.
Los Angeles Chargers EDGE Khalil Mack certainly isn't in the right situation to contribute to winning, and that's not his fault. The Chargers are horrendous at almost everything, so no one would blame Mack for wanting to leave Los Angeles and join a team that isn't 0-5.
Unless the Chargers pull off a miracle turnaround and make the playoffs after a 0-5 start, something no team has ever done, they should invest in the 2027 NFL Draft.
That starts with trading away veterans to contenders or teams looking to make a playoff push. The Panthers fall into that category.
Still a talented player, but Mack is 35 years old and is on an expiring contract. GM Dan Morgan and the Panthers wouldn't have to cripple their upcoming draft to land Mack.
A reasonable trade package for Mack would just be a fourth- or sixth-round pick. Carolina doesn't have a fifth-round pick in the 2027 NFL Draft, but it does have two fourth-rounders and a sixth.

title: Panthers' Offseason Signing Ranked As 10th Best in NFL, But That's Too Low
full_text:
Entering Week 6 of the NFL season, the Carolina Panthers are 2-2 and can widen their lead in the NFC South, particularly over the Saints and Buccaneers.
Carolina's growth has primarily been on offense , with QB Bryce Young and that side of the ball stepping up since OC Brad Idzik took over play-calling duties.
That said, the Panthers' offseason was defined by defense. Sure, the offensive line was revamped from last year, but the marquee signings were all on defense.
One of Carolina's big additions has been phenomenal over four weeks of action and is shaping up to be one of the best signings of the NFL offseason.
CBS Sports' Garrett Podell dropped his top-10 free-agent acquisitions through Week 5. There are obviously huge names on the list, such as Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III and 49ers WR Mike Evans. However, the Panthers also have a worthy inclusion: ILB Devin Lloyd landed at No. 10.
Lloyd agreed to a deal with the Panthers on March 9th. Carolina's green-dot linebacker signed a three-year deal worth up to $45 million, with $25 million guaranteed.
Slotting at No. 10, Lloyd feels too low on this list. This isn't a situation where the Panthers signed a player who hadn't broken out yet. Lloyd was already a second-team All-Pro in 2025 and made the Pro Bowl for the first time.
Even with an All-Pro season, the Panthers managed to sign Lloyd for less than $15 million annually, which shouldn't be possible. Before free agency, Lloyd's projected value was roughly $60 million over three years.
Now, after signing with Carolina, Lloyd has continued his elite play, forcing turnovers and stopping the run. The production, combined with the contract value, means Lloyd should be higher on this list.
Other great players are on this list, but Lloyd could at least move up over No. 9 Nakobe Dean, who has played well but doesn't have the same takeaways as Lloyd does.
Aside from a Week 1 performance in which no one on the defense was ready for the Bears' offense, led by QB Caleb Williams and HC Ben Johnson, Lloyd has been nothing short of outstanding.
In the other two games, Lloyd was either the best player or among the three best players on the field. This was especially evident in Week 2. Posting 9 tackles, 2 TFLs, 2 interceptions, 1 sack, and 1 touchdown, Lloyd put together an all-time performance on the road against the Atlanta Falcons.
No one else on this list has had a performance as good as Lloyd's Week 2 this season, or, for some players on the list, in their careers.

title: Panthers Suddenly Have 3 Open Roster Spots. What is Dan Morgan Planning?
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers came out of the bye week hoping to get a little healthier. Instead, Dan Morgan has some roster decisions to make.
Carolina placed defensive tackle Cam Jackson on injured reserve Tuesday with a shoulder injury, leaving the Panthers with just 50 players on the active roster. That gives them three open spots, and it just so happens that three players are working their way back.
Trevor Etienne, Taylor Moton, and Tershawn Wharton were all designated to return to practice Tuesday. So, yeah, the easy answer is right there. Those three guys come back, and those three spots are gone. But I don't think Morgan has to play it that way.
Etienne looks like the first guy who will be back. Dave Canales said Monday that the rookie running back was ready to be activated, so it wouldn't be surprising at all if one of those spots belongs to him.
Moton and Wharton are different situations. Neither participated in training camp, with Moton dealing with blood clots discovered during the offseason and Wharton coming back from neck surgery. Getting them back on the practice field is one thing, but being ready to play in an NFL game is another.
The Panthers have three weeks to make that call after opening their practice windows. That gives Carolina some time to see where both guys are instead of immediately throwing them onto the active roster. It also means Morgan doesn't have to be in a hurry to fill every open spot.
I'm not saying Morgan is about to go out and make some huge move. Three open roster spots don't automatically mean a trade is coming, but we've seen enough from Morgan to know he's going to keep messing with this roster if he thinks he can make it better.
The Panthers made several moves during the bye week, and with injuries starting to pile up, there are still a few areas where another body wouldn't hurt. Xavier Legette, Jaycee Horn, and Mike Jackson have all been dealing with injuries, and now Cam Jackson is headed to IR.
Depending on how some of those situations play out, Morgan could decide one of these spots is better used somewhere else, at least for now. He doesn't have to make all three decisions right away. Carolina can activate Etienne, see how Moton and Wharton look, and still have some room to work with.
That's what makes this worth watching.
Maybe it ends up being that simple. Etienne, Moton and Wharton come back, and there are your three spots. But with the way Morgan has worked this roster, I'm not ready to assume that's how it plays out just yet.

title: The Panthers' Most Indispensable Player Isn't Who You Think
full_text:
Ask me who the Panthers' most indispensable player is, and Bryce Young is probably the answer I'm supposed to give. He's playing the best football of his career, this offense finally looks like it knows what it wants to be, and we've already seen what happens when Carolina doesn't have the quarterback position figured out.
And believe me, I don't want to see what this team looks like without Young right now.
Tetairoa McMillan would be right there for me, too. He already has 385 receiving yards through four games and just put up 14 catches, 192 yards, and two touchdowns against Detroit. I've gotten to the point pretty quickly where when Young throws one up to McMillan, I'm almost expecting him to come down with it.
Then there's Chuba Hubbard, who I think sometimes gets lost in these conversations because he isn't the shiny new toy. But watch what happens to this offense when Hubbard gets rolling. Young doesn't have to do everything, defenses can't just come after him, and Carolina can actually control a game a little bit.
So I get it if you pick any of those three. If somebody tells me Young is the answer, I'm not going to spend 20 minutes telling them they're wrong.
Before you tell me I've lost my mind, I'm not saying Lloyd is better than Young. I'm definitely not saying I'd rather build a football team around a linebacker than a quarterback. I'm looking at this Panthers team right now and asking myself which player I'd be most nervous about losing.
For me, it's Lloyd, and I think that probably says as much about this defense as it does about him.
I still don't know what to make of this defense. Carolina is giving up 387.2 yards per game, the pass rush hasn't consistently gotten home, and Jared Goff just threw for 412 yards against them. There have been drives where I've sat there wondering if they're ever going to get off the field.
Somehow, they keep finding a way.
The Panthers have eight takeaways through four games and five fourth-down stops. They held Atlanta to three points, Cleveland scored 21, and Detroit piled up 452 yards before Carolina finally made the stop it needed at the end. I'm not going to sit here and tell you it's always pretty because it definitely isn't.
That's where Lloyd comes into this for me. In the three games he's played, he has 31 tackles, two interceptions, and a sack. Against Atlanta, he had nine tackles, two interceptions, a sack, and took one of those interceptions back for a touchdown.
That wasn't just a good game. Dave Canales said afterward that he didn't know if he'd seen a better performance from a linebacker in 17 years of coaching in the NFL.
And yeah, I know Carolina already played without Lloyd once. He missed the Cleveland game with a calf injury, and the defense didn't completely fall apart. The Browns scored 21 points, and Bobby Okereke and Tyrel Dodson gave Carolina two experienced linebackers to lean on.
But I also watched Lloyd come back against Detroit, play every defensive snap, and finish with nine tackles. He even chased down Detroit's fourth-down hook-and-lateral to kill a scoring chance. That's the kind of stuff I'm talking about.
He's become one of those players I find myself watching when Carolina needs something. Maybe it's a third down, maybe the other team is driving, or maybe the defense just needs somebody to make a play before things start getting away from them. More and more, I expect Lloyd to be somewhere around it.
Maybe that's why I look at “best player” and “most indispensable player” a little differently. If you ask me who Carolina's best player has been through four games, I might say Young. McMillan would be right there, and I wouldn't argue much if somebody picked him.
But this isn't about who I'd take first in a draft. It's about the player I'd be most nervous about losing right now.
I didn't expect my answer to be a linebacker.
Devin Lloyd is just that good.

title: Early Week 6 NFL Odds for Huge Panther-Eagles Matchup Revealed

A Xavier Legette drop stood between Carolina and a shocking upset. Now, the two teams are in very different states. The Panthers are well-rested after their bye. Meanwhile, the Eagles will be traveling back from London amid heartbreak after a stunning last-second collapse.
The two teams seem to be in very different situations than one another , and this week marks one of the biggest rest advantages any NFL team will have over its opponent. Will the Panthers win? The odds don't think so.
The Carolina Panthers open as road underdogs to the Philadelphia Eagles. They are -102 on the moneyline on DraftKings , with the Eagles sitting at -118, so it's not as if there's a huge gap between these two teams.
The spread is a minuscule 1.5 points. The Panthers are -115 to cover, while the Eagles are -105 to do the same. Vegas expects a very tight game between these two playoff hopefuls.
The over/under is set at 42.5 points. The over is -105, and the under is -115. Based on all this information, the final score is expected to be somewhere in the ballpark of 22-20 for the Eagles. Regardless, it is expected to be close.
This is somewhat surprising. It is always difficult to be road favorites against any NFL team, but the Panthers are coming off a huge upset victory and are as well-rested as you can be.
They're likely to get Jalen Coker, Monroe Freeling, and Jaelan Phillips back. They're still without Jonathon Brooks, Xavier Legette, Jaycee Horn, and Mike Jackson, but they're going to be healthier than when they beat a better team, the Detroit Lions.
The Eagles are also traveling a long way after losing a game in which they scored a go-ahead field goal with eight seconds left. It's as defeated as a team can possibly be, but the odds don't believe it will make that much of a difference.
Plus, the Eagles' offense isn't built to take advantage of Carolina's weaknesses like Detroit's was, and even then, the Panthers got numerous key stops. Home-field advantage appears to be doing a lot for the Eagles in this week's odds.

title: Will Jalen Coker Be Back in Week 6? Injury Update, Return Timeline for Panthers WR
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are emerging from their bye in Week 6 and the hope is that wide receiver Jalen Coker will make his return to action.
Coker suffered an injury in the second half of the Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns that forced his early exit from the contest and led to Coker missing the Week 4 game entirely.
With an extra week of rest, there is optimism that Coker will be able to suit up in Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Here's what we know about Coker's injury and return timeline.
Coker is currently dealing with a quadriceps injury, which isn't his first rodeo with the injury during his career.
The day after suffering the issue, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport said the injury was a "minor quad strain" and the expectation was he wouldn't miss much, if any, time.
Well, Coker did end up missing time despite logging a few limited practices in Week 4, but that was also a sign he wasn't far off from returning.
Head coach Dave Canales offered a positive update on Coker on Monday, as he told reporters that Coker is "on track" to play this week.
However, Canales also cautioned that the Panthers had to evaluate Coker throughout this week of practice before determining whether or not he will play.
"Dave Canales: WR Jalen Coker (quad) is 'on track' but has a couple of big days of practice ahead of him this week heading into Sunday's game at PHI," The Athletic's Joe Person reported.
All signs are pointing to Coker returning this week, but we will still be glued to the Panthers' injury report, with the first installment coming on Wednesday.
A limited practice would keep Coker on the right track, but a full practice would almost guarantee he'll be ready to go for Sunday.
Assuming he plays, Coker is definitely a starting option.
While the Eagles' secondary has a lot of talent on paper, that has not produced desired results against opposing passing attacks this season.
According to CBS Sports , the Eagles are tied for the fourth-most fantasy points per game allowed to wide receivers.
As far as Coker himself is concerned, he ranks as WR11 overall in terms of fantasy points per game, according to Fantasy Pros , which makes him a borderline WR2 play.
Until further notice, Coker is a starting option in all formats, regardless of matchup.

title: 3 Crucial Panthers Injuries to Monitor Ahead of Big Eagles Matchup
full_text:
The bye week has come and gone for the Carolina Panthers . Now it's time to build on the Sunday Night Football win and keep the first-place spot in the NFC South.
Carolina doesn't have it easy this week, though, as the Panthers head to Philadelphia , to face the 2-3 Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field.
The Eagles are coming off a disastrous loss in London, with the Jaguars winning on a game-winning field goal. Both teams already have plenty of reason to play with desperation, and the Eagles will undoubtedly bring that intensity against Carolina.
With that said, Carolina will need all the reinforcements it can get. The Panthers have been one of the NFL's most injury-prone teams in the NFL this season. Entering Week 6, here are 3 key injuries to monitor
Taylor Moton is one of many prominent Panthers to be ruled out during training camp. Dealing with a blood clot in his lung, Moton hasn't played a down of football this season, but is set to be the starting right tackle once healthy.
Moton's return is now in sight , as he's been taken off the PUP list and activated to the 21-day practice window. This doesn't mean he can return this week, but it means that the return is coming sooner than later.
Panthers' head coach Dave Canales spoke on Moton's return, saying that while he's cleared medically, he hasn't seen football this year.
Moton's timeline will be based on his appearance on the practice field and how quickly he can ramp up. That said, Moton hasn't been ruled out for this week yet, even if theres an outside chance.
During the Panthers' primetime win against the Detroit Lions, Freeling suffered a knee injury that ruled him out for the remainder of the game. Obviously, when a knee injury happens, it's easy to think the worst, but thats not the case here.
Speaking with reporters during the bye week, Canales said that he's "hopeful" Freeling can suit up in Philadelphia.
Canales added to that this week, "I mean it's timely certainly, and Monroe's doing everything he can to make himself available for this week."
Freeling's presence could be a huge factor, especially since theres no guarantee Taylor Moton will return this week.
If both are out, then sixth-year tackle Stone Forsythe will get the start, which is a tall task against a very talented Eagles defensive line.
Similar to Freeling, Phillips injury occurred during the SNF win, as Carolina's premier pass rusher left the game after hurting his hamstring.
Canales gave an update on Phillips on Monday, saying that he "has a chance" to play against the Eagles. Phillips could be an X-factor in this game, as Jalen Hurts is still one of the more mobile QBs in the NFL.
Phillips would also be making his return to Philadelphia, where he played roughly half of last season before leaving to join the Panthers in free agency.

title: Chicago Bears Roster Analysis: 3 Players Ben Johnson Can't Trust
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are 3-2 after an embarrassing and injury-filled 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
The good news is that Caleb Williams was a full participant in the team's walkthrough and could be on his way back from a hamstring injury.
Chicago's starting quarterback was injured in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings and returns at the best time possible.
The bad news is that Bears coach Ben Johnson learned during this stretch that there are three players who can't be trusted in the offense right now.
On Sunday, Tyson Bagent proved why this team is in trouble at quarterback without a healthy Williams.
Case Keenum did too, to a lesser degree, but everyone understood the 38-year-old was an emergency option.
Bagent tanked his trade value during the two-pick, 87-yard, 12-of-21 dud in Green Bay. Worst of all, he may have given Johnson pause about handing him the offense again if Williams has any re-injury concerns.
It's unclear what Chicago's future is at the position behind Williams.
It's hard to imagine it being Bagent after Week 5.
It's very difficult to justify giving Roschon Johnson any of the backup snaps behind D'Andre Swift until Kyle Monangai returns from a turf toe.
Monangai isn't on track to return this coming weekend against the Atlanta Falcons after not practicing this week.
Johnson had six rushing yards on five carries against the Packers, with his longest rush of the day being three yards. While he did haul in five catches for 34 yards, that's not sustainable.
Johnson benefitted from having Bagent play it safe when he wasn't airing the ball down the field to minimal success.
Besides his rookie season, Johnson hasn't seen much success on the Bears. We'll see if Zavier Scott or Salvon Ahmed get a chance off the practice squad against Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
Garrett Bradbury has had a rough go at it at the center spot for Chicago this season.
While he wasn't the worst offender against Green Bay, he didn't help establish the run with a solid interior push.
Against the Vikings in Week 2, he had four penalties in one half . Things have gotten better for Bradbury, but not by much.
Rookie Logan Jones may not be far off from getting the call to start in the middle, especially if the offense continues to sputter.
Bradbury's best chance of sticking is Williams being too tough to catch once he's back under center.

title: Bears Wednesday Injury Report: Bad News For Kyle Monangai, Caleb Williams Progresses
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have put out their first injury report of the week ahead of their Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons.
The Wednesday injury report was an estimation, as the Bears did not practice. The estimated injury report did give us some insight into the statuses of running back Kyle Monangai and quarterback Caleb Williams, though.
That insight is Williams appears to be on track to return, while Monangai is on the path to miss another game.
We'll go over the latest on Williams, Monangai and more as we take a look at the Wednesday injury report for Week 6.
LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring): Did not participate LB Keyshaun Elliott (quad): Did not participate RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe): Did not participate DL Dayo Odeyingbo (quad): Did not participate DB Tyrique Stevenson (hip): Limited participation DB Kyler Gordon: Full participation QB Caleb Williams: Full participation
The estimated full practice for Williams amounts to more progress for him and the momentum that has been building since last week for him to come back this week continues to grow.
“Yeah, it’s still fluid, but, you know, I feel good about the plan that we have in place at this point," head coach Ben Johnson said when asked if he plans for Williams to be back this week.
As for Monangai, he has now missed four practices in a row with his turf toe injury. Initial reports suggested he could miss multiple games, so he's on track to do just that. We'll see if he can get an upgrade in participation on Thursday.
Edwards, Odeyingbo and Stevenson all left Sunday's game early due to injury. Head coach Ben Johnson said Stevenson is day-to-day while Odeyingbo is "likely to miss some time," so the Bears should be without their top two edge rushers thanks to the suspension of Montez Sweat .
Another full practice for Kyler Gordon keeps him on the right track, but Johnson strongly hinted the Bears will take it all the way up to the full 21 days.
"Considering all options, our intent with Kyler from the get-go was to make it through these 21 days to make sure that he's physically where he needs to be to help this football team," Johnson said .
Knowing that, it's possible the Bears could keep Gordon out one more game, as his 21-day window doesn't expire until next week. However, the Bears could sure use him back this week given how poorly Chicago's secondary played last week.

title: Gervon Dexter Trade Looking Worse for Bears With Each Quality Game Former DT Plays
full_text:
It's reunion week for Bears defensive tackle Grady Jarrett in more ways than one.
He'll be going back to Atlanta, where he spent the first 10 years of his 12-year career. There will be plenty of former teammates to talk with, including one he played right alongside in Chicago for a season-plus. That, of course, is defensive tackle Gervon Dexter .
The Bears traded the fourth-year defensive tackle there just before the season and Dexter has made the most of being in a different defensive system with an outstanding start and a contract extension. So, for Dexter this becomes a "How do you like me now" week.
“I talked to Gervon when he signed his extension," Jarrett said. "I was super happy for him, happy for his family. Loved my time here with him and excited for him, another young player that’s just going to continue to get better. Got a fresh start in Atlanta, so I couldn’t be happier for him.
Gervon Dexter looks like a MONSTER in the ATL pic.twitter.com/B2lIDLGkqn
"I know the people down there are great people so I’m excited for him. But as far as talking every day we both are getting ready for an opponent this week so we ain’t breaking bread or talking every day. But like I said, I definitely love him as a man, as a former teammate and excited for his future, excited for him and he looks like he’s having fun doing his thing."
Dexter is currently graded the fourth-best defensive tackle in the league out of 133 Pro Football Focus graded. He is seventh as a pass rusher and his old problem of being unable to stop the run seems to have vanished as he is 15th in run defense. With the Bears, Dexter never rose above 25th in the league overall and 39th against the run.
Gervon Dexter has been amazing this year lol Ryan Poles is the worst GM ever
Bears coach Ben Johnson has much more on his mind than Dexter's new team and role, but he couldn't help noticing how he leads Atlanta's defense up front.
“He's a phenomenal football player," Johnson said. "We know that about him. It was one of those things; I think it was a win-win for both sides in terms of him getting a fresh start and going down to a really good style of defense that matches his skill set. He's playing hard. He's getting out of the stack. He's chasing the ball down. Which is really the M.O. of their entire defense."
Johnson didn't exactly go into how this was a win-win for the Bears. It looks like a win for the Falcons and one for Dexter. Perhaps that's how he meant it, although unlikely.
Gervon Dexter Sr. is a beast pic.twitter.com/G2AWuD7H6h
All Bears GM Ryan Poles got for Dexter was a fifth-round pick next spring and cornerback Clark Phillips III. Phillips hasn't played a single down of defense for the Bears and has been on the field for 14 special teams plays. He wasn't active for two of their five games.
Poles used a second-round pick for Dexter, who left with class when he put out a heartfelt message to Chicago fans.
It was a trade easy to second guess because the Bears' other defensive tackles besides Jarrett were Neville Gallimore, James Lynch, Kentavius Street, and rookie Josh van den Berg.
Gervon Dexter is thriving with the Atlanta Falcons after the Chicago Bears traded him before the season. Haize breaks down Dexter’s 81.9 PFF grade, improved run defense and strong pressure numbers before asking the uncomfortable question: Did Ryan Poles move him too early, or… pic.twitter.com/BegrIAyAyi
Van den Berg was the player the Bears slated to have a big role as a rookie and he has one tackle in five games, and 82 plays, 59 of the plays coming on defense.
Kentavius Street actually became the starter alongside Jarrett and has seven tackles, a tackle for loss and one-half more sacks than Dexter. Dexter has 13 tackles, two for loss, and half a sack.
The truth in this one is Dexter wasn't signing with the Bears anyway, because they couldn't afford to keep a player they had spent three years developing. He got four years and $78 million from Atlanta.
Meanwhile, the Bears have Montez Sweat in the middle of a four-year, $98 million deal and the first week in a two-week suspension for a performance enhancing drug violation. He has two sacks. They also are paying cornerback Jaylon Johnson, who is coming off one of the worst games in his career and is in the middle of a four-year, $76 million contract. Then there's Kyler Gordon, who might remain out again this week for the 20th regular-season game out of 23 since he signed a three-year $40 million extension. And now T.J. Edwards is likely to miss Sunday's game with a hamstring injury, his eighth missed game out 23. He signed a two-year $20 million deal this year. And they spent $40 million for safety Coby Bryant and won't get a down from him until December at the earliest.
Regardless of what anyone thinks of Dexter's playing ability, the Bears got virtually nothing back in exchange for unloading him after developing him. Maybe they could have afforded to keep him alongside Grady Jarrett if not those deals they gave players who are sitting around now or playing only sparngly.
It's easy to wonder where Dexter and their defense might be if they'd kept him and not invested so heavily in a handful of players who spent so much time being injured
Bears Week 😤 @GervonDexter pic.twitter.com/Ue4KevX4B6

title: Montez Sweat Suspension Only Makes Bears' Need for Khalil Mack Stronger
full_text:
The Bears' pass rush will take a major hit over the next two weeks with edge rusher Montez Sweat serving a suspension for violating the NFL's Performance-Enhancing Substance Abuse Policy.
Whatever Sweat was taking actually seemed like much more of a hindrance than an enhancement, as he stumbled out of the gates to begin the season. That's a story for another day, though. He's still easily their top pass-rusher when he's on his game (although you could argue that Austin Booker has quickly closed that gap).
The Bears officially activated Shemar Turner on Tuesday, and he'll play a role in the pass-rush. However, they've also been a rumored destination for future Hall of Fame edge rusher Khalil Mack. The hypothetical of bringing the former fan favorite back to the Windy City now makes more sense than ever.
Mack is still playing at an extremely high level. Despite everything else around him falling apart with the 0-5 Chargers, he's been a lone bright spot. The 36-year-old currently leads the team with 3 sacks and 5 TFLs.
However, with the sink rapidly sinking and Mack playing out a one-year deal, many have questioned whether they should trade him rather than lose him in free agency. They would also be doing him a solid by trading him to a contender. The Bears would make a lot of sense in that regard.
Meanwhile, the Bears' pass rush has performed better than expected to begin the season (before Sunday's game against Green Bay, anyway). However, on top of Sweat's suspension, they're also dealing with an injury to Dayo Odeyingbo . Ben Johnson confirmed that he'd miss a few weeks when speaking to reporters earlier today.
Mack probably wouldn't play against Atlanta if they were to pull off a move in the coming days, but he also wouldn't need a ton of time to get caught up to speed. He could potentially make a dent in the snap count for the team's Week 7 matchup against New England next Thursday.
The money the Bears had tied up in the defensive line was virtually the only potential reason for pushback on the Mack conversation. However, Sweat's suspension voided all future guarantees on his contract. Chicago would save $21 million by cutting ties with him next offseason.
If Sweat were playing near the top of his game, they wouldn't have an issue paying that contract. He wouldn't be a cut candidate if he were living up to the contract. Unfortunately, Sweat's 2 sacks rank third on the team, and he's coming off a game in which he failed to make a dent in the box score against Green Bay's makeshift offensive line.
Sweat will have (at least) ten opportunities to prove his worth once he returns to the lineup. He's behind the 8-ball, though.
Meanwhile, Mack is playing out a one-year, $18 million deal. He'll conceivably command the same, if not a bit less, next offseason. If he can bring more impact than Sweat at a lesser price, that would be an easy decision for Chicago. Especially if it'd only take a fifth-round pick to get him in the building.
The idea of the Bears trading for Mack was a homerun last week. It's suddenly become a grand slam.

title: Bears Hallmark Movie Question Gets Predictable Ben Johnson Answer
full_text:
With so many critical issues facing Ben Johnson this week, it's apparent some people don't really understand what's important to the Bears and their coach.
An embarrassing loss to their biggest rival, whether Caleb Williams will return; who would replace him if not; is Kyler Gordon coming back; and what about Montez Sweat's performance enhancing charge and suspension ... all are weighing heavily on the coach's mind.
Yet, what is Johnson asked about Wedesday? Of course, what about the Bears Hallmark Network Christmas movie, Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story.
A special airing of the movie in advance was held on Tuesday and Johnson was asked Wednesday at Halas Hall if he got to attend.
Caleb Williams and his mom on the red carpet for the new Hallmark movie, Holiday Touchdown: A Bears Love Story It premiers October 17th. 🐻⬇️ pic.twitter.com/7NJJWIiMBY
"Not a chance," he deadpanned, showing at least his priorities are in place.
Johnson wouldn't even give inquiring minds much of an idea what to expect in the movie.
"I have no idea. I have no idea," he said. "It sounded like a couple of our guys made it out there."
Boys cleaned up nice for the Hallmark holiday movie premiere 📸: @mdwojak94 pic.twitter.com/C6uVnVNid2
Quarterback Caleb Williams and tight end Colston Loveland did go to the premier. Team CEO Kevin Warren wasn't at the stadium talks with Roger Goodell and Illinois politicians, but he did make it to the screening of the Hallmark movie.
Another vital member of the Bears organization was there, too. Staley Da Bear attended the red carpet premiere at the Gorton Center in Lake Forest. They sent the top people, er, mascots.
It's probably a safe bet on Kalshi that this movie won't be quite as popular or impactful as "Brian's Song."
Johnson didn't act like a complete Scrooge. He did placate everyone by talking about what he saw when he was participating in the filming, because he is in the movie. There was nothing said about if he has a shirtless scene.
"Yeah, I tell you, the best part for me was just seeing another profession in their element," he said. "I have a ton of respect for the lead actors and actresses and how they interacted, and then the director taking control. I thought it was pretty cool to see behind the scenes just how that all took place."
The Bears Hallmark movie comes out this week so Colston Loveland will finally be featured.
The movie stars Lyndsy Fonseca as Avery and Robert Buckley as Matt, whoever that is.
"Honestly, there’s some similarities to what we do here in a lot of ways, just being able to choreograph a bunch of individuals on the same page," Johnson said, so as not to alienate anyone. "There’s urgency. And yet you still want to see it all come together in the end. So, it was fun to watch."
Besides Johnson, the other Bears who appear in the movie are Cole Kmet and Colston Loveland.
If you watch one Hallmark Christmas Movie . . . you've watched them all . . . just sayin' . . . pic.twitter.com/EcQb8ihImD
Former Bears Dan Hampton, Charles "Peanut" Tillman and Mike Singletary are also in it.
The real question that went unanswered was whether Johnson would be spending Saturday night in Atlanta the night before the game watching the movie.
We probably all know the answer to that.
Good. Would’ve been a bad look to go watch a shitty Hallmark movie after the ass kicking you got on Sunday https://t.co/Uhb4SBjyGY

title: Bears Viewed as Possible Suitor for Projected Dolphins, Commanders Trade Candidates
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have had two key positions in the crosshairs as spots they could add to via trade since the offseason and nothing has really changed.
Those two positions are the interior of the defensive line and at edge rusher. Things have calmed down in the latter area since it was a massive concern during the offseason, but with an injury to Dayo Odeyingbo and a suspension for Montez Sweat , adding at edge rusher has come back to the forefront.
For our purposes here, though, we're focused on the interior of the defensive line, which hasn't been good enough.
In run defense, the Bears rank ninth, which is good, but they are also giving up 4.4 yards per carry, which ranks tied for 21st.
In the pass-rush, the Bears haven't gotten much sack production from the group, which is why they miss Gervon Dexter. Through five games, Kentavius Street remains the only interior defender with a sack.
CBS Sports' Carter Bahns recently identified some buyers and sellers ahead of the trade deadline and he pegged the Bears as one of the teams he expects to be buyers.
And, in the process, Bahns identified Miami Dolphins defensive lineman Zach Sieler and Washington Commanders defensive lineman Daron Payne as possible options for Chicago.
"In order to maximize the team's upside upon Williams' return, general manager Ryan Poles needs to bolster the defense, especially up front. The Bears rank just 20th in quarterback pressure rate and lack depth on both the edge and interior," explained Bahns.
"The edge rusher spot should be a higher priority than defensive tackle since the Bears were mostly quiet at that position in the offseason and just saw Marcus Davenport abruptly retire after Week 4," Bahns added.
Both Sieler and Payne are realistic trade candidates.
Payne is in the final year of his contract and the Commanders are sitting at 1-3-1 and will likely be sellers at the deadline, and Miami isn't going anywhere, either, at 0-5 and it would make sense to unload a 31-year-old player in the midst of a rebuild.
Sieler offers versatility with his ability to play inside and out, so he could help Chicago at multiple spots, and he brings juice in the pass-rush.
The 31-year-old has twice tallied 10 sacks in a season (2023 and 2024). He had 5.5 in 17 games last season and has two through five games in 2026, which would lead the Bears' interior defenders.
Sieler's run defense has been lacking this season, as evidenced by his Pro Football Focus run defense grade of 31.6, but Sieler has always been been a plus run defender with grades of 63.2 or better in each of the previous seven seasons.
Payne has been a fairly effective pass-rusher during his career. He had a career-high 11.5 sacks in 2022, and while he hasn't come close to that total since, he does have 11 sacks combined the previous three campaigns. He has one so far this season.
The veteran's run defending skills have been an issue the last handful of seasons, but he is showing improvement in that area this season with a PFF grade of 67.6, his highest since 2020.
While Payne may only be a rental given his contract situation that makes him a free agent after this season, Sieler is under contract through 2029, but the Bears wouldn't be tied to him, either, as Sieler doesn't have any guaranteed money left after 2026.
Given his superior past production in the sacks department and versatility, we would prefer Sieler over Payne, but Chicago would be in better shape than it is now by acquiring either player.

title: Caleb Williams Injury Status Confirms Bears QB is on Path for Week 6 Return
full_text:
The long wait for Chicago Bears fans to see their starting quarterback again should be over this week. While speaking to the media, Bears head coach Ben Johnson confirmed that Caleb Williams would be a full participant on the Wednesday injury report, according to NFL insider Ian Rapoport . Because the Bears are only planning a walkthrough instead of a full practice, the injury report will only be an estimation, but this is a significant development, nonetheless.
Williams was listed as a limited participant in the Bears' final Week 5 injury report last Friday, though he remained inactive for Sunday's game. Barring any unforeseen setbacks, he should continue to be a full participant throughout the week, which would all but confirm that he will be back in the starting lineup in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.
If there was one silver lining from the Bears' disastrous Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers , it's that there should never again be any discussion whether Ben Johnson's offense works better without Williams. Tyson Bagent, who was making his second consecutive start, was utterly lost and turned the ball over twice before he was benched for Case Keenum , but Keenum fared no better and also turned it over twice.
The Bears converted just four of 14 third-down attempts against the Packers and averaged a meager 3.6 yards per play. Opportunities to gash Green Bay's defense for big gains regularly presented themselves, but neither Bagent nor Keenum had the arm strength, the athleticism, or the vision to make it happen. It's that magical playmaking ability that the Bears have missed most about Williams .
Honestly, Week 5 was a trip down memory lane for Bears fans to a not-so-distant past, when what we saw on Sunday was the best that could be expected from the Bears. But that's all in the past. Williams has proven to be a legitimate playmaker and a franchise quarterback. Even if he's not at 100% health, the Bears' offense should once again be one of the most dangerous in the league once No. 18 is back under center.
Amazingly, the Bears have gone 2-1 since Caleb Williams was first sidelined by a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Case Keenum led the way to an upset Week 3 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles before Tyson Bagent threw for nearly 300 yards en route to a dominant Week 4 win over the New York Jets. That 31-7 shellacking at the hands of the Packers stings, but the Bears are still 3-2 and firmly in the race for the division title.
If Williams does indeed start on Sunday, he'll have his work cut out for him. The Bears' defense got exposed last week and will now be severely shorthanded. Dayo Odeyingbo's injury update from Ben Johnson suggested that he'll miss some time, and Montez Sweat has been suspended for two games for violating NFL policy.
The Falcons offense, led by superstar running back Bijan Robinson, has been surging over the past month, and I don't expect Chicago to give them much trouble. If the Bears are to get back into the win column, they're going to need a dominant offensive performance. Luckily, Williams is itching to do exactly that.

title: Dayo Odeyingbo Injury Update From Ben Johnson Puts Bears in Precarious Spot at Edge Rusher
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were hit with a tough blow on Tuesday after it was revealed edge rusher Montez Sweat would miss the next two games because of a suspension .
And now, the Bears will be even more short-handed at edge rusher thanks to the injury to Dayo Odeyingbo .
According to Bears head coach Ben Johnson on Wednesday, the veteran defensive end is expected to miss time with his quad injury, which forced his early exit from the Week 5 game.
The good news is, he will avoid an injured reserve stint, which means the Bears do not expect him to miss more than three contests.
"Bears head coach Ben Johnson said Dayo Odeyingbo will likely miss time with a quad injury, but it shouldn't require a stint on IR," Kevin Fishbain of The Athletic relayed.
Odeyingbo entered the season as a major question mark after his disappointing first season in Chicago that included a torn Achilles. But he has been everything the Bears could have hoped for through five games.
Odeyingbo has posted three sacks in that span, the second-most on the team behind Austin Booker, and he leads the Bears with 14 pressures.
Now, with no Odeyingbo and Sweat for quite possibly the next two games, that's five sacks and 27 pressures wiped out from the Bears' defense.
With Odeyingbo and Sweat out, the Bears are going to need Austin Booker to anchor the pass-rush.
Booker has been hot the last two weeks with three sacks and four pressures in that span, and he leads the team with four overall, which is just 0.5 shy of his career-high.
Booker has expressed frustration with playing time . Well, now he's going to get a lot more.
Elsewhere on the roster, the Bears have Jamree Kromah, Daniel Hardy, James Lynch and Shemar Turner, who was activated off Chicago's PUP list after Sweat was suspended.
Those four players have a combined total of 3.5 sacks during their careers, and all of them have come from Lynch. Turner has just five career games under his belt and Kromah has never played a regular season snap.
It's too bad that veteran defensive end Marcus Davenport decided to retire recently because the Bears could really use him.
Chicago would be wise to explore its options in free agency because, as we saw last week, the secondary can't be trusted to hold off a passing attack if there isn't consistent pressure.

title: Bears' Best Free Agent Edge Rusher Options Amid Sweat Suspension, Odeyingbo Injury
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are teetering on the brink of being in a really bad spot at edge rusher.
The Bears were rocked with the suspension of Montez Sweat on Tuesday. The veteran edge rusher will miss the next two games because of a PED suspension.
Before that, the Bears were already dealing with an injury to Dayo Odeyingbo, who left the Week 5 debacle early with a quadriceps injury. Hopefully we'll know more about his injury on Wednesday, but until then there is a chance Dayo misses time.
It goes without saying that not having both of those guys for any period of time would be devastating, as they've combined for five sacks and 27 pressures this season and the Bears don't have any sure options on the roster outside of Austin Booker.
Even though a game or two isn't a lot of time, this is a stark reminder of how quickly things can go south. Knowing that, Chicago needs to explore its option in free agency.
Reddick was once one of the most consistently productive edge rushers in the NFL, with the 32-year-old posting double-digit sacks in four straight seasons from 2020 through 2023.
His career has hit the skids the past two seasons, though, with Reddick posting just 3.5 sacks in his last 23 games in that span.
Reddick posted 2.5 sacks in 13 games during a 2025 season in which he dealt with injury. The year before that, Reddick held out for a large chunk of the season before tallying just one sack.
Not great, obviously, but that's at least one reason why he's still available at this time. Perhaps better health will yield better production.
Another former top-notch edge rusher, Bosa's decorated career includes five Pro Bowls and four double-digit sack seasons. The down side has been his injury issues.
Bosa looked like he would be a steal for the Bills last season after he posted four sacks over the first eight weeks, but the wheels came off after that and he had one sack over his final nine contests, including playoffs.
There were rumblings that Bosa might retire during the offseason, so he may not even be available. But, if he is, the Bears should definitely kick the tires.
Floyd was a first-round pick of the Bears all the way back in 2016, but his tenure was a disappointment, to say the least.
Floyd figured things out after his stint in Chicago, though, with the veteran posting 8.5 sacks or more in each of the next five seasons after leaving the Bears, and that 8.5-sack campaign came as recently as 2024.
The former No. 9 overall pick had just 3.5 sacks for the Atlanta Falcons last season, but the Bears are in a spot that they would glady take that production given the current state of the edge rushers room.

title: Montez Sweat's Contract Ramifications and Bears' Updated Cap Space Ater Suspension
full_text:
Montez Sweat's suspension will hurt him in the wallet and make his future a bit more uncertain, but it will also give the Chicago Bears more cap space.
Sweat was suspended two games by the NFL without pay for violating the league's policy on performance-enhancing substances on Tuesday.
While this is obviously bad news for the Bears' defense, it is also bad news for Sweat's bank account and his remaining salary.
According to Spotrac , Sweat will forfeit $2.3 million of his 2026 salary, and the rest of his $12.7 million salary is unsecured because the suspension voids all future guarantees.
"Bears DE Montez Sweat will forfeit $2.3M of 2026 salary per his 2-game suspension for violating the league's PED policy," Spotrac said. "Additionally, the $12.7M remaining on Sweat's 2026 salary is now unsecured, as the PED suspension voided all future guarantees."
There is no impact on Sweat's contract for next year, though, as he did not have any guaranteed money on the final year of the contract to begin with.
With Sweat giving up that money because of his suspension, the Bears now have more cap space to work with.
According to Spotrac , the Bears are now sitting with $11.4 million in cap space, which is 15th-most in the NFL.
That amount gives Chicago the flexibility to do something big or small, and they may want to do the latter because their depth at edge is extremely shaky.
We would not expect anything big in the short term from the Bears and instead Chicago will likely wait until the NFL trade deadline, when the pool of available players is at its deepest.
In the short term, a move might be necessary, depending on the status of defensive end Dayo Odeyingo, who is dealing with a quadriceps injury .
We are still waiting on an update for Odeyingbo, and that update will come on Wednesday, when the Bears release their first injury report. Hopefully head coach Ben Johnson will have some specifics on Odeyingbo before that.
If there is no Sweat and Odeyingbo for the next game or two, the Bears will be in a precarious spot.
Austin Booker has been good this season with four sacks in five games, but the depth behind him is shaky, at best, with guys like Daniel Hardy, James Lynch, Jamree Kromah and Shemar Turner, who was activated off the PUP list on Tuesday .
Lynch is the only one who has notched sacks during his career and he has 3.5 in 74 games. Not exactly an inspiring group.
On the free-agent market, the Bears' options include players such as Haason Reddick, Joey Bosa, Leonard Floyd and Denico Autry. Nothing exciting there, but that's what you have to expect in the middle of the season
Again, the Bears' desire to make a move will probably be heavily reliant on Odeyingbo's status. If he's out multiple games, kicking the tires on one of those players becomes much more likely.

title: Bengals' Prized Offseason Acquisitions Already Paying Major Dividends
full_text:
Bye weeks can move rather slowly. However, there's plenty to discuss when it comes to the 2026 edition of the Cincinnati Bengals.
First off, the pass game is looking exactly like everyone had hoped. It's early, but Joe Burrow and Tee Higgins are one of the top quarterback/wide receiver duos in the league. Then, you have the major upgrades to the defensive line.
It's only been five weeks, but Dexter Lawrence has already proven that he is still one of the strongest anchors on a defensive line in the league. One stat from Pro Football Focus even backs that up.
PFF has revealed that the Bengals have the highest defensive stuff rate in the NFL, at 30%. Rounding out the top five is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Miami Dolphins, Seattle Seahawks, and the Green Bay Packers.
The Bengals are getting everything they wanted and more with the addition of Lawrence. PFF has Lawrence graded as the third best defensive tackle in the NFL. That overall grade includes the fourth best grade in pass rush at 82.4 and the 10th-best rush grade at 72.8.
Lawrence has given opposing offenses fits all season long, but it's not just him who is reaping the benefits of being a part of this defensive line.
The Bengals' strong interior defensive line is opening doors for the pass rusher. Boye Mafe, who was another offseason acquisition, is having a strong start to his 2026 campaign.
Mafe has recorded three sacks and one forced fumble in five games. Mafe currently ranks as the 12th-best edge rusher in the league, according to PFF .
With a lot of the talk regarding the defense being about the weakness at linebacker and some struggles in the secondary, so far this season, the defensive line has been elite.
The pass game is rolling, the defensive line is playing some of the best football in the NFL, and even the offensive line has elevated its game. The Bengals are so close to getting it all together.
Having an early bye week can be a rough draw for a lot of teams. However, this season, it may have just come at the right time for the Bengals. This team is potentially on the cusp of finding greatness. Now, they will have a full week to dissect the issues in the running game and some areas on the defensive side before they play in an all important matchup with the Baltimore Ravens.
When the Bengals do take the field against the Ravens in two weeks, you'd best believe their AFC North rivals already have some concerns about the defensive line they will be seeing.

title: Bengals' Offensive Duo Off to an Explosive Start in 2026
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals didn't get a good draw as it pertains to where the bye week landed on the schedule. A bye in Week 6 is brutal for any team.
With so much season left after the bye week, there's no doubt that health is going to play a major role down the stretch. The win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday was a nice way to enter a bye week, but it still felt like the players and coaches knew they left a lot on the table.
There's no time to sulk in the negative, any win is hard to come by in this league and should be celebrated. It's time to highlight the positives, and the Bengals have a dynamic offensive duo that has been one of the best connections in the young season.
On paper and on the field, the Bengals have one of the most dangerous offenses in the league. Quarterback Joe Burrow is basically playing with two number one options at wide receiver. While Ja'Marr Chase gets most of the attention, and rightfully so, Tee Higgins is having a monster 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , Burrow to Higgins has the fifth most receiving yards of a quarter/wide receiver duo in the league.
The only duos ahead of the Bengals stars is Matthew Stafford and Devante Adams, Jordan Love and Christian Watson, Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, and the dup everyone expected to be at number one, Tyler Shough and Chris Olave.
Higgins had a quiet outing against the Dolphins this past Sunday, but he had a good reason, given that he was dealing with an adductor injury. But before Week 5, Higgins was having the strongest season of any receiver on the team.
With Chase having a monster game in Miami that led to arguably the greatest touchdown reception of his career, it seems this offense is finding its rhythm right before they play a very vital game against the Baltimore Ravens in two weeks.
The offense has a lot of things going its way. Burrow's connection with Chase and Higgins is as strong as ever, and the offensive line is playing some of the best football they've played under head coach Zac Taylor.
If we're nitpicking, the run game is going to be the focus as the team goes through the bye week. For now, letting Burrow throw nearly 60 times a game doesn't sound so bad.

title: Amarius Mims Among Top Early Contenders For Major 2026 NFL Season Award
full_text:
The Bengals may soon sport the best right tackle in the NFL. ESPN's Bill Barnwell dropped his quarter-season awards article last week and has Amarius Mims third on his Protector of the Year rankings.
The young Georgia product has not allowed a full sack in 2026 and is slotted only behind 49ers offensive tackle Trent Williams and Broncos guard Quinn Meinerz in Barnwell's gauge.
"After taking a major step forward a year ago, the Bengals right tackle has leveled up again and emerged as arguably the best pass-protecting right tackle in the league," Barnwell wrote . "The Bengals have a quarterback in Joe Burrow who wants to get five eligibles out into pass routes, and when they do, help a tackle, it's usually Orlando Brown Jr. Mims has been one-on-one against pass rushers at the third-highest rate in the league this season, and he has excelled in a pass-happy offense, allowing just a half-sack and two quick pressures on 169 pass-rush snaps. He's also 12th in run block win rate, suggesting that the 2024 first-round pick is holding his own as a run blocker, too."
Mims somehow only has a 62.8 Pro Football Focus grade despite all those great marks. There's a huge gap between that RBWR listed by Barnwell and his career-low 45.5 PFF run-blocking grade, but all in all, he's been exactly what fans should expect in Year 3.
At this rate, Mims will reset the offensive tackle on a contract extension sometime next offseason. Cincinnati should try to do it as quickly as possible once the season ends to get ahead of other deals that will happen in the ensuing months.
Bengals coaches have been impressed with 6-8, 350-pound mauler this season.
"There's a lot of really talented people, but there's a fraction of the players in this league that truly can be special, and he is in that fraction," Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said after facing T.J. Watt and the Steelers. "T.J. Watt is one of the best to ever do that job. To be matched up one-on-one as often as he was without help yesterday (he got some, but not a lot), and to just be consistent and to take the right set.
"There's such confidence for him in knowing, 'If I just take this set on the angle that I need to take it on and my eyes are in the right place and I strike when I'm supposed to strike,' there's very little the guy across from him can do to counter that. He just has to stay on the path he's on."

title: 'Circle On The Schedule' - Elite NFL Cornerback Praises Ja'Marr Chase, Looks Forward to Each Matchup
full_text:
Since joining the Cincinnati Bengals in 2021, Ja’Marr Chase has cemented himself as one of the league’s most dominant wideouts.
This season already, Chase has notched 27 receptions for 289 yards and 4 touchdowns, for 10.7 yards per catch and 57.8 yards per game. Continuing his rising legacy, that has already seen the former LSU Tiger tally five Pro Bowl appearances in his first six seasons.
Earlier this month, when talking on the PFF NFL Show , Browns star Denzel Ward spoke on the difficulties of playing Chase.
When asked who the toughest receiver he faced, Ward responded, “I would say definitely in the division, I'd say Ja'Marr Chase.”
“…I feel I've definitely done well against him, but I just know the type of matchup and type of game it’s gonna be going against him and Burrow. I think their connection makes it even tougher to go against. But, he's one of the guys, I think, that I definitely circle on the schedule, like, ‘okay, this is gonna be one of the harder games I play,’ and it's gonna be a great matchup."
Ward then elaborated on what makes Chase a difficult player.
“He's able to make plays after the catch. So he's able to catch a ball and go all the way to the end zone. So it's like, you gotta tackle him right there once he catches it 'cause if not he's someone that could take it all away, and score on one play. Burrow's gonna give him chances, but he's just a physical route runner, and then it's really, I think, the hardest part is once he gets that ball in his hands.”
Last summer, when appearing on The Sitdown w/ Malik Wright , Chase was asked his toughest opponent, where he was quick to answer Ward.
“It’s easy. I mean, Denzel,” Chase said. “It’s twice a year. It’s one on one majority of the time. He got great feet. He knows leverage, he knows splits. He’s one of the best I like playing.”
In his career against the Browns, Chase has totaled 42 catches for 481 yards and 4 touchdowns, with his best game against the AFC North rival coming in early 2022, where he went for 119 yards through 10 receptions and 1 touchdown.

title: Latest 2026 NFL Draft Class Ranking Leaves a Lot to Be Desired for Bengals
full_text:
The start of the 2026 season has not gone the way the Cincinnati Bengals had hoped. After a 2-0 start, the Bengals dropped two straight games before their meeting with the Miami Dolphins in Week 5.
Week 5 became a must-win situation, and the Bengals did just that. It wasn't the prettiest performance, but the Bengals secured a winning record before their bye, taking down the Dolphins 31-24.
A bye week is usually a time for reflection. It's a shame the Bengals' bye comes so early in the season, but it's never the wrong time to take a closer look at how the team arrived at a 3-2 record. Speaking of reflection, NFL Draft On SI recently ranked the performance of each team's 2026 NFL Draft class. The rankings show the Bengals' 2026 class has a lot to prove.
Justin Melo of NFL Draft On SI has put the Bengals' 2026 draft class as the 20th best class after five weeks in the season. Melo gives the class a C+ while acknowledging the group as a whole hasn't had a lot of opportunities.
"Cashius Howell has been among the top-performing rookie pass rushers. No other members of this seven-prospect class are really playing meaningful snaps yet, but it remains early, and Howell looks like a real find," wrote Melo .
According to Pro Football Focus , Howell had one of his stronger games in his young rookie season. The rookie defensive end earned his highest run grade of the season at 67.8.
Howell looks to be on the trajectory of being an impact player for the Bengals. But will there be another player who takes the leap this season?
Coming into this game, there was a real chance the Bengals could have been without Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Both were active and made an impact on the game, which means rookie wide receiver Colbie Young may have to wait for his moment.
Young turned some heads during training camp, and it feels like sooner rather than later, fans will get to know his name well.
One of the biggest reasons the Bengals' rookie class hasn't made a bigger impact is that those ahead of them on the depth chart are simply the better talents at the moment. That's a good problem for any team to have.

title: Bengals' Offense Has Finally Found Strength in One Major Weakness
full_text:
The worst week of the NFL season is the bye week. That's where the Cincinnati Bengals find themselves in Week 6.
After a sloppy 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, the Bengals will have a week to recover and prepare for a major matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
Everyone can agree this team has a lot to work on if they want to avoid a 0-2 start in the AFC North. But there are a lot of positives to take away from the first five weeks of the season. One of the biggest positives has actually been the play of the offensive line.
Since Joe Burrow took his first steps on the field as a member of the Bengals, the team has struggled to protect their star quarterback.
Every season, the conversation turns to how the Bengals cannot protect Burrow, and every fan feels that is one of the biggest hurdles holding back this team. Well, that hasn't been the case in 2026.
According to Pro Football Focus , the Bengals have a pressure allowed rate of 20.6%, which is fourth best in the league. Only the Atlanta Falcons, Kansas City Chiefs, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers have posted a better percentage.
Protecting Burrow is the most important goal for this team every time they step on the field. The Bengals' offensive line has allowed just nine sacks this season. That ties them with the Indianapolis Colts for seventh-best in sacks allowed.
After Sunday's game in Miami, it's clear that the offense is clicking. The Bengals were dominant in the red zone, and Burrow connected with four different targets on touchdown passes in the win. If everyone stays healthy, this offense could reach heights that would even surprise the likes of Burrow and his explosive collection of offensive talent.
However, the defense is another story. For now, just celebrate the wins, and this offensive line is giving the fans something to be proud of. After years of discussion around protecting Burrow, the offensive line is in position to keep the franchise signal-caller upright.
Burrow has thrown for 1,361 yards, 11 touchdowns and three interceptions in five games. He has a 71.4% completion percentage, 104.4 QB rating and a 75.3 QBR. He also received a major compliment for his recent play from national NFL analyst Mark Schlereth.

title: Joe Burrow Gets 'Brady-esque' Praise After Bengals' Week 5 Win
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals entered their early bye week on a high note with a 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday.
Sure, there's plenty to pick at from the Bengals' performance, but earning a win in the NFL should never be overlooked. With all the talk about what needs to be fixed before the team takes the field in two weeks, there's one area that's doing just fine.
That area is the offense, and the guy who leads that unit. Quarterback Joe Burrow was in elite form on Sunday. Fox analyst Mark Schlereth, who called the game, sees a lot of one legendary quarterback in Burrow's game.
During a conversation about Burrow on The OG Football Show, Schlereth had nothing but praise for the Bengals superstar.
"I spent about three hours watching Joe Burrow type and I walked out and thought to myself, I can see why they never run it," Schlereth said. "He's so Brady-esque in that he's the best scrambler in football that never leaves the pocket. He never escapes out of the back of the pocket. He's always working toward the line of scrimmage, even if it means he's going to take one in the teeth."
Any time a player is compared to Tom Brady, ears are going to perk up. Brady is arguably the greatest ever to play the game. When someone who has the accolades at the highest level, like Schlereth, says Burrow has the attributes of Brady, it's coming from a strong source.
A lot of the talking coming into the game against the Dolphins was about the Bengals relying too much on their pass game. After throwing 54 passes in Week 4, Burrow had 32 pass attempts in Week 5. The workload was reduced, but the success rate was still high as Burrow completed 23 of those 32 passes and tossed for touchdowns with a QBR of 126.3.
Having a strong run game to back up Burrow is obviously vital. However, this team goes as far as nine can lead them. Seems like a good idea to give him as many opportunities to make a play as the coaching staff can.

title: Bengals Star Ja'Marr Chase Gets 'People's Elbow' Fines Wiped Out on NFL Appeal
full_text:
Ja'Marr Chase got a win in his celebration battle with the NFL. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport posted on X Wednesday afternoon that Chase won his appeals for fines the NFL handed down to him and Tee Higgins for their "people's elbow" celebrations during the Week 2 win against the Texans.
There is no word on whether Higgins had all of his fines rescinded. Each fine was $14,926. The NFL fined Higgins four times and Chase twice from that one game. The two players were fined $89,556 for the arm signage.
"Bengals WR Ja’Marr Chase won appeals of fines for his 'people’s elbow' celebration, as two fines of $14,926 were rescinded from the #Texans game," Rapoport posted on X. "From the appeals office letter, 'On appeal, Mr. Chase … further contended that even if he committed the violation, his fine should be reduced because he received no warning that this was not allowed. He added that this is a new celebration with his teammate and that it is not offensive. Mr. Chase finally stated that the NFL is assuming the worst of him and his teammate without discussing with the NFLPA.'"
A bunch of these fines from an oddly-heavy Week 2 got rescinded this week, and Chase is the latest to get his money back.
He revealed the fines to the media when they came down and implored the NFLPA to help its stars.
"I don't know. I'm trying to figure out because that's not what it is," Chase told the media about getting the league's perspective on what they think the gesture is. "This is literally like a wrestling move. You know what I'm saying? So I don't know. Maybe I should stop. I don't know. Maybe I could do it like this (he did a tweaked version of the move at the podium). Keep doing it. I don't know, man. I don't know. It was something different for us, something we try to be unique with. Just stopping the fun. So it is what it is."
The league clearly changed its tune on what the "people's elbows" meant, and Chase at least got his bread back.
