title: 'That's Just The Media' - Jordan Battle Backs Up Comments Against Miami With One of Best Bengals Outings
full_text:
Jordan Battle talked the talk and walked the walk on Sunday.
The Bengals safety became the first player with multiple interceptions in the same game for Cincinnati since Logan Wilson in 2023. He revealed the ball-patting tell for Miami passer Malik Willis, and that bold callout paid off.
Now, Battle addressed the performance after the game and did admit he couldn't see Willis's eyes on either of the interceptions, but he had the script all the same.
Battle finished with seven tackles, two picks and a 79.2 Pro Football Focus grade (third-best on Bengals defense).
"That's just the media. You know, everybody's looking for the next story, and obviously it went big, went viral, and that's just part of football," Battle said about the patting comments.
Battle got the first pick off a deflection and the second one off a great read in the open field. It was a strong performance on the ball, but he can still clean up the tackling more.
The safety was the only Bengal to miss multiple tackles on PFF's grading following the game. He missed two of the Bengals' six missed tackles.
"Yeah, pretty much like I feel like everybody's saying it, just finish," Battle said about what the team needs to do next. "Games like that got to be able to close them out. I feel like even better than we did. Give up the late touchdown and the offense obviously getting the ball back as well. So it's got to be better. But closing out, doing a better team effort late in games."
Something the whole team feels . There is no clear top team in the NFL right now, and the Bengals can be that, but they can't keep committing untimely mistakes as they have in the first third of the season.
"We got to be smarter. We got to be smarter. Two fumbles in the red zone. A couple of personal fouls that hurt us, hurt our field position, and gave them points on the board. We got to be smarter," Joe Burrow said after the win.
Cincinnati has a few days off before getting back together and working on the Ravens matchup in Week 7.

title: Bengals Pass Catcher Expected to Miss Rest of 2026 NFL Season With Major Injury
full_text:
The Bengals lost a key depth piece for the season on Tuesday. WLWT's Charlie Clifford posted on X that backup Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral muscle in Sunday's 31-24 win over Miami and is done for the rest of the 2026 campaign.
Hudson had just been signed to the active roster for the rest of the season, but his time gets cut short in 2026. He finishes the season with seven catches for 33 yards and a score against the Dolphins.
" Bengals tight end Tanner Hudson suffered a torn pectoral and is expected to miss the remainder of the season, his agent tells WLWT," Clifford posted . "Brutal news for a reliable pass-catching option in Cincinnati."
Zac Taylor noted the injury in Monday's press conference but didn't indicate it would be this serious. Cincinnati also saw depth linebacker Swayze Bozeman break his forearm and go on in-season injured reserve.
The team signed former Notre Dame linebacker Jack Kiser to replace him and could add another piece to replace Hudson on the roster or practice squad ranks during these bye week days.
Cincinnati is trying to put together a winning streak after the days off and take advantage of the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL by most metrics.
They have to clean up the self-inflicted wounds to fully maximize it.
"Trust me, I'm not going to sit here - we got to win games in this league, and we've all sat in this room and seen some get away from us," Taylor said on Sunday. "We won the game, and I'm excited about that. Then, our defense created a turnover there at the very end that gave us three extra points that made it a 7-point game that made it feel a little bit different. We did some good things. There are some positive things we did, but there are also some things that we don't turn the ball over in the red zone like that: the kickoff, the PAT, the field goal. Those are things that we're better than that, and we got to clean that up."
Cincinnati takes on the Ravens next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

title: Browns Should Consider Flipping Jerry Jeudy For This Overshadowed Wideout
full_text:
The current situation of the Cleveland Browns ' wide receiver room is headlined by the excellent play of both rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, who have combined for 34 catches for 449 yards and three touchdowns through the first five games of the season. Cleveland’s next leading receiver is second-year guy Isaiah Bond with 86 receiving yards. Bond struggled with a couple of drops vs. New York, but has gotten just nine targets this season.
Past those three, the rest of the room seems to be up in the air, and the one guy who is the odd man out is popping up in more and more trade rumors. That would, of course, be Jerry Jeudy, who is currently sixth for Cleveland in receiving yards and receptions.
Jeudy’s cap hit of $10.3 million this season, as well as $13.4 million in 2027, does not seem worth the price at the moment or in the future. Cleveland will be looking to trade him ; that’s no secret, but could it be for another receiver who has also seemingly lost his place in the room?
That would be the Jags wideout Brian Thomas Jr.
Thomas is now in his third season with Jacksonville, and after an unbelievable rookie season that showed him producing 87 receptions for over 1,200 yards and 10 touchdowns, his play has slowed down. The Jaguars hired Liam Coen last season, and since then, it doesn’t seem like Thomas has been a focal point of the offense.
An ankle injury also caused Thomas to miss three games last year, but through five games this season, the Jags offense has pivoted towards Parker Washington, Brenton Strange, Jakobi Meyers, and even sixth-round pick Josh Cameron over Thomas.
Now, a trade involving Jeudy for Thomas would have to come with some sweetening on the end of Cleveland, as Thomas is three years younger than Jeudy, and Thomas is making just $4 million on the cap this year, and just $4.6 million next season.
The Browns would most likely have to give up at least a fourth- and fifth-rounder alone, but if the Jags don’t see much value in Jeudy, Cleveland would have to ramp it up to a third, possibly.
Cleveland and Jacksonville have a recent history of trading with each other, as we know from the Travis Hunter & Mason Graham trade, along with the trade that brought Tyson Campbell to Cleveland in exchange for Greg Newsome.

title: Why Denzel Boston’s Case For ROTY is Rock-Solid Through Five Weeks
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have two rookies of the year on the defensive side of the ball and now may have found one on the offense. Second-round pick Denzel Boston has broken tackles, ran past, and out jumped defensive backs on his way to leading all rookies in receiving yards. Through five weeks of the season, Boston finds himself the front runner for Offensive Rookie of the Year.
The 6’4 receiver has 330 yards and three touchdowns through five games. During key moments of drives Deshaun Watson looks for the big-framed target for crucial first downs. Boston has taken the top off of the secondary and has multiple touchdowns over 30 yards and is averaging over 20 yards per reception.
The Browns have a surprising 3-2 start, which is due to Boston’s play-making ability. In Tampa Bay he caught a post pass and broke multiple tackles, rumbling his way to a touchdown, bringing life to the offense. In the win against the Carolina Panthers, he used his strong hands and great route running to secure a crucial two-point conversion. He caught a would-be game-winning deep pass against the New York Jets, until the special teams and defense made it null .
No other rookie has meant more to his offense than Boston. He was the 39th pick in the 2026 draft, but he has looked like he should have been drafted much higher. Ohio State’s Carnell Tate was drafted fourth overall to the Tennessee Titans and he is behind Boston in rookie receiving yards with 274 and zero touchdowns. Tate has not helped a maligned Titans’ offense as they are 0-5.
Boston’s teammate and 24th overall pick, KC Concepcion is fourth in rookie receiving yards with 149. The Arizona Cardinal’s third-overall pick at running back, Jeremiah Love, leads rookies in rushing with 245 yards. However, that is only good for 23rd overall in the league and the Cardinals are 1-4.
Jalon Daniels has been the best rookie quarterback so far this season for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers; however, he will get benched when Baker Mayfield returns from injury. First-overall pick Fernando Mendoza has not made a start this season as the Las Vegas Raiders have been relevant under Kirk Cousins.
Boston is averaging 66 yards per game, which, played out in a full season, would be over 1,000 with 10 touchdowns. While those expectations may be too high, it is very realistic. Concepcion was injured in last week’s game and rumors are swirling that Jerry Jeudy will be moved at the trade deadline. Boston will get many opportunities to make plays for the offense as the running attack has been one of the league's worst.
Watson is gaining chemistry with him every week and his production will be greater as the season progresses. Todd Monken coached the similarly framed Mike Evans during his best statistical season, so he knows how to use the big target. Boston is just getting started in the NFL and by the end of the season he will be considered a legitimate threat, and not just for a rookie.
The race for Offensive Rookie of the Year may be over before the halfway point. Nobody is close to Boston’s importance on their offense and the stats back that up. The future looks bright in Cleveland as they will have three rookie of the year winners on their roster.

title: How the Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Benefits the Cleveland Browns
full_text:
Marvin Harrison Jr. was just traded from the Arizona Cardinals to the Houston Texans.
Obviously, the deal does not directly involve the Browns, but it actually does impact the team more than it may seem.
With Cleveland shopping Jerry Jeudy , his value just increased if teams are looking at the numbers.
This season, both receivers have been in similar situations on their respective teams. Each guy was slated to be the team's number one receiver, yet did not see much action to begin the season.
For Harrison, he only had 13 targets through the first four games. Out of those targets, he had five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown.
For Jeudy, he has only been targeted 15 times. His stat line currently sits at eight catches for 81 yards and zero touchdowns.
While the stats are close, there are some other key factors to argue against the Browns getting a similar trade package.
Marvin Harrison Jr. was drafted number four overall just two years ago. We cannot forget that he was one of the best college prospects we've seen in a long time out of Ohio State.
Mike LaFleur on Marvin Harrison Jr.’s effort: "I think his running style is different than some other people's." ( @BoBrack ) pic.twitter.com/k8m26OtpKm
With that being said, there is still much to be seen from Harrison. At only 24 years old, he has a long NFL career ahead of him.
As for Jerry Jeudy, teams already know what they are going to get. A diva receiver who can step up given the right situation. Otherwise, he won't fit in and will constantly drop passes.
At 27 years old, there is still some time for Jeudy, but obviously not nearly as much as Harrison.
With the recent injury to KC Concepcion, Cleveland may wait longer to trade Jeudy.
In the case they still decide to move him, what could they get in return?
TRADE: Cardinals trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr. and a 2027 7th-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 2nd-round pick and 2027 6th-round pick. (via @rapsheet , @adamschefter ) pic.twitter.com/abCg6guHE0
For Harrison, the Cardinals got back a 2027 second and sixth. While the Browns are unlikely to get the exact same package for Jeudy with Harrison being the better player, they can still get close.
If the Browns just want draft capitol in return for their receiver, they will most likely be able to get a mid round pick and late round pick. Some say they could manage to get a third, but I think that depends on which team they trade with.
Another option could be a player swap. The Browns have some gaps in the running back, offensive line, and secondary rooms, and could look to use Jeudy as a way to level out their team.

title: Browns Injury Report Highlights Concerning Trend Following Team Ahead of Week 6
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are headed into Week 6 with a 3-2 overall record on the young 2026 regular season.
Losing in Week 5 to the New York Jets on the road, the Browns have some work to do to bounce back in a Week 6 meeting with the Baltimore Ravens at home. However, being at full strength may be an issue.
On Wednesday, Oct. 14, news broke that the Browns were expected to be without multiple players for practice due to injury.
Of the bunch, defensive tackles Mason Graham and Mike Hall Jr. stand out as big misses, with running back Quinshon Judkins and linebacker Carson Schewsinger also pulling eyeballs.
Both Graham and Hall Jr. missed Sunday's game against the Jets, but both second-years, Judkins and Schewsinger, are new additions. They left MetLife Stadium in boots.
Wednesday Pre-practice injury report - expected DNPs due to injury: Barnett (ankle), Collins (foot), Graham (knee, ankle), Hall (ankle), Howard (knee), T. Jenkins (back), Judkins (ankle), Ryan (calf), Schwesinger (ankle). RB Dylan Sampson has been designated for return and is…
Schwesinger, Judkins, Hall Jr. and Graham will all be the talking points for the injury report, especially because of how important each have been to their respective side of the ball.
But it is impossible to ignore that other relied-upon role players that may not practice much this week.
Defensive end Derek Barnett is working through an ankle injury, while defensive tackle Maliek Collins also likely sits out because of a foot injury. On the offensive end, Tytus Howard is fighting to get healthy following a knee injury he suffered in Sunday's loss to the Jets, while Teven Jenkins remains out with a back injury that has kept him sidelined all season.
Tight end Carsen Ryan, one of the Browns' 2026 NFL Draft picks, is still hoping to return to the field after picking up a calf injury.
If he remains out, the Browns will have weak depth at the tight end position . A move may have to be made before the weekend hits.
While the Browns being without plenty of players on Wednesday casts a lot of doubt on their availability for Sunday, running back Dylan Sampson did return to the field.
He was seen walking around the practice field as his practice window finally opened, following a knee injury that landed him on the injured list after a Week 1 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He wasn't doing much, as showcased by a video from ESPN's Danile Oyefusi.
However, seeing him at least back on the field is a good sign that he can return in due time.
The Browns not only need to get a bit more productivity from the running back room after the first five weeks of the season, but with Judkins and Rahiem Sanders out , the depth is running thin at the position.
Hopefully, Sampson can begin to ramp back up his workload and make a return to the offense.
Along with Sampson, wideout KC Concepcion returned to practice Wednesday. He was put in concussion protocol following a hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick.
Somehow, someway, he may be ready to go by the time the Browns and Ravens meet.
They'll meet at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Oct. 18.

title: Recent Report Shares Controversial Value For Browns WR Jerry Jeudy
full_text:
The Browns are in an interesting position with veteran wide receiver Jerry Jeudy ; Jeudy is now in his third year with the team, and many are sure his future is somewhere else. In his first year with the Browns, Jeudy posted career-highs in receptions, targets, and yards as he hauled in 90 passes for over 1,200 yards. 235 of those yards came in a single game where Jeudy really took it to his former team in Denver, as it set a record for the most receiving yards in NFL history for a wide receiver vs. his former team.
Last season really tested Jeudy and many of the Browns' players, as the three different starting quarterbacks for Cleveland never seemed to get good chemistry with Jeudy. In his second season, the wide receiver took a huge step back, posting just 50 receptions on 106 targets for 602 yards. Along with not developing chemistry, drops were a huge problem for Jeudy last season.
Cleveland drafting two receivers (KC Concepcion & Denzel Boston) in the top 40 of this year’s draft was a clear signal that they could be moving on from Jeudy in the near future. Through the first five games this season, Concepcion and Boston have both been targeted 29 times to Jeudy’s 15, for comparison, through the first five games last season, Jeudy was targeted 35 times.
But the question is, what’s the value of a player like Jeudy? According to NFL insider Jordan Schutlz Cleveland would like a 3rd or 4th rounder in compensation for Jeudy. The initial reaction to this was controversial, as many think that there is no way a team would be willing to give up that capital for Jeudy.
In the recent market for receiver trades though, a guy like Marvin Harrison Jr. just went for a 2027 2nd rounder and 2027 6th rounder, with a 2027 7th rounder going with Harrison to the Texans. The main bet on this trade for Houston is upside, Harrison is just 24 years old in his third NFL season, and when he was coming out of Ohio State, he was hyped to be one of the next great receiver talents, hence why he was taken fourth overall in the 2024 Draft.
Harrison and Jeudy’s first two years in the league are relatively comparable as Harrison tallied 103 receptions for 1,493 yards and 12 touchdowns, Jeudy caught 90 passes for 1,323 yards, but just 3 touchdowns on 20 less targets.
Looking at other recent receiver trades , players like DJ Moore also commanded a 2nd round pick, while guys like AJ Brown and Jaylen Waddle commanded more compensation that involved a first round pick.
Realistically, though, Jeudy compares to players like Dontayvon Wicks, who was moved to Philadelphia for a fifth and sixth-rounder, or Jakobi Meyers, who was traded from Vegas to Jacksonville for a fourth and sixth-rounder in 2025. That may be the top of what Cleveland could get for Jeudy, and if not, the Browns may have to settle for a late rounder if they want to move on from him.

full_text:
In week six of the 2026 NFL Season, the Cleveland Browns are set to play host to their rival Baltimore Ravens.
For the Ravens, their superstar quarterback Lamar Jackson has been dealing with an ankle injury since week four. Last week, the backup quarterback Tyler Huntley got the start against the Atlanta Falcons in their primetime win.
However, just as the Browns thought they wouldn't have to face off against one of the NFL's best, new reports came out Wednesday morning.
Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a realistic chance to return for Sunday’s game at Cleveland, per league source. pic.twitter.com/O82hES7z4t
According to Adam Schefter, Jackson has a "realistic chance" to return to action on Sunday in Cleveland.
For the Browns, even if Jackson doesn't play it is not going to be an easy game by any means.

Over the past few seasons, Tyler Huntley has really been the best-fitting "stunt double" for Jackson, as he has been able to step in for Jackson during times of injury.
The Browns are also familiar with Huntley , as he was with Cleveland for two small stints in 2024 and 2025.
It doesn't have to be said, but of course the Browns would rather face Huntley.

The Ravens under their new head coach Jesse Minter have been incredibly efficient in all three phases of the ball.
On offense, the Ravens run the ball better than every team in the NFL other than two. Through just five games, the team has a total of 822 rushing yards and nine rushing touchdowns.

With that being said, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson will have to play one of his better games in Cleveland if they want to get the win.

title: Is Quinshon Judkins’ Time As the Browns' Starting Running Back Coming to a Close?
full_text:
After five games, the rushing attack continues to be a no show for the Cleveland Browns.
So far, quarterback Deshaun Watson has led the team rushing twice, and the club’s running backs are averaging just 3.5 yards per carry, and that’s including Raheim Sanders’ 4.8 yards per carry average on nine attempts and Jaleel McLaughlin’s 15.5 on two.
Of course, that points to starter Quinshon Judkins as the main responsible in the backfield for the Browns’ woes on the ground, as he’s carried the ball 73 times for 221 yards and a paltry 3.0 yards per carry average to go with his lone touchdown for the season.
With Sanders now on IR , and the team signing third-year pro Audric Estime off the Vikings' practice squad, there are bound to be some changes for Cleveland’s backfield.
Yet, no one should expect Estime to arrive bearing a savior’s mantle. He’s started just two games throughout his career, and hasn’t played a down in 2026. Throughout a 20-game career, he’s carried the ball 122 times for 508 yards with three scores. He’s also caught 17 balls for 130 yards, so with an average of less than one catch per appearance, don’t expect him to make much of a difference as a receiver out of the backfield, either.
Nonetheless, there will be another shakeup coming soon for the Browns’ ground game, maybe even this week against the Ravens.
The answer could be a back already on the team’s roster -- Dylan Sampson.
The second-year player out of Tennessee injured his left knee in Week 1 and landed on the IR without logging a carry against the Jaguars. After missing the last four games, he’s now eligible for having his 21-day practice window opened by the club, meaning he could come back as early as this week.
“I think there is a possibility we’ll open up his window for this week,” said head coach Todd Monken on Monday .
Despite not being much of a factor on the ground as a rookie -- his 2.7 yard per carry average on just 65 attempts for the year was actually much worse than Judkins’ 3.5 in 2025 -- Sampson proved to be a valuable asset as a receiver out of the backfield, logging 33 catches for 271 yards and two scores.
While not as physical as Judkins between the tackles, Sampson has the speed, acceleration and change of direction skills to be a factor when getting the ball in space or running outside the tackles.
The Browns’ current staff must find a way to scheme him more effectively than their predecessors. After all, Sampson was viewed by some as a steal in the fourth round of last year, and Judkins' continued struggles this year might finally be opening the door for him.
And what makes Sampson’s return even more critical for the team at this particular time is the fact that Judkins is “day-to-day” with an ankle injury that could sideline him for the foreseeable future, although we’ll know more about his condition, and Sampson’s as the week progresses. If neither Judkins nor Sampson can play next Sunday against Baltimore, then a practice squad call-up could be in the works for Jarret Patterson, signed last week .
Of course, the Browns’ ground game woes go beyond Judkins and the other backs. The team’s offense line has struggled mightily to open up lanes for the running backs, as the team currently holds the highest percentage of run plays with the first contact occurring at 0 or less yards.
Percentage of runs with 0 or fewer yards before contact through Week 5: 1.) Rams: 34.8% 2.) Bengals: 35.0% 3.) 49ers: 36.2% 4.) Panthers: 36.8% 5.) Bills: 37.5% 6.) Bears: 40.3% 7.) Broncos: 40.4% 8.) Lions: 40.5% 9.) Giants: 42.6% 10.) Ravens: 42.6% 11.) Vikings: 42.7% 12.)…
The team’s 3-1 start to the season felt really good before last weekend’s letdown against the Jets helped expose some of the Browns’ many shortcomings. If Monken can’t find a way to fix them A.S.A.P., that three-game winning streak will start fading like a distant memory really quick.
Whenever he does come back, Sampson should get a nice chunk of the workload. Then, it will be up to him to show everyone in Cleveland that there's an NFL starter in him, somewhere.

title: 3 QB's Browns Could Target in 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
Even though the Browns are 3-2 and quarterback Deshaun Watson has looked better than ever in his five seasons with the team, Cleveland will likely draft a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.
Here are three prospects to watch out for:
The dream of drafting Manning seemed to end after the Browns won their third game in Week 4, as the most likely path to selecting the Texas quarterback would require the No. 1 pick.
However, that doesn't seem to be the case anymore.
Manning has faced his fair share of struggles this season, and they came to a head in Saturday's loss to Oklahoma. Manning threw two critical fourth-quarter interceptions: one pick-six and another that set up the Sooners to win.
Manning will likely declare for the 2027 draft, but he might not even be the first or second quarterback taken. If the Browns finish in the middle of the pack and draft around No. 15, Manning could slide to them.
Coming into the season, the talk was all about Manning as the No. 1 quarterback prospect for 2027, with Moore ranking No. 2. But even Moore has struggled this season.
The Oregon quarterback has played in only three games, and a concussion he suffered against USC in Week 4 kept him out of Saturday's game against Nebraska.
Moore could return this season, but it's unclear how he will perform.
Moore has thrown for 926 yards and nine touchdowns, with no interceptions, this season.
Simmons might not have been on anyone's radar as a first-round pick heading into the season, but he's played well at Missouri. Most people remember Simmons starting a few games for Ole Miss last season, but he got injured, which led to Trinidad Chambliss taking his job, and he never got it back.
Now, Simmons is playing well in his first season with the Tigers, throwing for 1,434 yards, 14 touchdowns and one interception in six games.
Simmons is already getting love to join the Browns, as Pro Football Focus's Gordon McGuinness mocked him to Cleveland in a mock draft on Tuesday.
"Simmons appears to be one of the biggest in-season draft risers, with Yahoo Sports' Nate Tice placing him in the top 10 of a recent mock draft." McGuinnes wrote. "Given how the Browns retooled their offensive line and wide receiver corps heading into the 2026 season, I think now is a great time for them to find a quarterback to build around. Simmons has earned an 87.5 PFF passing grade and produced a 17.6% positively graded play rate so far this season."
The Browns could end up sticking with what they have, but if they do consider making moves this offseason and bringing in new faces, these are the best options so far.

title: Where the Browns Rank in the NFL Standings and Team Statistics Through First 5 Weeks
full_text:
Through the first five weeks of the NFL Season, the Cleveland Browns are a very middle-of-the-pack team.
In some cases, they fall on the lower side of the spectrum. Ultimately, the Browns are not playing like a top team statistically anywhere.
In the official week six NFL power rankings, the Browns fell four spots from 17 to 21.
However, 21 is way better than 32, which is where the team was ranked after that ugly week one loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
While the rankings themselves mean virtually nothing, Cleveland is being looked at by experts as a near bottom ten team in the league.
But what do the actual stats say?
The major stat that stands out for Cleveland is the number of sacks allowed. So far in 2026, the Browns have allowed Deshaun Watson to be sacked 19 times. This leads the entire NFL.
Additionally, the Browns are failing to score touchdowns. They are tied for third-worst with only nine touchdowns this year.
On a positive note, the Browns have only thrown two interceptions this season (T-6th), but also have four rushing fumbles, which ties them for fourth most.
The final offensive stat that shows a major issue the Browns have is the average yards per carry. With only 3.7, the Browns find themselves tied for eighth-worst.
Defensively, the Browns look a lot better on the field than the stats give them credit for.
Cleveland has a total of six forced fumbles (T-9th) and four interceptions (T-8th). On top of that, they have a total of 16 sacks (6th) and 324 tackles (T-10th).
As for what needs to be cleaned up, the Browns are allowing 11.5 yards per reception (T-23rd). This number, accompanied by the 10 receiving touchdowns they have given up (T-25th), shows that secondary depth truly is another issue the Browns could invest some assets into bulking up.
Looking at some other numbers, the Browns are among 10 teams that have made every field goal attempted this year. Their total of 10 made field goals ties them for sixth most.

Clearly, the numbers show that the Browns have some major problems with the offensive line, secondary depth, and running game situation.

title: What Raheim Sanders Landing on IR Means for Browns' Current Running Back Room
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are set to lose another one of their running backs due to injury.
In Sunday’s disappointing 17-12 loss to the New York Jets , the Browns ended the game down two of their running backs, both their lead option in Quinshon Judkins, as well as their back up Raheim Sanders.
Now, Sanders will miss at least the next four weeks after being placed on the injured reserve. This forced Cleveland’s hand in finding a running back to fill in during Sanders’ absence with Judkins presumed to miss time as well.
#Browns have signed RB Audric Estime and placed RB Raheim Sanders on IR for at least four games. Big loss.
In response to Sanders injured reserve designation, the Browns signed Audric Estime to the 53-man roster. He will likely take on a large amount of the work as Cleveland’s top running back if Judkins isn’t cleared.
Here are the running backs that can step up in the meantime for the Browns moving forward:
It was just announced yesterday that the Browns were signing Estime off of the Minnesota Vikings practice squad , but with the injured reserve move for Sanders, it’s now official.
Estime spent his first NFL season with the Denver Broncos, where he saw playing time in 13 games as a depth piece. Then, he spent his next season with the New Orleans Saints, appearing in seven games. His career totals include 122 carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns.
While Estime is only 23-years old, he has the type of skill set the Browns are looking for in their offense, as he can be a pass catcher out of the backfield as well. His combination of size and speed makes for an interesting pairing in an offense that’s desperate for run game help.
He’ll spend the next week getting up to speed on Cleveland’s playbook and should see playing time this Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens.
McLaughlin is the veteran option in the running back room for the Browns, as he spent his first three years of his career with the Denver Broncos before being signed by Cleveland.
If Cleveland feels they want more experience out of the backfield, then McLaughlin would be the smarter option to feature more in their offense. McLaughlin’s career totals include 228 carries for 1,124 yards and four touchdowns.
In McLaughlin’s Browns debut, he scored a 28-yard rushing touchdown on one carry against the Pittsburgh Steelers . That was promising to see him breakthrough in his first appearance, which could be a case to use him more in an offense in need of a spark.
The only way Patterson will see any playing time on the Browns main roster is if another injury occurs to one of their running backs. For now, Patterson remains on their practice squad waiting for his next opportunity.
In Patterson’s career, his stats include 126 carries for 503 yards and three touchdowns split between the Washington Commanders and the Los Angeles Chargers.
He’s another player with more experience, but not enough for Cleveland to view him as one of their top options. If another injury comes up, Patterson would hear his name called to likely back up whichever healthy running back remains.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Applauds Dallas Cowboys Defense For Players-Only Meeting
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys could have gone into crisis mode following the embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in primetime to kick off Week 5, but after a few extra days to digest the brutal setback, the team decided it was time for a "come to Jesus" meeting.
Cowboys star linebacker DeMarvion Overshown revealed that the defense held a players-only meeting to make sure everyone was on the same page and to iron out any issues.
“Look at ourselves in a mirror. We put what we wanted our standard to be... on the board," Overshown said of the meeting. "We went bullet point by bullet point: Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it?"
Since the revelation, there has been discourse about whether that players-only meeting means the team's season is in a crisis , but head coach Brian Schottenheimer doesn't seem willing to hit the panic button.
In fact, Schottenheimer was encouraged by his players huddling up to work out their issues.
Schottenheimer was asked about the media when speaking to the media ahead of Wednesday's practice, and was nothing but supportive of his players and their decision to rally together behind closed doors.
"I love it. I’ve said from the very beginning: the best teams I’ve ever been around are led by the locker room. And my information that I received from some of those guys that called that meeting, it was very productive. It was very open and honest ," Schottenheimer told the media on Wednesday.
"The pride of that unit is strong. There’s some really, really prideful men in that room, and we’re going to get it fixed. I have no question about that. But it doesn’t bother me at all. It means everyone’s rowing in the same direction, trying to get this thing fixed."
We will have to see whether the unit can rally together and whether the meeting got everyone on the right page, but it will help the players to know that their head coach fully has their back.
Add in the players-only meeting getting everyone on the same page, and the team's decision to bring in Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant under Christian Parker, it's good to see that the team is still working to improve after a slow start to the year.
We'll get our first look at how the meeting and coaching staff additions make a difference when the team takes the field on Sunday night against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.
Kickoff between the Cowboys and Packers is set for 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock.

title: Dallas Cowboys Legend Urges ESPN To Suspend Stephen A Smith Amid Recent Controversy
full_text:
Last week, ESPN talking head and notorious Dallas Cowboys hater Stephen A. Smith made headlines by calling out Lane Johnson after his abrupt retirement . Johnson announced he was stepping away from football to focus on his mental health, which led to Stephen A. criticizing and seemingly mocking the Philadelphia Eagles legend .
Smith received a lot of backlash for his comments and was called out by current and former ESPN employees, which led to not one, but two apologies on his podcast and First Take .
Stephen A. discussed his own mental health struggles after the passing of his mom and said that he takes the matter very seriously, but some believe he should have faced some punishment for his comments.
Cowboys legend Terrell Owens is among those who believe ESPN should have handed down some punishment, including a possible suspension, to send a message . Owens made the comments during this week's episode of his Get To The Point Podcast .
Stephen A. has apologized for his controversial comments, but T.O. still believes ESPN should have been proactive in making sure that something like this doesn't happen again.
As long as Stephen A. can say whatever he wants without any repercussions, there is no reason for him to improve.
“I don’t understand how there are no consequences for Stephen A.’s actions, especially with ESPN and Disney being the corporations they are, for him to speak so insensitively about a topic like mental health the way he did,” Owens said. “Why isn’t he suspended? For him to speak so recklessly to a guy and then try to backtrack and say he’s had mental health issues. If you knew that, then you’re smart enough not to speak on something affecting millions of people, millions of people, and something that’s a very sensitive topic.
“He’s never played football. Maybe his mental is not the same as a football player’s mental. His stresses or whatever he’s going through to get to where he is, sitting behind a desk getting paid by ESPN, don’t compare to what a football player has to deal with.”
ESPN has too much invested in Stephen A. Smith to actually hold him accountable, so T.O. is fighting a losing battle, but it's nice to see someone speak out against one of the most powerful voices in sports media.
After receiving backlash for his comments mocking the timing of Lane Johnson's retirement, Smith received a barrage of backlash from members of the media, including former ESPN host Trey Wingo.
Wingo said Smith's comments and response were "truly embarrassing."
This is embarrassing for him… truly embarrassing https://t.co/pTchM7tMBI
Amid the fallout, Smith issued a lengthy apology for his comments, acknowledging that he crossed the line. It was a rare moment for Smith to accept that he may have gone to far, and one that he hopefully learned from moving forward.
"Bottom line is this, doesn't matter what my intent was, it was how it was received," Smith said. "I messed up. ... Here's the reality of the situation: I was wrong.
"There's a lot of people in this country, in this world that are going through mental health issues. And the biggest regret I have for all of this is the fact that it might have given people that wanted to open the door to seek help a reason to pause and hesitate and not do so. I can't emphasize enough how sorry I am about that, because it is a real issue."

title: DeMarvion Overshown Injury Update: Cowboys Star LB Could Return in Week 6
full_text:
One player Dallas Cowboys fans were excited to see in Christian Parker’s scheme was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown . The former Texas standout has been a difference-maker whenever he’s on the field, but injuries have been a major concern.
This year, Overshown entered the season fully healthy and ready to be the green-dot linebacker for Parker . Unfortunately, injuries became an issue once again as Overshown went down with a hamstring injury during the loss to the New York Giants.
Overshown has missed the previous four games, but there’s a chance he could be back in action on Sunday night as the Cowboys visit the Green Bay Packers . Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Overshown is nearing a return, although he did say they would be cautious with the injury.
"We're not going to rush him back. He's working tremendously hard to come back ... No setbacks. The [hamstring injuries] are different, they are tricky. He's a powerful, athletic, muscular guy. At the end of the day, you got to feel right to go run-and-hit the way he likes to run-and-hit," Schottenheimer said via Nick Harris .
Overshown had seven tackles during the Week 1 loss before being injured. The third-round pick from 2023 has now appeared in just 20 games after dealing with multiple knee injuries prior to this hamstring issue.
When he was healthy in 2024, Overshown had 90 tackles, five sacks, and a pick-six in 13 games.
Once Overshown returns, the Cowboys will have a slight dilemma on their hands. Rookie Jaishawn Barham replaced Overshown as the starter opposite Dee Winters and has been one of the pleasant surprises on defense.
Through five games, Barham has 28 tackles, four tackles for loss, and a forced fumble. While Winters has slightly better numbers (35 tackles, three tackles for loss, and a fumble recovery), Barham has been the more impactful player. He also has the highest ceiling, perhaps even greater than Overshown at this point.
Ideally, the Cowboys will keep Barham as the starter, allowing him to work alongside Overshown. The next question is which player keeps the green dot and serves as the defensive communicator. Perhaps it’s best to keep Barham in the role where he’s been excelling and allow Overshown to take over for Winters.
It’s something the coaching staff needs to figure out quickly, but having two inside linebackers capable of handling that role is the exact type of problem they will enjoy dealing with.

title: Joey Porter Jr. Details Brutal Illness That Spoiled Cowboys Home Debut
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered an embarrassing 24-16 home loss on Thursday Night Football last week to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who entered the game winless and led by an undrafted rookie quarterback.
It might have not mattered much, but the Cowboys certainly missed the presence during the game of newly-acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was surprisingly ruled inactive prior to kickoff due to an illness. The team eventually decided to send him home to rest up.
Porter Jr. played a handful of snaps in his Cowboys debut against the Houston Texans a few days prior in Week 4 and looked solid, making it a disappointment for Dallas fans to find out he would not be available for his potential home debut.
Porter Jr.'s Cowboys home debut will still have to wait, but ahead of Week 6's primetime matchup against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field, he's finally revealing what happened when he came down with an illness before Week 5.
While speaking with reporters on Wednesday, Porter Jr. didn't hesitate to admit how awful he felt the day of the Tampa Bay game.
He tried to tough it out but simply couldn't deal with the nausea as he made his way to AT&T Stadium.
“My throat was itchy in the morning when we had our little walkthrough and I was trying to get on top of it,” Porter said, per ESPN's Todd Archer. “I told them about it. They gave me the right stuff for it and then throughout the day it just kept getting worse and worse. And on my way to the game, that's when I realized when I was throwing up outside of my Uber on the way to the game. So it was brutal, not going to lie.”
Fortunately, Porter Jr. has had a mini bye to get healthy in time for Week 6. After being on a snap count against the Texans, he said he expects to take on a larger role in Green Bay on Sunday night.
The Cowboys defense has struggled and there's no doubt Porter Jr.'s return and increased snap count will make the unit better as a whole.
Against Houston, he played 16 coverage snaps while allowing zero targets and zero catches.
Sure, this was with limited playing time. But considering that DaRon Bland got torched all day long by CJ Stroud and the Texans' receivers, it says a lot that Porter Jr. didn't allow any production on his side.

title: Cowboys' Plan For Malachi Lawrence Could Make Von Miller Completely Irrelevant
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are want to give rookie edge rusher Malachi Lawrence a push this week and that could spell trouble for veteran edge rusher Von Miller's role with the team.
On Wednesday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer heaped praise on the first-year edge rusher and noted how Lawrence had a very good game last week against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, something we pointed to in our stock report .
Adding to that, Schottenheimer said the plan is to give Lawrence more snaps moving forward, which fits into the promise Schotty made for changes in Week 6 .
"He's played very well. I think he's starting to show the flash and the acceleration and the ability to rush the passer that we knew we were getting when we drafted him. I think he had a very good game against Tampa Bay, and you'll see him get more opportunities," Schottenheimer said of Lawrence .
Lawrence had his best game as a pro last week with two pressures and his first career sack, which depressingly puts him in a tie for the team lead, and he added one run stop for good measure.
Nothing Earth-shattering, but definitely a step in the right direction after he has had a quiet start to his career. And, with the defense struggling badly and desperately needing some change, it only makes sense to give Lawrence a longer look.
With Lawrence set to get more snaps, someone is going to pay the price, and that someone could and should be Von Miller.
Miller has been a massive disappointment through five games. He might be delivering on being a Hall of Fame teammate , but he has not delivered on the actual football field, with Miller tallying six pressures and zero sacks thus far, per Pro Football Focus .
Another glaring issue, especially in Week 6, was his run defense. Miller just could not set the edge against Tampa Bay and the Cowboys paid the price for it.
But, hey, it's OK. Miller said the Cowboys aren't paying him for what he does on the football field.
As Miller has struggled to get anything going this season, he has also begun to see less snaps. He had a season-high 29.6% in the second game of the season, but since then he has been on the field for 25%, 25.5% and then a season low 13.9% of plays.
With Miller simply not being effective through five contests, the youth movement in Dallas should come at his expense.

title: Cowboys’ Players-Only Meeting Is Frightening Sign That Season Is Cooked
full_text:
It seems to happen every year, but it never helps. Teams that fall way short of expectations begin to feel the pressure, which often leads to the dreaded “players only meeting.” For the 2026 Dallas Cowboys, they have reached that point.
It was revealed earlier this week by linebacker DeMarvion Overshown that the defensive players got together without the coaches to discuss their shortcomings this year. Overshown said it wasn’t a “fire drill,” but instead a chance to hold one another accountable.
“Look at ourselves in a mirror. We put what we wanted our standard to be... on the board," Overshown said , per The Athletic's Jon Machota. "We went bullet point by bullet point: Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it?”
While the idea is noble, the results are rarely positive. But you don’t have to take my word for it, Super Bowl winners Travis and Jason Kelce believe these meetings are a terrible sign. If their opinion isn’t enough, listen to Super Bowl winning head coach Mike Tomlin.
Tomlin was a guest on the Kelce brothers podcast, New Heights, and was asked his opinion on what a players only meeting means.
“I think you’re dead,” Tomlin said.
Coach Tomlin knows, if your team is having a players-only meeting your season is COOKED NEW EPISODE OUT NOW !!!! @allstate pic.twitter.com/s7BxDm4Hsg
Jason Kelce said they both agreed, saying it would make more sense to have a meeting with everyone. As for Tomlin, he thinks it would be better to simply not hear about it, saying hearing about the meeting makes it “BS.”
”Hey if it did occur, I’d like to not hear about it. The fact that you hear about it is what makes it BS,” Tomlin said.
The Cleveland Browns had a players-only meeting in 2022 following a poor start, which didn't turn things around following an early-season meltdown. They finished 7-10, which was disappointing. They held another in 2024 , but finished 3-14.
Another team that was unable to find success was the Miami Dolphins, who went 7-10 following their Week 1 players-only meeting.
In the NFC East, the Philadelphia Eagles had a meeting called by A.J. Brown late in the 2024 season. Philly believed they were contenders, but after the meeting, they went 0-2 and were defeated easily in the playoffs by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
If any team can claim their meeting was a success, it would be the Houston Texans, who held a meeting in October of 2024. They were able to finish strong, going 10-7 and made it to the Divisional Round.

title: Cowboys' Christian Parker Insulted By Former Head Coach After Mike Pettine Hire
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker entered training camp surrounded by expectations that he could be the next big thing in the NFL coaching world during the 2026 season.
Instead, his first year as Dallas' defensive coordinator can't be off to a much worse start.
Parker's defensive unit is among the worst in the NFL through five weeks. There's no shortage of talent, but the Cowboys have started off with a 2-3 record largely due to countless mistakes made on defense.
As a result, the Cowboys recently announced the hiring of former Cleveland Browns head coach Mike Pettine as a senior defensive assistant. He has a history with Parker and could help him manage the defense, but with that hire came some harsh words from an anonymous head coach directed at Parker.
Per reports from ESPN's Ed Werder, a former NFL head coach had some harsh words for Parker following the Cowboys' hire of Pettine.
“They finally hired a real coach. Pettine is legit. Dallas will walk away with that division now," the anonymous coach told Werder.
Many reporters and fans on social media pointed to the possibility of this quote coming from Rex Ryan, the former New York Jets head coach who had Pettine on staff as his defensive coordinator from 2009-12. However, that's only speculation.
That said, Ryan has never been one to shy away from sharing his true feelings. After all, he interviewed for the Cowboys defensive coordinator job in 2024 after Dan Quinn left for the Washington Commanders but Dallas chose to go with Mike Zimmer instead.
Perhaps these comments, if they indeed are coming from Ryan, are directed as a shot at Dallas more than Parker since the Cowboys chose not to hire him and are on their third defensive coordinator in three seasons. Still, these aren't exactly kind words for a first-year DC that still has everything to prove despite the poor start.
Unfortunately for Parker, the Cowboys can't wait around for him to figure out the defense. The roster is loaded with talent across the board and there's simply no excuse to not at the very least win a playoff game this season.
If things don't change fast, the Cowboys may not even sniff the postseason, even in a wacky NFC East.

title: Tyler Guyton Injury Update Gives Dallas Cowboys Huge Sigh of Relief
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys saw multiple players get injured during the Week 5 debacle against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with left tackle Tyler Guyton included in that group.
Guyton came down with a back injury that led to his early exit from the contest. On Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer noted X-rays were negative, but he did not have an answer about whether or not Guyton would miss any time.
Well, now we have that answer, as ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports that the MRI came back clean on Guyton's back and he is not slated to miss any time.
"And Cowboys left tackle Tyler Guyton tweaked his back Thursday night against Tampa Bay, but his MRI came back clean and he's not expected to miss any time," Fowler reported.
The Cowboys are fortunate this week in the fact that they've had three extra days of rest because their last game was on Thursday night, so that gave Gutyon more time to get right.
Dallas will put out its first injury report of the week on Wednesday, so we'll have a clearer picture of where Guyton is then. Any semblance of practice would be a good sign.
Guyton entered this season in a make-or-break situation after two lackluster seasons to begin his career that were marred by injury and inconsistent play.
But Guyton has answered the bell thus far, with the former first-round pick not only staying healthy, but playing at a high level.
Through five games, Guyton has yet to permit a sack and has given up just two QB hits and 12 pressures in all, according to Pro Football Focus .
He has been a sensational run-blocker, as evidenced by his elite 90.0 run-blocking grade, which ranks fourth among all tackles. Guyton's 73.8 overall grade is 15th at the position.
Guyton's most impressive performance came in Week 3 against the Houston Texans, when he squared off with two of the best pass-rushers in the NFL in Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson.
In 32 snaps against Hunter, Guyton gave up two pressures. In eight against Anderson, just one pressure. Neither player was able to sack Dak Prescott in those 40 combined snaps.
Has he been perfect? No, of course not, but Guyton has been far better than at any point over his first two seasons in the NFL and that's about all the Cowboys could have hoped for.

title: 3 Things Broncos Must Get Right to Beat Seahawks
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have faced some of the NFL's best teams to start this season.
That trend continues on Thursday night against the reigning World Champion Seattle Seahawks . The Broncos will host the Seahawks at Mile High in a game that could be viewed as a potential Super Bowl preview.
In an alternate universe not too far away, Bo Nix never suffered a broken ankle in the divisional round of the playoffs, and he was on the field to host the New England Patriots in the AFC championship game at Mile High. We all know which team would have represented the AFC in the Super Bowl if Nix was on the field that day.
Now, whether a Nix-led Broncos team would have prevailed against the Seahawks in the Super Bowl is anyone's guess; but I would have wagered that Denver would have kept things close, even if it meant trading field goals.
When the fourth quarter rolled around, Nix and the "Heart-Attack Horsies" — who had become so resilient and battle-tested in late-game, big-moment situations — would have found a way to get it done against Seattle, instead of unraveling as Drake Maye and the Patriots did.
That would have been my guess, had Nix not gotten hurt. But that's not the football universe we live in. The Broncos' magical season came to an abrupt and bitterly disappointing end. But the Seahawks know the truth, too. It should have been Denver.
For these reasons and more, you can believe that both teams have had this game circled on the schedule since it dropped. Both teams are 3-2, with all their goals and aspirations still on the table in front of them.
If the Broncos are going to win against another tough non-conference opponent, three things will need to fall into place. Instead of calling them 'keys to victory,' here are three things the Broncos absolutely must get right to beat the Seahawks.
Amid Nix's early-season slump, many people have lost sight of what this kid has accomplished and what he's capable of. He's no stranger to starting slow, either, whether it's individual games or seasons.
Nix didn't storm out of the gate in Year 3 with Josh-Allen-circa-2020 numbers. So what? Allen's Year 3 rise was a thing to behold, but he didn't have to face the murderer's row of competition to start the season that Nix has.
According to Gridiron Stats and Info , the Broncos have faced the toughest schedule of opposing offenses to start this season, and the second-toughest schedule of opposing defenses . And yet, they're 3-2.
In all the years I've been watching football, let alone covering it, I've never seen the NFL hand a team such a schedule. On one hand, the Broncos earned their first-place schedule by winning the AFC West and earning the conference's No. 1 playoff seed; on the other, the NFL could have done a better job of spreading out some of these matchups.
The Kansas City Chiefs, Los Angeles Chargers, and the Las Vegas Raiders all have to face the teams of the NFC West and AFC East — just like the Broncos — but the NFL didn't expose them to the buzzsaw consecutively out of the gates as it did Denver. What am I getting at here?
The intense, singular level of competition Nix has faced to start this season is obviously one of the reasons why he has struggled. I believe there's more between-the-ears stuff going on with Nix, but some fans are losing sight of just how insane his schedule has been.
But if you think back to last year, Nix started off pretty slowly. He didn't really find his groove until the fourth quarter of Week 7's historic comeback win over the New York Giants, when he became the first player in NFL history to score two touchdowns on the ground and through the air in the same period.
From there, Nix turned a corner, and he didn't face anywhere near the level of competition he is facing this season. If the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, he will find his footing and then BOOM — he's off and running.
"You were the underdogs..." - @tracywolfson "We're the overdogs" - Bo Nix 😂 pic.twitter.com/sVx3izRHc0
Clutch-time play has been one of the hallmarks of Nix's tenure in Denver. But another hallmark is how he elevates against tougher opponents or in big-time situations. A primetime showing against the Seahawks would qualify.
Nix hasn't been perfect, but he is 6-2 in primetime. If you count last year's Christmas Day game against the Chiefs, he's 7-2 in primetime games.
In Week 3, Nix faced the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday Night Football , and while it wasn't always pretty, he turned it on when he needed to and stormed back to beat a Super Bowl contender 30-26. The Broncos need that big-game version of Nix if they're going to beat the Seahawks.
The good news is, Nix views this Seahawks matchup as one of those moments, and he acknowledged that both teams will have their dander up.
"Absolutely. There'll be some extra juice on both sides, and I think this is why you play the game," Nix said of the Seahawks. "This is why you want to be an NFL quarterback."
Nix doesn't have to be perfect. But he does have to excel in critical situations, like third down, red zone, and end-of-game.
The Seahawks' defense is a tough draw, but Nix is due for a game that reminds everyone who he is and what he's capable of.
Without a ground game, the Broncos will be dead in the water against Seattle. As it applies to Nix's slump, Sean Payton said it best after the Broncos' ugly 23-17 win over the Chargers last week: "The hardest thing to do in this league is play that position if you're not rushing the ball.”
The Broncos currently rank 25th in rushing, averaging just 86.2 yards per game. But with Payton calling the plays again in Week 5, the Broncos did take some steps forward as a rushing offense.
Payton stayed committed to a run-pass balance , allowing running back J.K. Dobbins to find a bit of a groove late in the game to help salt it away at SoFi Stadium. Dobbins had his best game of the season, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries against a tough Chargers defensive front. The Broncos eclipsed the 100-yard rushing mark as a team — a step in the right direction.
The Seahawks have a great defense, but the run game is one of the few chinks in their armor. Seattle ranks top-10 defensively in all the major categories, with the exception of run defense (11th) and red-zone efficiency (27th).
The Seahawks barely rank outside the top 10 in run defense, but that's where the Broncos have to focus their first- and second-down attack because if Nix is faced with third-and-longs against this defense, it's a recipe for disaster. Seattle leads the NFL in takeaways, with 11, and ranks No. 7 in sacks.
With how much Nix seems to be worried about turning the ball over against one elite defense after another, the best way to cool Seattle's jets is to get the run game rolling. I'm not talking 'three yards and a cloud of dust,' but if that's what it takes, I'd rather see Nix faced with 3rd-&-4 than 3rd-&-7 or 3rd-&-9.
The onus falls on Payton to call some well-designed rushing plays and to stick to it throughout the game. And let's not forget about the Broncos' starting five; they're a big reason the ground game has been so impotent this season, but it's time to break out of this run-blocking funk.
This can't be a game where RJ Harvey only gets three carries (like last week). Payton has a formidable one-two punch in Dobbins and Harvey, but he's got to use them that way to get the full effect.
If the Broncos don't rush for north of 100 yards in this game as a team, it's going to be a very long night for Nix. If they are able to establish the run and be productive, it should help insulate Nix and coax him out of his shell by setting him up in much more favorable third-down situations and keeping the Broncos on the field on extended drives that lead to points.
There's a chance Riley Moss could play this game, as he's listed as questionable with the rib injury that kept him out of action last week. However, Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out, along with safety…

title: Broncos Week 6 Injury Report: Final Decisions on Surtain, Hufanga
full_text:
The Denver Broncos will officially be without star safety Talanoa Hufanga for Thursday's game against the Seattle Seahawks.
Releasing their final Week 6 injury report , the Broncos ruled out Hufanga with the ankle injury he picked up in last week's victory over the Los Angeles Chargers — an injury that's expected to sideline him for the next few games.
Hufanga was marked as "DNP" (Did Not Practice) on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, making it evident that Denver was bracing for his absence .
The Broncos also ruled out perennial All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II with his own ankle injury sustained in Week 4. 9NEWS' Mike Klis reported " there is hope " Surtain can return for next week's matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.
Fellow cornerback Riley Moss was listed as questionable after getting in three straight limited practices. Moss missed Week 5 with a ribs issue.
Jahdae Barron and/or Kris Abrams-Draine are the next men up on the depth chart if Moss joins Surtain on the inactive list.
“I would say this, it’s time," head coach Sean Payton said Monday regarding the challenges of preparing on a short week. "There are two things, time and then the second thing is proper recovery from the last game. For each player, getting their body ready for a short work week, so that the time and the recovery—those are the two things that hit me right away with that question.”
Elsewhere on the injury report, safety Brandon Jones (foot), left guard Ben Powers (biceps), and defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (shoulder) were all full practice participants and given no game designations; they will play versus Seattle .
Unfortunately for the Broncos, the Seahawks gave the all-clear to the NFL's current receiving leader, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who emerged from Week 5 with a minor ankle injury. Smith-Njigba was limited on Monday and Tuesday before being upgraded to full on Wednesday.
“You feel great football I.Q, and then you put that with great talent and hips," Payton said of Smith-Njigba on Tuesday. "He can really transition, and then he’s a really good YAC player. So he’s catching it cleanly with his feet on the ground. All of the above.”
The Seahawks did rule out three of their own: running back Zach Charbonnet and linebackers Chazz Surratt and Drake Thomas. Every other player on their roster is expected to be available for Thursday Night Football .

title: Talanoa Hufanga Expected to Miss Time—But Broncos Have Answers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos expect to be without safety Talanoa Hufanga for the next two to three weeks. That hurts, with the Seattle Seahawks coming to town on a short week and the Broncos already being down two secondary starters, potentially.
ESPN 's Jeremy Fowler reported the Hufanga timetable on Wednesday, but he did qualify it with "depending on how he recovers."
Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury, per sources. One source estimated about 2-3 weeks, depending how he recovers. pic.twitter.com/8Eo02Dmbd0
Hufanga suffered the injury late in the third quarter of the Broncos' 23-17 win over the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, making a tackle for a loss. He's now set to miss his first game since joining the Broncos as a free agent in the spring of 2025.
Through five games, Hufanga has been an impact player, totaling 23 tackles (12 solo), three tackles for a loss, one sack, one forced fumble, one fumble recovery, and two interceptions, one of which he returned to the house.
Hufanga earned AFC Defensive Player of the Week honors for that pick-six game — a 30-26 win over the Los Angeles Rams at Mile High. He picked Matthew Stafford off a second time in the end zone to end the game on Sunday Night Football .
Hufanga started all 17 games in his first year as a Bronco, totaling 106 tackles on his way to being named a second-team All-Pro. He was viewed as a big injury risk when the Broncos originally signed him, due to how his last couple of seasons with the San Francisco 49ers played out.
Hopefully, Hufanga is back in time to host the Kansas City Chiefs for the Broncos' rematch at Mile High in Week 8. But it might not be until after the Broncos' Week 10 bye, if he doesn't recover as quickly as the team hopes. Ankle injuries can be fickle.
The good news is, the Broncos haven't placed Hufanga on injured reserve, which hints that the team believes he'll be ready to return inside of four weeks. Until then, though, the Broncos need a plan at safety.
Devon Key stands to be the Broncos' starter at safety next to Brandon Jones while Hufanga is out. The Broncos still have JL Skinner and Tycen Anderson on the 53-man roster, but don't be surprised if they elevate veteran safety Taylor Rapp from the practice squad.
The Broncos wanted Rapp for a reason , and he's had a month-plus to settle in and assimilate the playbook. It wouldn't be a complete shock to see Rapp go from the practice squad to the starting lineup while Hufanga is out, given his extensive experience, but the Broncos are likely to give Key the first bite at the apple.
But if Denver was waiting for the right time to deploy Rapp and make use of his veteran experience, there may not be a better one than this. Since entering the league in 2019, Rapp has more career starts (72) than Hufanga does NFL games (71).
Rapp has played in some huge games with the Los Angeles Rams and Buffalo Bills. He won a Super Bowl as a starter with the Rams a few years back.
That's a lot of experiece to let languish on the sideline or practice squad with Hufanga out of commission. Jones has been playing lights-out himself, and he and Rapp could make a solid safety duo.
Key is talented but very inexperienced. He may be a first-team All-Pro special teams ace, but he's yet to turn the corner as a reliable safety on defense.
The Broncos rolled the dice by letting P.J. Locke go in free agency this past offseason, hoping that Key could step in and serve as a bona fide No. 3 safety. The fact that Denver went searching for Rapp at the end of training camp may hint at how the team views Key from a reliability standpoint.
The Broncos have the horses to survive Hufanga's absence. But it's going to be dicey without cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs), too.
There's a chance Moss could play against the Seahawks on Thursday night, but the Broncos might be shorthanded again at cornerback.

title: Mile High Roundtable Renders Predictions & Picks for Broncos-Seahawks on TNF
full_text:
Hot on the heels of notching their first win at SoFi Stadium in the Sean Payton era, the Denver Broncos are faced with yet another challenge, and one even more enormous.
The defending World Champion Seattle Seahawks are coming to Mile High for a Thursday Night Football throwdown. It's a short-week turnaround for both teams, with the Broncos coming off a win and the Seahawks off a loss.
Broncos-Seahawks was the Super Bowl many people expected last season before Bo Nix's shocking ankle injury. When the 2026 schedule dropped earlier this year, this game was circled as a potential Super Bowl preview.
Despite both teams sitting at 3-2, few people currently view the Broncos as a true Super Bowl contender, but that's no different than the general consensus at this time last year. The narrative around the Seahawks, though, is strikingly different.
What's the disconnect? Offense. The Broncos' offense and the quality of quarterback play haven't been at a Super Bowl level — but the season is still young.
How will Broncos-Seahawks shake out on Thursday night? We're going around the table to see how the Denver Broncos On SI / Mile High Huddle staff foresee this one playing out at Mile High. You can connect with each staff on X (their handles are linked next to their names).
Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 4-1 : Another week where the Broncos decided to take the first three quarters off before finally showing up. At some point, it gets a little anticlimactic. That point, for me, is now. It worked against a winless, decimated Chargers team — even though Denver barely eked out a win — but it absolutely will not work against the reigning Super Bowl champs, who come into this game a little ticked off following a loss to San Francisco. Denver being home should help, but the magic won't be enough this time around. Fortunately, a much-needed mini-bye awaits.
Pick : Seahawks 23, Broncos 20
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 4-1 : The Seahawks have one of the best defenses in the NFL. Their offense isn't great, but Jaxon Smith-Njigba is one of the best receivers in the game, and the Broncos may be without three starters in the secondary. I expect the Denver defense to put up a fight, but it's hard to trust the Broncos' offense, especially against a top defense, on a short week.
Pick : Seahawks 23, Broncos 13
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 3-2 : The brutal reality is that the misfiring Broncos aren't as good as their 3-2 record suggests. However, despite the mismatch on paper, the Broncos' key strength is sheer resilience and late-game moxie. Payton might become the clubhouse leader for Coach of the Year if he can get this offense going. Ultimately, Denver lands a few haymakers and wins a close one as the short week dramatically levels the playing field against all the odds.
Pick : Broncos 28, Seahawks 24
Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 3-2 : Thursday games are some of the most unpredictable. The Broncos have the home-field advantage, while the Seahawks could be missing some key running backs. I expect this to be a big defensive battle. The team that turns it over less wins the game. Unfortunately, the Seahawks get a key turnover late and win a very close game, with the Broncos' offense once again struggling to get anything going consistently.
Pick : Seahawks 20, Broncos 17
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 3-2 : The Broncos are a different team at home. Nix has only lost three games at Mile High — two his rookie year and one last season. With Broncos Country at his back, he has a penchant for conjuring some Mile High Magic against the stiffest competition. Nix admitted on Tuesday that both sides will have some "extra juice," so I'm going out on a limb to predict he and the offense look at least a little better, even against this defense. Bold, I know. I won't forecast sudden early-game success offensively, but I can promise you Payton has a little something special queued up for Mike Macdonald after his " cold war " hot-mic comments dropped a few weeks back. Can this secondary cover for the potential loss of three starters? The Broncos better come ready to tackle, and JSN can't be allowed to take over this game.
Pick : Broncos 23, Seahawks 20
Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 3-2 : The Broncos' offense is off to a rather putrid start. While they have played one of the toughest schedules to date, even with that qualifier, the stats and the film state the obvious: it's simply not good enough. With cold, bad weather in the cards and a quietly struggling Seahawks offense, expect a classic Thursday night slop fest. Fortunately, for Denver, this team knows how to win ugly. While explosive plays and turnovers are obvious stats to watch, as they were against the Rams, I expect red-zone conversion percentage to be key. With what will likely be limited possessions and opportunities in that area, coming away with seven instead of three on offense and doing the opposite on defense likely determines the game. The boobirds come out with another ugly offensive performance, but the Broncos endure.
Pick : Broncos 17, Seattle 13
James Campbell ( @JamesC_MHH ) 2-3 : The Broncos are facing the reigning Super Bowl champions on a short week, pitting Nix against an incredible defense. The Broncos' defense will have its share of wins against Sam Darnold, but JSN's quality will be evident against a depleted secondary. If Nix is to silence his detractors, this is the game to make a statement, limit his mistakes, and take the shots when they present themselves. Sadly, Seattle's relentless defense forces a few turnovers and gets at least one defensive score before making the score look even more lopsided late.
Pick : Seahawks 38, Broncos 10
Lance Sanderson ( @LanceS_MHH ) 2-3 : This game feels like the Spider-Man meme because both teams have great defenses that have to drag their respective offenses to a victory. This game is going to be a slog. The weather is going to suck , and neither team can get the ground game going, so I expect a low-scoring affair with a couple of turnovers from each side. I'll take the home team on a short week.
Pick : Broncos 9, Seahawks 6
Erick Trickel ( @ErickTrickel ) 2-3 : The Broncos are beat up in the wrong spots to take on the Seattle Seahawks, and their own struggles play into the opponent's strength. With a short week and the Seahawks coming off a loss, they'll be pushing for the win to send a message about how they can beat a Broncos team with Nix in the lineup, given the hoopla about why Denver missed the Super Bowl. Unfortunately, the Broncos' issues on offense are still there, and weren't magically fixed because Payton took back the play-calling. The offense becomes an even bigger issue against the tough Seahawks defense. A defensive bout incoming, with Seattle netting the win.
Pick : Seahawks 17, Broncos 9
Dylan Von Arx ( @DylanVonArxMHH ) 2-3 : The Broncos survived an encounter with one of the worst teams in the NFL and have a quick turnaround this week to face the Seahawks. Denver's offense is sad and uninspired through five weeks, and facing one of the best defenses in the NFL may completely break them. Unfortunately, I don't think Nix gets his confidence back against the ferocious Seattle defense, and the Broncos take an embarrassing loss at home.
Pick : Seattle 28, Broncos 13

title: 5 Broncos Sleepers Who Could Steal the Show vs. Seahawks on TNF
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' offense has been questionable at best, but their defense has started to bounce back after some early struggles.
That said, after five games, this team isn't playing at the same level as last year's Broncos, leaving fans to grope for explanations for the significant drop-off we've seen. Even so, the Broncos are looking to reach 4-2 after a short week against a tough Seattle Seahawks team looking to bounce back from a Week 5 loss.
Winning in the NFL is never easy, and this is one of the toughest frames in the early-season gauntlet the Broncos have faced thus far. The Broncos are beaten up, taking on an opponent that can attack where they're weak and injured.
We could see a defensive bout on Thursday Night Football . The following Broncos could play a big role in whether this team comes out on top against the defending World Champions, and they could be flying under Seattle's radar.
Let's talk sleepers with a big role to play in Week 6.
The Seahawks have a talented defensive line, but they also have a vulnerability against pulling guards in the run game. Despite Powers’ faults, he's one of the best pulling guards in the NFL.
Denver hasn’t run many pulling concepts this season — not that they were a large part of the offense last year either — but this could be the game to activate them to help get this struggling run game going.
Unleash Powers in this way, and reap the rewards.
Bo Nix is having issues , but Franklin has been his security blanket in many ways this season. Denver should look at dialing up some deeper targets to Franklin to force Nix out of his funk.
Granted, Seattle is a tough team to do this against, given its style of defense, but Franklin could be the key to jump-starting Nix’s resurgence with Pat Bryant on injured reserve.
The Seahawks have one of the best offensive lines in the NFL this season, but they have some issues inside against the run. Uwazurike is coming off his best game in an expanded role.
The Broncos need him to continue ascending to keep the D-line rotation alive.
With Talanoa Hufanga likely out for this one , Key will step in as the starter next to Brandon Jones. When Key has taken the field on defense, he hasn't been good.
Key will face a lot of pressure, as the Seahawks' offense will likely key in (pun intended) on the Broncos' depth safety and challenge him over the top.
The Broncos' special teams unit has been good, though it had some issues punting against the Chargers. Denver's coverage guys were solid, though, and Skinner has been playing great on special teams.
Skinner could also see some snaps on defense with Hufanga’s injury, giving the Broncos a bigger downhill safety presence, so that will be something to watch for.
