title: Courtland Sutton Offers Strong Opinion on His Career-Low Start to the Season
full_text:
Courtland Sutton is off to a career-low start to his ninth NFL season. Bo Nix's slump hasn't helped matters, especially given that Sutton plays a quarterback-dependent position, but throwing out his 2020 campaign, which was mostly lost to an ACL tear, this is the slowest start to a season he's ever had.
Throw in the first-year learning curve of offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling the offensive plays the first four games, only to have Sean Payton take the play sheet back for Week 5, and the Broncos' juggling of how to fit in new wide receiver Jaylen Waddle, and it's been a struggle for Sutton this season.
The two-time Pro Bowler is on pace for a forgettable season statistically, but the 3-2 Broncos continue to win more games than they lose. Sutton's impact on this offense has been forgettable through five games, but he's striving to cultivate the right mindset and not allow his dip in production to affect his approach as a pro.
On Tuesday, the Broncos practiced for the first time this week in preparation for Thursday night's home tilt against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks . When asked after practice how he's handling not getting the ball as much this season, Sutton said, "Day by day, bro. Day by day."
Then the Broncos team captain let the fan base and media in on how he maintains his resilient mindset.
"Come to work every day, smile on my face, ready to work. You never know when the ball's going to find you," Sutton said on Tuesday. "I feel like the moment that you decide to take a step down, take a step away from it because things aren't going the way you want them to go in that specific moment, that's when you start to see failure creep in and doubt and all of these other negative emotions."
Sutton has just 11 catches for 104 yards thus far, but he was able to find the end zone for the first time this season last week in L.A. That used to be a solid single-game stat line for him.
Sutton has only been targeted 25 times, and the fact that they've only translated to 11 receptions illustrates how out of sync his chemistry with Nix currently is. That's a low target-to-reception ratio, but Sutton plans to keep his head down, do his thing, and not let these individual setbacks affect his attitude or mindset.
"Just staying prepared, staying ready, not allowing the circumstance to dictate my attitude, my effort, the way that I come to work, and the way that I attack my days," Sutton said. "So just staying prepared so that when my number is called, I'm ready."
As for Sutton's take on Nix, the veteran wideout has his guy's back completely, understanding that, as the quarterback, he carries "a lot of weight on his shoulders." If you polled anyone in the Broncos' locker room, Sutton believes you'd get the same response from each of Nix's teammates.
"It's not even just myself; I think if you ask all the guys in that locker room, the offensive guys, defensive guys, special teams, everyone has his back. We all know that for us to have success, we need 10 to be able to have that success," Sutton said of Nix. "We're going to always have his back no matter what, good, bad, or indifferent, because it would be the same way vice versa."
Sutton says that he and Nix have a lot in common as competitors who want everything to be perfect. So when it's not perfect, and frustration begins to settle in, they do a good job of reminding each other to "wipe it" and move on to the next play.
"When things aren't perfect, we get frustrated. So he sees me when something may happen in practice, and he comes over, and he's like, 'Wipe it. Let it go. On to the next one,'" Sutton said of Nix. "For us to be able to have that relationship, to both be able to go back and forth and say, 'Hey, look, wipe it, let it go. I got your back. You got my back. Let's go to the next play,'
"I think, like I said, you ask any of the guys in the locker room, everyone has that same mentality of wanting to have each other's back. And especially when it comes to 10, I think we all have that mentality of wanting to make sure that he feels comfortable, confident to be able to go out there and play fast."
Sutton may not be putting up Pro Bowl numbers right now, but he's fulfilling his role as a locker room leader. He's helping to keep his quarterback confident and rallying support in the locker room.
The Broncos continue to rally around Nix, and if the best predictor of future outcomes is past outcomes, odds are, things will finally click for the third-year quarterback, and he'll be off and running. It doesn't help that the Broncos have faced the NFL's toughest schedule based on opposing offenses and the second-toughest based on opposing defenses.
I think some fans and folks in the media are losing sight of that because Nix hasn't taken those obvious steps forward that everyone expected him to in Year 3. But the level of competition Nix has faced to start this season — honestly, I've never seen anything like it, and that includes the Peyton Manning and John Elway eras. This Broncos team drew the shortest of short straws.
And yet, the Broncos are 3-2. From what I know about Sutton, Nix, and this Sean Payton-led team, all this early-season resistance training will eventually pay dividends for the Broncos, and they'll reach critical mass.
In the NFL, it's more about how you finish than how you start. Amid the rocky road of this early-season gauntlet, it hasn't been pretty, but the Broncos are still finding ways to win.
When they finally pull away from the first eight-week portion of this schedule, watch out. This team is developing a big, durable callus. And when everything finally clicks, nobody is going to want to see the Broncos on the schedule.
They've just got to keep their heads above water until this eight-week gauntlet is behind them. With selfless leaders like Sutton and others, I feel more than a little confident that the best is yet to come this season.

title: Kelberman's Korner: The Biggest Issues Currently Plaguing Broncos QB Bo Nix
full_text:
Let me start off by saying that Bo Nix isn't playing particularly good football at the moment. Certainly nothing like the Denver Broncos quarterback we all watched lead the club to what should have been a Super Bowl appearance just nine months ago.
Regarding the Broncos' slumping offense , which has surprised given this year's expectations, Nix is certainly worthy of fault. His efforts are more timid, apprehensive, and unconfident than the gunslinger of 2024 and 2025. He's supposed to be the franchise cornerstone, and has looked the farthest thing from it entering Week 6 .
Speculation points back to Nix's January ankle injury and subsequent surgeries as the primary suspects, with the masses theorizing he's become physically or mentally bothered by it. But that cannot be confirmed nor denied at this juncture.
What can be confirmed is that the proverbial blame pie has many slices to go around — and many individuals deserving. The argument to revive Denver's offense does not simply start and end with Nix.
Here are some of the other things that must be fixed sooner rather than later:
While veteran starter J.K. Dobbins upped his game a bit in last week's victory over the Chargers, the truth remains that Denver's offense ranks 25th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, and Dobbins himself is averaging under four yards per carry.
The Broncos are getting negligible ground contributions from RJ Harvey — their best pass-catching RB — and Tyler Badie, who's only seeing snaps due to rookie Jonah Coleman landing on injured reserve.
Coleman appeared to be the club's best true runner when he was healthy, so perhaps his potential return in Week 7 will alleviate some of the pressure from Nix, and rewire a pass-run ratio that got completely out of wack under now-former play-caller Davis Webb.
So much for Denver's supposedly "elite" front-five. With the exception of left tackle Garett Bolles and right guard Quinn Meinerz, the starting offensive line has struggled to generate push at the line of scrimmage — particularly for the ground game.
Left guard Ben Powers and right tackle Mike McGlinchey are playing at replacement-level standards, and the Broncos may soon want to think about a long-term future without those aging vets. Center Luke Wattenberg is financially protected by his 2025 extension, but he's made several errant snaps and is arguably the weakest link among the OL.
The pressure is mounting on Broncos offensive line coach Chris Morgan because, as the cliché goes, successful football starts up front. And they're the antithesis of that at the moment.
If you searched hard enough, you could probably find Courtland Sutton's face on a milk carton somewhere. Yes, he scored (on a wide-open pass) against the Chargers, but it's evident the now-31-year-old receiver isn't quite separating downfield like he used to.
Beyond that, the Broncos have utterly failed to incorporate their big offseason acquisition, Jaylen Waddle, who currently has more drops (5) than games with at least 20 receiving yards (2). Twenty . Most No. 1 WRs eclipse that on a single drive. But not Denver's.
Perhaps Nix's most reliable pass-catcher, second-year man Pat Bryant, is shelved on injured reserve for another three weeks, eligible to return in Week 11 following the Broncos' bye.
Reserve WRs Marvin Mims — who's disappointed amid a contract year — and Troy Franklin have been non-factors through the air as Denver ranks 26th in yards per play and points per game, and 25th in passing yards per game.

title: Why Detroit Lions Did Not Take Out Key Players After Comfortable Lead
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were able to secure a comfortable Week 5 road victory at State Farm Stadium, defeating the Arizona Cardinals, 45-21, to earn their third victory of the 2026 NFL season.
Given the game was out of reach in the fourth quarter, many supporters wondered why several key Lions' players remained in the contest.
For a team that has dealt with a myriad of injuries the past couple of seasons, taking unnecessary risks ahead of the bye week appeared a little risky.
Speaking to reporters earlier this week, Dan Campbell was asked at what point he is willing to take out starters in a game.
“ Look, I'm with you. I think there is a fine line, and I've mentioned this before. First of all, we've gotten in a couple of these games where they've, just for this season alone, to where all of a sudden, something didn't go our way and now within four or five minutes we're back in this tight game that doesn't need to be a tight game," Campbell said. "And so, you want to make sure, you want to feel dang sure, that you've got it wrapped up. But you also, when you feel like you're starting to play some of your best football, you want them to get that feel, that flow.
"But those are valuable reps to get on offense and defense," Campbell added. "And so look, there's an argument to have pulled some guys on defense on that last drive. But I just felt like it was important that our guys play together. It's the best defensive performance we've had to date in 2026, and I wanted those guys to play together. To me, that was important in the moment."
The former NFL tight end has shared in the past about a past game, when he was the interim coach of the Dolphins, where the team let up and starters were forced to go back into the game.
"To go back with what you said about Miami, what happened, we were up huge. We were up three touchdowns, and I think there were eight minutes left and I pulled the starters," Campbell recalled. "And all of a sudden, within a matter of three minutes or whatever, they scored two touchdowns and we couldn't do anything on offense. I had to go and put starters back in the game.
"That's the worst scenario," Campbell continued. "Because now, you hate to say it, but if you're going to do that, your mind, it's different. 'I'm out of the game now' and now you've got to try to get them restarted again. That's not fair to the players. It's not. Right, wrong or indifferent, that's what it was.”

title: One Detroit Lions DE Whose Stock Is Rising
full_text:
Detroit Lions defensive end DJ Wonnum has been a welcome addition to the defensive line. A recent stretch of solid play has the veteran defender trending in the right direction, especially after a solid outing in Week 5 against the Arizona Cardinals.
Wonnum, a free-agent acquisition of Brad Holmes and the Lions this past offseason, recorded two sacks and three total pressures in the winning effort. And for his performance, he earned a 67.4 Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade, including a season-best 69.6 overall mark.
Additionally, he logged a sack, a couple of pressures and a season-high PFF pass-rush grade of 76.5 in Week 4 against his former team: the Carolina Panthers.
Furthermore, Wonnum possesses five sacks through five games, tied for fourth-most in the NFL and two more than he generated all of last season.
And his pass-rush grade for the 2026 campaign now stands at 65.5, ranking 43rd among 106 qualified EDGE defenders.
Slowly but surely, he's been proving his worth as a pass-rusher; in the process, he's provided a much-needed boost to Detroit's pass-rush unit over the last couple of weeks.
“He’s playing at a high level,” Lions head man Dan Campbell said of the veteran EDGE on 97.1 The Ticket. “I thought he really bounced back from last week. He played really well in the run and certainly in the pass game. He’s creating issues opposite of Hutch (Aidan Hutchinson). And man, he keeps doing that, with the firepower we have on that D-line, and you become very dangerous.”
Quite notably, Wonnum has also provided the Lions with a solid EDGE complement to Hutchinson. And the former Michigan sack artist, who has four sacks to his name so far this season, has certainly taken notice.
“Yeah, I love it,” Hutchinson said of his pass-rushing counterpart. “It's great, because if I get more attention during the game and he's winning his one-on-one's, then teams look at that and go, 'Maybe we don't send the slide here every time. Maybe we gotta switch it up.' So to me, it's a win-win all the way around. We just gotta keep rushing like that and keep playing fast.”

title: Detroit Lions 2026 First Quarter Grades: Offense
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have had plenty of success offensively early in the 2026 season.
Through five games, the Lions rank sixth in yards per game (393.8) and tied-for-first in points (32.8) under first-year coordinator Drew Petzing. While they've had to deal with some slow starts, the group has proven to be just as explosive as in years past.
Moving forward, putting forth more consistency in this area will be key to the team reaching its goals of contending for another division title.
Here are grades for each Lions offensive position group for their performance in the first five games of the 2026 season.
Through five games, Jared Goff has been playing at a very high level. He remains without a turnover, and became the second quarterback ever to have at least 12 touchdown passes and zero interceptions through five games.
While Goff hasn't had many explosive throws, he's done exactly what he's done best in Detroit. He pilots the offense efficiently, and has distributed the ball amongst his plethora of playmakers across the board.
The veteran has had some issues with sacks, as he's been sacked 11 times through five games. Some of this deals with his overall lack of mobility, which has been a drawback throughout his career.
Still, Goff remains one of the top performing passers in the league through the first quarter of the season and could be in line for another big year.
Jahmyr Gibbs has been electric for the better part of his first season as the team's true bell-cow running back. He has two games of over 150 rushing yards, including last week against the Cardinals, and just passed Barry Sanders for the most touchdowns by a player under 25 years old.
Gibbs also has 27 receptions already, which puts him on pace for a career-high in that category. He has proven to be a reliable option in the short game, which allows the offense to continue to stay ahead of the chains.
With Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve, the second running back role has belonged exclusively to Sione Vaki. Though it hasn't resulted in many opportunities, as he's carried the ball 15 times for 51 yards, it's the closest to an extended look that Vaki has gotten in three NFL seasons.
Pass protection also remains an area of concern, as the two backs have been inconsistent in this area. However, both appear to be improving and capable of handling the workload that comes with the position.
Amon-Ra St. Brown leads the NFL in targets through five weeks with 57, and is tied-for-fourth in receptions with 37. The USC product has been consistently utilized heavily throughout his time in Detroit, and the start of the season has been no different.
It was a quiet start to the season for Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa, but both have put together strong games in recent weeks. Williams scored his first two touchdowns of the season last week, and had his first 100-yard game of the season the week.
TeSlaa, meanwhile, had just two catches in the first two weeks before delivering some big moments in weeks 3 and 4. He didn't have a catch last week, but adds another threat in the passing game.
One area of concern that the team has is their depth, as Tom Kennedy is expected to be out for the season with an MCL injury. Tay Martin is the only other option on the active roster, so Detroit could look to the practice squad for more depth moving forward.
Sam LaPorta has had a strong start to the season with 27 catches and three touchdowns. There's been some lingering drama off the field regarding his contract, but on the field he appears to be in top form.
LaPorta has anchored the run game with his blocking ability as well, performing well in this aspect of the game as well.
However, the backup option hasn't been as good as Brock Wright has struggled up to this point. The third spot has been revolving, as Tyler Conklin has been active in the role for three games while Jackson Meeks has been active for two.
The Lions' new-look offensive line has yielded some good returns. The biggest piece has been rookie Blake Miller, who has started four games and allowed nine total pressures in that span. While he has taken some lumps, returns have been overall encouraging regarding his performance up to this point.
Penei Sewell has been advertised amidst his change from right to left tackle. Meanwhile, they've gotten good performances from their interior line with guards Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge and center Juice Scruggs.
Change could be coming to the group, as Cade Mays is set to return in the near future from a training camp wrist injury. It remains to be seen what fallout that will have on the group, as Scruggs could slide over to left guard but it won't be easy for the team to move away from Mahogany.

title: Detroit Lions RB Earns NFC Offensive Award After Cardinals Win
full_text:
Detroit Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs has been rewarded for his stellar performance against the Arizona Cardinals.
The league announced the former first-round pick was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week, following a Week 5 contest in which he recorded 151 rushing yards and two touchdowns. He also secured five receptions for 56 yards against the NFC West foe.
It was the fourth occasion Gibbs was acknowledged for his stellar play (twice in 2025, once in 2024).
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters prior to the teams Week 6 bye, expresse he was also really impressed with Gibbs' blocking prowess.
“I hit him up this morning. I said, 'One of my favorite clips of everything you did,' he had a ton of eye-opening plays, 'was his protection rep on the fourth-and-1, (Lions tight end Sam) LaPorta's touchdown.' That was outstanding," said Campbell. "And to me, that's why he's different. All this other stuff, of course he's got that and it's rare. It's that. He's unselfish and he's tough and he's willing to do anything for his teammates.
"And he might as well have scored on that because he's excited as anybody is that he helped get LaPorta a touchdown and protect (Jared) Goff so he could make that throw," Campbell added further. That's unselfishness. That's our guys. That's our guys.”
Additional Lions Insider Analysis: Release of Veteran Safety Jalen Mills Signals Major Return Could Happen Soon
He's him pic.twitter.com/N4jsa53glC
Gibbs was able to secure a lucrative new contract extension prior to the start of the season. Following a brief absence away from the team during training camp, the 24-year-old has showcased why he is among the top players at his position.
Running backs coach Tashard Choice marveled as what Gibbs accomplished early in his career. The former Texas Longhorns position coach expressed he kept tabs on the speedy running back early in his career.
"Having the chance to watch Gibbs from afar for these last three years, and every single week because of (friend Kelvin Sheppard) Shep and because of Jah, I kept wanting to watch the Lions' games,” said Choice. "To see him progress, to see how smart he is, ,I tell him he's one of the smartest running backs I've ever coached. He's jus t a natural football player .
"So, having an opportunity to get around him now coaching, I'm going to be harder on him even more."

title: Former Packers WR: Detroit Lions Jared Goff Is Best QB in NFL
full_text:
Detroit Lions quarterback Jared Goff has had a stellar start to the 2026 NFL season.
After Detroit was able to soundly defeat the Cardinals in Week 5, many supporters have suggested the former No. 1 overall pick should be in the league MVP conversation at this point in the season.
In a recent segment on "First Things First," former Green Bay Packers wide receiver Greg Jennings explained why the 32-year-old should be currently considered the best signal-caller in the league.
"He should be atop the mountain. You talk about historic things that happen. Regardless of how you feel about Russell Wilson, but 12 touchdown passes, zero interceptions through the first five games of a season. Two guys. Those are the two (Goff and Wilson). Gibbs, Goff. One of the reasons Gibbs is having the successful year is because he has a quarterback that can put him in position," said Jennings. "I am not trying to take credit away from Gibbs, but there is a level of lack of appreciation .
"Because of the style in which Jared Goff has to play in comparison to other quarterbacks," Jennings continued. "We just never really give him the boost that we would give somebody that can extend plays with his legs. It looks a little more sexy. That is not Jared Goff's game. But what is his game is always going to be "Mr. Consistent." Completion percentage is always going to be there. Going to throw a lot of touchdowns. A lot of yards."
The Lions are the fist team in NFL history to produce a quarterback with 1,400 or more passing yards, 12 passing touchdowns and a running back with 500 or more rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns, through the first five games of the regular season.
Goff has remained steady and has excelled playing his game. He is not forcing any throws and will simply take a sack instead of forcing the football into dangerous windows.
While he may not garner a lot of headlines like Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes, Jennings wanted to share why Goff deserves more credit than he has been receiving.

title: Three Trades Lions Could Make to Acquire Budda Baker
full_text:
If the Detroit Lions are looking to be aggressive at the 2026 trade deadline, one target could be on the team they just defeated.
With the Arizona Cardinals off to a rough start and having already made one deal, safety Budda Baker could be a candidate to be traded. The Cardinals traded Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday, and could be looking to add more draft capital.
Though the Lions are set to get a key part of their defense in Brian Branch back from injury, there is still some uncertainty looming at the safety position with Kerby Joseph still dealing with a lingering knee injury.
With the cap space available, the Lions could make a big splash and acquire Baker before the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Here are three possible proposals involving Baker that could land the Lions more help at the safety position.
Lions trade: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 sixth-round pick. Cardinals trade: Baker, 2028 fifth-round pick.
This would be an option if the Lions are looking to get some capital back in return, hence a bit of an overpay with a third-round pick. The consensus on Baker's value is that it would take a mid-round pick, as he's 30 years old and still on the hook for another season of an expensive contract.
For Detroit, the deal makes sense as they'd add future capital along with 1.5 seasons of the former All-Pro safety. His versatility and ability to get after opposing quarterbacks with well-timed blitzes, as Detroit saw Sunday, would add another layer to Detroit's defense.
Lions trade: 2027 fourth-round pick. Cardinals trade: Baker.
This is the best estimate for what it may take for Detroit to land Baker straight up. Because he's on the older side, as well as the money he's still due, the asking price may not be super high even with all the accolades he's accumulated throughout his career.
Baker is well-worth a fourth-round pick for Detroit given their current safety situation. While the overall likelihood of this deal depends on Joseph's prognosis, there's a real argument to be made that he would elevate the defense.
Lions trade: TE Sam LaPorta, 2027 third-round pick. Cardinals trade: Baker, EDGE Josh Sweat, 2027 fourth-round pick.
To be clear: LaPorta is by all means a cornerstone player for Detroit. Even with recent rumors about contract extension talks reaching an impasse between player and team, the Lions' track record suggests that eventually a deal will get done or the team will use the franchise tag to keep him for another year.
However, for the sake of making a blockbuster deal, why not include LaPorta in a hypothetical deal? The Cardinals already have one of the NFL's best tight ends in Trey McBride, and adding LaPorta would add another passing threat and give new head coach Mike LaFleur the ability to scheme up some unique 12 personnel looks.
Meanwhile, the Lions would get two defensive difference makers. Like Baker, Arizona's current situation has lent credence to the thought that Sweat could be dealt. Sweat asked for a trade during the offseason, with the Lions being a natural fit at the time due to their need for pass-rush help.
Even with early returns being positive on the addition of D.J. Wonnum, the Lions could always use more help for a defense that currently leads the league in sacks, and with LaPorta's contract expiring they could capitalize even with how expensive this deal would be given Sweat and Baker's contracts.

title: Release of Lions Veteran Safety Jalen Mills Signals Major Return
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a decision on veteran defensive back Jalen Mills.
According to the team, Mills was released from the practice squad, after being elevated on three occasions this season.
Safety Brian Branch has returned to practice, and if the front office feels that Mills has fulfilled his obligations, it would pave the way for the former second-round pick to return to game action after rehabbing from an Achilles injury.
With the hamstring injury to Rock Ya-Sin potentially being long-term, there is a pathway for Mills to return, should the front office decide to place him on the injured reserve list.
The team will practice all next week, and should provide the medical staff ample opportunity to evaluate if Branch can suit up and how much he can play against the Green Bay Packers .
Lions rookie Keith Abney had not played the safety position since middle, but he was called upon to man the back end along with Chuck Clark against the Arizona Cardinals.
“Thought he was solid. I thought he was solid," said Campbell. "The things that popped up for him were the, 'Hey, I haven't done this before,' which is what you want for a rookie. He's learning as he goes, but we feel very confident that he will learn from those and he won't make those mistakes again. So, I thought he played a good game. First start, first NFL start at safety, never played safety. He's banked some reps for us. We've been cross-training him. But, just man, there's meat on the bone there and he's got room to grow and we feel like he can continue to grow and get better.
"So, that was good. The other thing I want to mention before I got started, I should have said this, man, our fans were outstanding, man. They traveled well to Carolina," Campbell added. "We just didn't give them anything to cheer about. But, I mean, they took over that stadium and you could hear them. And by the end of it, it was good stuff, man. So man, we hear them. We hear you and we love it. We love it.”
The former NFL tight end indicated Abney has a feel for the safety position, which could bode well for his chances of earing increased playing time the rest of the season.
"I think that's a lot of it is, man, what is my responsibility? Some of this, we talk about quarter key. Depending on formation, three by one, two by two, am I getting too vertical to me? Well, if it does, then I stay engaged," Campbell explained, when asked what the coaching staff emphasized to the young defender. "If not and everything starts to go away, I quarter key, read the quarterback's eyes, then feel the pattern match or feel what's coming to me. So, it's different than corner because now you're seeing the whole big picture. And sometimes those guys, when you see the whole big picture , it's too much.
"But, he's kind of got a feel. He's got a feel for it. He's kind of crafty that way. And he's a little bit of jack of all trades and just a young growing player. And that was a step in the right direction yesterday. That was good to see. I mean, he's worth continuing to work with at safety.”

title: Lions First Quarter Rookie Report: Early Evaluations on 2026 Draft Class
full_text:
The first five weeks of the NFL season have offered the Detroit Lions a look at their crop of rookies.
It has been a bit of a mixed bag for Detroit's batch of newcomers, as they've had some who have already emerged into big roles while others are still finding their footing.
Here's a look at how each of the Lions' draft picks, as well as the undrafted free agent who made the active roster, have performed through the first five weeks of the NFL season.
Miller has made four starts already at right tackle, with an injury keeping him out of the Week 2 matchup against Buffalo. It's not hard to see why the team went with him as the starter, as Larry Borom really struggled in his only start in Miller's absence.
In the run game, Miller has been very encouraging to start his career. He has routinely handled his assignments, and has been serviceable in the passing game as well. Miller ranks first among rookie offensive tackles with a pass-blocking grade of 79.3.
Miller does rank fourth in pressures allowed with nine, but has performed better in that category than Spencer Fano, who was drafted eight picks ahead of him in the top-10.
Overall, Miller still has some strides to make but has made an encouraging first impression in his debut season.
Moore had an encouraging debut in the preseason, recording a sack in his only appearance during the exhibition slate. However, it has been less than a smooth transition for the Michigan product in the regular season.
He has appeared in all five games, but just notched his first two tackles of the season on Sunday. Moore has notched four pressures but zero sacks up to this point, and has played double-digit snaps in just one of the last three games.
Part of Moore's smaller role has been the emergence of D.J. Wonnum , who currently leads the defense with five sacks. Moving forward, Moore will need to produce more or risk falling down the depth chart.
Rolder was inactive each of Detroit's first two games and has played on defense in just one game up to this point. Detroit's defense is full of veteran linebackers, although they have just lost one as Devin White suffered a forearm injury that is expected to require surgery.
The Michigan product does have a tackle for loss to his name from the Carolina game, and could have a bigger role awaiting him because of White's injury.
Abney has logged defensive snaps in two games up to this point, those being the season-opener and the Week 5 win over Arizona. They have been two different roles, as he spent the opener logging snaps at nickel and played safety against the Cardinals.
In between those two games, he was inactive Week 2 and used exclusively on special teams in weeks 3 and 4. However, with some injuries in the secondary, the coaching staff elected to give him an opportunity at the safety position against Arizona and he delivered a solid showing.
He notched his first-career interception on a Hail Mary at the end of the first half, and notched six tackles. It was encouraging, and he may be worthy of a longer look even with Brian Branch returning potentially after the bye.
Law suffered a season-ending torn ACL in offseason workouts and remains with the organization on injured reserve.
Gill-Howard has been one of the surprises of the draft class up to this point, as he's earned a legitimate role already. He flashed serious pass-rush ability throughout the preseason, and that momentum has carried over into the regular season.
Gill-Howard has played at least 24 snaps in every game , and has eight tackles and one sack to his name already. He ranks 16th amongst all interior defenders in pressures with 13, and that number is first amongst rookie interior defenders.
While it hasn't always been flashy, it appears as though Gill-Howard has already carved out a niche and has high expectations moving forward after a strong start.
West, the team's seventh-round pick, was waived on cut day but returned to Detroit on the team's practice squad. However, he was released from the practice squad on September 11 as the team brought back Levi Onwuzurike after cutting him from the active roster.
A month later, West remains a free agent.
O'Neill has found a role on special teams for Detroit, as he has been active in every game. Though he has logged just eight total defensive snaps, he has seven total tackles across his various reps on special teams.
While he's buried on the defensive end depth chart at this point, O'Neill has become a staple on special teams coverage units and seems to be around the football every time it's kicked or punted.

title: Detroit Lions WR Jameson Williams Wins Fine Appeal
full_text:
Detroit Lions star wide receiver Jameson Williams earned a victory away from the field this week.
According to NFL media, "Lions WR Jameson Willaims won both his appeals of fines of celebrations against the #Bills, as amounts of $14,926 and $11,941 were rescinded. On one, Williams denied his "brief gesture" was offensive and argued "that marijuana is legal in some states if that was the gesture he was making."
The appeals officer, Derrick Brooks, shared with the former first-round draft pick, “Although I rescinded this fine, please make every effort to celebrate with your teammates in the best professional manner possible.”
The league has been cracking down on celebrations deemed inappropriate through the first quarter of the 2026 NFL season.
#Lions WR Jameson Williams won both his appeals of fines of celebrations against the #Bills , as amounts of $14,926 and $11,941 were rescinded. On one, Williams denied his “brief gesture” was offensive and argued “that marijuana is legal in some states if that was the gesture he… pic.twitter.com/tQ3wu2KNZf
Recently, the NFLPA and the league released a joint statement that clarified the expectations for players celebrating postive results out on the football field.
“Football is the greatest game in the world. NFL players are admired by millions of fans, including young people competing at every level of the sport. The passion, emotion, and personality players bring to the field are a big part of what makes the game special and connects them with fans worldwide. Good sportsmanship is equally important.
To clarify the line between player expression and conduct that may result in discipline, players were reminded this week that the following are prohibited and may result in a 15-yard unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, a fine, or both:
1.) Gestures that depict violence, including the use of guns or other weapons, or gang-related signs. 2.) Gestures that depict smoking or drug use. 3.) Gestures that are sexual in nature.
“Conversely, recent celebrations imitating drinking a beverage will not be considered violations or result in discipline. The league-wide guidance provides players with greater clarity on how they can celebrate while remaining within the rules. When conduct falls into a gray area, the league will contact the player and provide direction before imposing discipline. The player will be advised that continued use of the identified celebration may result in future fines.
“Individual and team celebrations are part of the game and help players connect with fans. Providing clear, consistent guidance allows players to express themselves while upholding the principles of sportsmanship that have long been a hallmark of NFL football.”

title: Packers-Cowboys Wednesday Injury Report: Two Enormous Problems Emerge
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have some potentially significant injury issues ahead of Sunday night’s home game against the Dallas Cowboys.
First, it’s the state of the defensive line. With Warren Brinson on injured reserve and Javon Hargrave headed to injured reserve, the Packers have only five available defensive tackles on the roster.
However, the starting nose tackle, Jonathan Ford, didn’t practice on Wednesday due to a calf injury. Following Hargrave’s Achilles injury against Chicago, Ford would have been in line for a considerable bump in playing time.
Plus, starter Devonte Wyatt (ankle) and backup Anthony Campbell (ankle) were limited participation. Campbell missed the last three games but will be counted on to help pick up the slack.
At least Jordon Riley was designated for return following last year’s torn Achilles. The Packers almost certainly will give him more than one week to get ready, though, following a major injury.
“We’ll work that throughout the course of the week,” LaFleur said of Campbell. “If he’s ready to go, he’ll be in there; if not, we’ll have to get somebody else ready to play.”
The Packers really don’t have anyone else, though, with undrafted rookie David Blay the only player on the practice squad.
The surprise absence at Wednesday’s practice was starting cornerback Keisean Nixon. Nixon, who is off to a strong start to the season, was sidelined by a groin injury. He played the first 58 minutes against the Bears before joining some starters on the bench after the 2-minute warning.
Of course, it’s too early to rule out Nixon. He signed with the Packers in 2022 and has played in all 73 games.
Combined with Benjamin St-Juste sitting out practice due to the hamstring injury sustained on special teams against Chicago, the Packers might have to roll with rookie Brandon Cisse and veteran Carrington Valentine against the Cowboys’ high-powered passing game of quarterback Dak Prescott and receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
“Well, I think it all starts with the quarterback,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said before Wednesday’s practice. “He’s a baller. But then you’ve got two wideouts – really multiple wideouts that can make big-time plays – but obviously the two stars. You’ve got a tight end [Jake Ferguson] that’s a really good player, a running back [Javonte Williams] that’s a really good player.
“I think all those, just the whole collection of them, I think Schotty [Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer] does a really good job as an offensive coordinator. So, it’s a great a challenge.
Ford, Hargrave, Nixon, St-Juste and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) were the five players who did not practice.
Left guard Aaron Banks, who has missed the last three games after dropping out at halftime of the Week 2 game of the Jets, was limited participation.
What will the Packers do at that position considering Laken Tomlinson has played well? LaFleur called it a “fluid” situation.
“Just trusting the process, trusting my training in the offseason,” Tomlinson said of his first two games. “I did have that surgery in February and got healed up from that, but just trusting the process, trusting my training and I knew I still had it in me and I wanted to give that a legit shot.
“I trained my tail off this past offseason and watching film, doing anything I can, gained like 10 extra pounds of body mass, just give myself the best shot. Fortunate enough to have the opportunity here.”
With Dallas coming off a Thursday game, it is in pretty good shape. While 12 players are listed on the initial injury report, six of those players are full participation. That includes premier receiver CeeDee Lamb (thigh) and two starting offensive linemen, left tackle Tyler Guyton (back) and left guard Tyler Smith (thumb).
Cornerback Joey Porter, who allegedly was plagued by a back injury while with the Steelers, was limited participation on Wednesday with an ankle injury.
Did not participate: DT Jonathan Ford (calf), DT Javon Hargrave (Achilles), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), CB Keisean Nixon (groin), CB Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring).
Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/toe), DT Anthony Campbell (ankle), C/G Jacob Monk (quad), DT Jordon Riley (Achilles), S Evan Williams (illness), WR Savion Williams (ankle), DT Devonte Wyatt (ankle).
Full participation: Edge Lukas Van Ness (shoulder).
Riley and Savion Williams have been designated to return from injured reserve and are within their 21-day practice windows.
Did not participate: CB Cobie Durant (hamstring), OLB Von Miller (rest), LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring), T Drew Shelton (hamstring), CB Ameer Speed (knee).
Limited participation: CB Joey Porter (ankle).
Full participation: S Alijah Clark (hamstring), LT Tyler Guyton (back), WR CeeDee Lamb (thigh), OLB James Houston (shoulder), CB Shavon Revel (knee), LG Tyler Smith (thumb).

title: Packers Wednesday Update From Practice: Help Arrives in Nick of Time
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers felt so good about their defensive tackles during training camp that they took seven into the regular season.
Attrition, however, has been cruel. Warren Brinson missed the start of the regular season with a calf injury, returned to practice and promptly suffered a groin injury that sent him to injured reserve. Next, productive veteran Javon Hargrave suffered a torn Achilles during the waning moments of Sunday’s win over Chicago.
That leaves the Packers with five players. One of them, Anthony Campbell, went undrafted in 2025, suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut in Week 2 against the Jets and missed the last three games.
Fortunately for the Packers, help is on the way. Jordon Riley has been designated for return from the physically unable to perform list.
The Packers grabbed Riley off the Giants’ practice squad late last season to help with the run defense. He was an immediate asset but suffered a torn Achilles in his fourth game with the team.
In the NFL, it’s funny how things work out sometimes in terms of depth and injuries. Headed into the season, the Packers seemed to have one of those good-problems-to-have with the glut of talented defensive tackles.
Injuries, however, intervened. Now, the Packers are short on defensive tackles. There’s timing. And then there’s perfect timing. Riley’s return could hardly have come at a better time.
Really, the only way the timing could have been better would have been for him to be a couple weeks into his comeback so he could play against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. It’s hard to believe the Packers would allow Riley to play after just one week of practice, but better late than never.
“He was here all summer long with our trainers and our strength staff. I don’t want to speak for anybody, but it appears to me he’s ahead of schedule and he will be a big bonus for us,” coach Matt LaFleur said during training camp.
“I thought he did a really nice job. He’s come in here, he’s been a great teammate – and that’s paramount. I think he’s really fit into what we do here. So, I’m excited for when he does come back.”
Riley was a seventh-round pick by the Giants in 2023. He played in 21 games during his first two seasons with them, including five starts in 2024.
He’s listed as 6-foot-5 and 338 pounds.
“Just stopping the run,” he said of what he’d add to the team when he joined the Packers last season. “We got so much talent in the pass rush, but we ain't going to get there if we don't stop the turn. So, I think I'll come in just stopping the run, making it my priority to stop the run, and then, obviously, first-, second-down pass, if that comes then making my rushes to go get a sack.
“But at the end of the day I feel like they brought me in to come stop the run. Like help out on that end and then let our edge rushers eat.”
Not practicing CB Keisean Nixon CB Benjamin St-Juste WR Skyy Moore DT Javon Hargrave (obviously) DT Jordon Riley has been designated for return. pic.twitter.com/BoVI4c0j9R
Four players were with the rehab group to start practice. That includes starting cornerback Keisean Nixon. He played all but the final eight snaps on Sunday’s win over Chicago, exiting with other players at the 2-minute warning.
Also not practicing were cornerback Benjamin St-Juste and receiver Skyy Moore, who dropped out of the Chicago game with hamstring and ankle injuries, respectively. The fourth player was Hargrave, who will wind up on injured reserve.
Receiver Savion Williams, who was designated for return from injured reserve last week following a preseason ankle injury, was back on the field.
Also practicing on Wednesday after returning on Friday were left guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and guard/center Jacob Monk (quad).
“Yeah, I would say it’s going to be pretty fluid,” LaFleur said of handling Banks, who has played in only one-half of a game this season, given the success of his replacement, Laken Tomlinson. “We’ve got to see where he’s at. He hasn’t practiced in a really long time, and I think those other guys have come in and done a really good job.”
At right guard, the success of Travis Glover the past two weeks appears to have carried over to the start of this week, with Glover getting the early work instead of Kevin Zeitler.
Without Moore, the Packers will have to sort out who will be back to return punts and kickoffs. Against Chicago, star receiver Matthew Golden returned punts and rookie receiver J. Michael Sturdivant joined Matthew Golden on kickoffs.
Given Golden’s production on offense, would the Packers want to risk him in that role?
We’ll kind of work through that through the course of the week,” LaFleur said before practice. “Certainly, MG’s value, he’s so valuable as a wide receiver for us, but it could be a week-to-week thing with that.”
Coming full circle at defensive tackle, the Packers will roll with starters Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks, nose tackle Jonathan Ford, rookie Chris McClellan and Campbell.
How much could Campbell reasonably contribute after a long layoff?
“We’ll work that throughout the course of the week,” LaFleur said. “If he’s ready to go, he’ll be in there; if not, we’ll have to get somebody else ready to play.”
There isn’t anyone else, though. Undrafted rookie David Blay is the only player on the practice squad, and he only recently joined the team.
So, would the Packers have to line up with only four against Dallas’ powerful offensive line?
“Potentially,” LaFleur said. But, “That would be less than ideal.”

title: We Asked About Play-Action Passing; Packers Provided Explosive Answer
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Before the Green Bay Packers faced the Chicago Bears last week, we asked why the Packers weren’t leaning into their play-action passing game more.
At the time, Jordan Love had some of the best play-action stats but coach Matt LaFleur used it less than most teams.
“I think you have to stay in manageable situations,” LaFleur said last week. “If it’s second-and-20 and you run a play-action, it’s probably not going to be as effective as if it’s even second-and-7. I think that [not needing an effective run game to have an effective play-action game] could hold true for some of the first-down situations, but it’s more when you’re in get-back-on-track (situations) that I think it’s less effective.”
On Sunday, LaFleur and Love dropped a series of play-action bombs on Chicago’s secondary. The result was one of the best games of Love’s career and a combined 330 receiving yards from Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft.
Love’s play-action numbers were downright absurd. Even with limited success running the football again, Love according to Pro Football Focus was 12-of-14 passing for 245 yards with one touchdown and a 142.6 passer rating.
According to Sumer Sports, Love was 10-of-12 for 212 yards. That’s not just the most play-action yards for a quarterback this season but the most in a regular-season game since Jared Goff in 2024.
Why? And how? It’s not as if the Packers ran the ball well. They finished the day with 2.7 yards per carry, though a solid 4.0-yard average in the first half helped. They finished last in the league last week with 1.1 yards per first-down carry.
Taking out Tyrod Taylor’s kneel-down to end the game, the Packers had as many first-down runs that gained 0 yards or worse as 3 yards or better (four apiece). MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson combined for 11 carries for 14 yards.
But the Packers kept dialing up play-action passes and Love kept answering with big-play completions.
“Ultimately you’ve got to go out and you’ve got to execute, though,” LaFleur said before practice on Wednesday. “Whether you’re dropping back, screening, throwing the quick game, play action, you’ve got to go out there and execute. And our guys went out there and did a really good job.
“It all starts up front, just giving Jordan the time to be able to allow some of those long-developing plays to develop. It starts up front. It’s not just the O-line. MarShawn (Lloyd) had a key block on the first one in terms of when they brought the corner blitz.”
Even without run-game support, Love had 66 more play-action yards than any other quarterback last week, according to Pro Football Focus. Among quarterbacks with more than five play-action dropbacks, he was first in completion percentage (85.7) and yards per attempt (17.5).
“I felt like we were rolling, definitely, play after play, drive after drive, making big plays,” Love said after the game. “It’s definitely a good feeling when you’re having a lot of explosive plays (and) putting up a lot of points. Obviously, defense played a huge part in that, getting us the ball back with all those turnovers, keeping them out of the end zone.
“It’s one of those things we’ve talked about. It’s flow state – feels like you’re flowing out there – just play after play we’re making those. It felt good to be able to do that at home.”
With Love flowing, Watson and Golden were exploding. They combined for 266 yards.
Highest yards per route run among WR in Week 5 so far Christian Watson       4.77 Matthew Golden        4.56 Mike Evans                   4.35 Xavier Hutchinson    4.06 George Pickens          3.42 pic.twitter.com/ru4ZR7M9fM
“I’ve said this a million times, I feel like – every week’s a new week,” LaFleur said on Monday. “Obviously, we’re always trying to get our playmakers the ball and those two guys are our best playmakers in that room right now. So, if their number’s called and the coverage presents itself the way that it did, then they’re going to get opportunities.
“You can’t control what the defensive call is, but you want to try to as much as possible put those guys at the point of attack and in position that if the coverage plays out the way you want it to, they have opportunities to go make plays. I can’t say enough about those two guys, just the plays that they made.”
While the data shows teams don’t need a successful run game to have a successful play-action attack, it doesn’t hurt. Whether it’s the mere threat of the run or the difference between second-and-7 and second-and-10, the Packers probably know that last week’s success against Chicago isn’t sustainable until they build some semblance of a relevant run game.
“We’re inconsistent, but yeah, there’s been some good ones,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “I think we still need to just be more consistent. We’ve had some negative runs put us behind the sticks in every game, so we just got to make sure we’re finding yards in those plays and not losing yards. I think once we do that, we’ll be able to get more runs called, we’ll be able to be more consistent and just be better as an offense.
According to PFF, 29 quarterbacks have at least 100 total dropbacks. Comparing play-action passes to standard dropbacks, Love is plus-19.8 in completion percentage (second), plus 4.1 yards per attempt (second) and plus-67.8 in passer rating (first).
Ten quarterbacks are averaging at least 1.7 yards more per play-action dropback than traditional dropbacks. Two of those quarterbacks have top-10 rushing attacks, three have bottom-10 rushing attacks and the other five are in the middle.
Why doesn’t it matter? Because linebackers are trained to stop the run.
“What I like to say is that you don't have to establish the run because the run was established in Pop Warner,” said Aaron Schatz, a founder of Football Outsiders and now with FTN Fantasy.
Can the Packers keep it going against the Cowboys? If so, it will be up a lot more than Love, Watson and Golden.
“It’s everybody,” LaFleur said. “It falls on everybody who’s in protection, and then obviously the wideouts have got to go do their thing, and those guys were making plays. They made some tough contested catches, and that’s part of the reason it was so effective.”

title: Grading the Six Players From Packers’ Top-10 Draft Class With Huge Test Looming
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Who says you need a first-round pick to have an impactful draft class?
Having sent two first-round picks to Dallas in the Micah Parsons trade, Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst has turned lemons into lemonade with his six-man draft class.
In his recent draft-class rankings , NFL Draft On SI’s Justin Melo ranked the Packers ninth. He gave them a B-plus, saluting in particular cornerback Brandon Cisse and edge player Dani Dennis-Sutton.
Going through each individual, here is our grade for the six players. Plus, it’s a look ahead to ahead to their challenges on Sunday night against the Cowboys.
It didn’t take long for Brandon Cisse to emerge as the no-doubt-about-it starter. With 1.5 sacks and two pass breakups, there’s been a lot more good than bad in his five starts.
According to Pro Football Focus, 109 cornerbacks have played at least 68 coverage snaps. Cisse is 70th with a completion rate allowed of 68.8 percent and 90th with 16.9 yards allowed per catch. Those numbers seem terrible, but he’s only been targeted 16 times and given up 11 catches. That makes him 19th with 16.1 coverage snaps per reception allowed.
Of the 14 rookie cornerbacks to play at least 40 coverage snaps, Cisse is No. 1 in snaps per reception.
Cisse has given up more than two catches in only one game – Week 3 against Atlanta – and was charged with three receptions allowed for 20 yards the last two weeks combined. He’s missed too many tackles but the mentality is there, which is a good starting point.
He’ll obviously face a much, much bigger challenge on Sunday night against Dak Prescott and premier receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. We’ll know a lot  more about Cisse after this game and then next week at Detroit.
Chris McClellan has played a lot as defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon has leaned on a rotation to minimize everyone’s workload. Playing 29 snaps a game, the box-score production hasn’t been there with only five tackles and one quarterback hit.
The Packers drafted McClellan over Vikings run-stuffer Domonique Orange because of his ability to be a three-down player. They’re still waiting for that to show up because he hasn’t produced in either phase.
Of the 100 defensive tackles with 53 pass-rushing opportunities, McClellan ranks 89th in PFF’s pass-rush productivity, which measures sacks, hits and hurries per pass-rushing snap, and 91st in pass-rush win rate.
Of the 13 rookie defensive tackles with 20 pass-rushing snaps, McClellan is eighth in both categories. Two of his three pressures came against the Bears.
During one run play against the Bears, he wound up being pushed about 8 yards downfield. There were some impactful reps, though.
Chris McClellan is off to a quiet start. Without Javon Hargrave, they'll need more of this. pic.twitter.com/W0dpIs6HrN
With Javon Hargrave out for the rest of the season with a torn Achilles and with Warren Brinson on injured reserve, the Packers need more from their five remaining players. McClellan is front and center in that conversation. He will face a huge test against the Cowboys, who feature three-time Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith and 2025 first-round right guard Tyler Booker.
The Packers were thrilled that Dennis-Sutton fell into their laps in the fourth round. That optimism seems warranted. He has 13 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four quarterback hits and two tackles for losses. Barryn Sorrell, a fourth-round pick last year and a starter this year, has 13 tackles, a half-sack, one quarterback hit and no tackles for losses.
Third of three clips on Dennis-Sutton. Here's his sack. pic.twitter.com/716KYQ8yI9
Of the 99 edge players with at least 50 pass-rushing opportunities, Dennis-Sutton is 47th in pass-rushing productivity – just behind T.J. Watt and Khalil Mack – but 87th in pass-rush win rate.
Of the 16 rookie edge players with 20 pass-rushing snaps, Dennis-Sutton is sixth in PRP and 12th in win rate. Of his nine pressures, four came against the Jets and three against Chicago.
He has used his length and strength against the run. In fact, his average distance of tackle vs. the run has produced a loss of 0.7 yards; only the Vikings’ Andrew Van Ginkel is better. His aggressive play has worked against him in the bootleg game …
First of three clips on Dennis-Sutton. He has been suckered frequently by bootlegs, like this one. pic.twitter.com/vhFyUwiTPi
But this play against a receiver screen was impressive.
Second of three clips on Dennis-Sutton. The awareness and hustle here is excellent. I don't think an offense schemes for an edge player to ruin a receiver screen. pic.twitter.com/6KdjjkAmkq
Dennis-Sutton played a lot on the right side of the defense against Chicago. If he stays there, that would mean a match against the Cowboys’ excellent young left tackle, Tyler Guyton.
Jager Burton’s starting debut was a disaster as he allowed 10 quarterback pressures against the Falcons. Burton allowed five quarterback hits in that game. Only one guard has allowed more hits this season.
The team quickly pivoted by signing veterans Laken Tomlinson and Kevin Zeitler to the 53-man roster and Mekhi Becton to the practice squad. At this rate, Burton might not be heard from for the rest of the season.
That doesn’t mean his career is over, obviously. The Packers were bullish on him throughout training camp; one bad game shouldn’t change the outlook.
With Keisean Nixon and Carrington Valentine entering the final season under contract, the Packers took a flier on Domani Jackson with the 201st pick, hoping to get the best out of a touted prospect who had a disappointing senior season at Alabama.
Jackson didn’t make the roster and is on the practice squad. Taken a few picks later, Lions defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard has 13 pressures. All of Green Bay’s defensive tackles have 21 pressures, led by Javon Hargrave with six.
Grade: F (for now, obviously).
Trey Smack was the only kicker who was drafted and is one of three on a roster. He missed two kicks in the first four games – a missed extra point and a blocked field goal – but had three against Chicago. Smack, fellow rookie Drew Stevens of Washington and veteran Eddy Pineiro have each missed a league-worst five kicks.
“It’s something we can build off of,” special teams coordinator Cam Achord said on Tuesday. “We talked about it (that it) wasn’t always going to be perfect. Whether you’re a kicker or another position, you’re a rookie. There’s going to be a bump in the road, and he’s got the right mental makeup to trust the process, trust what we’re doing in practice, trust what he did the first four weeks. Good contact on the ball, and just trust it. And I think he’s going to be fine. I have no fear about that.”
For field goals among the rookies, Smack is 7-of-10 (70.0 percent), the Giants’ Dominic Zvada is 11-of-14 (78.6 percent) and Stevens is 9-of-11 (81.8 percent).
The stats suggest the grade should be an F, but he’s really only had one bad game.

title: Packers Broke the Bank for These 12 Players; Six of Them Are Broken
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The hits just keep coming for the Green Bay Packers.
The Packers are one of the most injured teams in the NFL , with many of the ailments being significant injuries to key players.
Including defensive tackle Javon Hargrave’s torn Achilles in the waning moments of Sunday’s game against the Bears, six of Green Bay’s 12 players with average salaries of at least $10 million are out of the lineup. They total $128 million in average annual salary.
In terms of cap dollars, they are consuming $72.08 million. That’s almost 24 percent of the cap not contributing to the lineup.
Here they are, with the dollar figures being their average annual salaries.
The Packers hoped Micah Parsons would be back for this week’s game against the Dallas Cowboys. Parsons no doubt wanted to be back to face his former team, as well. Instead, he hasn’t even started practicing.
His brother said the “best bet” would be Parsons returning in Week 10 against the Vikings or Week 12 against the Rams, the games bridging this year’s bye.
“First of all, you’ve got to get him back on the practice field,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “There’s a lot of testing that goes on before he gets medically cleared to get out there, and then I’m sure we’re going to want to give him some time to get back to playing football. As you see with most guys that are coming off a major injury, it takes a little bit of time.”
When healthy, Bako-Bewele is one of the best right tackles in the NFL. The Packers gave him a huge contract extension at the start of training camp in 2023, only for him to completely tear the patellar ligament that he partially tore last year. He’ll wind up playing 676 of about 2,100 snaps in 2025 and 2026.
Fortunately for the Packers, Anthony Belton is playing better. He has allowed zero pressures the last two games, according to PFF.
“He’s done a nice job,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said on Tuesday. “He’s firmed the pocket up. I think that was the biggest thing the first couple weeks was just the push that we were feeling in the pocket.
“I think him and Laken (Tomlinson at left guard) have done a really nice job just firming that up, allowing Jordan (Love) to see and not have that pocket pushed in his face. There were a couple reps in the game that, obviously, we got to clean up with him but, for the most part, he’s out there competing and doing a nice job.”
We might be able to erase Aaron Banks from this ledger at some point. Banks was inactive in Week 1 with a knee injury and started Week 2 but suffered a toe injury that held him out of the second half and then each of the last three games.
Banks has played 22 snaps this season. He returned to practice on Friday, though, so a decision will have to be made at some point whether Banks or Laken Tomlinson will start at left guard.
“One thing we have to keep in mind too is where do we fit those guys into the best five,” Adam Stenavich said. “We’ll evaluate that but, yeah, that’s going to be an interesting thing as we go through the next few weeks, for sure.”
After an injury-plagued 2025 season, the Packers gave Jayden Reed a three-year, $50.25 million contract extension in April. However, he wound up suffering a season-neck injury that required surgery. It ended his season after 41 snaps.
The Packers believed Skyy Moore could pick up the slack but he suffered an ankle injury early against Chicago and could miss a little time.
“Losing Skyy for however long he’s going to be out, that’s going to be interesting,” Adam Stenavich said. “We’ll see where Savion (Williams) is at this week. But J-Mike (J. Michael Sturdivant) is definitely going to have a bigger role, for sure.”
Josh Jacobs’ NFL future remains in limbo. Green Bay’s running game without him is averaging 60.4 yards per game – almost 20 yards worse than any other team – and ranks 31st with 3.05 yards per carry.
Javon Hargrave was averaging 30 snaps per game as a valuable role player on the defensive line. Even while missing the Week 2 game, he led Green Bay’s defensive tackles in pressures and pass-rush win rate.
The Packers are down to five defensive tackles: Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks are the starters, Jonathan Ford is the nose tackle, Chris McClellan is a rookie and Anthony Campbell is a first-year player who made his NFL debut in Week 2 but suffered an ankle injury and hasn’t played since.
“We see who we have, we see who they have and see if we can put the pieces together,” defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon said on Tuesday. “But whoever’s up on gameday, I truly believe this, they have to play in some role for your team or why are you up on gameday? So, if they’re up, they’re going to be up and playing.”
The Packers have 28 players with average salaries of more than $2.0 million per season. They’re not big-ticket items, but cornerback Benjamin St-Juste ($4.9 million), receiver Skyy Moore ($2.5 million), running back Chris Brooks ($2.43 million), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper ($2.15 million) and tight end Luke Musgrave ($2.12 million) add another $14.1 million of average salary to the ledger.
Combined with the six expensive players listed above, those 11 players on the sideline have average salaries totaling $142.1 million. That’s 37.4 percent of the team total.
Not counting Hargrave, who remains on the 53-man roster, the Packers have almost $99 million of average salary on injury lists (injured reserve, physically unable to perform or non-football injury), according to OverTheCap.com . That’s $11 million more than the next team, Carolina, which the Packers will host in a few weeks. Their next two opponents are Dallas and Detroit, which have a combined $66.4 million on the shelf.
A formula at OverTheCap.com shows the Packers have the lowest contract utilization in the NFL, a byproduct of so many high-priced players being out of action.
“It truly is a next-man-up mentality and guys got to get ready to play,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday. “That’s just the nature of the beast and I think that’s one of the luxuries of having a 70-man roster. And we tell our players this all the time: Whether you’re on the active or you’re on the P-squad, you got to get ready to play.”

title: Packers Don’t Sign Short Cornerbacks, But They Just Did to Practice Squad
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have definite height requirements that they haven’t veered from in decades.
However, they did make a noteworthy exception to the rule by signing cornerback Elijah Culp to the practice squad following a Monday workout, a source confirmed what originally was reported by Easton Butler .
The Packers made it official on Tuesday afternoon and released guard Josh Gesky.
Culp ended his college career at James Madison. At pro day, he measured only 5-foot-9 3/4. That’s just fractionally taller than Ahmad Carroll, the Packers’ first-round pick in 2004. He was 5-foot-9 5/8. Carroll was a bust and the Packers haven’t taken another corner shorter than 5-foot-10 since.
What Culp lacks in height, he makes up for in speed with a 4.39-second time in the 40-yard dash and other physical attributes.
“I knew I had to run fast, man,” Culp said after pro day .
Short corners usually find a home as a nickel, and that is how Green Bay views him.
Culp is well-traveled. He opened his college career at Austin Peay in 2020 before transferring to Troy for 2021 and 2022. He transferred to Charlotte, where he redshirted in 2023 and started nine games in 2024.
At James Madison in 2025, he was third-team all-Sun Belt Conference with one interception and eight pass breakups in 13 starts. The interception came against Oregon in the College Football Playoffs.
PFF charged him with a 44.4 percent completion rate and only 9.9 yards per catch in 2025. That includes 1-of-2 for just 5 yards against Oregon and 1-of-5 for 7 yards in the opener against Louisville.
“I really like, honestly, his growth off the field at this point in time, even better than his growth on,” Dukes coach Bob Chesney said last season . “We knew what he could do on the field, but what he's doing off the field now and how he's growing into it, just a really good young man that's going to make a lot of people proud later in life when football is done.”
Culp, who was the No. 44 cornerback prospect in this year’s draft, according to The Athletic’s Dane Brugler, went undrafted and signed with the Cardinals, where he competed for a job in training camp. He recently served a stint on the Colts’ practice squad.
“My whole career I’ve been the underdog,” he told The Touchdown before the draft . “Even at high school, some of my coaches didn’t think I could make it – I was 5’7” back then, and so getting on the field was tough. But when I did get on, I brought that dog mentality, and they couldn’t take me off.
“So, really, I only started playing varsity in the 11th grade. And then by my junior year, I started to see the hard work pay off. It took some time to get there, but I reached the top. As a senior, I had 26 pass breakups. You just don’t see that. But my body grew as my game got better.”
That underdog mentality powered him through the draft process.
“That's my number one motivation,” Culp said at pro day . “Two is just like God gave me this blessing. I don't want to let him down. I'm grateful and I'm blessed for the opportunity. So that's why I wake up every day, even the days I don't want to.”
On the active roster, the Packers have starters Keisean Nixon and Brandon Cisse along with Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden. St-Juste dropped out of Sunday’s game against Chicago with a hamstring injury, meaning the team could be a man down at corner for this week’s game at Dallas. The only player on the practice squad is Domani Jackson, a sixth-round pick this year.
The Packers had a full practice squad so had to make another move. With the additions on the offensive line and with guards Jacob Monk and Aaron Banks returning to practice late last week, the team opted to release Josh Gesky, who signed with the Packers after going undrafted.
“Man, it would mean a lot,” to make it in the NFL, Culp told The Touchdown. “My family has been very supportive of me, helped me chase my dreams through four different schools. And reaching the NFL would change a lot of people’s lives, and it would definitely change ours.
“So I feel like everybody – me, my mom, pops, brothers – would all be very emotional when that call comes. They obviously know how much I’ve invested in this and I know what they’ve put in too. It would be a dream come true.”

title: Consensus NFL Power Rankings: After Stunning Fall, Stunning Rise for Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – How low could they go? And now, how high did they rise?
After a blowout loss to the Falcons and a lackluster win over the Buccaneers, the Green Bay Packers were 24th in l ast week’s Packers On SI Consensus NFL Power Rankings . However, their dominating win over the Bears on Sunday certainly changed the narrative.
First, what are the Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight of the best national power rankings and turn them into one better-than-the-best power ranking. Following a 31-7 win over Chicago, the Packers zoomed up all the way to 14th. That’s a 10-spot improvement based on one victory that seemed more in line with the preseason expectations.
Here are this week’s rankings, with more extensive analysis available by following the links.
Nobody moved the Packers up further than Mike Florio , who shot them up 12 spots from No. 23.
He liked Green Bay’s approach to the rivalry win: “When your adversary keeps talking, stay quiet and wait for your opportunity.”
The Packers rocketed up 10 spots from No. 22 in Conor Orr’s rankings.
“I get that I cannot, one week, punish the Steelers for what I considered a fluke victory over the Bengals (at the time) because Aaron Rodgers had too much time in the pocket, then vastly pump up the Packers for a deep aerial assault of the Bears, without drawing some ire,” he wrote. “The difference here is that Matt LaFleur has figured out how to run play action without a running game. And it’s leading to massive chunk plays.”
The Packers were the biggest movers in Pete Prisco’s rankings , leaping up 10 spots from No. 24.
“They were able to unleash Jordan Love against the Bears,” he wrote. “It needs to stay that way going forward. The deep passing game is their best option.”
The Packers zoomed up nine spots from No. 23 in the rankings selected by Josh Kendall and Chad Graff.
This week’s theme is who have they beaten. For Green Bay, it’s the woeful Jets, the Buccaneers with a backup quarterback and the Bears with a backup quarterback.
“The win over the Bears looks more impressive than it probably was considering the quarterback play Chicago got, but there’s no sense in apologizing for a win over a bitter rival that’s talking a lot of smack,” they wrote. “Jordan Love was exceptional Sunday, and Christian Watson looks like a true No. 1 wide receiver.”
The Packers shot up nine spots from 23rd in the rankings voted on by ESPN’s team beat writers.
This week’s theme is the biggest issue on defense. Rob Demovsky focused on the serious injuries to key players.
“In back-to-back weeks, the Packers lost linebacker Edgerrin Cooper and defensive tackle Javon Hargrave to season-ending Achilles injuries,” he wrote as part of a larger analysis. “Cooper was their best linebacker; Hargrave their most experienced defensive lineman. And who knows when edge rusher Micah Parsons will play?”
The Packers took the express lane up 11 spots in Nick Shook’s rankings, with the offense reaching Shook’s expectations.
As part of a longer writeup, Shook said: “Love delivered a fantastic performance, throwing for 367 yards and two majestic touchdowns to Christian Watson, demolishing a Bears team that couldn’t stop giving the ball to Green Bay’s suddenly feisty defense. Adding Micah Parsons into this equation soon makes the Packers one of the teams we must pay close attention to going forward.”
The Packers moved up six spots from No. 24 in Frank Schwab’s rankings.
“Through all the (justifiable) angst over the Packers' start, they're 3-2 coming off a blowout win over the Bears, who were the favorite to win the division,” Schwab wrote as part of a longer analysis.
“The Packers looked mostly poor during the first four weeks, but they find themselves in a good place now. There are things to clean up, but the trio of Jordan Love, Matthew Golden and Christian Watson might keep Green Bay in the playoff race.”
Ralph Vacchiano was the one writer who took a conservative approach. He inched the Packers up only three spots from No. 25 .
“The Packers' blowout win over the Bears was certainly out of nowhere, and probably some sweet revenge for Matt LaFleur’s team,” he wrote as part of a longer analysis. “The Packers still can’t really run the ball, and that’s going to hold them back. But Love and an improving defense have been enough to get them to 3-2. It doesn’t look pretty, but they have a chance to stay on their offensive roll with the Cowboys, Lions and Panthers up next.
The Cowboys are 20th in our rankings following an upset loss to the Buccaneers last week. They ranged from 15th to 23rd, including No. 21 at Fox Sports, where Ralph Vacchiano has them one spot behind Green Bay.
“I’m sure there have been worse losses in recent Cowboys' history than their Thursday night debacle at home against the winless Buccaneers, but I can’t think of any right now,” he wrote. “It’s pretty clear by now that Jerry Jones’ weird rebuilding of his defense created something worse. But where has the offense gone?”
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide another perspective. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1 but have been in retreat. They fell to +3000 before facing the Jets and +3300 before hosting the Falcons but crashed to +6000 after losing to the Falcons. They stayed at +6000 after winning at Tampa Bay and briefly moved to +5000 after beating the Bears but are back at +6000.
In NFC North Super Bowl odds, the Bears are +1700, the Lions are +2200 and the Vikings are +2200. The Bears’ odds actually improved after losing to Green Bay; they had been +2000.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds (-112), fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, and are now 11th at +184. Among the division teams, the Vikings are -370, the Lions are -178 and the Bears are -146.
Quarterback Jordan Love opened at +2200 to win NFL MVP and remained there entering the Atlanta game. He plunged to +10000 but rebounded to +7500 after his powerhouse showing against Chicago.
At DraftKings, the NFC North championship odds still have the Vikings at the front and the Packers at the rear. The Vikings are a strong favorite at +100, followed by the Lions at +300, the Bears at +360 and the Packers at +730. Green Bay was +990 at this time last week. By implied probability, the Packers went from a 9.2 percent chance of winning the North to 12.1 percent.
