title: Packers-Cowboys Matchups: Green Bay Has Only One Advantage (But It’s Huge)
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers are riding high after a 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears, and will now move to their second of four consecutive games against teams that hope to be in the NFC playoff picture by the end of the season.
The Dallas Cowboys are coming to Lambeau Field for a Sunday night matchup, and they’ll be on extended rest after losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Thursday night.
Can the Packers string together some success, improve to 4-2 and get their season fully on track after it looked destined to be headed off the rails through the first month of the season?
Here are the matchups that will determine whether they do or not.
Jonathan Gannon and Dak Prescott are familiar with each other. Gannon was the defensive coordinator for the Philadelphia Eagles in 2022 and faced Prescott once during that season. Prescott threw for 347 yards, three touchdowns and led the Cowboys to 40 points against an Eagles team that fell just short of a Super Bowl.
They faced off when Gannon was the head coach in Arizona in 2023. Prescott threw for 249 yards, one touchdown and one interception while only being able to muster 16 points. Last year, Gannon held the Cowboys’ offense down again, allowing just 17 points.
Of course, the personnel is drastically different. Green Bay’s defense was dominant against Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum on Sunday. Yes, those are backup quarterbacks, but the Packers have struggled against Tommy DeVito in the not-so-distant past.
This week is a much more difficult challenge. The Cowboys are loaded with talent on offense, especially at receiver. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are arguably the top receiver duo in the NFL. The Packers’ secondary has been a potential sore spot during the season, but they have not really been tested by a top-tier receiver since facing Justin Jefferson in Minnesota the first week of the season.
Can the pass rush, which had four sacks on Sunday, make Prescott uncomfortable without Micah Parsons on the field? Last year, the answer was no. The Packers sacked Prescott once as he put up 40 points on Green Bay’s defense.
This is the matchup that will decide the game on Sunday. One potential key to watch is Prescott’s propensity to make some mistakes. The Packers are coming off a game in which they had five takeaways, including three interceptions. In a game that could be a shootout, takeaways could decide the game.
Much like the passing defense is coming off its best game of the season, Green Bay’s run defense was excellent against Chicago. Some of that was due to game flow, with the Bears chasing a two-score deficit for most of the game. Some of that was also due to the absence of Kyle Monangai, who is Chicago’s most violent runner.
Still, they held D’Andre Swift to 43 yards on nine carries. They held the Bears to 81 rushing yards, which was more than 100 yards less than their season average and by far their lowest total of the season.
Dallas averages just 3.8 yards per carry. The question for the Packers is how much will the absence of Javon Hargrave affect their run defense. Hargrave’s injury likely bumps rookie Chris McClellan into an even bigger role. Plus, first-year player Anthony Campbell will have to rebound quickly after missing the last three games with an ankle injury. Are either ready?
They’ll face an offensive line that is big and got a boost last week with the return of Pro Bowl guard Tyler Smith. Perhaps that will kickstart a ground game led by Javonte Williams. Overall, the Packers are riding higher coming into the game, but the unknowns on both sides make this too tough to call.
Dallas made some significant changes after their defense was one of the worst in football in 2025. Christian Parker was named defensive coordinator, Caleb Downs was drafted in the first round, and they did some work on their defensive line, including trading for former Packers edge Rashan Gary.
Through five games, Gary has 15 pressures and one sack. That appears to be another trade with the Cowboys that the Packers won.
Dallas’ defense is putrid. It’s ranked 30th in passing yards allowed per play and are last with an opponent passer rating of 120.5. They have zero interceptions and are 29th in sack percentage.
Conversely, Jordan Love is coming off his best game of the season. His reconfigured offensive line has afforded him much better protection than the one that stood in front of him for the first three weeks.
Green Bay’s offense tore apart the Chicago defense. Love completed 25 of his 31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns. He had as many completions on passes thrown 20-plus yards downfield as total incompletions. Both of his top receivers went for over 120 yards and Tucker Kraft looked as good as he has all season.
“Obviously, we’re always trying to get our playmakers the ball and those two guys are our best playmakers in that room right now,” coach Matt LaFleur said of Christian Watson and Matthew Golden’s combined 266 receiving yards vs. Chicago.
Sunday could mark the debut for Kevin Zeitler at right guard, although Travis Glover has played well since earning the starting job for the last two games.
Either way, there appears to be some stability up front for the Packers. Love is comfortable in the pocket – and a comfortable Love is not a sight a lot of defenses want to see. A bad defense definitely does not want to see that.
The stoppable force meets the movable object.
That’s not a joke, these teams are both ranked last in the NFL in this phase of the game. The Cowboys gave up 241 rushing yards against Tampa Bay. With Kenny Clark in the middle of the defensive line, they are last with 168.4 rushing yards allowed per game – 12 yards worse than any other team – and 29th with 5.10 yards allowed per attempt.
The Packers’ run game is so bad that we’re calling a game in which MarShawn Lloyd ran for 31 yards on 10 carries a step in the right direction.
It’s true. Lloyd looked more comfortable as a runner than he has during his career. He found the end zone twice, including running over Jaylon Johnson en route to his first score of the game. Is this the week the Packers’ ground game finds some traction?
It’s hard to say, but if there were ever a team to find some room to rumble against, it’d be the Dallas Cowboys.
Dallas’ special teams has one of the top kickers in football with kicker Brandon Aubrey, who is in scoring position as soon as the ball crosses the 50-yard line. He has struggled more than he usually does this year, as he’s 9-of-12 on field goals.
Their return game is led by KaVontae Turpin, who has some juice and is able to take the ball the distance. He did struggle last week against the Buccaneers with a costly fumble that resulted in points for the Bucs.
Green Bay’s special teams have been solid if unspectacular. The emergence of Trey Smack as a weapon at kicker and Skyy Moore providing competence in the return game has given them a baseline of at least average play.
Moore did leave Sunday’s game with an ankle injury, and Matthew Golden replaced him as a punt returner. That’s a situation worth monitoring this week, though coach Matt LaFleur said there was short-term concern for Moore – meaning it’s more likely that not that he will miss this game. Golden did have a nice debut with a 17-yard return late in the first half, when he looked more comfortable returning punts than he did all of last season or in training camp this summer.
Smack missed two field goals and one extra point after having a total of two missed kicks (one extra point and one field goal that was blocked) the first four games. Smack’s accuracy is something to watch this weekend.
“We’ve got a ton of confidence in him, and I think he’s built the right way in terms of his mindset,” LaFleur said on Monday. “I think you’ll see a guy that’s pretty determined. I don’t think he’ll be shaken up by that at all.”

title: Playoffs? After Terrible Start, Here’s Where Packers Stand in NFC Playoff Race
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL when they were booed off the field in their loss to the Atlanta Falcons two weeks ago. Their victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers didn’t exactly create more confidence in their playoff viability.
So, what a difference one game can make. The Packers blasted the Chicago Bears on Sunday. For all of the stupid penalties and sloppy play, they have a 3-2 record. If the season were to end today – with 12 games remaining, the season, obviously, is a lot closer to the starting line than the finish line – the Packers would be in a familiar place.
The Packers are in fifth place in the latest NFC playoff standings. That’s the No. 1 spot among the wild-card teams.
2. San Francisco 49ers: 5-0
11. Philadelphia Eagles: 2-3
13. Washington Commanders: 1-3-1
14. Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 1-4
15. New Orleans Saints: 1-4
16. Arizona Cardinals: 1-4
Again, there’s a lot of season to be played, so Green Bay’s win over Chicago is carrying most of the weight in the playoff standings. The Packers, Lions, Bears and Seahawks are in fifth through eighth place in the NFC, respectively, with 3-2 records.
Seattle has the worst conference record among those teams so is eighth. That leaves the NFC North teams jockeying for position. In the division-games tiebreaker, Green Bay, which is 1-1 against NFC North foes, has more wins than Detroit (0-0) and Chicago (0-2).
The point here is that the Packers, for everything they did wrong during the first quarter of the season, are right where they need to be. The key for this opening stretch of games has been to stay afloat until Micah Parsons returns on defense and Josh Jacobs (potentially) returns on offense.
So far, it’s mission accomplished. But one game can’t be just one game. It must be the starting point.
“Man, it’s stacking,” quarterback Jordan Love said after the game. “You’ve just got to keep stacking stuff. Great win today but it’s all about how we get back to the film room, continue to build on this performance, continue to build on the plays we did well, cleaning up some of the stuff we didn’t do as well, and just attacking it.
“It’s going to be a new opponent next week, a new defense, so we’ve got to keep building on this. It feels good when everybody’s clicking and making plays. It’s something that we’ve got to keep it rolling.”
Of the eight teams with winning records, the Packers are the only team with a negative scoring differential.
Going in the order of the playoff standings, the Vikings are plus-45, the 49ers are plus-61, the Giants are plus-3, the Panthers are plus-12, the Packers are minus-8, the Lions are plus-16, the Bears are plus-23 and the Seahawks are plus-29.
Green Bay’s three wins have come against teams with a combined six wins, giving it a strength of victory of.400. That doesn’t seem too good, but the Vikings’ five wins have come against teams with eight victories and Detroit’s three wins have come against teams with four victories.
“There was a whole lot on display out there today,” receiver Christian Watson said after a dominant performance. “The defense came out to play. They put us in the best possible position, getting the ball back for us, what, five times? We can’t ask for much more from the defense. Obviously, we were able to put some points out there on offense, make plays when our numbers are called. That was big-time.
“I think that we all knew what we were capable of. We’ve got to just find a way to consistently be that, consistently be even better than that to obviously achieve the goals we want to achieve. That’s the team that we are.”
Five games, obviously, is a small sample size. But it’s not so small that remaining strength of schedule is irrelevant.
According to Tankathon , the Packers’ final 12 opponents have a combined winning percentage of .492. That’s in a six-way tie for 18th.
The Vikings have the toughest remaining schedule in the NFL, with their remaining opponents having a .568 winning percentage. The Bears are seventh at .533 and the Lions are ninth at .525.
After a soft open to the schedule, the Packers scored a big win over Chicago in their first big test on Sunday. They will host the Dallas Cowboys (2-3) on Sunday night, play at the Lions (3-2) the following Sunday and then host the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers (2-2) on Thursday night.
Then, it’s a trip to New England to face the Patriots (3-2) and a home game against the first-place Vikings (5-0) before the pseudo bye week preceding the Wednesday night game at the Los Angeles Rams (2-3).
“I think just keeping the main thing the main thing,” safety Xavier McKinney said after the game. “Obviously, every week we want to go in and be 1-0. I think that we did a great job throughout the whole week of keeping the main thing the main thing.
“Having that urgency, having that mindset of going in and not really worrying about really the opponent but worrying about what we’re doing internally and figuring out how we can go out there and execute the play as given to us. I think that’s what we did this week and it was able to show today.”

title: Packers Injury Updates, Including Micah Parsons and Perplexing Achilles Tears
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers don’t practice by a power substation, but they are in the general vicinity of paper plants and an animal-rendering facility.
Whatever the reason, the Packers continue to get hit by big injuries. The latest was defensive tackle Javon Hargrave suffering a torn Achilles toward the end of Sunday’s win over the Bears. That injury was especially deflating to coach Matt LaFleur after the game.
Deflated Matt LaFleur’s opening statement. pic.twitter.com/q649Vz6EoH
It was the second season-ending Achilles injury in as many weeks, with Hargrave’s coming on the heels of star linebacker Edgerrin Cooper’s last week.
“I think it’s a fluky deal,” LaFleur said on Monday, “but, once you go through this, you always are looking back at everything you do and trying to figure out why certain things happen.
“It was definitely unfortunate. I know it took a lot of wind out of my sails last night after the game when you have a devastating injury like to anybody, let alone to a guy that has come in here and done things the right way and been a real asset to our football team.”
According to data from a few years ago , there are an average of about 20 Achilles tears per season since the NFL moved to a 17-game schedule. That includes training camp, preseason and regular season.
The Packers have had two this season. Plus, tight end John FitzPatrick and defensive tackle Jordon Riley sustained Achilles injuries in Week 16 and Week 17 of last season, respectively. So, the Packers are clear outliers on the spectrum with a perplexing four Achilles tears in their last nine games.
“Unfortunate,” LaFleur said.
Asked if there’s time during the season to dive into the search for reasons or if that’s an offseason project for the medical staff, LaFleur said:
“I hope everybody’s diving in and, if people have solutions into how do you avoid that, we’ll listen. If we have to adjust things from a practice standpoint and whatnot or a training standpoint, we’ll definitely listen to that.”
Micah Parsons will not practice this week, meaning he will not get to play against his former team, the Cowboys, on Sunday night at Lambeau Field.
His brother, who knows as much about Parsons’ comeback as anyone, said his “best bet” would be the Week 10 home game against Minnesota or the Week 12 game at the Rams. (The Packers have a short Week 11 bye before facing the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve).
Your best bet would prolly be Minnesota or the rams
“As soon as they give us the green light, he’ll be out there,” LaFleur said. “That hasn’t happened yet, but I think we’re getting closer.”
After this week’s game against Dallas, the Packers will play at Detroit. LaFleur was asked if playing on Ford Field’s artificial surface would preclude him from returning for that game.
LaFleur said, no, it wouldn’t. Rather, the short timeframe between now and facing the Lions would be the predictable obstacle.
“First of all, you’ve got to get him back on the practice field,” he said. “There’s a lot of testing that goes on before he gets medically cleared to get out there, and then I’m sure we’re going to want to give him some time to get back to playing football. As you see with most guys that are coming off a major injury, it takes a little bit of time.”
At the end of training camp, general manager Brian Gutekunst said he thought Parsons might be close to returning after the four-week PUP window.
That, obviously, is not going to be the case. Did something change?
“I think we were all hopeful,” LaFleur said. “He’s a physical specimen, he’s a creature of nature for sure and, sometimes, you’ve got to make sure that your body is [fully ready]. You don’t want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg.”
The Packers’ depth at defensive tackle has evaporated in a hurry.
Warren Brinson started the season on the sideline due to a calf injury. In his first practice a couple weeks ago, he suffered a groin injury and was placed on injured reserve. And now, Javon Hargrave will miss the rest of the season.
That leaves the Packers with five defensive tackles: starters Devonte Wyatt and Karl Brooks, nose tackle Jonathan Ford, rookie Chris McClellan and first-year player Anthony Campbell. Campbell suffered an ankle injury in his NFL debut against the Jets and has been inactive for the last three games.
“Well, hopefully, we’ll get Campbell rolling this week, but it truly is a next-man-up mentality and guys got to get ready to play,” LaFleur said. “That’s just the nature of the beast and I think that’s one of the luxuries of having a 70-man roster.
“We tell our players this all the time, whether you’re on the active or you’re on the P-squad, you got to get ready to play. For those that we anticipate playing in the game that are up on gameday, we’ll make sure that they get the adequate amount of reps.”
David Blay, an undrafted rookie, is the only defensive tackle on the practice squad. The aforementioned Jordon Riley is on PUP following last year’s torn Achilles. He’s “pretty close” to returning to practice but, like Parsons, he’s going to need practice time to get ready to play in a game.
Finally, the depth at receiver has eroded, as well. Jayden Reed suffered a season-ending neck injury against the Jets in Week 2 and his backup, Skyy Moore, suffered an ankle injury early against Chicago.
“I would say in the short term, there's a little bit of concern, but nothing like too long term,” LaFleur said.
Savion Williams, who opened the season on injured reserve, was designated for return last week and was limited participation at all three practices but was not added to the roster.
“He's definitely getting closer,” LaFleur said. “I'm hopeful that we can get him there, but we'll kind of work through the week and see where he's at.”
The Packers have three receivers on the practice squad, including Isaiah Neyor, who has been with the team since August 2025.

title: Texans Injury Report: 4 Players Miss Practice Before Jaguars London Trip
full_text:
The Houston Texans have released their first injury report heading into their Week 6 matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars following their Wednesday practice.
And in all, four players wound up not participating, while a few others found their way onto the injury report as either a limited or full participant.
Let's take a look at the latest on the Texans' injury report from Wednesday's practice, and sort through what it all could mean for this weekend's game as the team travels overseas to London.
LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) S Jalen Pitre (shoulder) RB David Montgomery (groin) OT Trent Brown (knee)
WR Nico Collins (rest) CB Jamarcus Ingram (elbow) LB Henry To'oTo'o (shoulder) DE Will Anderson (rest) TE Dalton Schultz (rest) DE Jadeveon Clowney (knee) DE Logan Hall (rest)
WR Tank Dell (knee) LB Wade Woodaz (thumb)
Two of the non-participants from the Texans' Wednesday practice were to be expected: that's running back David Montgomery, who's dealing with a groin injury, as well as defensive back Jalen Pitre, who suffered an AC joint sprain during last weekend's game against the Tennessee Titans. As of now, their status is considered week-to-week, meaning there's a good chance that both could be sidelined for Week 6 against the Jaguars, yet might not have to be forced on injured reserve, which would take them out for a minimum of four weeks.
The two other DNPs from the Texans' practice— linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair and Trent Brown— have both been dealing with some nagging injuries through the past couple of weeks that effectively left them to sit out of Wednesday's practice. However, considering both played in last week's game against the Titans while dealing with their respective injuries, it'd be fair to assume that both are still on track to play in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
The Texans officially activated the 21-day return window for Henry To'oTo'o on Wednesday, who's been sidelined for the past four weeks due to a shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1 against the Buffalo Bills. A limited participation in practice is a great sign that his return is right around the corner. However, he might still be ruled inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars if unable to complete a full practice. If that's the case, Jake Hansen will remain Houston's fill in as their WLB.
Another aspect of the Texans' injury report that can't go unnoticed: wide receiver Tank Dell has participated in his first full practice since being designated to return from his knee injury suffered back in 2024. That means, if all goes smoothly over the coming days, there's a chance that Dell could make his long-awaited return to the lineup in Week 6. But until the Texans officially activate him from injured reserve , we won't know for sure about when he'll officially be good to be elevated on the gameday roster.

title: 4 Noteworthy Quotes From Marvin Harrison Jr.'s First Texans Presser
full_text:
The Houston Texans finally got Marvin Harrison Jr. in the building for his first practice with the team on Wednesday, only a few days out from his first game in uniform against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 6.
And after that Texans' practice, Harrison Jr. was able to speak to the media for the first time since the deal to ship him out from the Arizona Cardinals went down earlier this weekend.
Let's sort through four of the more notable points to come out of Harrison Jr.'s first presser as a part of the Texans:
One thing Texans fans will notice pretty quickly about Harrison Jr. is that he's a pretty reserved personality.
However, even while not your typical alpha, outspoken NFL wide receiver, he made sure to express the excitement he has in store with his new situation, along with pairing up next to his college quarterback in C.J. Stroud .
"I'm excited to be here," Harrison Jr said. "I'm excited to help this team win games. I'm excited to be with C.J. again, and help C.J. to the best of my abilities."
"Always watched the Texans from afar. Obviously, just watching C.J. So, it's pretty surreal to be able to play with him now again, and just help him out the best I can."
As for Harrison's biggest goals for both now and the future, he kept things pretty simple:
"Help the team win. Period."
While the process for Harrison Jr.'s move out of Arizona was a bit different than your typical trade, it seems Harrison Jr. himself found out Houston was his ultimate destination a little bit before the entire world did–– or at least until DeMeco Ryans made it clear during his post-game presser after beating the Tennessee Titans.
"My agent told me, obviously, before the news broke to you guys," Harrison Jr. said of how he found out about the trade to Houston. "DeMeco kind of did his thing as well. But, yeah, before that."
As to whether or not Houston was the place he wanted to be, he set the record straight that he really had no control over where he would be headed after the Cardinals.
"When you get traded, you don't really have that option, you know?"
Harrison Jr. was also asked about how he felt about some viral clips circling around social media showcasing some of his routes run during his time with the Cardinals: some of which might've not looked the most polished or with 110% effort that you'd expect.
look at the effort on this route from Marvin Harrison Jr. on 2nd and 6 pic.twitter.com/xu6jK6VJwe
However, Harrison Jr. simply brushed off those types of comments or concerns. Simply put, everybody has their own opinion, and he knows the player and person he can be.
"I mean, everybody has their own opinions," Harrison Jr. said. "That's really the best way I can put that. Everybody has their own opinions and what they're going to gather from information."
"I know who I am as a player. I know who I am as a person. However people want to label me or think of me, that's their opinion."
Harrison Jr.'s first team session in the Texans' facility on Wednesday also meant he was able to be coached up by DeMeco Ryans for the first time .
And based on first impressions, Harrison Jr. had one clear takeaway on what Ryan’s brings to the table: energy.
"Energy, man. Energy. That's one thing you can always pinpoint, especially with a defensive guy," Harrison Jr. on what he's noticed about DeMeco Ryans. "They always want to bring the energy. You can kind of see that throughout the whole team, and the energy he brings day in and day out."

title: Texans Make Marvin Harrison Jr. Plans Clear for Week 6 vs. Jaguars
full_text:
The Houston Texans finally got their new wide receiver addition Marvin Harrison Jr. in the building for his first team practice on Wednesday, coming just a day before the team is set to take the flight overseason to face off against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London for Week 6 .
And it seems like for the Texans, they won't be waiting long at all before they're able to see their new trade acquisition on the field for a regular season game.
Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans spoke to the media after Wednesday's team practice, where he was asked about what Harrison Jr.'s availability would look like for the week ahead. Ryans noted that the team will be playing their new wide receiver in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said newly-acquired WR Marvin Harrison Jr. will make his Houston debut Sunday in London vs. the Jaguars. pic.twitter.com/qfcrSg3SWC
It's a quick turnaround for the Texans' new wideout after being less than a week removed from his time with the Arizona Cardinals .
In just a week's time, Harrison Jr. was notified he'd be traded from the Cardinals, was deemed inactive for Week 5 against the Detroit Lions, saw the trade go down on Sunday afternoon , and he's now seemingly ready to go for his first game with Houston––albeit a little far away from home in London.
As to how much the Texans wind up utilizing Harrison Jr. in his first game with the team? To this point, that remains a bit of a mystery.
There remains a chance that while the 24-year-old will be active and on the field for Week 6 against the Jaguars, he might not be a true featured part of the game plan until closer to the second half of the season.
However, from the initial signs that the Texans and DeMeco Ryans have seen from their new pass-catcher at Wednesday's practice, he appears to be pretty confident that Harrison Jr. has caught onto his new system and situation quite well.
"I thought Marvin did a really good job today getting acclimated," Ryans said of Harrison Jr.'s first Texans practice.
"Coaches have done a great job in the background, just really working with him, getting him caught up to speed on our plays, the verbiage of what we're doing. He got in, ran some plays today, did a good job."
Harrison Jr. also seemed to take it upon himself to get further adjusted with the Texans' offense a little earlier upon his arrival this week.
Ryans explained that Harrison Jr. had come into the Texans' facility for individual work during his first night in town with assistant wide receivers coach Tiquan Underwood, thus allowing him and his acclimation process to get a day ahead of schedule.
"Getting a player caught up, it isn't hard when the player is attentive and he's locked in on getting the details down. So Marvin's first night here, he was with our assistant wide receiver coach, Coach Tiquan [Underwood], and they were grinding," Ryans said of how Harrison Jr. is adjusting.
"They were working late at night. They were in the playbook, grinding, and that allowed him to get a day ahead. Now, he was able to go out there today and just fit right in seamlessly. So, when you put the work in and you're dialed in, you can make it work."
Now, that urgency and hard work to get on the same page as this Texans' offense early seems to already be paying off for Harrison Jr.
He'll be on the field this weekend against the Jaguars in a brand-new uniform, catching passes from his college teammate C.J. Stroud , and might end up being a key part of the Texans' offensive game plan a bit earlier than expected if he's able to keep up at this pace.

title: Texans' Braden Smith Return Creates Intriguing O-Line Dilemma
full_text:
The Houston Texans are getting some reinforcements on their offensive line this week.
According to an announcement from the Texans, the team is officially activating veteran offensive tackle Braden Smith from injured reserve.
We have activated Braden Smith from the Reserve/Injured list and made other roster moves. pic.twitter.com/iGGwgOV2QE
Smith––one of the Texans' big offensive line additions from this offseason–– has been stuck on the injured reserve list since the start of the 2026 season due to a foot injury he suffered back in August.
The Texans officially activated his 21-day return window for the Wednesday practice before their matchup against the Tennessee Titans, yet felt it would be better to let him rest once more before officially elevating him to the active roster.
Fast forward to their preparation for Week 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, and now, Smith is ready to get back in the lineup. And that's good news for the Texans' offensive line: their big $20 million investment from this offseason will finally be able to suit up for a regular season game.
But the Texans have a decision on their hands as it relates to slotting Smith into their offense: is he going to be starting right off the bat, or will they continue to roll with Trent Brown, who's been Houston's right tackle for the first five weeks of the season.
Heading into the 2026 season, the general consensus remained that Smith could have the edge over Brown when it comes to their starting right tackle spot.
After all, the Texans made sure to invest a steep $20 million in his services via free agency just a few months ago with the intent of him being an upgrade upfront.
But Brown had an appealing case himself entering this season: he started the second half of the 2025 season, where he helped the Texans rattle off a perfect 8-0 record, then a Wild Card win against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
So if Houston was confident in Smith's ability, and he performed well in preseason and training camp, keeping him at that right tackle spot isn't a wild idea even if Smith were healthy. With him being placed on injured reserve, though, the Texans essentially had their right tackle decision made for them.
Now though, the Texans have a decision on their hands. Brown, through the first five games of the season, hasn't been the most exemplary tackle: playing 335 snaps to record six penalties, 13 pressures, two sacks, and one QB hit.
The Texans, if they felt there was an ability to improve at their tackle spot opposite Aireontae Ersery, have a clear opportunity to shift things around for Week 6. Smith is healthy, practicing in full a few days out from their trip to London, and should be ready to take on those starting duties if Houston's staff entrusts him with that spot.
Time will tell if the Texans decide to make a pivot within their offensive line unit. So far into the 2026 season, Houston hasn't forced a change upfront unless the move was in the event of injury.
And after finally rattling off a win in Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans in dominant fashion, perhaps a big offensive line change isn't on the radar for Houston.
However, if the Texans' offensive line has a route to perform better than they have through the first quarter of this regular season––and so far, it hasn't exactly been a top unit in the league––it’s something the Houston brass should at least consider.

title: Texans Injury Update Hints Key Defensive Starter Is Nearing a Return
full_text:
Through the first five weeks of regular season action, the Houston Texans have faced a handful of noteworthy injuries on both sides of the ball to leave them a bit depleted in one way or another.
On the offensive end, we've seen the likes of Nico Collins, Ed Ingram, and most recently, David Montgomery due to miss some time. Defensively, Jadeveon Clowney, Kayden McDonald, and now Jalen Pitre have been struck by the injury bug as well .
However, in the case of one recently-injured name on the defensive side, there's a good chance his return to the field sits right around the corner: that's starting linebacker Henry To'oTo'o .
Texans general manager Nick Caserio r ecently had an interview with 95.7 The Fan before the team's Wednesday practice where he noted that To'oTo'o will have his 21-day practice window activated from injured reserve.
To'oTo'o has been out of the Texans' lineup since he went down with a shoulder injury in their Week 1 game against the Buffalo Bills. That injury would end up shifting him to the injured reserve for at least four weeks, and leave him sidelined until Week 6, at a minimum.
And upon the announcement of the injury when it first happened, there was an expectation that To'oTo'o could be out longer than that four-week stretch on injured reserve. KPRC2 's Aaron Wilson had reported the issue could take "a few months" to fully recover from.
But with the news surrounding his practice window now opening, there's a good chance we'll be able to see To'oTo'o on the field sooner than that expected timeline.
To'oTo'o has remained a key fixture of the Texans' linebacker room when healthy, starting a total of 36 games throughout his four years in the building.
Throughout the 2025 season, To'oTo'o put together a solid season, recording 95 tackles, nine TFLs, 2.5 sacks, and four passes defended. That year was able to net him a two-year extension before the 2026 campaign started, and will keep him in the mix until 2028.
The Texans activating To'oTo'o's practice window doesn't mean he's set to return this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It only means that the veteran linebacker is one step closer to his return to the field, which is due to be at some point over the next three games.
After the Texans' Week 6 date against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London , they head back home for Week 7 against the New York Giants, then have a bye in Week 8 before facing the LA Chargers on the road right after.
Any of those games are technically in play for To'oTo'o to be activated for, depending on how well he does in practice across the next 21 days. If he's able to practice in full for consecutive days, then that could be a hint that his return is pretty imminent.
However, based on the placement of the Texans' bye week, there's a good chance that Houston opts to keep him sidelined for the next two weeks, ensuring he's 100% with a full week of rest during the bye, to then get him ready to go against the Chargers in Week 9.
Regardless, how he performs in practice, and the capacity that he's able to participate in, will be a huge indicator of what to expect for his timeline to get back on the field.
But overall, things seem to be trending in the right direction to see To'oTo'o back out there next to Azeez Al-Shaair as Houston's starting weak-side linebacker in the near future.

title: Texans GM Explains Weeks of Work Behind Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
full_text:
The Houston Texans added a new big name to their wide receiver room over the weekend by adding 2024 No. 4 pick Marvin Harrison via trade with the Arizona Cardinals; ultimately acquiring him and a sixth-round pick in exchange for a second- and seventh-round pick .
And it's a deal for the Texans that's not only significant when diving into what Harrison Jr. could bring to this offense, but the move is seemingly one that's been in the works for some time now–– according to general manager Nick Caserio.
During an interview with Seth Payne and Sean Pendergast on 95.7 The Fan , Caserio broke down what the process looked like when it came to making the move for Harrison Jr. with the Cardinals and their general manager, Monti Ossenfort.
And per Caserio, the two had discussed the move for "a few weeks," and had even agreed to the deal on Friday night, even if initial reports didn't describe things that way.
"We had talked for a few weeks, and then the deal– he and I agreed to the deal Friday night," Caserio said of the Harrison Jr. trade. "Like, the deal was basically done Friday night. We kind of had an agreement in place. I gave him my word, he gave me his word."
"That's how you do business, that's how [Monti Ossenfort] and I do business. But he wanted to handle it a certain way as it pertains to the communication. and some of the other things. So, we certainly didn't have a problem with that at all. We kind of followed his lead there a little bit. I think he communicated with Marvin that he was going to be an active Saturday morning."
#Texans GM Nick Caserio told us how he and Cardinals GM Monte Ossenfort closed the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade. Caserio says the deal was basically done on Friday night and the outcome of the Titans game had no impact on the consummation of the trade. pic.twitter.com/KGe6d2ri5L
So instead of the move being announced a couple of days before Week 5's game for both Arizona and Houston, the two hashed out the agreement, Harrison Jr. was inactive, then got to Sunday afternoon where Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans broke the trade news during his post-game presser.
A common theory that had surfaced surrounding the Texans' negotiations for Harrison Jr. was that Houston had to win their Week 5 game against the Tennessee Titans for the trade to be deemed official.
Caserio, though, explains that wasn't quite the case.
"And so, the trade was done Friday night. We had agreed to the parameters. There was a few things that we had to finalize and work out," Caserio continued. "So what happened in a game had absolutely zero bearing on whether or not we were going to consummate the transaction."
"We're not going to agree to something, and then see what happens in the game, and then back out of it. Like, we're not gonna do that. I don't operate that way. Like, we're not going to operate that way.
Overall, a bit of an unorthodox procedure when it comes to an NFL trade, and one that took a bit longer to develop, all things considered. But in the end, the Texans and Cardinals both checked the boxes they needed to make the trade come to fruition.
The Texans had their eyes on Harrison Jr. and his situation for weeks , and were willing to pay the desired cost to get him on their roster. The Cardinals wanted a second-round pick in exchange for their top-five pick from 2024, and managed to do exactly that. A job well done for both sides.

title: Jalen Pitre Injury Update: Texans DB Could Have Caught a Big Break
full_text:
We now know a bit more about the injury that Houston Texans defensive back Jalen Pitre suffered in Week 5's road trip against the Tennessee Titans.
And it seems like, while there is a chance that Pitre misses some time, the Texans avoided any worst-case scenario surrounding the health of their star defender.
According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero of The Ringer , Pitre has suffered an AC joint sprain in his shoulder that leaves his status as week-to-week.
Texans DB Jalen Pitre suffered an AC joint sprain Sunday and is considered week-to-week, per source. Good news overall for one of Houston's standouts, who avoided a major injury.
Pitre first went down with the shoulder injury during the second half of action in the Texans' Week 5 matchup against the Titans. Pitre would inevitably end up not returning to the action, and head coach DeMeco Ryans had noted that the team was still evaluating his status moving forward.
And now, with a bit more clarity on the severity of Pitre's shoulder issue, it does seem to hint towards a possible absence for him in their upcoming Week 6 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
However, without any expectation of a lengthy recovery, or any signs of short-term injured reserve being in play, it's great news for the Texans to hear.
Pitre has long been an integral piece of the Texans' defense as a versatile nickel/safety. He's been on the field for over 90% of Houston's defensive snaps this season as a fifth defensive back to play alongside Houston's strong corner and safety unit.
In the five games that Pitre has played this season, he's put together 24 combined tackles, one tackle for loss, five passes defended, and a forced fumble; really making an impact all over the defensive side as he has since emerging as a full-time starter in his rookie season back in 2022.
The Texans may have to do without his services for a game or two this season––which they had to also navigate in 2025 when Pitre missed three games with a concussion––but a week-to-week status might be the best-case scenario, considering the uncertainty that was surrounding his health after Week 5.
While the length of Pitre's injury absence is far from confirmed, there's a good chance that the Texans end up being without him for just two weeks, simply because of the placement of their bye in Week 8.
Houston could take their trip overseas against the Jaguars in Week 6 , then travel home to face the New York Giants in Week 7 without Pitre, then allow their star defender an extra week of rest before they're back in action in Week 9 against the LA Chargers.
For however long that Pitre does remain out, it feels like a safe bet that fifth-round rookie Kamari Ramsey will be the one called up to take his reps as a similarly versatile contributor at nickel and safety.
Ramsey is one of the few names on the Texans' roster with experience playing both at safety and nickel during his time in college at USC, and already managed to get snaps his way in place of Pitre when he went out in Week 5 against the Titans.
So far this season, Ramsey has played in 40 defensive snaps for the Texans, where he's recorded six tackles and one tackle for loss. If Houston's coaching staff trusts their rookie to claim Pitre's snaps for the time that he's out, Week 6 can be a massive opportunity to see those numbers jump across the board.
The Texans will have a couple of practices at their disposal before traveling to London this week to plan out their defensive plans more in depth without Pitre for Week 6. However, knowing that their star defender won't be sidelined for an extremely long period of time is great news for all involved in Houston.

title: Texans Week 6 Consensus Power Rankings: How Win No. 1 Changes Things
full_text:
The Houston Texans finally got their long-awaited first win of the 2026 season down in the books following their dominant 26-3 victory over their division rival, the Tennessee Titans, in Week 5 .
And because of that win, the general consensus surrounding the Texans seems to have taken a slight boost compared to where things stood this time last week. Back then, Houston was still at a winless 0-4, both sides of the ball had some glaring issues, and led to many selling their stock on this group .
Now, the Texans certainly might not have those same issues fixed by now––even after their recent trade to acquire Marvin Harrison Jr.––but they are in a bit of a better spot than they were previously now that they have what hopes to be their first win of many.
With that in mind, let's sort through a new batch of consensus power rankings to see just where the Texans stack up as they roll into Week 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London .
Sports Illustrated's Conor Orr has the Texans at their highest spot in these consensus rankings by far. Spoiler alert: everyone else we have listed has Houston outside of their top 20 teams, while Orr is able to find them a spot in the top 15.
"Of the teams whose seasons are theoretically dead in the water, Houston provides the faintest glimmer of hope. Braden Smith, Tank Dell and Kayden McDonald are on the way, the Titans are up next on the schedule and 1–4 looks far better (with three examples of playoff teams in the last 25 years, by the way)."
Nick Shook went against the grain last week when he decided to shift the Texans up two spots from their previous ranking to land at 23, even after a loss. This time around, it's the exact opposite: Houston finally won a game, and Shook drops them back down to 25.
"Houston did what everyone expected it to do: take care of business against the worst team in the NFL. C.J. Stroud added another fruitful week to what is quickly becoming a very strong rebound season, the Texans finally got a little bit more out of their ground game (despite losing David Montgomery to injury), and the superior AFC South team walked away with an easy win. It’s a start, and we'll see what becomes of the Marvin Harrison Jr. trade, but it’s going to be a long climb out of 0-4."
ESPN 's writers were polled this week on their power rankings, where the Texans saw themselves right outside of the top 20. When D.J. Bien-Aime was tasked to point out Houston's biggest weakness on defense, that would be "health at all three levels."
"The Texans have dealt with injuries to key players. Pro Bowl linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair sat out time because of a groin injury. Nickelback Jalen Pitre just sustained a shoulder injury against the Titans, defensive tackle Kayden McDonald was on IR because of a quad injuryto start the season, and linebacker Henry To'oTo'o landed on IR after Week 1 because of a shoulder injury. That has factored into their defense giving up 234 passing yards per game (23rd). Overall, Houston is tied for 15th in scoring defense (22.4 per game) after ranking second last season (17.4)."
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff continue the trend of placing Houston right outside of the top 20, but give them a welcomed boost of three spots compared to where they were this time last week.
"Finally, some positive vibes in Houston! Beating the Titans is hardly much to celebrate these days, but at long last, the Texans are in the win column, and reinforcements are on the way. After trading for Kayshon Boutte just before the season, the Texans added another wide receiver this weekend in 2024 No. 4 pick Marvin Harrison Jr."
Pete Prisco made sure to have some praise for Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud for the strong start to the season he's had, which is more than justified. Even at a 1-4 record, Houston's signal-caller is averaging a career-high in passing yards (280.4 yards per game), is completing over 64% of his passes, and hasn't thrown an interception in five games.
"The offense with C.J. Stroud has been playing good football. The change to DeMeco Ryans calling plays seemed to work as they ready to play a big game this week with Jacksonville."
Ralph Vacchiano gives the Texans a nice boost of three spots, yet wants to see this roster keep up their momentum in Week 6 as they travel to London and face a much more difficult test in the Jaguars, compared to what the Titans just allowed.
"It says a lot about parity in the NFL that the Texans think they’re still in the race enough to trade a second-round pick for WR Marvin Harrison Jr...  Blowing out the Titans on Sunday isn’t enough to convince anyone that they can. This week’s game against the Jaguars in London will be a much bigger test. The sooner DeMeco Ryans and QB C.J. Stroud figure out how to tap Harrison’s old potential, the better."

title: Why Texans' DeMeco Ryans Is Fired Up About Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade
full_text:
The Houston Texans are the latest team in the NFL to make a major splash trade after the events of their Week 5 win over the Tennessee Titans–– ultimately trading a 2027 second and seventh-round pick for wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. and a sixth-round pick from the Arizona Cardinals .
It's a move from the Texans that has many excited for what's ahead, not only for fans outside of the building eager to see Houston have another weapon offensively, but also for several inside the facility ready to work with a top-five draft pick from just two summers ago.
And perhaps one of the most pumped up about the Texans' recent move is their head coach, DeMeco Ryans, who was the one that first announced the move during his post-game presser from Week 5 , and has since gone a bit more in depth about why he's so ready for Harrison Jr. to enter the mix.
Ryans recently appeared on Texans Radio after Houston's win over the Titans to unpack the move for Harrison Jr. trade among other topics.
And for Ryans, he's not only excited for what Harrison Jr. can add to the Texans offense, but also for the purpose of the 2023 No. 4 pick getting a fresh start in a new home.
“I’m fired up, man. Also, it is exciting to break news. It's fun, now I see why everybody's fishing for information," Ryans said with a smile. "To add a guy of Marvin‘s caliber, it’s a huge get for us. Huge get for the Texans. I’m fired up for Marvin."
"When you’re in a situation and it may not be going great, to get a breath of fresh air, go to a new place. I know Houston’s gonna be great for Marvin."
Harrison Jr.'s 2026 season hasn't gone exactly as expected, having logged just five receptions for 85 yards and a touchdown. But situationally, it seemingly wasn't the best fit by any means.
The Cardinals have been under .500 ever since he arrived in 2023. Harrison Jr. was gradually phased him out of the offensive game plan year over year, and quarterback-wise, things have never been the most seamless for him either.
Yet, in Houston? There's a good chance all three of those factors can turn around for the better, and thus, give the Texans reason to believe they can get the most out of the 24-year-old wideout.
Another aspect that Ryans sees as a major benefit for Harrison Jr. in his new situation–– as many have pointed out–– is the fact that he'll be paired up with his college quarterback, C.J. Stroud ; someone he has strong, prior chemistry catching passes from, and will now have an opportunity to build onto that connection once again.
"Having that prior relationship with C.J., I think it’s gonna go great for him," Ryans continued. "I’m excited to add him. I know he’s been a big-time playmaker in college; his first season in the NFL, he took off."
"Just go be yourself. Bring a great attitude. Everyone speaks about how hard a worker Marvin is; I’m excited to work with him. I talked to him on the phone, and he was elated. I can’t wait to meet him. I just know he’s gonna bring great energy to our building.”
Based on the Texans' strong investment of a second-round pick in Harrison Jr.'s services, it's a clear message that their lead decision-makers are confident in what their newest wide receiver can bring to the table.
And in Ryans' mind, if Harrison Jr. is able to be the hard-worker and high-end talent that he's been advertised as upon his arrival, the move could be an overwhelming success for the Texans in due time.

title: Texans Could Exploit Jaguars' New Offensive Line Injury in Week 6
full_text:
The Houston Texans have a date with another AFC South opponent on the horizon for Week 6 coming fresh off of their encouraging 26-3 win over the Tennessee Titans this past weekend.
And in the days ahead of the Texans' Week 6 trip to face the Jagaurs in London , we now know that Jacksonville will be down a key piece of their offensive line for this week, and for the next several games.
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Jaguars starting left tackle Anton Harrison is expected to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery when he returns from London.
#Jaguars starting LT Anton Harrison, starter since 2023, is expected to undergo arthroscopic knee surgery when he returns from London, per me and @JFowlerESPN . During the surgery, the doctor will determine how long Trevor Lawrence’s blindside protector is out — weeks or months. pic.twitter.com/euMcFlKvBa
It's a major loss for the Jaguars' offensive line, as Harrison has remained a steady starting piece of this offensive line for the last four seasons.
Ever since he was a first-rounder back in 2023, Harrison has started over 50 regular-season games in Jacksonville, yet might now be trending towards a placement on Injured Reserve.
So how does such a big loss for the Jaguars' offensive front impact the Texans' chances this week? Well, it certainly bodes well for their pass rush, which has been a unit that's gradually come alive over their past few games.
With the Jaguars now down their starter on Trevor Lawrence's blindside, Jacksonville will now likely turn to backup tackle Walker Little to hold down the fort for whatever stretch he's going to be sidelined.
And of anyone on the Texans' defense to benefit from that swap on the Jaguars' offensive front, it's going to be veteran defensive end Danielle Hunter; someone who primarily lines up against the opposing left tackle on a weekly basis, and now has an easier assignment on his hands with an experienced, yet not quite as consistent contributor in Little.
Looking back to the last time these two teams faced off against each other––which came back in Week 10 of the 2025 season–– it was a game to remember for Hunter .
The star defensive end put up one of his most impressive performances since joining the Texans , and perhaps just as a pro altogether: seven tackles, 3.5 sacks, and a forced fumble that eventually led to their 36-29 win, sparking what would be an eventual eight-game win streak to end the year
And who was the Jaguars' left tackle in that Week 10 matchup? It wasn't Anton Harrison––who lined up on the right side for most of the day––it was Walker Little; who presented a clear array of problems in pass protection, and might be put in a position for some similar struggles this weekend in London.
So far this season, Little has yet to start for the Jaguars, though he has been active for 39 games since being selected in the second round of the 2021 NFL Draft, and has 19 games of starting experience throughout his career.
Against this dominant Texans pass rush, though, that's remained one of the best in the NFL for the past couple of seasons, it could lead to Lawrence being forced under a bit more duress than he has been this season, as he's been sacked just 10 times through five games.
As for the Texans' defense, they've recorded 18 total sacks through that same stretch. Last week against the Tennessee Titans, it was Will Anderson who stepped up to the occasion for 3.0 sacks on Cam Ward , managing to tie his career-high in the process.
If the Texans' elite edge duo can keep pressure consistent on the Jaguars' passing game and make them feel the loss of Harrison on their blindside, then the road to a second-straight win might become a little easier on the road in London.
Therefore, expect Houston and their coaching staff to make that pass rush a primary emphasis in practice before Week 6 gets underway.

title: Colts Open Week 6 With Several Key Names on Injury Report
full_text:
At this point, Indianapolis Colts fans are probably tired of watching injuries take a toll on this roster.
It feels like the same story we've seen over the last decade-plus, and through five weeks of the 2026 season, injuries are once again making life considerably more difficult for Indianapolis.
Wednesday's injury report featured several notable names, including two players who left practice for concussion evaluations.
And for a team sitting at 2-3, the last thing Indianapolis needs is more injuries to important contributors.
Offensive lineman Matt Goncalves and rookie defensive end Jaylahn Tuimoloau were both limited Wednesday after leaving practice to undergo concussion evaluations.
Whether either player passed those evaluations remains unclear, but both situations deserve attention heading into Sunday.
Goncalves has been a valuable piece of the offensive line, and with Daniel Jones already struggling to find consistency, losing another contributor up front certainly wouldn't help.
Tuimoloau's situation might be even more frustrating considering the current state of Indianapolis' defensive line.
With Arden Key recently landing on injured reserve, Indianapolis needs its younger pass rushers to step up and produce . Potentially losing another body along the defensive front would only make that challenge more difficult.
Linebacker Jaylon Carlies also missed practice with the rib injury that sidelined him against Pittsburgh. Considering how poorly this linebacker room has performed through five weeks, Indianapolis can hardly afford another week without one of its starters.
Jalen Travis was another nonparticipant after suffering an ankle injury against the Steelers.
Perhaps no position group has been more affected by injuries this season than wide receiver .
Alec Pierce hasn't played since Week 2 against Kansas City, and without his ability to stretch the field, this passing attack has looked considerably less dangerous.
Outside of Josh Downs, there just haven't been many sparks from this group. Downs leads the healthy receivers with 20 catches for 249 yards, but he appeared on Wednesday's report as limited with rest/hamstring listed.
Fortunately, Downs participated in individual drills, suggesting the issue may not be particularly serious.
Keenan Allen did not practice due to rest, while Ashton Dulin remained sidelined with a hamstring injury. One encouraging development was Darius Slayton returning as a full participant after a knee injury kept him out against Pittsburgh.
Slayton hasn't made his Colts debut, but Indianapolis desperately needs someone who can threaten defenses vertically while Pierce remains sidelined.
Right now, opposing defenses simply don't have enough to fear from this passing attack .
Daniel Jones was listed with an ankle injury but practiced fully Wednesday, which is certainly a positive development.
Jonathan Taylor was limited strictly for rest, while Charvarius Ward also received a rest day.
Tight end Will Mallory was another full participant as he continues working toward a potential return from injured reserve.
There's still time for several of these situations to improve before Sunday's divisional matchup against the Tennessee Titans. But the bigger concern remains the same.
Indianapolis is already struggling to find consistency on both sides of the ball, and continuing to lose important contributors certainly isn't making things any easier.
At 2-3, this team needs to start stacking wins. Getting healthy would be a pretty good place to start.
Michael Greene is a graduate of Indiana University and the Scouting Academy. He's in his first year covering the Indianapolis Colts and NFL, with a unique focus on fantasy football.

title: Colts Have Several Trade Targets to Consider After Marvin Harrison Jr. Miss
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts entered the 2026 season with high expectations, but their offense has developed a glaring weakness at wide receiver . Injuries and a lack of consistent downfield production have limited Daniel Jones' options in the passing game, leaving Indianapolis searching for answers.
With the NFL trade deadline approaching, the Colts must determine whether their current group is capable of getting the job done or if outside help is necessary. The team has playoff aspirations, but its recent performances have exposed some limitations that could become increasingly difficult to overcome as the season progresses.
Acquiring another receiver would give Indianapolis an opportunity to address one of its most pressing concerns. However, making a deal is easier said than done, especially for a team that has already made a significant investment in its present roster.
The question is whether the Colts can find a worthwhile addition at the right price, or if they're better off trusting the players they already have.
The Colts have lacked consistent production from their wide receivers through five games. Josh Downs leads the group with 249 receiving yards, while Keenan Allen has 145 and Laquon Treadwell has 157. Tight end Tyler Warren actually leads the team in receptions with 30, highlighting how much Indianapolis has relied on its tight end to keep the pass game afloat.
Injuries have complicated the picture. Alec Pierce, one of Indianapolis' most important downfield threats, appeared in just two of the team's first five games and is out until further notice Darius Slayton, a midseason addition, is yet to play a game as he deals with a knee injury.
Still, the Colts cannot afford to ignore the position as the trade deadline approaches. The team did its research on a possible trade for Marvin Harrison Jr., but he was moved to Houston after Indy determined the asking price was too steep.
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have identified several wide receivers who could be worth monitoring, giving Indianapolis potential alternatives if it decides its current group needs reinforcement.
One wide out that Graziano threw out as a possible trade candidate is Jacksonville’s Brian Thomas Jr. The third-year player enjoyed a breakout rookie season but regressed in year two and has since fallen behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order. While he may be of interest to receiver-needy teams, Jacksonville is reluctant to trade him, especially with their 4-1 start to the season
Another player whose name is generating some buzz is Browns receiver Jerry Jeudy. Cleveland is building around a young core and Jeudy appears to have fallen out of favor with the Browns prioritizing the development of their two rookie receivers, Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion.
Cleveland reportedly set their asking price at a third or fourth-round pick for Jeudy according to Jordan Schultz , but Schultz isn’t convinced they’ll find a partner willing to meet that price. Fowler echoed a similar sentiment, saying “My sense is while they are not actively shopping Jeudy, a strong offer could change that.”
It appears the Browns are simply holding out until they receive a suitable offer.
The third option Graziano and Fowler listed was Chargers’ receiver Quentin Johnston. Johnston has had a rough go of life in the NFL in his first three seasons as drop issues plagued him early on. Now, the Chargers sit winless at 0-5 with a trip to Kansas City on deck before their bye. If Los Angeles is still without a by the time their bye week rolls around, significant change could be on the way.
“Someone the other day mentioned the possibility of a Chargers fire sale,” Graziano said. “Teams will have an eye on potentially helpful players from a Chargers roster that obviously hasn't come together…Johnston is certainly intriguing.”
The price tag for Johnston is unknown, but if the Colts had any interest, a late-round pick could do the trick. Johnston could fit into Shane Steichen’s offense as a possession receiver, but has an $18 million fifth-year option fully guaranteed coming up in 2027.
Working through the rest of the possible trade targets, Rashod Bateman is someone Fowler said he’s keeping tabs on.
“Zay Flowers is the dominant wide receiver in the Ravens' offense, which means Bateman's production comes and goes,” Fowler said. “Bateman's contract is tradable -- he is due $6.5 million this year and $8.25 million in 2027 -- and other teams have had interest in the past. The Ravens are in contention and might not want to move players, but Bateman is at least a name on my list.”
Lastly, Jauan Jennings came up as an option. The former 49ers receiver signed with the Vikings this offseason but has gotten lost in the offense, logging just two catches so far this season. Minnesota is unbeaten and could be hesitant to move anyone. But if the season begins to go the other way for the Vikings, then Jennings could be on the move around the trade deadline.
Jennings’ contract is relatively cheap with a cap hit of $4.3 million, so that’s not an obstacle in the way of a possible move.
Looking at the options listed by Graziano and Fowler, there are definitely some intriguing ones, but there are a number of variables to consider.
Firstly, the Colts don’t have much draft capital to work with in the trade market. No first-round pick in 2027 makes it difficult to justify trading away a second or third-rounder, and with general manager Chris Ballard likely on the way out of his position, the Colts would be wise to hold onto their 2027 picks for Ballard’s successor.
That said, there is a desire to win this season in Indianapolis, so they could choose to throw caution into the wind and see what happens. Considering the options, I don’t think that’s necessary, but there are players available who could be a fit.
We can rule Thomas out right away as the Jaguars would never trade within the division. Jeudy is a realistic candidate to be moved, but I don’t see him being a needle-mover for the Colts.
I personally would steer well clear of Johnston. While a change of scenery could change the entire trajectory of his career, he’s too volatile an option for the Colts to consider when they need proven and consistent production.
Bateman and Jennings are interesting discussions, and the Colts should absolutely do their due diligence on what it would take to make a trade happen. Neither will lead the way as the clear top choice receiver in the Indianapolis offense, but both bring proven experience and solid role-playing production.
Plus, since both contributed to multiple playoff runs with the Ravens and 49ers respectively, Bateman and Jennings both come from a winning culture, which the Colts may be a valuable intangible and something they need to infuse into an otherwise mediocre roster. Still, without a 1,000-yard season between them, the Colts need to try and buy low. With Bateman, I don't think the Ravens would be willing to move him at a low price. With Jennings, it's possible, but he'd most likely be a rental until the end of the season.
All things considered, I wouldn’t rule out any sort of trade on the Colts side of things. The team is in desperate need of pass-catching help. Of the options that are available as of now, none are true building blocks for the long-term, but there are some possible band-aids available to help Indianapolis get through 2026.

title: Week 6 Power Rankings: National Media Sends Clear Message After Steelers Loss
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts suffered a frustrating 34-22 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. As a result, the picture is becoming clearer on where Indianapolis stacks up against the rest of the league.
At 2-3, the Colts defense has struggled tremendously at times with tackling, coverage and putting pressure on the quarterback. Offensively, injuries at wide receiver have limited the vertical passing game, and red zone struggles have recently been an issue, too.
As a result, Indianapolis has slid down the list in nearly every publication’s Week 6 power rankings. With numerous issues to point to, here's where some of the biggest names in NFL media have the Colts ranked heading into Week 6.
Sports Illustrated: 24th (Week 5: 17th)
“If there is no Jonathan Taylor, there is no Colts offense,” Sports Illustrated’s Conor Orr wrote of the Colts, who come in at 24th, seven spots down from last week and the largest drop by any of the publications listed.
The Colts couldn’t get Taylor going at all against a physical defensive front which held him to just 3 yards per carry on Sunday. If that’s any indication of what’s to come for this Colts offense, then Shane Steichen is in hot water.
ESPN’s team of beat reporters dropped the Colts down two ranking places after the loss over the weekend, pointing to poor tackling as a symptom of a larger defensive dilemma.
“The Colts have a litany of issues on defense, but tackling is a fundamental problem that affects many areas,” Stephen Holder wrote.
Holder added that the Colts rank 28th in the league in yards allowed after contact (482) and are 31st in yards allowed per play (6.2), placing the majority of blame on “the team’s underwhelming linebackers.”
The Colts did sign Germaine Pratt earlier in the week as they look to revive a struggling linebacker core, continuing the trend of bringing in former Lou Anarumo defenders. But considering how that strategy has worked out thus far, I wouldn’t expect Pratt to move the needle.
Pro Football Talk: 23rd (Week 5: 22nd)
Minimal movement for the Colts in Mike Florio’s Week 6 rankings. Florio again kept his analysis brief, but took a powerful stance in the process.
Florio simply wrote, “It feels like an overhaul is inevitable.” Hard to argue with that assessment. The Colts emphasized the fact that this is a must-win season and the levels of urgency are as high as ever. Yet, the product on the field has underwhelmed.
The Athletic: 25th (Week 5: 19th)
Chad Graff and Josh Kendall have the Colts at 25, a steep slide from their No, 19 spot from a week ago. In their eyes, Indianapolis may have made a mistake this offseason they’re not willing to come to terms with.
“They’d never admit it (at least not yet), but perhaps there’s some buyer’s remorse after giving Daniel Jones a two-year, $88 million contract in March,” they said, adding Jones wasn’t the reason for Sunday’s loss, but also hasn’t contributed much to the team’s only two wins so far.
“And when you’re making more than $40 million a season, the expectation is that you’d better be delivering victories.”
Fox Sports: 20th (Week 5: 18th)
After being the highest publication on the Colts in Week 5, Ralph Vacchiano moved Indianapolis down two places this week, leaving a harrowing outlook for this team if problems aren’t corrected quickly.
“The Colts have too much talent on offense to continually come up so empty,” he said. “Maybe things will start clicking when WR Alec Pierce returns…But head coach Shane Steichen is an offensive guy, and he needs to come up with some answers, because he doesn’t have the defense to prop his team up. If the struggles continue, he’s going to find himself on the hot seat long before he gets to their Week 13 bye.”
In Vacchiano’s eyes, things could get late early for the Colts, and if things do go completely sideways, the bye week could be a week of change for the franchise.
NFL.com: 24th (Week 5: 22nd)
Indianapolis drops two spots in Nick Shook’s latest rankings, who still seems a little bit split on the Colts through five games. Like Vacchiano, he thinks the Colts are capable of more.
“There are moments in which you see Indianapolis’ potential,” he wrote. “But each time I watch these Colts, it leaves me wondering what could be.”
Shook cites putting too much stock into a receiving core he deems as “underwhelming” and has some worries about the offensive line as well.
Bleacher Report: 23rd (Week 5: 23rd)
No change for the Colts in Bleacher Report’s rankings, and the lack of change in the rankings seems to align with the current state of the franchise.
“The Colts are stuck in mediocrity,” analyst Maurice Moton writes. “Nonetheless, the Colts must sort out their defensive issues…The Colts gave up 127 rushing yards to the Steelers, who entered Week 5 with the 22nd-ranked rushing offense.”
Like many who share the same defensive concerns, the thought here is until there’s more consistency on that side of the football, the Colts will remain stuck in a cycle of mediocrity.

title: Colts Turn to Familiar Face Germaine Pratt After Rough Start at LB
full_text:
The Indianapolis Colts entered the 2026 season with arguably the weakest linebacker room in football, and through five weeks, they haven't done much to prove otherwise.
After another rough defensive performance against Pittsburgh, Indianapolis is turning to a familiar face for help, signing veteran linebacker Germaine Pratt to the practice squad on Tuesday.
Pratt appeared in 12 games for the Colts last season, starting every one of them and recording 101 tackles, five tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries.
Those are respectable numbers for a player who joined the team midway through the year, but his return says just as much about the current state of this linebacker room as it does about what he brings to the table.
Indianapolis made a pretty significant gamble this offseason by trading Zaire Franklin to Green Bay and electing to address the position primarily through the draft.
So far, that gamble hasn't paid off.
The Colts rank 28th in total defense, allowing 384.2 yards per game, while surrendering 27.6 points per contest. Tackling has been another major concern, with Indianapolis allowing 482 yards after contact through five games.
The problems certainly extend beyond the linebackers, but this group has been one of the biggest contributors to Indianapolis' defensive struggles.
Second-round pick CJ Allen played just 11 defensive snaps through the first four games before finally seeing 24 against Pittsburgh. Bryce Boettcher has received more opportunities, but his early performances haven't exactly inspired confidence, either.
For a team that desperately needed immediate contributions from its rookie linebackers, the lack of production has been disappointing.
The biggest advantage Pratt brings to Indianapolis is his familiarity with defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo.
The two spent six seasons together in Cincinnati before reuniting in Indianapolis last October, meaning Pratt already understands the defensive system and what Anarumo expects from his linebackers.
That familiarity should make his transition relatively straightforward, assuming the Colts eventually elevate him from the practice squad.
But to think Pratt is suddenly going to turn this struggling linebacker room into a strength is probably asking a little too much.
He was a solid contributor last season, and his experience could be especially valuable for Allen and Boettcher, two young players Indianapolis absolutely needs to develop.
At this point, it doesn't particularly matter where the Colts find help at linebacker. Whether it's Pratt, another veteran addition or the development of their rookies, Indianapolis needs better production from a position group that has been a liability through five weeks.
