title: The Biggest Decision Kevin O’Connell Got Right vs. Saints (And What It Means Moving Forward)
full_text:
The 5-0 Vikings have certainly been one of the more fascinating teams in the NFL in 2026.
The only other undefeated teams are the 49ers and Chiefs, both widely seen as serious contenders across the league. The Vikings, on the other hand, have raised more questions than answers for some. The squad clearly has a dominant defense and an elite special teams group, but the offense has taken time to find an identity.
Luckily, that seemed to shift against the Saints.
Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell is starting to embrace an offensive identity that often contradicts many of the core principles he had previously set in place, and it may just be the best way to let the offense thrive.
Kyler Murray looked good on Sunday , made even more impressive by the sheer amount of adversity the Vikings’ offense faced due to injuries. The offense took the field without wide receiver Jordan Addison, running back Jordan Mason, left tackle Christian Darrisaw and left guard Donovan Jackson, and they lost tight end T.J. Hockenson to a concussion on the team’s first drive. Not exactly ideal.
Luckily, Justin Jefferson was cleared to play after being labeled a game-time decision with an ankle injury.
Despite all of that adversity, the offense had its most complete day so far, and O’Connell deserves credit for trusting his QB to make it happen.
Murray delivered the ball effectively to ten different pass catchers in the afternoon. Unfortunately for an already frustrated Jauan Jennings, he was the only Viking targeted who didn't catch a pass. Murray, though, was precise, effective, and most importantly, played his game.
His 229 yards through the air and 51 on the ground didn’t fit the traditional O’Connell mold of deep shots and passes over the middle, but they led to an impressive 109.6 passer rating and an offense that flashed exciting potential (H/t: Bring Me the Sports ' Will Ragatz).
Lotta green dots for the Vikings' QB1, who understands the power of stacking completions. And this doesn't even show his 50 rushing yards. pic.twitter.com/UKs6mgKkIo
The Vikings’ passing game certainly didn't get off to a hot start this season. They lost Murray early in Week 1 to a concussion, opening the door for a three-TD day on only 133 yards from Carson Wentz after he was given incredible field position by his defense all game.
Murray returned in Week 3 against the Buccaneers but never quite found his footing. The film often looked awkward, with wide receivers’ breaks often coming after Murray’s internal timer had already sent him scrambling.
But Sunday showed the building blocks for something special, and I can’t overstate how impressive that is given the injury woes on that side of the ball. If the team comes out of the bye with a relatively clean bill of health, their Week 7 matchup against the Colts suddenly gives them a chance to put it all together against a defense that allows the fifth-most yards per game before entering a truly challenging November stretch .
This is where champions are forged. pic.twitter.com/ETt56Vk2fU
O’Connell is progressing and learning to lean into his offense's strengths. If he keeps growing, the sky is the limit for this Vikings squad in 2026.

title: Coller: Kyler Murray Showed Vikings His Full Potential in Win vs. Saints (Why That Matters & What's Next)
full_text:
Week 5 of the NFL was defined by madness, crazy finishes and unexpected results. There was a tie, an overtime blocked field goal and a nose tackle-long snapper situation. It was easy to overlook one Vikings player's performance that may impact the remainder of the season.
That would be quarterback Kyler Murray’s 24-for-30 passing day in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday .
Murray produced 224 passing yards and 51 rushing yards, as well as a breathtaking touchdown pass to Justin Jefferson (h/t NFL) and zero turnovers. Pro Football Focus graded him the sixth-best quarterback in Week 5 , and ESPN ’s QBR scored him as having the seventh-best performance.
OH MY JETTAS ✈️ @MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/9JQWo9ugMo
While it’s easy to overlook Murray’s play because it came against the Saints, who entered having allowed the most points in the NFL and because the Vikings only put up 23 points (thanks to two red zone fumbles), there were things that happened in the game that showed the potential of what Murray can be in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense.
One reason to be excited for the Vikings' offensive outlook is Murray's connection with Jefferson.
All summer long, Murray and Jefferson connected in training camp on downfield passes. When the season arrived, Murray got hurt 11 plays into the opening game and then when he came back, Jefferson got hurt on the first drive. In their first game together, Murray found him six times on seven targets for 79 yards.
As a reminder, every quarterback who has ever directed passes in Jefferson’s direction except J.J. McCarthy has had immense success. Here are the passer ratings when targeting Jefferson from 2020 to 2024 (per PFF ):
Murray hasn’t had a connection like that since he played with DeAndre Hopkins early in his career. Maybe you noticed the Cardinals just traded Marvin Harrison Jr. —their supposed “generational” receiver—to the Texans over the weekend.
The other thing Murray has thrived on during his career is finding the tight end. Over the last two weeks, he has comfortably done so. Against the Dolphins, he went 13-for-13 throwing to T.J. Hockenson and when Hockenson got injured early against the Saints, he continued to work the ball to backup TE Gavin Bartholomew, who had five receptions in the game.
It seems Murray and O’Connell are on the same page with quick passing, as Murray completed 11-of-11 throws between zero and nine yards from the line of scrimmage. In previous years, he’s been one of the most accurate QBs in the NFL on short passes, completing 82.8% in 2024. He’s currently the NFL leader at 90% on quick throws.
That’s the sign that it’s working. But the sign that Murray is really getting into a groove is his playmaking confidence outside of the structure of the play.
Murray's scrambling was a throwback to previous years when he was considered one of the most difficult quarterbacks to capture in the NFL.
He converted third downs by either taking advantage of deep coverage or blowing past pass rushers who were trying to track him down. His most impressive play was an instant escape act with star rusher Chase Young in his grill. He spun backward, rolled out and found running back DeeJay Dallas for a third-and-11 conversion. It was a Heisman Murray play.
Combining that type of QB performance with a running game that’s been successful despite missing Jordan Mason for four weeks , the No. 1 defense and No. 1 special teams unit in the NFL could give the Vikings a chance to seriously contend in the NFC, especially with only one other team standing out above the rest thus far (49ers).
As the Vikings go into the difficult part of their schedule after the bye week, when they face the Lions, Bills, 49ers and Packers, they will need one thing that has eluded Murray throughout his career: Consistency.
In 2024, Murray led the Cardinals to a 6-4 record and had a 100.8 passer rating, only for them to win only two games the rest of the season as Murray struggled. In 2021, Arizona opened with seven straight wins before finishing with only 11 and a first-round exit from the playoffs.
The season is still young, so we can’t turn one strong showing into evidence that the Vikings will be holding the Lombardi Trophy at the end of the year. However, we can say that the model for them winning games is clear, and it’s going to take high efficiency, protecting the football and playmaking from Murray.
For the first time vs. New Orleans, Vikings fans saw all of that come together.

title: 3 Most Likely Jauan Jennings Trade Destinations as Vikings Rumors 'Heat Up'
full_text:
It's far from an overreaction to say that Jauan Jennings's brief time with the Minnesota Vikings should be classified as a colossal disappointment .
Brought in to be the No. 3 wide receiver behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, Jennings hasn't come close to looking the part, entering the Vikings' bye week with more games played (four) than catches (two), along with only nine receiving yards and a career-worst 40.2 offensive grade on Pro Football Focus .
For what it's worth, that's the second-worst grade among 179 WRs this season. It's safe to say both Jennings and the Vikings could use a fresh start, which seems to be a growing possibility if the latest buzz is any indication.
Appearing on Tuesday's episode of "The Pat McAfee Show," NFL insider Ian Rapoport said that he expects discussions around a potential Jennings trade to heat up a little bit over the next, probably, couple of days and weeks ."
From @PatMcAfeeShow : In the wake of the Marvin Harrison Jr trade, another WR whose trade market is expected to heat up is #Vikings WR Jauan Jennings. Would a #49ers reunion make sense? pic.twitter.com/DR6mY1OvYb
Jennings is on a one-year contract, making it easy for the Vikings to hit the reset button if they're looking for a trade. A deal would save the Vikings $5.03 million in cap space while creating just over $4.5 million in dead money, according to Spotrac , which comes off the books once the 2026 season ends.
Despite the slow start to the year, Jennings's name still has value, making him an attractive rental option for any WR-needy teams. With that in mind, here are the three most likely trade destinations for the Vikings' offseason addition.
Sometimes, what's old becomes new again. Like Rapoport pointed out, the 49ers make too much sense as a potential trade destination to ignore.
Drafted 217th overall by the Niners in 2020, Jennings spent his NFL career in the Bay Area before moving to Minnesota . The former Tennessee Volunteer was solid but didn't blow anyone away early on in his San Francisco run. However, that changed in Years 4 and 5. Jennings amassed 1,618 receiving yards and 15 TDs on 132 receptions between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, which is the type of player the Vikings thought they were getting.
Sometimes fresh starters don't work out, though, and a return home might benefit not only Jennings, but the 49ers, too. After all, San Francisco currently has several wideouts—De'Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Ricky Pearsall, and Christian Kirk—on injured reserve, and now Deebo Samuel is dealing with a hamstring injury . That's without mentioning the Brandon Aiyuk situation .
The 49ers need receiver help, so who better than a familiar face like Jennings? Doing business with a fellow undefeated NFC team might not seem ideal, but if the Niners' desperation helps the Vikings in the long run, there's good reason to do business.
Speaking of undefeated squads, the Chiefs are another team that likely wouldn't mind some WR help.
Entering Week 6, tight end Travis Kelce is the only Kansas City pass-catcher on pace to hit the 1,000-yard mark this season. Even though the Chiefs are undefeated, Patrick Mahomes clearly needs another weapon, especially as top WRs Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy are both averaging career lows in receiving yards per game at 47.5 and 33.3, respectively.
Adding Jennings to the mix would be a huge gain for Mahomes, especially if the current Vikings wideout is motivated by a fresh start. Knowing the Chiefs previously coveted him could also boost Jennings's confidence, as ESPN's Adam Schefter reported in May that the AFC West leaders were interested in signing him before the Vikings won the sweepstakes.
With their WR depth clearly a concern, don't be surprised if the Chiefs are among the first in line to make an offer for Jennings.
Sticking with the AFC, the Dolphins might be Jennings's best path to turning his season around and potentially securing a significant payday in March.
The Dolphins might not have Super Bowl aspirations like the Chiefs or 49ers, but they offer an opportunity to be the big fish in a small pond. Miami's wide receiver situation starts and ends with Malik Washington and rookie WR Caleb Douglas, who hasn't played since Week 2 due to an ankle injury .
With every other Dolphins pass-catcher averaging 25.4 or fewer receiving yards per game, it's easy to see why a proven veteran like Jennings would be attractive. At the same time, a trip to South Beach could benefit Jennings, who'd easily be in contention for Malik Willis's busiest weapon. Thriving in the role would boost his value heading into free agency, where the Dolphins will have over $110 million to spend —the third-most room in the NFL, according to Spotrac .
On top of that, he'd be reunited with Dolphins offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik, who was the 49ers' offensive pass game specialist (2021) and offensive passing game coordinator (2022) during Jennings's first two pro seasons. It's been a while since they worked together, but that doesn't mean they can't rekindle some magic.

title: Vikings Verdict: Judging Super Bowl Hopes, Jauan Jennings  & Other Overreactions to Begin Bye Week
full_text:
The Vikings are undefeated as their bye week arrives , despite taking the path less traveled. They've won ugly, but the Purple and Gold have found a way to pull out a win each time thus far, resulting in first-place status in the NFC North to begin Week 6.
Now, with some time to sit with their thoughts, how will the Vikings proceed moving forward?
Is the Super Bowl actually on the table? Should general manager Nolan Teasley trade his disappointing free agent?
Let's judge some potential Vikings overreactions after the Week 5 win.
At 5-0, it's natural to start to look ahead to the playoffs, but the Vikings are also one of the more unusual undefeated teams in recent memory. Powered by a suffocating defense, an elite special teams unit and an offense that may have started to figure things out, not many NFL teams would want to see Minnesota on the schedule.
Wins all count the same, of course, but the Vikings' previous opponents have a combined record of just 8-17. Meanwhile, the final 12 games feature just four opponents with losing records, putting their unblemished win/loss column to the test.
If the Vikings offense has truly turned a corner, then there's no reason Minnesota shouldn't be in the conversation at the end of the season. The "49" in 49ers may as well stand for the number of injuries they've faced this season, and as another 5-0 squad, they could be a threat to the NFC crown if they can get healthy.
If the Vikings' offense sputters again and the defense slips even slightly, though, this could easily become a .500 team. Still, barring an epic collapse, the Vikings will almost surely make the playoffs, and a one- or two-seed would go a long way towards a potential run.
The Vikings are arguably peaking and now have to sit for the next two weeks thanks to an early bye. While the bye week will help to get some key players back —like Jordan Mason, Christian Darrisaw and more—an argument could be made that Minnesota would have rather suited up in Week 6 to keep this thing rolling.
Kyler Murray has completed 83% of his last 43 passes and put together his best game as a Viking in Week 5 against the Saints. Getting healthy will be an important step toward the ultimate goal, but for anybody out there who believes in momentum, this bye week couldn't have come at a worse time. Ultimately, it probably won't affect the budding offense too much.
There are 11 other Vikings with more receiving yards than Jauan Jennings this year, and the question on everyone's mind is, " Should the Vikings trade him ?"
A coveted free agent, Jennings has not found a home on the Minnesota offense, notching two catches for nine yards. Head coach Kevin O'Connell has been asked multiple times (h/t VikingzFanPage) about Jennings's lack of production and has quickly pointed out his contributions in the run game.
Fair, I suppose, but he wasn't brought in just to run-block a few snaps a game; the Vikings either need to find some ways to get Jennings involved in the passing game or cut this experiment short. His trade market would surely be robust despite the slow start to 2026, and the Vikings may admit defeat if things don't change ahead of the deadline.
In the Week 5 win, Vikings rookies played just 42 combined offensive and defensive snaps, including 20 from fullback Max Bredeson. Sunday wasn't much different from the rest of the year either, as the rookies have been used sparingly so far in 2026.
The good news, though, is that the Vikings are winning without any significant contributions from their rookie class . So does it matter?
Ideally, getting solid production from at least a few rookies would be some assurance that things are set up for the future. Instead, 2027 might reveal how good (or bad) this class could be. With established starters at many of the positions like linebacker, edge or cornerback, it's not terribly surprising the rookies haven't gotten much of a look.
Not to mention, first-round pick Caleb Banks was always going to be a project .
Still, is there maybe a little too much up in the air after five games?

title: One Offseason Decision Is Already Haunting Vikings as Bye Week Arrives
full_text:
Week 6 is here, which means it's already time for the Vikings to take some time to reflect as their bye arrives. Minnesota is five games into the season now, meaning there's a large enough sample size to dissect this year's offseason decisions, especially those aging like warm milk.
When the Vikings signed former 49ers wide receiver Jauan Jennings to a one-year, $8 million deal in May, it looked like an impactful move that would take the team's passing offense to the next level.
Jennings was a touchdown machine for the 49ers in 2025, finding the end zone nine times on 55 catches in 15 games. In fact, 10.5% of his catches while with the Niners resulted in a TD. Vikings fans loved the idea of having a proven red-zone target to take pressure off Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
Instead, there has been very little return on Minnesota's investment. Jennings has played four of the Vikings' first five games, catching two passes for nine yards on five targets while playing 201 offensive snaps, continuously proving to be the Purple and Gold's worst offseason decision.
So far, Jennings has been outplayed by multiple Vikings receivers below him on the depth chart. Tai Felton, Jeshaun Jones and Myles Price all have more receiving yards than he does and have played significantly fewer snaps. That's without mentioning Jennings is on track for career-worst performances (h/t Pro Football Focus ) when it comes to:
Yards after catch per reception
Passer rating when targeted
Jennings' struggles look even worse given that injuries have also run rampant through the Vikings' locker room.
Addison missed the team's Week 5 game, and Jefferson left Week 3's contest with an ankle injury. Still, Jennings was unable to step up when the team needed him.
Minnesota is already panicking about the situation, activating Jones when he returned from his suspension and signing veteran free-agent wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. to try to find more production.
The Vikings aren't done there.
On Monday, the team worked out a few more free-agent wide receivers , according to KPRC 2 Houston's Aaron Wilson. JuJu Smith-Schuster is the most notable name on the list, but D’Wayne Eskridge and Dayton Wade were also in attendance.
It is sad that the Vikings are resorting to free agency since they aren't getting production from Jennings. The investment the team made in him feels like a total misuse of salary cap space, a poor use of offensive snaps and a roster spot that could go to a player who could contribute more.
Minnesota could be more patient with Jennings' offensive struggles if he were making an impact in other ways. However, the 29-year-old wide receiver does not play on special teams and has been a non-factor in the Vikings' struggling offense. If general manager Nolan Teasley wants a fresh start, a trade would create just over $5 million in cap savings while bringing on $4.5 million in dead money, per Spotrac .
For now, the Vikings must feel haunted by the decision to sign Jennings even though it made total sense at the time. There is a chance that he can turn things around after Minnesota's bye week, but unless that happens, Teasley must be wondering how he could have used the salary cap space and the roster spot better during the 2026 NFL season.

title: Vikings' Snap Count vs. Saints: Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 5
full_text:
The Minnesota Vikings defeated the New Orleans Saints in Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season despite injuries piling up for the Purple and Gold and some important mistakes being made on the field.
The 23-13 victory keeps the Vikings undefeated heading into their bye week at a time when the rest should help multiple key players get healthy in time for the next game in two weeks against the Indianapolis Colts.
One key reason that Minnesota was able to keep its winning ways alive was how head coach Kevin O'Connell used the players he had available and how those players were able to contribute to Sunday's contest.
Here are five observations from the Vikings' snap counts against the Saints.
Starting tight end T.J. Hockenson was coming off a huge game against the Miami Dolphins where he caught 13 passes for 119 yards. Sadly, he only played two snaps before having to leave the game with a concussion.
Gavin Bartholomew stepped into his role and played 44 offensive snaps along with eight special teams snaps. He finished second on the team in receptions (5) and receiving yards (33) while earning a 71.3 Pro Football Focus grade for the game.
Typically, it is a great thing if a player is on the field for every possible snap. Even though Josh Metellus was one of only two players who were in the game for all 45 defensive snaps, he struggled mightily against New Orleans.
Metellus had the lowest PFF grade of all Minnesota defenders on Sunday (46.7). The problem is that the Vikings are trying to limit Harrison Smith's snaps but still maximize his efficiency. Meanwhile, Theo Jackson is getting 31 defensive snaps, and Jacob Thomas only got three.
Blake Cashman was the other defensive player to participate in all 45 defensive snaps. He turned that into a team-high nine tackles, one for a loss, and one quarterback hit, on his way to a 79.2 PFF grade for the game.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores can't afford to take Cashman off the field this season. He is a stabilizing presence in the middle of the defense and deserves to play every possible snap if he is able to.
Jauan Jennings played 49 offensive snaps against the Saints. He was held without a catch and was only targeted once in the game. There is absolutely no chance that giving him that many reps is the most efficient thing for the offense.
He was outplayed by Jeshaun Jones and Tai Felton, both of whom had fewer offensive opportunities. After the bye, it wouldn't be shocking if Jones starts cutting into Jennings' snaps more significantly to get more value out of the routes.
When Hockenson left the game and didn't return, Bartholomew stepped into the receiving role at tight end, and Yurosek became the blocker. However, he showed that he could do a lot more than just block because he caught a pass on Sunday.
Yurosek can block to keep offensive tackle Caleb Tiernan from trying to do what Josh Oliver was doing before his season-ending injury. The fact that he was on the field for 39 offensive snaps and 14 special teams snaps shows how much the coaching staff believes in him.

title: 3 Winners, 4 Losers of A.J. Brown's Potential Return to Patriots Roster
full_text:
On Wednesday, New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel officially activated A.J. Brown's return to play period , meaning that he can be elevated off of the injured reserve anytime in the next 21 days. Brown, who the Patriots acquired from the Philadelphia Eagles for a 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-round pick, went down in the team's season opener against the Seattle Seahawks 36 days ago with a high ankle sprain.
Brown practiced in a limited capacity for the first time since Week 1. With his 21-day return-to-play window opened, the Super Bowl-winning wide receiver could return to play as soon as this week against the New York Jets.
But how does his return affect the rest of the Patriots? How does Brown's presence provide more or less opportunity for the players and coaches on and off the field? Here are some winners and losers of Brown's return:
For practically a game and a half, McDaniels has been running the Patriots offense with just four wide receivers. After Mack Hollins went down in the third quarter of Week 4 against the Buffalo Bills, the veteran offensive coordinator was forced to reach deep in his bag of tools to utilize the potential of his Patriots passing game.
Since being cut to four receivers, the Patriots receiving corps have hauled in five touchdowns (not including Drake Maye's pass to Hunter Henry, read more for details). McDaniels' effectiveness with spreading the ball and utilizing alternative targets in the wake of both Brown's and Hollins' injuries, have been nothing short of stellar.
Now, with Brown re-entering the fold, McDaniels can expand his playbook — one that he designed specifically with Brown as the number one option. The Patriots get the length of the field to work with and the ability to spread out opposing defenses, as Brown's downfield receiving skills come to play.
In light of a weakened receiver room, Efton Chism III has stepped up in ways not many had expected. In Week 4, he scored the game-winning touchdown on a league-wide highlight reel worthy play. Chism also hauled in a career high five receptions and 57 yards in their win over Las Vegas on Sunday.
However, Chism's unforeseen impact is in part because of the absences at receiver. In Week 1 — the only week where the entire receiver room entered the game healthy, the second-year undrafted free agent was a healthy scratch. From Weeks 2-5, Chism's snap percentage rose an average of 12% per week, playing 76% of snaps in Week 5.
While Brown's return will certainly sideline Chism more than he's seen in the past couple weeks, the scrappy and super athletic receiver may have earned himself more playing time than the Patriots originally planned on giving him this season.
Doubs was the Patriots first big free agent signing at receiver in years. He entered the season expecting to be the team's number two target, lining up opposite to Brown.
After Brown's injury, Doubs became the most targeted player on the Pats' offense. But of the 23 looks quarterback Drake Maye has given him, he's only hauled in 13. Doubs inefficiency to make catches has surrounded his first several games in New England.
Upon Brown's return, Doubs will slot back into the secondary receiver postion, which doesn't only allow him to play the position he learned all summer but also keeps defenses' top secondary players off of him.
Similar to Chism, the tight end group has also thrived in Brown's absence. Both the veteran Henry and rookie acquisition Eli Raridon have caught a touchdown this year and have been reliable presences in the passing game.
Henry, who's played with Maye in all three years of the young star's career, is a common safety net on third or fourth down plays. While Henry will still be the number one tight end, Brown will be a reliable out for Maye, as well.
Raridon, on the other hand, may see less involvement in the passing game. Because the receiving group was limited to just four players, often times, Raridon found himself on the field with Henry  — operating in two tight end sets. Adding a fifth receiver to the group reduces the need for Raridon to be on the field at the same time as Henry.
Prior to Sunday's game, Raridon was averaging one per game across his three games with playing time.
After a definitively slow start to the season, Drake Maye has been the best quarterback in the NFL across the past two weeks , throwing for 643 yards and notching seven total touchdowns.
Though it feels like Maye has finally gotten used to a new — yet dwindled — receiving group, having his number one receiver back in the fold can only beneft the young quarterback who's found confidence and caught fire in recent weeks.
On Wednesday, Maye had a lot to say about practicing with Brown, including, "I think it definitely opens up other parts of the field and other parts of the game for guys. I think you see it in the NBA; it's probably the closest thing that I can think of."
Drake Maye says that having A.J. Brown back at practice was “awesome.” pic.twitter.com/yuN3mD9i6x
Over the summer, reports indicated that Brown and Maye's connection was fantastic. In the less than three quarters of real game action they saw, the pair connected for three catches and 26 yards and missed on one deep shot to the end zone. Brown will provide more opportunity for Maye to move the ball through the air.
Williams is another player whose playing time has increased significantly in response to the injuries.
A third-round pick in last year's draft, Williams hasn't provided the level of use you'd expect from a player taken so highly. His ability to spread the field and haul in deep passes has been exhilirating, but his average reception yardage of 27 yards per catch isn't sustainable nor consistant.
Williams has just five catches on the year, three of which came against the Raiders in Week 5. With Chism showing flashes of success, Williams may find himself on the bottom of the depth chart at the wide receiver position.
Offensive tackle Marcus Bryant returned to practice along with Brown, signaling that the two (when officially elevated to the active roster) will be the third and fourth players the Patriots reactivate off of injured reserve/non-football injurt.
New England can only activate eight players off of the injured reserve, and have already done so with four (including Brown and Bryant). They'll be stuck with 11 players on IR, and will only be able to activate four of them.
You start with EIGHT spots to use for a “designated-to-return” player. 1️⃣ - ST Brenden Schooler 2️⃣ - OT Marcus Bryant 3️⃣ - WR A.J. Brown 4️⃣ - WR Mack Hollins 5️⃣ - 6️⃣ - 7️⃣ - 8️⃣ - Who are your other four? 🤔 ⬇️ https://t.co/QM0uOzFeot pic.twitter.com/JlVQ4n9fse
Taking into account future injuries, as well, the team will have to be very cautious of which injuries deserve IR designation and which players can stay on the active roster while they rehabilitate their injuries.
Several starters like Hollins, FB Reggie Gilliam, and P Bryce Baringer are expected to make full recoveries of their injuries at some point this season.
Brown's return — though a worthwhile one, takes up another IR return designation of which the Patriots have very few.

title: Patriots Week 6 Injury Report: A.J. Brown Returns, OTs Banged Up Bad
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots have gone through a lot of injuries these last five weeks. They've been forced to put more players on injured reserve at this point in the season (19) than they did all of last season. They've been banged up , but have still won two-straight games to improve to 3-2.
But they're getting some players back this week ahead of their matchup with the New York Jets.
"I mean, I think that we'll just focus on this week and see if guys are ready to go," Mike Vrabel said Wednesday about handling injuries ahead of this week and next week's Thursday Night Football game. "We obviously know we have a shortened week next week. It can’t impact our decisions to try to do everything we can to win this week. Then we’ll figure out where we are after that."
Here's the initial injury report for the Patriots, including some returners off of injured reserve.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (neck)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (hamstring)
Here's the Jets' initial injury report for Week 6, including a few major pieces of their offense sidelined.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (quad)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (finger)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (ankle)
The biggest story for the Patriots? The return of A.J. Brown, who missed Weeks 2 through 5 with a high-ankle sprain . He was designated to return off of IR this week, and will work to try and play this week against a Jets team he should thrive against.
But the Patriots aren't sure yet how he'll impact the offense ... or if he'll even be activated by Saturday. The Patriots will have three weeks to officially decide if they'll remove him off of IR and stick him on the 53-man roster.
"He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He hasn't been out there for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then we have a 21-day window, and we'll go from there."
Brown participated in practice , going through drills with his receivers coach, Todd Downing. There didn't seem to be any limitations in how he looked (at least when reporters were present).
A.J. Brown goes through a catch possession drill with WRs coach Todd Downing: pic.twitter.com/ipUvbBZmUx
The Patriots also started the 21-day window for second-year offensive tackle Marcus Bryant, who was placed on IR ahead of the regular season with an ankle injury.
Last week against the Raiders, the Patriots lost both TreVeyon Henderson and Will Campbell in a matter of minutes. Both players would leave the game and wouldn't return, and after tests on Monday, could end up missing some time .
When reporters were present during Wednesday's practice, neither of them were spotted on the field with their teammates. Campbell did speak prior to going out to practice, but he only participated in a limited capacity.
When Campbell was ruled out, the Patriots turned to first round rookie Caleb Lomu . He would play pretty good football from the left side — allowing just one pressure in 47 snaps.
"I think all the times that they have to be able to get some game action, whether that's at the jumbo tight end or getting some snaps in there at different times in practice and being able to work on both sides is critical," Vrabel said Monday on Lomu's first month. "I think that's something that the swing tackle has to be able to do. He has to be ready to go in the game. I know he's working hard, and he's going to try to take advantage of whatever opportunity comes his way."
As for how the Patriots can replace Henderson's skills at running back , they'll have to rely a lot on third-string Corey Kiner, and practice squad players Lan Larison and Hassan Haskins. The team had Haskins in the building during the preseason and the first two weeks of the season, but just signed him back this week just in case.

title: How the Patriots Offense, WR Room Changes After Getting A.J. Brown Back
full_text:
FOXBORO — He's yet to be officially added to the 53-man roster, but New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown was back at practice Wednesday. The star wideout, who has been on IR since after the team's season-opening loss in Seattle, now has 21 days to be activated to the active roster as the team designated him to return .
Brown has been present in the locker room over the past two weeks , often walking in with cleats on and a slight wrap on his right ankle. His high-ankle sprain held him off the field, but hasn't kept him away from his teammates.
"I think he's stayed engaged. I think it's difficult sometimes to stay engaged, but I think his routine was really good," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Wednesday. "(His) ability to be around guys in the meetings, and then also focus on his rehab and just treat everything as a pro and be where he's supposed to be and work hard to get back."
Now that Brown is in uniform practicing and nearing his return, here's how the Patriots' wide receiver room is impacted .
Brown's ability to stretch the field and be the team's go-to weapon past the sticks is part of the reason why the Patriots traded a first round pick for him in June. We haven't been able see that part of his game yet, but it's coming.
Drake Maye did try to take a shot deep to Brown in Week 1 , but Josh Jobe was flagged for defensive pass interference and the ball fell incomplete. The Patriots would score on that drive on a pass to Eli Raridon, but Brown wasn't used in any deep routes for the remainder of his time on the field.
Since he's been out, the Patriots have relied a lot of Romeo Doubs and Kyle Williams to stretch the field down the sidelines. It's worked in spurts, but it hasn't been as consistent as the Patriots might have hoped. Getting Brown back will unlock that part of Maye's passing arsenal.
Maye has thrown for seven touchdowns in the last two weeks, and has seemingly found his groove slinging the football. He was able to connect with Doubs twice, DeMario Douglas twice, and Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III once each.
That's a group that really doesn't offer the same level of threat that Brown has, but the Patriots got outstanding production out of them four. With Brown now sliding into that mix, his ceiling is far higher than any other wideout on the team.
If Maye has been able to tap into the skills he had a season ago with that group, imagine what he can do once Brown straps the pads on Sundays.
But because Brown is returning, that means that the snaps that Douglas and Williams got a week ago might start to dwindle . Last week against Las Vegas, the Patriots were down Mack Hollins ( who was placed on IR with a calf injury suffered in Buffalo ). His absence allowed the likes of Douglas, Williams and Chism to step into larger roles they might not have been in otherwise.
With Brown back in the WR1 role, he'll certainly get the lion's share of targets and receptions outside the numbers. The Patriots will still rely on Doubs across the middle and Douglas/Chism in the slot, but one would imagine that the passing game will now flow through Brown — and not the others.
A few weeks ago, you could make the argument that the Patriots might entertain a trade for a receiver like Brian Thomas Jr. or Marvin Harrison Jr. (who's now been sent to the Houston Texans). While that felt unlikely considering the captial the team gave up to get Brown in the first place, if the Patriots didn't expect him to come back quickly, they could have gotten on the phone to try and make a move.
Instead, this is their big "trade" acqusition. Getting Brown back, a healthy Brown back, should be the cherry on top of what was back-to-back great offensive showings. If he can remain on the field and a legit threat every single week, the Patriots will enjoy their return on investment they made back in June .

title: Patriots Make Massive Roster Decision on WR A.J. Brown This Week
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots just came off a 45-17 thumping of the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 5, where they had three different pass catchers find the end zone. They're now just one step closer to adding another elite weapon to their offense.
Wide receiver A.J. Brown will be out at practice Wednesday as the team prepares to take on the New York Jets in Week 6, head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed. This move begins his 21-day window to be activated off of injured reserve. Brown was placed on IR following the team's 13-10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks in the season opener after suffering a high-ankle sprain.
"A.J. will be out there to practice," Vrabel told reporters ahead of practice. "(We'll) see how that goes."
Brown , the Patriots' top offseason acquisition this year, caught just three passes in his season debut for 26 yards before departing off the field and into the blue medical tent.
He's missed the last four games, but has been spotted a lot more often in the Patriots locker room — often wearing cleats with a slight wrap on his right ankle. He was in a chipper mood last week, chatting with Drake Maye and reporters at his locker.
On Monday, Vrabel didn't shut the door of a possible return for Brown, saying there is a chance that he could be active on the practice field. Today, he doesn't know how much he'll impact the offense out of the gate, but looks forward to getting him up and moving.
"He hasn't been out there, so I can't tell you until we actually see it," Vrabel said. "He's been out for four weeks, so we'll get him back out there practicing and see if he's ready to go in a couple days. And if not, then 21-day window and we'll go from there."
Last week, the Patriots had just four wide receivers active against the Raiders (Kyle Williams, Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism III). This came after Mack Hollins, who injured his calf against Buffalo in Week 4, was placed on IR. The team declined to elevate Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner or Chandler Brayboy from the practice squad.
"Those receivers, they, they don't care who catches the ball," Vrabel said Sunday. "They don't care who catches a touchdown. They're just as excited for the next guy if it was them, and I think that that's truly what we wanna build around here, you know? And I gotta get it to be the entire team. I gotta get the entire team to look at it like that."
Once Brown returns to game action, he'll easily be the Patriots' top option in the passing game. His downfield abilities, along with the chemistry that he began to form with Drake Maye during the summer months , can help elevate this Patriots offense that's now starting to find its groove.
After Brown went down in Week 1, the Patriots' offense drastically changed for the worse. Maye, operating efficiently, threw three interceptions in the fourth quarter. While it's been more than a month away, there's no doubt in anyone's mind that adding Brown back into this huddle will help.
"Obviously, a great player. A.J., any time the presence in the huddle and the presence that he carries out there," Maye said after the Seahawks game.
The Patriots don't need to officially activate Brown off of IR this week , but because he's set to return to practice, he'll have three weeks to be added to the active roster. If the Patriots decide not to add him to the 53-man roster, he'll revert back to IR and his season will be over.
There is currently one open spot on the 53-man roster. The Patriots also decided to start offensive tackle Marcus Bryant's 21-day window this week.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame Quotes From Week 5 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
FOXBORO — Now sitting at 3-2, the New England Patriots have a sense of confidence around them that they might not have had a few weeks prior. A big win over the Las Vegas Raiders , where the offense put up a season-high 45 points, helped propel them onto a winning streak.
But the team enjoyed the victory for so long before their mindset shifted.
"Last week doesn't matter," Mike Vrabel said after the game. "We're gonna have to focus on the Jets in the division here at home. We still have a lot to improve and to clean up."
Here are some of the biggest quotes following the win, and what they mean for the direction of the Patriots heading into a divisional battle against the New York Jets.
It felt like the Patriots offense could do no wrong. They had their way with the Raiders defense, and Maye — who had struggled really up until Week 4 — looked like a changed man. He threw four touchdowns, ran for another and led the Patriots to their second-straight win. It was a victory that really felt like a more confident group.
Mike Vrabel on where the team has improved: "There's just a lot of things that we have to do to improve, and we have to come back. Again, the players, the effort in which they play with and being able to get stops in the red zone and finish off drives and not let penalties affect us, like, those are all positives. Those are things that crumbled us early in the year, especially offensively, and so we were able to overcome that. But eventually, you're not gonna be able to overcome some of the mistakes that we made and some of the penalties."
Drake Maye on how gratifying it was to score points on nearly every drive: "I'm just proud of these guys for stepping up. I mean, offense, defense, overall as a football team, that's a – I think we talk about identity with Coach Vrabel. I mean, that's a Coach Vrabel football team of stepping up, being ready to take advantage of your opportunity, and he always says when somebody gets their opportunity, he's excited to watch them play, and I think guys are living that."
Efton Chism III on the offense finding a rhythm: "We got so much belief in Drake and that he's one of the best quarterbacks in the league. We just got to continue to prepare each and every day lie that and, you know, not take Monday to Saturday for granted."
Gabe Jacas on his comfort level in the defensive scheme: "I'm 100% comfortable. I just play football. You know, it's a fun thing when you just out there playing free. You got 10 of the guys just willing to play for you and play behind you, and it's a good feeling."
Kindle Vildor on preparing to be signed from the practice squad all week: "I feel like I was able to prepare. Pretty much knew Wednesday when we got in, I knew that I'd be playing. So it was a typical game week for me, just able to watch the film and break it down on my own."
Robert Spillane on Drake Maye on the sideline: "It's fun to see Drake smiling big on the sidelines. That confidence is obviously back, so to be able to watch him lead and move the ball down the field was fun."
Last week's win was something that the Patriots can look back on and use as a defining step in a winning streak. Sure, Vrabel's comments about not going back in the past is true — but with a winnable game against the New York Jets coming up at home next Sunday, the Patriots can start to get this ball rolling.
Really, what kicked it all off was getting Maye to look like his usual self . In the first part of the year, he didn't have the same swagger that he did in 2025. Now that his teammates are commenting about how they've seen his confidence come back, the Patriots can start to ride the performances of their quarterback.
But there was plenty to clean up. Their 12 penalties racked up 116 total yards and they struggled to contain Brock Bowers for most of the game. All things considered, the 28-point win was far from perfect.
Getting some of the players that the Patriots expect to be big contributors rolling, like Jacas and A.J. Brown — who is eligible to be taken off of IR this week — will be major boosts to a team that starts to look like a real playoff contender after a shaky start.

title: Who Could Replace TreVeyon Henderson in Patriots Backfield? Here's 3 Options
full_text:
The New England Patriots didn't get good news when running back TreVeyon Henderson left their Week 5 win early with an ankle injury. They didn't get any better news when he was ruled out in the second half, and then even worse news when it was reported that he may miss a few weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
After already missing Henderson in the season opener , the last thing the Patriots — who are currently rolling to the tune of back-to-back wins — need are more injuries to hinder the offensive operation. But they'll have to make do without their second-year weapon.
It's easy to assume that Rhamondre Stevenson, who has been the starter all season, won't have the brunt of his carries impacted by Henderson's absence. In fact, he may be tasked with a bigger workload with a more precarious backfield behind him.
But the Patriots will need some valuable snaps out of their depth pieces. Here are all three of the internal options that they could turn to this week (and possibly into the future):
Kiner was the third option on the active roster and was the immediate option the Patriots turned to after Henderson's injury. But he didn't have a good first impression, fumbling his first snap of the game.
He would settle in, getting more chances in garbage time after the score bloated to 45-17 over the Las Vegas Raiders. Kiner would tie his season-high with six carries and rack up 52 yards — including a 32-yard rush late in the fourth. He also caught a pass for seven yards.
The Patriots traded a future pick for Kiner at the roster cutdown deadline, and he's been slotting in as a kick returner as well. He has the capabilities of making defenders miss at the point of attack, but will now have to prove it in a much larger capacity.
When Henderson didn't play against the Seattle Seahawks in Week 1, Kiner ran the ball six times for 11 yards. Even with the abilities to make things happen, I wouldn't expect a 10+ carry workload for the time being.
The Patriots had Larison all summer, and kept him on the practice squad after releasing him in August. He was elevated for his NFL debut in Week 1 when Henderson was inactive — a possibility this week.
In that game, Larison played just three offensive snaps and six special teams snaps. He would catch two passes for nine yards (including a first down) and return two kicks for 49 yards. Nothing too crazy to write home about, but something to make you wonder if there's more in the tank.
For the Patriots to have him play in Week 6 against the New York Jets, they'd need to activate him to the game day roster. That would be his second of three elevations for the season.
With only two running backs behind Henderson, the Patriots made a move Tuesday to add to their depth. The team announced that they signed Haskins — who they had in the preseason — to the practice squad.
Haskins, who played for Mike Vrabel on the Tennessee Titans to start his career, signed with the Patriots earlier in the summer ahead of the team's first preseason game. He would get on the field as a depth running back and kick returner, and would remain on the practice squad for the first two weeks of the regular season.
The addition of Haskins shows that this injury to Henderson could bleed into the next few games, which also includes a Week 7 primetime game against the Chicago Bears on a short week.
The Patriots will take the practice field for the first time this week on Wednesday afternoon, and Henderson's availability will be a big part of how the team can prepare their offense.

title: Could Elijah Ponder, Gabe Jacas be the Patriots Defensive Ends of the Future?
full_text:
One of the offseason needs identified most commonly by analysts for the New England Patriots was their lack of talent and development at edge rusher.
However, through five games this season, the personnel the Patriots are putting out on Sundays have shown that defensive ends may not be as big of a need as people thought.
Elijah Ponder, a second-year undrafted free agent from California Polytechnic, had arguably the most impactful performance on the defensive side of the ball on Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders. He got to the quarterback, sacking him two separate times and forced a fumble. He was PFF’s highest rated pass rusher from Week 5, notching a 92.2 grade.
It’s not just this small sample size that Ponder’s proven his legitimacy in. His pair of sacks brings his season total to 4.5 on the season, leading the team. He also has a team-high four QB knockdowns and he's tied for fourth on the team with total tackles (though he has the most tackles of all non-defensive backs and non-middle linebackers).
Across Ponder’s 15 games last season, he recorded 4 sacks. His emergence as the Patriots' best backfield havoc reaper will be a part of opponents’ game plan moving forward.
On the other side of the line of scrimmage from Ponder is Dre’Mont Jones. An offseason addition, the Patriots brought in Jones on a three-year, $36.5 million contract. Thus far, Jones’ impact has been minimal, recording just two solo tackles and one sack in the four games he’s appeared in.
Thankfully, another offseason addition for the Patriots has put in the work on the defensive front. The 55th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , Gabe Jacas, has been stellar at defensive edge. Using their second pick, the Patriots picked Jacas out of Illinois and, so far, he has not disappointed.
Jacas has already recorded 1.5 sacks, 17 total tackles, and had an interception in Week 2’s victory against Pittsburgh. In Week 4 against Buffalo, a fifth of Jacas’s pass rushes resulted in quarterback pressures (three of his 14 snaps). He also ranked fifth highest across the league that week in pass rush win rate.
In Sunday's dominant win over the Raiders , Ponder and Jacas combined for nine QB Pressures, according to Pro Football Focus. The two also had a total of eight combined tackles, and each had a 26.1% pass rush win rate.
Of all edge rushers who have been in the league for two seasons or less, Ponder ranks second in the NFL for total pressures with 18 and Jacas is fourth — in just five games, with 14 pressures.
Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas are DUDES pic.twitter.com/Hbj8saXg75
The pairs’ performances have provided relief to a Patriots front office, which has been desperate for elite edge play for years. Ponder and (24) and Jacas (22) may just have what it takes to grow into elite defenders and help the Patriots continue to win games on the defensive side of the ball.

title: Patriots TE Hunter Henry, IJM Host Annual 'Freedom to Play' Ping Pong Tournament
full_text:
BOSTON — Hunter Henry wanted to erase last year's defeat from his mind. He spent time in the New England Patriots locker room a week prior talking up his game, and then even before the tournament started, he had high hopes.
But at the end, the Patriots tight end fell in the final round of his second annual "Freedom to Play" ping pong tournament Monday evening.
In collaboration with the International Justice Mission — which works to help end slavery and human trafficking around the world — the event helped raise awareness and money for a cause near and dear to the tight end's heart.
"The more I learned about this organization and learned about the things that are going on across the world, I feel like it was important to kind of be a voice for the unheard," Henry told Patriots On SI.
Henry ran this event last year for the first time at SPIN Boston, helping raise hundreds of thousands of dollars for IJM. This year, along with plenty of current and former Boston athletes in attendance, the tournament was a smashing success.
Several of Henry's Patriots teammates were present to show up and participate in the ping pong festivities. Drake Maye (who Henry calls the second-best player on the team behind himself), Kevin Byard, Behren Morton, Tanner Arkin, Eli Raridon and Bryce Baringer all took to the tables. David Andrews , who played four seasons with Henry from 2021-24, also participated.
Rough showing for the rookies, as Eli Raridon and Behren Morton were both knocked out in the first round. Tanner Arkin lost to Drake Maye in the quarterfinals. pic.twitter.com/fQxSndvn4u
Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson , New England Revolution goalkeeper Matt Turner and Boston Celtics forward Luka Garza stopped by to watch.
"It's a very unifying cause," Mark Herzlich, former New York Giants linebacker and current director of IJM's Team Freedom, told Patriots On SI. "There's not a lot of political division around protecting kids from slavery, right? ... Hunter has done a great job of taking what is a heavy topic and bringing it into the light in a way that says, 'Hey, look, we're able to rescue kids. We're able to give these kids this freedom to play that we all have.'"
IJM's mission is to build safe communities around the world and eradicate slavery, as well as strengthening the justice system that can bring criminals to justice. It's an organization that Henry has been involved in for years, dating back to his time with the Los Angeles Chargers.
This is not the first time Henry and IJM have collaborated. Last year, for Henry's "My Cause, My Cleats" campaign, they worked with Daniel Nartey to help design his cleats for the Patriots' Monday Night Football game against the Giants . Nartey, a freed child slave from Ghana, created Henry's baby blue cleats.
In the past, Henry and his wife, Parker, have taken mission trips to Africa to see the work that the organization has done first hand. They've met survivors of child slavery and helped collaborate with local police officials to help stop the cycle of violence.
"That was really a turning point for us, being able to be there and be in the field and put faces to names and actually get to meet people," Parker Henry said. "People are not living with the same freedom and the same safety that we are, that we take so much advantage of."
Drake Maye falls in the semifinals, 11-8, to the defending champion — Julian, from Germany. Hunter Henry advances to the finals after a 15-13 win. He trailed 10-7 before a furious comeback. It’s a rematch of last year’s title game. pic.twitter.com/R1Mv2MVJsX
While the Patriots are currently sitting pretty at 3-2 and possessing second place in the AFC East, the results on the ping pong table weren't as consistent. Hunter Henry and Maye were, unsurprisingly, the best two players and each reached the semifinals. Arkin, an undrafted tight end, won his first round game before falling to Maye in the quarterfinals.
The rest of the players struggled. Baringer, Raridon, Byard Morton and Andrews all lost their first and only game of the tournament. Morton — the Patriots' rookie third-string quarterback — lost 11-1 in a tough outing.
At the end of the day, while Hunter Henry's competitive nature did take center stage , it took a back seat as he wanted to teach his teammates and others why this cause is so important to him.
"When I was young, I went to certain things and was able to learn a little bit about different causes," Hunter Henry said. "It's always good to get young guys and teach them some things, teach them different issues that are going on, maybe that they can support (and) maybe that they can be involved with in some aspect. It's always good to have the guys here."

title: Has Patriots WR Efton Chism III Earned More Playing Time?
full_text:
Behind four Drake Maye passing touchdowns on Sunday, the New England Patriots receiving arsenal proved they were ready to step-up to the challenge of a dwindled personnel group. Of the players asked to compete more than they usually would, none has stood out more than Efton Chism III.
A week ago in Buffalo, where the second-year undrafted free agent was asked to rise to the challenge of replacing Mack Hollins — who went down in the second half with a calf injury — Chism came up with two clutch receptions on the Patriots game-winning drive .
One for a first down, where Chism elevated vertically to haul in Maye’s pass, and the other for the game-winning touchdown on a thrilling 23-yard one-handed grab.
We can't stop thinking about the @EftonChism catch 😌 pic.twitter.com/Mj1gLu1DVU
With the Pats only suiting up four receivers in Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders, Chism naturally saw the most reps of his career in an NFL game, recording 57 offensive snaps. This was the second highest on the team , trailing only Romeo Doubs.
One of Chism’s more impressive plays came on a catch-and-lateral to TreyVeyon Henderson for a big third-down conversion.
Heads up backwards pass by Efton Chism III to help the Patriots get the 1st down pic.twitter.com/oN70ccHwNV
Chism recorded five receptions and 57 yards during his action-packed day against the Raiders. Both stat lines are the Eastern Washington alum’s NFL best.
On Monday, head coach Mike Vrabel teased the possibility of WR AJ Brown suiting up in Week 6’s game against the New York Jets. Brown, who went down with a high-ankle sprain in the season opener against Seattle, is currently on injured reserve, but eligible to be removed from the list this week.
If Brown does return for the Patriots this week, there is a possibility that Chism reverts back to his previous role in the receiver room, as the fifth or sixth option for Maye. In the first three weeks of the season, Chism only played 26 offensive snaps — which is 22% of his season-total 117 snaps.
However, with Chism’s proven impact on a heavier snap count, there is a likely chance that the 24-year-old earned a useful role among the receivers and will see the field almost as often as he did in the past two weeks.
While Chism’s frame and ability is quite different than that of Brown and Hollins , who are utilized most effectively when lining up as the split receiver, Chism could take the place of Patriots’ fourth-year receiver DeMario “Pop” Douglas.
Douglas recorded a 34-yard touchdown – his first of the season – in Sunday’s 45-17 victory against the Raiders, where he elevated past the defense in a busted coverage into a wide-open end zone. Despite receiving a 53% share of offensive snaps this season, Pop has caught just 13 passes for 147 yards.
The slot receiver played 20 less snaps than his positional counterpart Chism on Sunday, indicating that offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels may have a new favorite slot receiver.
This isn’t a suggestion that the Patriots will do-away with Douglas, who’s an unrestricted free agent in the 2027 offseason. Chism and Douglas are used simultaneously in multiple packages where the offense spreads out and an extra receiver is on the field.
But with Chism’s efficiency thus far, his added usage – even in a healthy receiver room, may lead to less snaps from players like Douglas or second-year receiver, Kyle Williams.
Detailing the impact of the receiver depth, Vrabel said after the game, “They're all ready to go. They all play different positions. That's not easy, you know, to learn three different positions and be able to step in there and block and make plays.”

title: Patriots Lose RB TreVeyon Henderson for Multiple Weeks With Ankle Injury
full_text:
It was announced Tuesday morning by ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson has been diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, following Sunday’s 45-17 victory of the Las Vegas Raiders , and will miss multiple weeks of action.
Henderson, who rushed four times for 22 yards and was the beneficiary of a 16-yard lateral reception from Efton Chism on Sunday, was removed from the game in the second quarter after being rolled up on by Raiders safety Jeremey Chinn during an 11-yard rush down the left sideline.
Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson suffered a high ankle sprain during Sunday’s win over the Raiders that now is expected to sideline him multiple weeks, per league sources. Henderson will not need surgery, and he is regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return… pic.twitter.com/MKDzQG9PZa
The running back is not expected to have surgery on his right ankle.
Henderson missed Week 1’s action against the Seattle Seahawks with an ankle injury suffered during Patriots training camp. Both ankle injuries sustained this season were to his right ankle.
Henderson was a second-round pick for the Pats in the 2025 draft out of Ohio State. In his rookie season, Henderson was the Patriots’ leading rusher, recording 911 yards and 9 touchdowns. In four games of play (including the two quarters of action in Sunday’s game), Henderson has 163 yards and one score.
Patriots running back depth chart without TreVeyon Henderson: - Rhamondre Stevenson - Corey Kiner - Lan Larison (PS) https://t.co/SXPa9JddWe
Now, the Patriots running back room is shortened to veteran rusher Rhamondre Stevenson and second-year player Corey Kiner, who recorded a fumble on Sunday while stepping in for Henderson. The Patriots practice squad includes Lan Larison, in his second-year with the Patriots after going undrafted in 2025.
The injuries for the Patriots have been a defining factor of their team identity this season, often relying on depth pieces to fill in the role for injured stars. Star wide receiver AJ Brown went down Week 1 against the Seahawks with a high-ankle sprain , and the injuries have continued to accumulate since.
The Patriots already have one running back listed on injured reserve with Myles Montgomery who suffered an undisclosed injury in training camp.
The team has lost 19 players to reserve rosters this season, with 13 actively on the injured reserve. It remains to be seen if Henderson’s injury will land him on the IR – which would mean he’d miss a minimum of four games.
The Patriots also lost starting left tackle Will Campbell on Sunday, who was diagnosed with a knee sprain and may miss several weeks.
With Henderson going down, New England will rely on Stevenson, in his sixth year with the team.
Mike Vrabel said about Stevenson: “We'll need Mondre's ability to create plays out in space and catch the ball," also saying how "it was good to see him fight to get back out there, being limited during the week.”
Stevenson was questionable to play in Sunday’s game with a knee injury , but collected 53 snaps where he rushed for 64 yards and hauled in three passes for 21 yards. Stevenson scored one of the Patriots six touchdowns on a 5-yard carry in the first quarter.

title: Gayle Benson Breaks Silence as Saints' 1-4 Start Puts Leadership Under Fire
full_text:
New Orleans Saints owner Gayle Benson declared the team's 1-4 start to the season was “not acceptable" on Monday, issuing a stern warning to leadership and staff as frustration mounts across the franchise and fan base.
Speaking at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club following Sunday's 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , Benson emphasized that accountability extends across the entire organization.
"That is not acceptable to me, and it falls short of what our fans deserve," Benson said. "I hear the frustration directed toward our team and our organization. It is not lost on me."
Benson emphasized that accountability begins with her but extends throughout the organization, specifically identifying General Manager Mickey Loomis , second-year head coach Kellen Moore , the coaching staff, and the players.
"I will not make excuses, and I will not accept this level of performance as our standard," Benson said. "I am committed to making the decisions necessary to improve this team."
While Benson did not say anything straightforward on whether organizational changes were imminent, her comments came nearly two years after she overruled Loomis and fired former coach Dennis Allen following a seven-game losing streak.
In what should have been a year of continued improvement from last season’s second-half success, along with an emerging quarterback in Tyler Shough , this year should have been full of great vibes. Instead, the Saints have been putrid throughout the first five games of the franchise's 60th anniversary season, which has featured several celebrations overshadowed by disappointing performances.
New Orleans suffered an embarrassing 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons during the 20th anniversary celebration of the historic 2006 "Domecoming" game. Six days later, the Saints lost to Minnesota during a ceremony honoring Drew Brees ' Pro Football Hall of Fame induction and his addition to the team's Ring of Honor.
At the end of both games, supporters of the Falcons and Vikings overtook the lower bowl of the stadium as “ATL” chants were heard throughout last Monday night, and “Skol” chants were also heard, but the latter were more audible because there were many Minnesota fans in attendance.
Benson referenced Brees' legacy while emphasizing the importance of restoring the standards that helped New Orleans win Super Bowl XLIV.
"It also includes a standard of preparation, discipline and accountability," Benson said. "The best way to honor that legacy is to uphold those standards today."
She also outlined the responsibilities of the organization's leadership:
"Kellen Moore and his coaches are responsible for preparing our players to perform. Mickey Loomis and our football staff are responsible for building a roster capable of sustained success. Our players are responsible for their preparation and execution. I am responsible for holding this organization accountable."
Despite her strong remarks, Benson acknowledged that public statements alone would not restore confidence in a franchise that has not reached the playoffs since 2020.
"Words will not restore our fans' confidence," Benson said. "Our performance must do that."
The Saints will attempt to end their losing streak Sunday against the New York Giants before traveling to Paris to face the Pittsburgh Steelers .
Benson concluded by reiterating her commitment to the franchise's supporters.
"We cannot change the results of our first five games. We are responsible for what we do next. I expect better. Our fans deserve better. And I am determined to see that we deliver it."

title: Social Media Rips Saints After Loss to Vikings, Lack of Homefield Advantage
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints' frustrating start to the 2026 season continued Sunday with a 23-13 loss to the undefeated Minnesota Vikings , dropping New Orleans to 1-4 and intensifying criticism surrounding second-year head coach Kellen Moore.
What was supposed to be a memorable afternoon celebrating Drew Brees' induction into the Saints Ring of Honor instead became another disappointing chapter in a season rapidly slipping away.
The Saints managed just 142 yards of total offense, while quarterback Tyler Shough struggled against Minnesota's relentless defensive pressure. Even an 87-yard fumble return touchdown by rookie safety Jonas Sanker wasn't enough to prevent New Orleans from suffering its fourth loss in five games.
The defeat also highlighted the Saints' deteriorating home-field advantage, with Vikings fans making their presence felt inside the Caesars Superdome.
As frustration continues to grow, three major talking points have emerged surrounding Moore's coaching, the defense's performance and the team's inability to protect its home field.
Of everyone facing criticism amid the New Orleans Saints' disappointing start, second-year head coach Kellen Moore has arguably received the most.
While Moore faced scrutiny throughout his first season, many fans remained patient, understanding that the franchise was undergoing a rebuild. However, that patience has steadily worn thin, particularly following the Saints' embarrassing loss to the Atlanta Falcons on the 20th anniversary of Domecoming .
The criticism reached a new level following Sunday's loss to Minnesota, marking New Orleans' third consecutive defeat, all coming inside the Caesars Superdome.
Much of the frustration centered on Moore's offensive play calling and his inability to make adjustments against Minnesota's relentless blitz packages.

Even Saints legend Drew Brees questioned the predictability of Moore's offense during Fox's broadcast, further fueling criticism of the struggling head coach.

What began as patience during a rebuilding process has increasingly turned into frustration, with fans questioning whether Moore is the right coach to lead the Saints into the future.

title: Drew Brees Questions Kellen Moore's Offense as Saints' Struggles Continue Against Vikings
full_text:
During the second half of the New Orleans Saints' 23-13 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , franchise legend Drew Brees openly criticized head coach Kellen Moore 's offensive approach on a nationwide broadcast.
Working as a Fox analyst shortly after being inducted into the Saints Ring of Honor at halftime, Brees pointed to New Orleans' inability to adjust against Minnesota's relentless blitzing defense .
Specifically, Brees called the Saints' first-down play calling "pretty predictable," questioned the lack of play-action passes, and criticized setup choices that left running back Alvin Kamara in unfavorable matchups.
"You gotta have answers," Brees said, highlighting the team's ongoing struggles in front of a national audience.
Quarterback Tyler Shough suffered through the toughest game of his fledgling career as the Saints (1-4) were held to a paltry 142 total yards—their lowest output since Week 2 of 2021.
Preliminary charting from Pro Football Focus showed Minnesota bringing blitz pressure on 23 of Shough's 27 dropbacks. The second-year passer managed only 16 completions on 25 attempts for 96 yards, throwing two interceptions and posting a career-worst 38.1 passer rating.
Head coach Kellen Moore admitted the team's offensive strategy was ineffective against the Vikings' aggressive scheme.
"I felt like we had a plan (against the blitz)," Moore stated. "Obviously the plan wasn't good enough. They did a better job."
"Obviously, that's on me."
The offensive struggles stemmed from an inability to sustain early momentum and adapt late. New Orleans opened with a promising 15-play, 66-yard scoring drive capped by a 1-yard Kendre Miller touchdown run, but the rushing attack completely stalled afterward. Over their next six drives, the Saints generated a mere 10 yards on the ground as penalties and negative plays continually forced them into obvious passing downs.
A reluctance to adjust the play calling aggravated these issues down the stretch. According to FTN Fantasy, New Orleans entered the contest utilizing play action on just 17.7% of offensive snaps—the fourth-lowest rate in the NFL. Against Minnesota, they called only one play-action pass, which gained 14 yards to Chris Olave .
Special teams miscues and missed chances further doomed the Saints. Jayden Price lost a fumble on the second-half opening kickoff, while Daniel Carlson missed a point-after attempt following an 87-yard fumble return touchdown by Jonas Sanker .
The defense's takeaway went unrewarded, while Minnesota (5-0) anticipated the Saints' aerial concepts, as demonstrated by Byron Murphy intercepting Shough on a late double move intended for Olave.
"They were really prepared for those moments," Shough remarked.
With a 1-4 record through five games, Moore faces mounting criticism during a difficult start to his second year, as New Orleans struggles with preparation, execution, and identity.
"Sometimes, you go through storms," Moore acknowledged. "Inevitably, storms end. But we're going through a little bit of one."

full_text:
The New Orleans Saints' struggles continued Sunday as they fell 23-13 to the Minnesota Vikings inside the Caesars Superdome.
The defeat dropped New Orleans to 1-4 for the second consecutive season, further exposing the growing problems facing second-year head coach Kellen Moore and a team that continues to take steps backward .
Here is the Good, Bad and Ugly from the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings.
In one of the few bright spots in the loss to the Vikings, Saints 2nd year safety Jonas Sanker provided a game-changing spark by returning a fumble 88 yards for a touchdown to tie the game at 13-13 late in the second quarter.
Sanker's touchdown demonstrated that New Orleans still has young players capable of making an impact despite a disappointing 1-4 start, though Daniel Carlson subsequently missed the go-ahead extra point.

The second-year defensive back has been tasked with helping rebuild a Saints defense that has undergone significant turnover, delivering an impressive defensive scoring play against Minnesota's undefeated squad.
Ultimately, the Saints' offense failed to capitalize on the momentum, leaving the defense with little margin for error as New Orleans dropped its fourth game of the season.
Shough has been the Saints’ best player throughout the season as he, along with a few others, is the bright spot on what is a bad football team at the moment and if it weren’t for him this season would be a complete disaster.
However, his performance was not good enough for New Orleans to win this game.

"It was obviously very difficult," Shough said of going up against Minnesota’s defense. "They presented a lot of looks. That's what they're extremely good at. I felt like we were ready for all those looks. We just didn't execute in some of those moments, and now we're second and 20, or third and 15, and — I mean, you're not — those odds are not really in your favor for those situations.
"And we got to be in those third-and-six, third-and-five, third-and-three ranges, where we can convert and dictate tempo. While the Saints’ defense allowed a putrid Minnesota offense to put up its best numbers of the season, the most concerning aspect of Sunday's defeat occurred off the field.
The game served as a stark reminder that the Caesars Superdome no longer offers the formidable environment it was once famous for.
Historically, New Orleans boasted one of the premier home-field advantages in the NFL, where deafening crowd noise and an unyielding Saints team made life miserable for visiting opponents.
That distinct edge appears to have vanished.
The Saints have lost all of their four home games this year (including preseason), extending a troubling pattern that began after former head coach Sean Payton left the team following the 2021 campaign.
Since Payton's departure, New Orleans has posted a sub-.500 record of 15-21 at home, managing just a single winning season in the Superdome (5-3 in 2023).
The situation has grown even more dire recently, as the Saints have dropped 14 of their last 17 home contests since the start of 2024.
Yet, the venue's atmosphere on Sunday was perhaps just as unsettling as the loss itself.
A massive contingent of traveling Vikings supporters made their presence felt, filling the Superdome with loud, distinct "Skol" chants.

For an organization that built its reputation on creating a hostile environment for opponents, watching opposing fans dominate sections of the stadium underscored the team's ongoing decline.
Understandably, persistent losing eventually takes a toll on crowd enthusiasm and game-day attendance.
With little evidence of progress on the field, fan frustration continues to mount alongside the team's home struggles.
Reestablishing a true home-field advantage will require more than past glory or fan loyalty.
It must be reclaimed by winning football games.
Until Moore and the Saints deliver better results in front of their home crowd, visiting teams and their fans will continue to feel right at home in New Orleans.
