title: Jets Rookie and Sophomore Week 6 Power Rankings: Kenyon Sadiq Falls to Lowest Ranking of the Season
full_text:
After dropping the last three games, head coach Aaron Glenn and the New York Jets were in a must-win situation against the Cleveland Browns. Despite sloppy conditions, the team came away victorious, narrowly defeating the Browns 17-13.
There were plenty of positives from the game: Braelon Allen and Garrett Wilson carried the offense with their playmaking, while the Jets’ defense wreaked havoc for Deshaun Watson, sacking him eight times.
Several of the Jets' rookies and sophomores stood out in the win, playing critical roles.
With that said, let’s take a look at where every Jets rookie and second-year player ranks heading into Week 6.
Note: Anez Cooper and V.J. Payne are currently excluded from the list. Both Cooper and Payne are on injured reserve, but are eligible to return after missing the first four games of the season.
A torn ACL in Week 2 ended Arian Smith’s sophomore season prematurely. Still, the former 2025 fourth-round selection didn’t impress on offense or special teams in limited action.
Coming off an underwhelming rookie season, Smith needed to play well to solidify his standing in New York for 2027. But with other receivers getting an opportunity while he’s recovering, it’ll be difficult for the former Georgia Bulldog to earn a role once he returns.
Smith must progress as a receiver if he wants to remain with Gang Green.
Geno Smith hasn’t been bad, nor has he been great either.
Through five games, Smith has completed 72.7% of his passes for 1,084 yards and six touchdowns. The 14-year veteran has been a solid game manager and has kept the ball out of harm's way.
Against the Browns, Smith kept the offense afloat, completing 56.7% of his passes for 182 yards and a touchdown. It wasn’t flashy, but he did enough to get them a win.
As long as Smith keeps New York in games and continues to protect the ball, we won’t be seeing the team turn to Cade Klubnik anytime soon.
While the rookie will remain on the sidelines, he can use this time to learn and develop behind the veteran.
For the third straight week, Kiko Mauigoa was inactive with a quadriceps injury. Even if he were active, the former Miami Hurricane wouldn’t have played on defense, as New York has solely depended on Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood at linebacker.
The second-year player has yet to play a single defensive snap this season, and at this point the only way he does is if either Davis or Sherwood gets hurt. But even that’s not guaranteed, as the Jets could turn to Jaden Keller or Trevin Wallace.
For now, Mauigoa will remain exclusively on special teams.
With Week 5 in the books, Omar Cooper Jr. is officially eligible to come off injured reserve this week. He could return to play in the team’s game against the Patriots, but it all depends on where he is in his recovery.
New York could desperately use the former Indiana Hoosier. Since Adonai Mitchell and he were sidelined, the Jets haven’t gotten much production outside of Garrett Wilson.
The team urgently needs consistent play from one of its pass catchers to ease the pressure off Wilson. Cooper gave us a small glimpse of his playmaking ability in Week 1, turning a short pass into a 30-yard gain to set up a touchdown a few plays later.
Hopefully, New York’s first round choice returns to the field sooner rather than later.
With the Jets adding Dane Belton and Minkah Fitzpatrick to the safeties room, along with re-signing Andre Cisco, it was going to be hard for Malachi Moore to see reps on defense.
So far, the second-year safety out of Alabama has played just nine defensive snaps. Despite this, Moore has put his head down and has earned his keep on special teams.
Yet again, Moore recorded another special teams tackle, putting his total at five for the season. He’s been one of Gang Green’s best players on the unit, earning a 71 special teams grade, per Pro Football Focus.
Given how the safeties group has played, Moore will remain out of the rotation. But if someone gets hurt, Moore is deserving of a few snaps.
Last week at this time, it seemed like D’Angelo Ponds would make his first career start against the Browns after Jarvis Brownlee Jr. entered the NFL’s concussion protocol.
However, Brownlee quickly progressed through it and was a full participant in the team’s practice, effectively ending Ponds’ chances of playing any defensive snaps.
The former Indiana Hoosier ended up with just two, primarily playing on the special teams. With the current cornerback group impressing with its performance in coverage, Ponds will remain New York’s top backup.
After missing the last three games with a thumb injury, Mason Taylor returned against Cleveland , posting season highs in receptions (3) and yards (24).
While his numbers weren’t flashy, he finished second on the team in yards and targets with three. With Cooper and Mitchell still sidelined, and Sadiq leaving the game with a concussion, Taylor must raise his game.
After leading New York in receptions last year, he’s had a rough start to Year 2 and needs to become more of a productive player if the team wants to remain competitive.
Two weeks ago, the Jets finally unleashed Kenyon Sadiq. The former Oregon Duck balled out, recording seven receptions for 105 yards and a touchdown.
Since then, however, Sadiq has largely flown under the radar. In the last two games, he’s posted just two catches (seven targets) for three yards and a fumble. With Taylor back in the lineup against the Browns, Sadiq took a step back, playing in just 13 snaps compared to Taylor’s 41.
A concussion limited his usage, but New York clearly prefers Taylor over him. In the first two games, Taylor played 78 snaps, while Sadiq appeared in 55.
Still, it’s early to say whether he’ll play next week against the Patriots, but hopefully Sadiq returns to full health soon.
Darrell Jackson Jr. had remained relatively quiet through the first four games. In 85 defensive snaps, Jackson recorded seven tackles and zero pressures.
With David Onyemata on injured reserve, the Jets hoped that the former Florida State Seminole would step up in his absence. Against Cleveland, Jackson finally emerged.
The 2026 fourth-round selection made his presence felt against the Browns, recording four tackles, a sack, two pressures, and two pass deflections in 29 defensive snaps.
This was Jackson’s best all-around game by far. If he can replicate similar success against New England, it’ll be hard to take away his reps once Onyemata returns.
One of the key matchups heading into this game was Azareye’h Thomas versus Denzel Boston.
Boston quickly emerged as quarterback Deshaun Watson’s favorite target downfield, hauling in 13 receptions for 284 yards and two touchdowns. Limiting him and his big-play ability was critical if New York was to win.
Thomas did his part, as Boston didn’t record a catch when lined up against him. For the day, Thomas allowed just two receptions (five targets) for 28 yards, earning a 76.4 coverage grade, per PFF .
Not only has Thomas excelled in coverage, but he’s also played well against the run, earning a 68.7 run-defense grade, ranking 41st among 102 cornerbacks.
With his play so far, the former Florida State Seminole continues to prove he’s among the Jets’ best foundational pieces.
David Bailey has had an up-and-down start to his rookie season.
He was generating pressure in the first two games, recording eight pressures and two sacks. In the last two games, however, Bailey logged just three pressures.
Against the Browns, the former Texas Tech star pass rusher finally had his breakout game.
Bailey dominated Cleveland’s offensive line, registering eight pressures and three sacks, earning an 85.4 coverage grade, per PFF .
He was the best player on the field for the Jets. With New York going up against its division rival next week, Gang Green will need the No. 2 overall pick to be just as impactful to win.
Offensive linemen don’t get the same love as skill players, but they also play a critical role in team success.

title: Sirianni-Hurts Duo Suddenly Reminding Eagles Fans of Painful History
full_text:
Before Nick Sirianni and Jalen Hurts arrived on the scene, the Philadelphia Eagles were no strangers to the funky loss.
Losses that had fans up for nights on end wondering how the team blew the game. Defeats that had fans wondering how positive the future would be. Sure, the team had won a Super Bowl during that time frame, but the Eagles had a history of losing in some of the most bizarre ways.
For five years, things were different. Sirianni had built a culture that never seemed to play down to competition. They had a quarterback who would never make the bone-headed play. Every time the Eagles were in a clutch situation, they always seemed to make the obvious and easy call to execute.
What makes the team's 2-3 start to the season so frustrating for Eagles fans isn't just the fact that they are on a three-game losing streak, or have the worst second-half offense in recent memory.
No, the underlying frustration in Philadelphia is because, for the first time in five years, Sirianni and Hurts look like every other coach and quarterback duo that had come before him. The logic has been lost. The clutch gene, nonexistent.
It's frustrating, because the most successful QB-HC duo in team history has finally come down to earth.
There are detractors to both Sirianni and Hurts citing the fact that it was general manager Howie Roseman who built such dominant rosters for the team over the last five years. The argument is that the head coach and quarterback only needed to not screw up, and they would win a lot of games.
Those arguments are disingenuous compared to what Eagles fans have gone through over the last nearly three decades.
Andy Reid, for example, had a top-five defense for most of his career, a franchise QB, a great running back, and failed to win a Super Bowl because he made decisions in big games that hurt the team. Chip Kelly lasted three seasons in Philadelphia. Doug Pederson caught lightning in a bottle, but was never able to duplicate the success in later seasons.
Pick a frustrating loss: every past head coach in team history has had them:
Sunday's loss to Jacksonville was not uncommon in Eagles history. In fact, they are a dime a dozen.
It's not just in Eagles history either. Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay are considered two of the most elite coaches in football right now. Shanahan has a penchant for losing in big moments, and McVay hasn't been back to the Super Bowl since 2021. During that same stretch, the Eagles won a Super Bowl by 18, and went to a second one.
The level of consistent domination the franchise has put forth over five years under Sirianni and Hurts is unprecedented. In many ways, Eagles fans should be more patient and appreciative of the two going forward.
But that's not how this city is. People will argue about needing a new coach and quarterback so long as the losing continues.
The frustration stems, though, not just based on execution or missed calls from the coaching staff. It's based on the fact no one has won quite like Sirianni and Hurts.
And for the first time in years, it seems like they both are running out of wins.

title: What to Expect as Eagles Open Practice Window for Four Players on IR
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Help could soon be on the way for the Eagles, after the team opened the practice windows for four players before Wednesday’s first practice of Week 6.
Those players are left guard Landon Dickerson, cornerback Jakorian Bennett, and tight ends Grant Calcaterra and rookie second-round pick Eli Stowers. The Eagles have 21 days before having to make a decision to add them back onto the 53-man roster or shut them down for the season.
Some tough decisions will need to be made to find room on the roster when the time comes.
Here’s a closer look at the four who could return:
Dickerson: The three-time Pro Bowl left guard played in the opener but didn’t play well. He said he had a bone bruise in his right knee and admitted he was embarrassed by his performance in that Week 1 win against the Commanders.
“You guys know Landon well, he works hard, he's determined to get back, and I think he's done a nice job taking care of his body to get himself back,” said head coach Nick Sirianni before Wednesday’s practice and before the news was made official. “Landon's a hell of a player and he's been a hell of a player for us.”
The move to put Dickerson on IR created turmoil on the offensive line. Cam Jurgens was moved from center to left guard. Then new center Drew Kendall, in his second season from Boston College, was plugged in at center.
Jurgens was eventually traded and, when Kendall couldn’t play in London, Willie Lampkin made his first career start at left guard and Jake Majors was elevated from the practice squad to make his first pro start.
Getting Dickerson back would be a most welcome addition.
Stowers: In the days leading up to the opener, the rookie said he expected to have a role against Washington. Then, hours later, he was placed on IR with a quad strain. He still needs to develop, but he should make the team feel better at the position.
Dallas Goedert missed two games with a knee injury, and the Eagles signed Zach Ertz to try to make up for some of the offense that was gone when Goedert had to sit. Stowers is an offensive-minded tight end, albeit one who is in just his third year playing the position, and was the John Mackey Award winner for the nation’s best tight end while at Vanderbilt.
Calcaterra: Another offensive-minded tight end, who returned this offseason on a one-year contract. He will provide solid depth.
Bennett: The cornerback hasn’t done much since the Eagles acquired him in a trade last summer, but like Calcaterra, he could provide depth if needed.

title: Sean Mannion Seemingly Teases Role Change for Carson Steele
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA - The answer to helping their suddenly young and inexperienced offensive line is right under the Eagles’ noses. That answer is Carson Steele. Design some plays where he is a fullback. Can there be anything more obvious than that? Steele can play fullback. He did it some while in Kansas City.
Sean Mannion was asked if it was a possibility this week when the Eagles host the Carolina Panthers.
“He did a phenomenal job in the preseason,” said the Eagles offensive coordinator. “He's wearing a ton of different hats with us out on the practice field, especially as we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries. He's a versatile player who can do a lot of nice things for us. We're looking to use all of our guys in every way possible. So, that's certainly something we're considering.”
Mannion’s response to that question on Tuesday sounds like there could be some snaps for Steele at fullback. That possibility could help an offensive line that started rookie right tackle Markel Bell and two undrafted free agents, left guard Willie Lampkin and center Jake Majors, against the Jacksonville Jaguars.
It was the first start in the careers of Lampkin, 24, and Majors, also 24, who was elevated from the practice squad to start in place of Drew Kendall, who is battling a knee injury and missed Week 5.
Steele was elevated from the practice squad last Sunday and played 20 special teams snaps, but zero on offense.
Mannion said the game plan was supposed to be pass-heavy, and it was, with Jalen Hurts attempting a season-high 40 passes, completing 21 of them for 220 yards, and a 62-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper.
The Eagles ran the ball just 18 times for a measly 22 yards (1.2 yards per attempt). Hurts had just two yards on two runs.
“I think we're always looking for ways to integrate him into the run game,” said Mannion. “Some of it is dependent on the opponent and the fronts they're giving us, the looks you're getting.”
The script could easily flip in Week 6, with the Panthers coming in with one of the worst run defenses in the NFL, ranking No. 31 of 32 teams.
Carolina gives up 168.4 yards on the ground per game, with an average of 5.4 yards per run.
It would help if the Eagles got Saquon Barkley back, but even if they do, Steele could have a fullback role if he is elevated again.
“You go into each game thinking, 'how are we going to win?'” said Mannion. “Different teams present different challenges in terms of their personnel, in terms of their alignments. So, that plays a part in the number of attempts, and you're always adjusting in terms of what you think will help us move the ball in the next series in terms of how you're calling it, run and pass.
“I feel confident this group's going to be able to move the ball. We had some nice runs earlier on in the run game. We just need to keep sustaining that. Then honestly, some of it isn't necessarily a negative. You feel better about some of the other calls you have on the sheet, and you get to those.”

title: Eagles' Biggest Strength Has Suddenly Become a Major Concern
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — For years, the Eagles’ offensive line has been the foundation of the organization’s sustained success.
That began to erode last season, and the once-dominant group derailed early in the 2026 campaign with injuries continuing to chip away at veteran Pro Bowl selections Landon Dickerson and Cam Jurgens, with the latter having since been traded to Baltimore. Meanwhile, future Hall of Famer Lane Johnson retired and Jurgens’ replacement at center, Drew Kendall, is dealing with a knee injury that cost him Sunday’s loss against Jacksonville in London.
The replacements – Willie Lampkin at left guard, Jake Majors at center and Markel Bell at right tackle – struggled mightily against the Jags.
The period of rapid transition, and the team’s ability to stay competitive in what’s shaping up as a flawed NFC East will hinge in large part on whether the young, lightly experienced group can develop quickly enough to hold the fort.
Moving forward, that trio is likely to remain part of the conversation—either as starters or high-leverage depth—until Dickerson returns, GM Howie Roseman adds reinforcements, or more likely, both.
Lampkin, the 5-foot-11 interior lineman who has drawn praise for his leverage and physicality since training camp, and Majors, the undrafted former Texas center who spent most of last season on the practice squad, almost have to be short-term responses to the attrition.
Bell, the third-round rookie drafted as a potential long-term successor at right tackle, is already in line to hold that spot for the foreseeable future following Johnson’s departure.
The combination represents a stark departure from the veteran-laden lines that fueled recent Eagles success.
Jordan Mailata remains the clear veteran anchor at left tackle but was withered by what he called a “week from hell” in response to Johnson and Jurgens being removed from the locker room on consecutive days. Tyler Steen has provided continuity at right guard, but the other three spots have been an issue, especially in pass protection.
Dickerson is eligible to return as early as this week against the Carolina Panthers, which would allow the Eagles to reinsert an established left guard. However, it may be a leap to expect Dickerson to regain his previous standard. Kendall is also expected to re-enter the mix once healthy.
Until those pieces return and prove durable, however, Lampkin, Majors, and Bell are the primary options available to coach Nick Sirianni and the staff.
The reliance on three players with this kind of minimal combined starting experience creates a very narrow margin for error as the Eagles try to reverse their early-season trajectory.
Roseman has long prioritized offensive line depth and has indicated the team remains focused on competing this year . To do that, additional investment on the offensive line will be needed.

title: Eagles' Snap Counts vs. Jaguars:  Biggest Winners, Losers & Role Changes in Week 5
full_text:
It was a game the Eagles deserved to lose, then suddenly, a game they deserved to win, only to lose in the end on a 57-yard field goal as time expired in a 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London on Sunday. The loss left the Eagles at 2-3, their first time below .500 since Nick Sirianni’s first year as the head coach in 2021.
Here are five observations from the snap counts:
The Eagles’ young offensive linemen got a heavy dose of experience by playing all 62 offensive snaps. They had combined for just 64 in their careers. Bell, of course, is a third-round rookie, but Lampkin and Majors were undrafted, and these were their first career starts. There is still developmental work to be done, and continuity and chemistry to build, but those things take time.
“These are three young players that we have a ton of confidence in,” said OC Sean Mannion. “They're talented. They're getting their first taste of real action. I think they're going to keep getting better. We feel good about the depth of this group while we're kind of weathering the storm through some of these injuries.”
With Dallas Goedert back after missing two games with a knee injury, the Eagles don’t seem invested in getting Ertz many reps. He got seven in London, and he is out of practice squad elevations, so if the Eagles want to keep him, they need to add him to the 53-man roster this week, cut him, or leave him on the practice squad. He needs eight more catches to set the franchise record for career receptions.
The receiver played a career-high 53 snaps. He has made the most of his reps all year, with four touchdowns on just seven catches, making him the first receiver in Eagles history to have four TDs in the first five games since Jeremy Maclin in 2014.
Davis was given a huge raise in the offseason, but his snap count is on the low side. He got just 35 on Sunday. Vic Fangio talked last week about trying to get him more time, but said this week that the defense was in a lot of nickel.
“Not much base, which only two of those guys play, so it kind of becomes three for two with him, [Moro] Ojomo, and Jalen [Carter]," said Fangio. "So those three, and then when you add the other two guys, it's going to spread it out some.”
He spent his whole career as a slot cornerback, but Moore was thrust into a safety role after Michael Carter left with an abdominal injury. Moore played 44 snaps and made five tackles.
“When you consider the lack of background, he's never played safety in his career, gets here after training camp, limited reps with our defense, he's getting some in scout team, I thought he did a pretty damn good job considering the circumstances,” said Fangio.

title: McMullen: Eagles Shouldn’t Bench Jihaad Campbell (Upside Is Too High)
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Vic Fangio spent part of Tuesday doing what defensive coordinators often do when reporters start sniffing around a lineup change: clarifying, downplaying, and perhaps even adding some revisionism to what's going on at the linebacker position in Philadelphia.
Yes, the Eagles planned to get Jeremiah Trotter Jr. on the field for some snaps opposite Zack Baun against the Jaguars in London .
The Eagles’ defensive coordinator confirmed as much at his weekly press briefing on Tuesday. However, Fangio said there was no plan to start Trotter over Campbell—a claim the veteran defensive mind called “an out-and-out lie.”
The new rotation never got off the ground after Trotter was ejected after scuffling with Jacksonville linebacker Bryan Thomas Jr. on the opening kickoff.
Because of circumstances, Campbell started in and finished the 19-17 loss to the Jags, playing 62 of the 72 defensive snaps. His 47.6 overall grade on Pro Football Focus was not impressive , and when asked about the second-year player’s performance by Eagles On SI, Fangio claimed Campbell “played okay.”
That’s not a ringing endorsement coming off the news that Trotter has earned more playing time with a nice performance against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4.
It’s also not a reason to start treating a 22-year-old 2025 first-round pick like a developmental project who’s running out of runway, or at least it shouldn’t be.
Campbell arrived in Philadelphia with the kind of size, speed, and length that make personnel executives take notice (6-foot-3, 235 lbs, and a 4.52-second 40-yard dash). The Alabama product also produced as a rookie when given the chance, posting 80 tackles, an interception, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery while earning All-Rookie recognition and grading out as the No. 15 of 88 LBs ranked by PFF .
This season, the PFF grades are shaky (No. 61 of 72), and coverage has been an issue at times. That’s real. It’s also the normal growing-pain portion of a young linebacker’s career, not a referendum on Campbell's ceiling.
Trotter, a more instinctive but less athletic option, has earned more playing time . Fangio is right about that. When Baun was out against the Rams, the local legacy as the son of the "Axe Man," Jeremiah Trotter Sr., filled in and delivered a 15-tackle day.
Fangio is a stickler for fundamentals and discipline, so it’s no surprise he seems to be gravitating toward the safer option who understands the scheme better.
A series-based rotation that keeps both fresh and gives Fangio a different look could be smart football and good roster management. However, linebacker is typically not a rotational position, so this can’t turn into a soft benching or even a signal that Campbell is on a short leash.
The Eagles moved on from the popular Nakobe Dean in free agency specifically to clear a path for Campbell. They traded up to draft him. They have already seen the traits—range, closing speed, the ability to blitz from different spots—that made him a first-round investment.
Linebackers who combine that athletic profile with the mental processing required in a Fangio defense do not grow on trees. You don’t accelerate that process by taking away snaps and eroding the confidence of a potential difference-maker.
Fangio has been careful not to draw comparisons to previous situations, like veteran Oren Burks holding off Trotter when Dean was injured on the road to Super Bowl LIX.
Campbell is not Dean, but he’s younger and more explosive, while still learning the nuances of Fangio’s complicated scheme.
Young players with Campbell’s upside improve when they play, not when they watch. Competition is healthy; the systematic reduction of a role is how you waste a draft pick.

title: Eagles' Michael Clay Reveals Thoughts on Ill-Fated Kickoff in London
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Leaks were springing up everywhere, and Michael Clay did his best to patch them anyway he could—chewing gum, an index finger, a thumb, personnel changes—yes, the last one.
The Eagles’ special teams coordinator was already without a couple of players on his unit, players who had been ruled out before kickoff against the Jaguars at London’s Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in Week 5. He then lost Jeremiah Trotter, Jr., when he was ejected on the opening kickoff; then Will Shipley and Michael Carter went out with injuries early in the game .
It’s not an excuse. It’s just the reality of the situation. It’s why head coach Nick Sirianni’s decision not to let Jake Elliott kick the ball out of the end zone right after the Eagles took a 17-16 lead with eight seconds left to play was so mystifying.
“You respect anybody that's going out there to jump on the grenade,” Clay said about what it meant to him that Sirianni turned himself into the fall guy. “But it's not just him. He takes a lot of heat, which I respect, but, obviously, I'm the special teams coordinator here, and we didn't get the job done."
Clay was juggling personnel throughout. He was on the sideline just before the ill-fated kickoff that led to the kickoff return that set up the Jags’ walk-off win on a 57-yard field goal by Cam Little.
“You're just trying to move around puzzle pieces,” Clay said. “You try to put personnel in your best spot. I think you saw I moved Kelee (Ringo) from the one to the four to the five, tried to put our best players in certain spots to make some plays. At times it worked out, and in the one spot that it didn't, it burned us, and that's on me as a coach.”
Jonathan Jones played a lot of special teams during his 11-year career, but not so many special teams snaps since 2022. He was on the final kickoff return, which was just his fourth special teams snap of the game. The cornerback played just three snaps in last week’s loss to the Rams.
So, he may have been one of those break-glass-in-case-of-emergency players Clay ran out there for the final kickoff.
Jones made the tackle, but had to chase Ameer Abdullah from behind to make the play. The irony is that if he had taken one second longer to bring Abdullah to the ground, time would have expired and the Eagles would be 3-2, not 2-3.
That’s a tough ask for any player in that situation, however.
“When you're in the heat of the moment, you're in full trail mode (you’re just thinking), ‘Let me get this guy down,’” Clay said. “I don't think anybody's gonna look up at the clock simultaneously then get the guy down who's running full speed ahead. An extra second off at some point in the game—you're not talking about this—but it would have been a perfect storm to happen.
“You know, they played well for 59 minutes, and the last eight seconds we didn't; we didn't do our job in terms of the kickoff coverage. At times, we got too deep in our coverage, didn't get off blocks, didn't make tackles when we needed to, and that's more on myself than anything else.”

title: Eagles Edge Hopes Hinging on Jalyx Hunt 'Miracle' and Jonathan Greenard Return
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – It didn’t look good when Jalyx Hunt’s left leg got bent backward, and he landed on it during the final play of the first half in London on Sunday. It wasn’t.
“It'll be pretty miraculous for Jalyx to play this week,” said defensive coordinator Vic Fangio on Tuesday as the Eagles begin preparation to host the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.
It sounds, however, like Hunt could be pushing to make a miracle happen.
“He's gonna be pushing the envelope and making the medical people clear him,” said Fangio. “He's not gonna be one of those guys that's gonna be hesitant to come back.”
Hunt stayed down on the field after the injury, as players and coaches exited through the tunnels at halftime. A cart was brought out to help him, but he chose to be helped off, leaning on two members of the training staff and keeping weight off his injured leg.
Fangio's comment about pushing the envelope to play could be read as a shot at Jonathan Greenard. Listed as questionable heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars, Greenard tried to test his injured ankle before kickoff at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The team’s trainers and Howie Roseman met with Greenard in the end zone, and the outside linebacker looked to be shaking his head back and forth, seemingly indicating he wouldn’t be able to play.
So, he missed yet another game, and he has played in just two of the team’s five games this season.
“Hopefully he'll be ready to go this week, but we gotta see,” said Fangio.
If he can’t, and Hunt doesn’t create a miracle, the Eagles' edge group will be down to Nolan Smith, Arnold Ebiketie, and A.J. Epenesa. The Eagles also have Mason Reiger and Joshua Weru on the practice squad.
Reiger, who played at Louisville, was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Miami Dolphins after the draft, but was released with an injury. Weru had a nice preseason, but he had never played football until signing with the Eagles via the NFL’s International Pathway Program. Growing up in Kenya, Weru played rugby.
Neither player, however, are Hunt or Greenard.
Hunt has yet to unleash the potential he showed during training camp in August and is looking for his first sack. Still, he is good at providing pressure on a quarterback and setting an edge in the run game.
Greenard was acquired in the offseason to replace Jaelan Phillips, whom the Eagles tried to re-sign in free agency, but he instead chose a better deal with the Panthers. Phillips has sacks in back-to-back games and has played 70 percent of the defensive snaps for Carolina.
“Greenard was gonna take a lot of (Phillips’ playing time and production), and unfortunately, he got hurt in our weight room before training camp started, missed all of camp, missed the first few games,” said Fangio. “Just started practicing and then got the ankle injury. So that was gonna be a big piece of it.”

title: More Bad News On Eagles' Injury Front: Will Shipley Will Miss Time
full_text:
If the Eagles are going to dig out of this three-game losing streak that has left them below .500 for the first time in five years, they are going to have to find a way to do it with running backs who started the season on their practice squad, because Will Shipley is expected to miss a couple of weeks.
ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday’s loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks.
The injury likely happened on Shipley’s first regular-season touchdown run, a 2-yard burst up the middle behind Willie Lampkin that tied the score at 7-7 in the second quarter of what would become a 19-17 loss to the Jags in London. He was done after just 13 snaps, leaving Dameon Pierce to man the backfield duties alone.
Pierce was added to the 53-man roster on Oct. 7. He has 45 games of experience. In his Eagles debut, he averaged 1.3 yards on 11 carries for 14 yards.
“We've had our eye on him for a very long time, since he came out of college,” said head coach Nick Sirianni, on the same day he and his team flew to England. “When you go through a draft, you only get, what, six, seven, eight picks or whatever it is that year?
“There’re a lot of guys you end up loving that it's like, 'Oh man, he's going to be good for them.' …He brings constant energy to the football team. He's obviously a very talented player and works extremely hard and runs extremely hard. I'm excited for his opportunity.”
The Eagles, who placed Tank Bigsby on injured reserve last week, need to cross their fingers that Saquon Barkley can return for Sunday’s visit from the Carolina Panthers.
Barkley missed Week 5 with a hamstring injury suffered early in the Week 4 loss to the Rams. The running back, who just two years ago ran for more than 2,000 yards and helped the Eagles win a Super Bowl, is averaging 5.1 yards per carry when he’s been able to play, but he’s only played 91 snaps through five weeks.
He’s already had a stinger that sidelined him early against the Titans in Week 2, and now he’s dealing with his latest setback. When he returns, he will find an entirely different offensive line blocking for him, with Lane Johnson retired and Cam Jurgens traded.
Carson Steele was elevated from the practice squad for the game and perhaps he may need to play a bigger role in the short-term.
Steele has fullback experience, so it was somewhat surprising that he didn’t have any offensive role against the Jaguars as a lead blocker, especially with an offensive line that is still trying to build continuity and chemistry. He got 20 snaps on special teams.

title: Eagles Report Card: Grading Every Position Group and Head Coach After Five Games
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles have lost three in a row and, at 2-3, are under .500 for the first time in five years. The grades won’t look pretty on the team’s report card, and perhaps a litany of injuries is the reason.
Still, the offense has been dreadful in the second half. It's averaging 4.6 points, 97.4 total yards, and has 5 three-and-outs. All three stats are last in the NFL.
Here grades for each position and the head coach:
After looking like an MVP in the first two games, leading a game-winning touchdown drive that ended in a touchdown pass with just nine seconds left against the Titans, Jalen Hurts’ play has dropped. He hasn’t taken to Sean Mannion’s overhaul of the offense as quickly as one would have hoped, and he doesn’t always seem to see the entire field. His rebuilt offensive line could be part of that, but his decision-making hasn’t been where it needs to be, and his completion rate is a career-low 57.8 percent.
His ability to pick up yards with his legs has been neutralized, rushing only 23 times – most of that on scrambles from the pocket – 101 yards and one TD.
Still, he gets credit for his eight touchdowns to just three interceptions, as well as the job he did in the first two wins.
Saquon Barkley has been hurt early in two games and missed one already. At 29, can he rebound and still help this team when he gets healthy?
Meanwhile, Tank Bigsby is on injured reserve, and Will Shipley could be put on IR too, after E SPN’s Adam Schefter reported that Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars and could miss multiple weeks. That leaves practice squad players Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele to carry the load.
The grade goes up from a ‘C’ because of Darius Cooper , who has four touchdowns on just seven catches. The Eagles haven't had a receiver since Jeremy Maclin in 2014 catch four touchdowns in the first five games of a season.
Tay Wicks has been decent, but the Rams’ Trent McDuffie took him out of the game in a Week 4 loss, and DeVonta Smith has missed two games with an injury. Makai Lemon has done some decent things and should only continue to get better and more involved.
Dallas Goedert picked up where he left off last year, snaring two touchdowns against the Commanders in the opener. Then he got hurt in Week 2 and missed two games. Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins don’t provide much offense, and rookie Eli Stowers is on injured reserve. The Eagles signed Zach Ertz, but an impactful role for the veteran has yet to develop.
Lane Johnson retired, and Cam Jurgens was traded the very next day. The Eagles have had three different starting centers in just five games. Continuity is a big key to successful offensive line play, and there just hasn’t been any yet.
Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter were given big raises, but Davis isn’t having the same impact he did last year. He played 61 percent of the snaps a season ago, but is playing just 46 percent this year.
Carter, on the other hand, has been playing with a broken bone in his wrist, which has hampered him, but his three sacks lead the team, and his five tackles for loss equal the number of TFLs he had last year.
Jalyx Hunt looked like a double-digit sack artist in the making, but he has none. Nolan Smith has two sacks, but he hasn’t shown the play-in, play-out consistency he should have at this point in his career. The big offseason acquisition, Jonathan Greenard, has missed three games with two different injuries and has played just 37 snaps. As for free agents Arnold Ebiketie and A.J. Epenesa, they haven’t contributed much so far.
Zack Baun continues to play at a high level, though he missed a game due to a concussion, which was the first time he missed a game with an injury since arriving here in 2024. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. was a force in his only start, collecting 15 tackles, and could be taking over the starting job from Jihaad Campbell, last year's first-round pick, who has been up and down.
Quinyon Mitchell notched his first regular-season interception in Week 5, adding to the four he has in the postseason. But neither he nor Cooper DeJean seems to be playing at the level they played at last year, when they both earned All-Pro honors, and Riq Woolen hasn’t had the bounce-back season the Eagles hoped he would have.
One of the team’s biggest question marks entering the season was here. It is more a liability than a question mark at this point. Andrew Mukuba remains inconsistent. Marcus Epps is hurt, but he wasn’t turning heads in the first three games he played before getting banged up. Michael Carter has done some decent things at the position, but the Eagles severely limited here.
The one and only ‘A’ on this report card is well deserved, with Jake Elliott already connecting on both tries beyond 50 yards, Braden Mann looking like an All-Pro, and Rocco Underwood flawless with his long snaps.
When your head coach has to admit to costing the team a game , as Nick Sirianni did after the loss in London, that’s not good. Neither is being 2-3.

title: Steelers WR Options Revealed: Who's Coming to Pittsburgh?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers should have a pretty good idea of what wide receivers can be had via trade ahead of the November 10 deadline.
Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano , five receivers who may end up being the best remaining player dealt at the position after Marvin Harrison Jr. landed with the Houston Texans are Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars), Rashod Bateman (Baltimore Ravens), Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers), Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings) and Jerry Jeudy (Cleveland Browns).
With nine picks in both the 2027 and 2028 NFL Drafts, Pittsburgh has the necessary assets to wheel and deal if it so chooses in the lead-up to the deadline.
Receiver stands out as one of the team's biggest needs with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on the reserve/injured list while both Roman Wilson (hand/finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have already been ruled out for the Steelers' Week 6 bout with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Of the names Fowler and Graziano mentioned, however, who are the best fits for Pittsburgh?
Intra-division trades aren't commonplace in the NFL, and there's always going to be some extra layers when such a deal takes place that could complicate the entire process.
For that reason, it's hard to imagine a scenario in which Bateman or Jeudy ends up in Pittsburgh before the deadline.
The Ravens currently sit atop the AFC North at 4-1 and are Super Bowl contenders, meaning trading away a key piece at receiver in Bateman wouldn't be practical even if rookie Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) returns from IR and makes a huge impact.
That doesn't even factor in the rarity of a deal between Pittsburgh and Baltimore, as previously alluded to. The sides have made just two trades involving players, with the most recent example coming in 2020 when defensive end Chris Wormley went from the Ravens to the Steelers.
Pittsburgh and Cleveland have swapped players more frequently within the past decade or so, as the Browns rerouted Justin Gilbert to the Steelers in 2016 while the black and gold sent Sammie Coates the other way in 2017.
Still, the organizations aren't at all likely to link up on a trade involving Jeudy, who has just 81 yards through five games this season.
Jennings was there for the taking for Pittsburgh in the offseason considering he was a free agent through early May. He ended up signing a one-year deal worth $8 million with the Vikings, but he has just two catches for nine yards this season despite playing 201 offensive snaps over four games.
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport stated this week that Jennings' trade market is expected to heat up. He's an intriguing name to watch for the Steelers as a buy-low candidate who has proven to be a quality starter in the past, evidenced by the fact that he put up a combined 1,618 yards and 15 touchdowns for the San Francisco 49ers between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns.
Jennings will likely command a strong market on an expiring contract due to his surprising lack of production when compared to his total body of work, but Pittsburgh should certainly be in the mix.
Thomas Jr. has only logged 105 yards in five contests for Jacksonville in 2026 as he continues to fade following a standout rookie campaign back in 2024, during which he put up 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns.
He's been floated as a potential trade candidate dating back to last season, though it always seemed as if the price tag was too high.
Now that he's failed to make much of a splash under Liam Coen for a second straight year, however, perhaps the Steelers could swoop in and get him at a discount.
The Ringer's Tom Pelissero wrote in "The Sweep" on October 10 that the Jaguars haven't shown any interest in dealing Thomas Jr., though that could theoretically change before November 10.
Johnston also hasn't done much for the Chargers this year, having recorded 108 yards in four games, but that could be attributed to the team's disastrous start at 0-5 that's seen the offense completely fall apart.
The 2023 first-round pick did post a combined 1,446 yards and 16 touchdowns between the 2024 and 2025 seasons, and Los Angeles picked up his fifth-year option for the 2027 campaign at a fully guaranteed $18 million (per Over the Cap ).
Johnston wouldn't come cheap for Pittsburgh from a salary cap perspective, and he may fetch a valuable pick for the Chargers as well.
Between Jennings, Thomas Jr. and Johnston, Jennings feels like the most logical trade option for the Steelers when taking the asking price and salary cap ramifications into place.
From an upside perspective, though, Thomas Jr. is quite easily the most fascinating name of the bunch.

title: Steelers Could Lose Another Starting DT After Ankle Injury
full_text:
Another interior defensive linemen for the Pittsburgh Steelers is dealing with an injury.
On their first injury report ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Steelers listed Keeanu Benton as a non-participant with an ankle injury.
Cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist), wide receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) and defensive tackle Cameron Heyward (NIR/Rest) all didn't practice as well.
Running back Rico Dowdle (toe), cornerback Jamel Dean (ankle), safety DeShon Elliott (knee) and EDGE rusher T.J. Watt (NIR/Rest) were all limited participants.
Elliott is still in his 21-day practice window , which was opened last week, while remaining on the reserve/injured list.
After watching Nick Herbig (four years, $100 million) and Darnell Washington (four years, $42 million) sign their extensions in early June, Benton had to wait until mid-August to get his own new deal from Pittsburgh.
When the time came, the 2023 second-round pick inked a four-year contract worth $72 million after recording a career-high  5.5 sacks in 2025.
The Steelers' new coaching staff has made it a point to move Benton around the defensive line more instead of having him primarily serve as a nose tackle, which was largely targeted at granting him more opportunities to get after the quarterback.
Benton has not posted a sack through five games up to this point while playing 190 defensive snaps, though, and he has seven pressures (per Pro Football Focus ).
It's too early to know whether or not Benton is in danger of missing Pittsburgh's bout with Tampa Bay this week.
Considering the Steelers are already down a key piece along the interior of their defensive line in Derrick Harmon, however, they could really use Benton vs. the Buccaneers.
Harmon was placed on IR last week with a foot injury he suffered in Pittsburgh's Week 4 loss at the hands of the Cleveland Browns.
He missed the Steelers' win over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 as a result, and he'll be out for a minimum of three more games as well.
Harmon's absence led to rookie sixth-round pick Gabriel Rubio being active for the first time this season vs. Indianapolis, however, and he flashed some really promising signs as a run defender while recording three assists on tackles over 14 defensive reps.
Rubio's snap count will likely rise if Benton can't suit up against Tampa Bay, and undrafted rookie Kevin Jobity Jr. could make his NFL debut as well after being inactive for each of the first five weeks of the campaign.

title: Elandon Roberts Clears the Air on Steelers Feelings
full_text:
Elandon Roberts shut down the notion that he had any issues with the Pittsburgh Steelers upon his return to the team.
Roberts, who signed to the Steelers' practice squad earlier this week , said that he has no hard feelings stemming from his surprise release at final roster cuts in late August and that he wouldn't have come back if that were the case since he would've been a distraction.
"It's real comfortable still," Roberts said. "Know the playbook still, know the expectation... I mean I have a great relationship with everybody upstairs. Coaches, everybody, so it's no hard feelings. If I had hard feelings, I wouldn't have came back because then that's a distraction to the team, and I'm here to do whatever it takes for the team to win and whatnot, so now I'm all good."
Inside linebacker was one of the position groups that was most in need of outside reinforcements during the offseason for Pittsburgh.
The organization didn't select any players at the position in the 2026 NFL Draft despite using 10 picks, and the group was ultimately the same heading into training camp as it was in 2025 after re-signing Cole Holcomb to a two-year, $5 million deal in March.
Given the unit's struggles last season, the lack of change was a pretty big surprise. Because Roberts was still on the free agent market come August, however, it wasn't too late for the Steelers to bring back the fan-favorite on a one-year contract and reunite him with Patrick Graham, who was Roberts' defensive coordinator with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025.
Roberts was impressive throughout the preseason, finishing with 10 tackles over two games, and it felt like he was playing himself into a sizable role heading into the regular season.
Instead, the Steelers let him go in what ended up being the team's most unforeseen transaction on roster cutdown day.
With little improvement at inside linebacker in Graham's system, Pittsburgh had to make a move to supplement the group.
Payton Wilson has shown some growth as a run defender, though he's run into issues finishing tackles at times and isn't as stout in coverage as he should be for a player with his athletic tools.
Patrick Queen , in the final season of a three-year, $41 million deal, has continued to be inconsistent and potentially would have already lost his grasp on his starting spot if the Steelers were confident Cole Holcomb or even Carson Bruener could take on his workload.
Though Roberts is currently on the practice squad, it's not far-fetched to believe he'll eventually take snaps away from Queen in the near future.
A thumper who's always specialized as a downhill run defender with clear limitations in coverage, Roberts is the type of high-floor veteran that Pittsburgh has desperately needed at the position since his departure ahead of the 2025 campaign. It also helps that Roberts picked up experience playing alongside Wilson and Queen for the Steelers in 2024.
He isn't going to patch up all of the problems in the middle of Pittsburgh's defense, but he'll certainly make a difference whenever he is out there.

title: Mike Tomlin is Still a Steelers Fan - And That's Awesome
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Life without Mike Tomlin has been a roller coaster ride for the Pittsburgh Steelers. That's to be expected after Tomlin's 19-year tenure as head coach came to an end after the 2025 campaign.
Now, the Steelers have a new head coach in Mike McCarthy, while Tomlin shines in a new commentary role.
But even as both sides move on, there is a deep respect and mutual love. It's showed up during Tomlin's first season as an NFL analyst. Some have accused him of showcasing his Steelers bias while on television. When asked about it on an appearance on the New Heights podcast, he told Jason and Travis Kelce that he doesn't care if that bias shows. The way he sees it, it's inevitable after spending two decades in Pittsburgh.
"To be honest with ya, I don't care if I do," he said. "How can you be somewhere 19 years, man, and had really a personal stake in most of the guys being there and not care for 'em? Not root for 'em? Not be for 'em? I'm not gonna pretend that I'm not. I can't do that. Certainly, I got a job to do and I'm gonna do it. But everybody knows where my heart is and where my support is, and I'm not apologizing for that."
That's one looming question as the Steelers navigate their first season without Tomlin. Under McCarthy, the team is 3-2 entering Week 6. It hasn't been perfect, but the brightest spot so far is their 3-0 record at home and a slightly improved offense.
Right now, the Steelers miss him like you miss an old pal. You loved the times and reminiscing, but you aren't eager for them to return. Currently, eyes are forward for both Tomlin and Pittsburgh.
Even with all of that love, it's clear that Tomlin doesn't miss being a head coach. Speaking about his new gig, he referred to it as "part-time work" for "full-time pay." Despite rising speculation that the NFL wants Tomlin back on the sidelines, the former Steelers coach is enjoying life on the call at Sunday Night Football.
The Steelers see light at the end of the tunnel when it comes to implementing a new coaching staff. A rocky start is hopefully in the rearview after an impressive win over the Indianapolis Colts.
Things won't be fully decided until the calendar flips. The Steelers brought McCarthy to Pittsburgh to help end their decade-long playoff win drought. If he can accomplish that, he'll have the fanbase's trust for the rest of his contract.
If he fails, the sentimentality for Tomlin will certainly grow. The fanbase already misses the person that Mike Tomlin is, but it remains to be seen how badly they miss him as their head coach.
Through it all, Tomlin is a huge fan of his former team, and that's great news for the Steelers organization.

title: Tyreek Hill No Longer Fits Steelers Plans
full_text:
A veteran wide receiver may be off the Pittsburgh Steelers' radar and out of their plans now.
According to ESPN's Xuan Thai , a Miami jury returned a mixed verdict in an assault and battery civil trial against Tyreek Hill.
Hill was found liable for two counts of battery but was not liable for the eight other claims made by Lakeeta Vaccaro, his estranged wife. Vaccaro was awarded $500,000 in compensatory damages as a result, and her claims for punitive damages were denied.
The NFL is still keeping tabs on the situation, though, and Hill remains under investigation.
“We have been monitoring developments in the matter, which remains under review of the personal conduct policy,” an NFL spokesperson told Pro Football Talk after the verdict was returned.
Thai noted that Drew Rosenhaus, Hill's agent, stated that the 32-year-old's playing situation is "fluid" while adding that "a deal could happen any time" while speaking with a local news station, but a suspension is at least still a possibility as the league continues its investigation.
As such, with potential discipline for Hill looming while he recovers from a dislocated knee along with multiple torn ligaments that he suffered with the Miami Dolphins in Week 4 of the 2025 campaign, there are a multitude of reasons why Pittsburgh may opt not to pursue bringing him in at this juncture.
Sure, the Steelers have a clear need for quality receiver depth with Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on the reserve/injured list while both Roman Wilson (hand/finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have already been ruled out for Week 6, but there are other ways in which they can satisfy that need beyond bringing in Hill.
The most obvious solution for the Steelers is to sign Brandon Smith, a training camp standout, to the 53-man roster after he was elevated from the practice squad for the first time this season in Week 5's win over the Indianapolis Colts, a contest in which he logged 16 offensive snaps.
Rookies Kaden Wetjen and Eli Heidenreich are already on the 53-man roster, though both are almost strictly special teamers and have yet to log a single snap at receiver during the regular season.
If Pittsburgh wants to go the free agent route without targeting Hill, Curtis Samuel, JuJu Smith-Schuster and Mecole Hardman are the top names still remaining in that regard.
The organization could also sign a veteran off another team's practice squad , with Scotty Miller (Chicago Bears), Van Jefferson (Washington Commanders), Nick Westbrook-Ikhine (Indianapolis Colts), Sterling Shepard (New York Jets) and Odell Beckham Jr. (Minnesota Vikings) among the most notable players who fall into that category.
A trade is a legitimate possibility as well , with Jauan Jennings (Minnesota Vikings), Jerry Jeudy (Cleveland Browns), Brian Thomas Jr. (Jacksonville Jaguars), Quentin Johnston (Los Angeles Chargers) and Calvin Ridley (Tennessee Titans) all potentially being available, though there's still nearly a month to go before the November 10 deadline.
The Steelers might not be able to afford to wait, however, meaning some moves might be on the horizon or already in the works.

title: Steelers Preparing for LB Trade?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers ' decision to re-sign Elandon Roberts could be just the first domino to fall for the team at inside linebacker.
During the latest episode of the "Steelers Collective" with Steelers On SI's Noah Strackbein and insider Mark Kaboly, the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Ray Fittipaldo noted that the timing of Roberts' return to the organization via the practice squad is a bit conspicuous and could potentially signal additional moves to come.
"It probably is an insurance pick, but the timing is very interesting," Fittipaldo said. "We're a month out from the trade deadline. Patrick Queen is in the last year of his deal. Cole Holcomb is on a cheap deal. I don't know if either of those guys do get moved, but what better guy to come in and replace one of those guys if a deal is made? I'm not trying to connect the dots here, but the timing is very interesting."
When asked if he thinks Pittsburgh's decision to bring Roberts back is a possible precursor to a trade at the position, Fittipaldo responded with, "That's what I'm saying."
The Steelers ' run defense against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5 was spectacular, as they held Jonathan Taylor to 45 yards on 15 carries in a 34-22 victory.
Still, Pittsburgh could really use a thumper in the middle of its defense. Payton Wilson has flown around the field this year and improved a bit as a run defender, though he's not exactly a plus in that regard and needs to become more of a secure tackler (18.4 percent missed tackle rate, per SumerSports ).
Queen has been the bigger liability of the two, even if his tackling has improved from where it stood in 2025. He's lacking both in coverage and against the run, and while his performance vs. Indianapolis was better than what he showed in Week 4 against the Cleveland Browns, he hasn't consistently played at a true starting-caliber level for a majority of his stint with the Steelers.
Roberts isn't an all-encompassing solution at inside linebacker. He remained a free agent after Pittsburgh let him go at final roster cuts for a reason, as the 32-year-old's athleticism continues to decline while having already been a well below-average coverage defender.
Where he does thrive, though, is as a physical run stuffer and sound tackler who can set the tone on defense. Roberts was impressive during the preseason for the Steelers, and while it was surprising when he was cut back in August , the organization now has a chance to right their wrongs.
As Roberts starts on the practice squad and works his way up, it feels pretty fair to assume that he's a better option than Queen is. He might not be far off from Wilson, either.
It's likely going to take some time to get back into the swing of things for Roberts, but there are plenty of reasons to be excited about what he'll ultimately bring to the table as an experienced, high-floor player.
Queen is the clear-cut No. 1 trade candidate at inside linebacker, and frankly across the entire 53-man roster, for the Steelers.
He's on an expiring deal, as Fittipaldo noted, and hasn't figured it out in Pittsburgh in two different defensive systems, first under Mike Tomlin/Teryl Austin and now Patrick Graham.
As a two-time Pro Bowler who is a relatively big name and has 106 starts under his belt, however, there's bound to be some level of interest in Queen if Pittsburgh does make him available ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.
Holcomb has only logged 20 defensive snaps this season and Wilson sure feels like he isn't going anywhere, which could make Queen the obvious odd man out should Roberts essentially step in and supplant him at some point.

title: 3 Realistic WR Trade Targets For Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers need wide receiver help if they want to make it through the latest rash of injuries plaguing the lineup. Entering Week 6 with a 3-2 record, the Steelers have played well on the offensive side of the ball, even with a shorthanded roster.
The Steelers have a few players on their active roster and practice squad that will likely get the first crack for Week 6. Players like Brandon Smith, Brandon Johnson, Eli Heidenreich and Max Hurleman could all enter the lineup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The other option is to pluck a veteran from another team's practice squad that they feel could plug in and play immediately. Names like K.J. Osborn, Mecole Hardman and Trey Palmer come to mind.
Alternatively, they could try to pull off a low-risk trade. Unlikely to part with the assets required to land a big-name player, the Steelers have been unafraid to add veterans this season. That could again be the case with these three players the Steelers could acquire for very little.
On the eastern side of Pennsylvania, the Philadelphia Eagles are selling off parts. They traded offensive lineman Cam Jurgens shortly after tackle Lane Johnson retired. They already sent AJ Brown out of town before the 2026 season began.
So, what are the Eagles trying get out of Marquise "Hollywood" Brown? The answer is nothing, evidenced by just one game played this season and a whopping two rushes for 12 yards. But last year he posted over 500 yards with the Kansas City Chiefs. The Eagles are set for a fire sale, and all it would take is a seventh or sixth-round pick to get the former 2019 first-round pick in Pittsburgh.
The Jacksonville Jaguars thought they had a gem of a receiver when they took Brian Thomas Jr. in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. That thought was reaffirmed by a 1,200-yard rookie season.
But it's been far less impressive since that first year. He posted just over 700 yards as a sophomore, and he continues to fall out of favor in Jacksonville. Through five games in 2026, he's played less than half of the team's offensive snaps, according to data from Spotrac, and has 105 yards and a single touchdown.
The Jaguars are trying to win with quarterback Trevor Lawrence, and Thomas isn't helping right now. He might help in Pittsburgh, however, where he can play with a different type of quarterback and offensive coach.
How much would Jacksonville need to be convinced? If the Steelers could get him for a day three pick in 2027, then it's a no-brainer. Anything close to the price the Houston Texans paid for Marvin Harrison Jr., and the Steelers have to walk away.
Back in 2024, Jalen Tolbert had the best offensive season of his career. He caught 49 passes for 610 yards and seven touchdowns. Aside from that, he's been a 200-yard receiver over his five seasons in the NFL.
Why that matters for the Steelers is that Mike McCarthy was Tolbert's coach in Dallas that season. Pittsburgh could give Tolbert the chance to shine again under McCarthy. Currently on the 0-5 Miami Dolphins and making $1.4 million in actual cash, the Steelers could land a player their head coach already trusts for virtually nothing.

title: Update: President Donald Trump Cancels Trip to Steelers Game
full_text:
President Donald Trump will not be in attendance for the Pittsburgh Steelers ' next game after deciding to cancel the trip to Tampa Bay.
According to CNN Senior White House Correspondent Kristen Holmes, Trump was expected to be at Raymond James Stadium for the Steelers ' Week 6 bout on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. However, he has since canceled.
Good news for the many people who hated this news— after we reported it, I am told they pulled down the trip. So… hope you kept your tickets! https://t.co/ZQNpS4EJii
The last time Trump watched Pittsburgh in person was in Week 7 of the 2024 campaign during a Sunday Night Football showdown vs. Aaron Rodgers and the New York Jets.
Trump was the guest of an individual suiteholder for that contest, which marked Russell Wilson's first start for the Steelers in his return from a calf injury.
The organization also honored the 50th anniversary of its Super Bowl IX team that night as Pittsburgh blew out the Jets by a score of 37-15.
The Buccaneers got off to a difficult start this season, losing each of their first four games.
Baker Mayfield, who signed a three-year extension worth $165 million last month, also suffered a dislocated thumb in Week 3 and has remained out ever since.
As a result, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has stepped in as the starting quarterback for the time being. After a rough debut in a Week 4 loss to the Green Bay Packers, however, Daniels helped lead Tampa Bay to an upset victory on Thursday Night Football this past week vs. the Dallas Cowboys.
Mayfield appears to be trending in the right direction, though the signs are still pointing towards Daniels getting the starting nod against Pittsburgh .
While Daniels and the Bucs proved that they can be competitive and come away with wins against quality teams, the Steelers cannot afford to let the opportunity for a win against an inexperienced backup quarterback slip by them.
Sure, Tampa Bay has one of the better defenses in the league and has gotten the run game going thanks to Bucky Irving, but Pittsburgh still by and large has the upper hand as long as Daniels is behind center.
The Steelers' offense showed up in a major way during the team's Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, putting 34 points up on the board, and their defense is still capable of at least holding opposing offenses in check even if the secondary isn't in good shape.
Make no mistake about it, the Buccaneers are a far more formidable squad than their 1-4 record would suggest, but Pittsburgh cannot let them earn the win this week considering their quarterback situation.

title: Steelers Star Must Step Up After WR Injuries
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers put together an impressive offensive showing in their 34-22 victory over the Indianapolis Colts in Week 5. For the second time in five games, the Steelers posted 30 points or more, while quarterback Aaron Rodgers has thrown for at least three touchdowns in three consecutive games.
What makes it even more impressive is the Steelers have made improvements on offense despite inconsistent wide receiver play. Thanks to the efforts of Rodgers and running back Jaylen Warren, this group might be finding steady ground.
The one player who cannot be ignored in all of this is tight end Pat Freiermuth. The 27-year-old had a fantastic Week 5 performance, hauling in five receptions for 44 yards and two touchdowns.
It was exactly what the team needed. Amidst a sea of injuries, the Steelers can find safe harbor thanks to the re-emergence of Freiermuth as a top tight end.
It’s long been known that Freiermuth is one of the best athletes at his position. He established that as a rookie in the NFL, but over the years, the offense has failed to prioritize him as they should.
This season, however, it appears that head coach Mike McCarthy is refusing to continue that. In all five games this season, Freiermuth has seen at least four targets. In this most recent contest, he was targeted seven times.
It’s emblematic of one thing - this team prioritizes Freiermuth. Rodgers trusts him as his top tight end, and he continues to go to him in tough situations.
One area the Steelers really focused on Freiermuth in their Week 5 victory was in the red zone. Both of his touchdown receptions came inside the 20-yard line, but it was a specific second quarter play that should give the Steelers confidence moving forward.
On the 1-yard line, the Steelers were expected to come out with jumbo personnel as they tried to power into the end zone. Instead, they came out with an empty set and five receivers out wide.
It was the perfect play call because it put Freiermuth one-on-one with a Colts linebacker, giving him a mismatch at the line of scrimmage.
Freiermuth took advantage. With a quick stutter step, the Steelers tight end created plenty of space for Rodgers to find him, giving the Steelers an early 14-6 lead.
Aaron Rodgers finds Pat Freiermuth for another Steelers TD! #NFL pic.twitter.com/hU254xEhwW
As the Steelers try to build momentum, they keep taking hits. Roman Wilson could miss time after dislocating a finger in Week 5. Michael Pittman Jr. was placed on Injured Reserve, meaning he will be out of action for at least three more weeks.
Despite the hits that keep coming, the Steelers should feel confident in their offensive weaponry. That’s thanks to Pat Freiermuth.

title: Two WRs Steelers Can Poach From Other Teams
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have a wide receiver problem once again. This time, however, injuries are the main culprit to blame.
The Steelers were victorious in Week 5, putting up 34 points in a win over the Indianapolis Colts. The offense has taken strides , putting up more than 30 points in two of the last three weeks. In the process, however, they've lost three wide receivers for multiple weeks. Michael Pittman Jr. is on the Injured Reserve with a foot injury, Roman Wilson has already been ruled out of Week 6 due to a dislocated finger and special teams ace Ben Skowronek left their Week 5 contest with a calf injury.
Even with their practice squad call-ups, the Steelers need another receiver once again. The team could swing a trade before they take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, but the likelier route this organization takes is plucking a player off of a practice squad or from free agency.
These two veterans stand out as the likeliest fits and most immediately available options for the Steelers to add temporarily.
A few seasons ago, K.J. Osborn was a legitimate trade target for the Steelers. Coming off of three straight seasons of at least 500 receiving yards, the former 2020 fifth-round pick was a coveted player around the NFL.
Fast forward to 2026, and he's on the Tennessee Titans practice squad. For the Steelers, that's exactly what they need. Osborn has 66 games of NFL experience, and he could come in and be ready to play as soon as Week 6.
He is not a flashy option, that's for sure. But as a temporary replacement, he is an easy addition.
As an added bonus, where did Osborn have success? His best days came as a member of the Minnesota Vikings, working with current Steelers offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio. That extra connection might be enough to convince the team to take a shot on Osborn.
The Steelers could also look to free agency to add former Kansas City Chiefs, New York Jets and Buffalo Bills receiver Mecole Hardman Jr.
A former Super Bowl winner with the Chiefs, Hardman brings the trait that the Steelers' coaching staff loves: versatility. He has the speed that the team is missing without Wilson on the field. He can play any of the receiver positions. Most importantly, he has experience returning kicks and punts. He's not just a flyer being taken to fill out the bottom of the depth chart, he's someone who can help across multiple situations for the next few weeks.
Plus, he played briefly with Aaron Rodgers as a player with the New York Jets. Rodgers was hurt in the season opener that year and Hardman was later traded away, but the two spent time together previously. If that went well, why not bring him back for a reunion?
Other names to monitor are just as unexciting. Former second-round pick JuJu Smith-Schuster is an option. Odell Beckham Jr. is on the Vikings' practice squad. Other free agent names include Tyreek Hill, KJ Hamler and Josh Reynolds.

title: Seahawks Should Give Velus Jones Jr. Chance to Contribute vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks made minor adjustments to their roster on Wednesday, signing running back Velus Jones Jr. from the practice squad and releasing wide receiver Irv Charles. Seattle re-signed Charles to the practice squad afterward.
It was mostly just small roster manipulation , as the move comes one day after activating Charles from injured reserve, releasing Jones and re-signing him to the practice squad. Those players have now swapped places, as the Seahawks had to initially activate Charles to the active roster.
Jones has been on the 53-man roster but has only played two offensive snaps in his four appearances this season. Will he play a bigger role in Week 6?
Despite being active for four games, Jones has mostly been a contributor on special teams. He's played 61 snaps in that phase, which is 49% of the team's total special teams snaps.
The Seahawks aren't getting Zach Charbonnet back this week, and Jadarian Price is also still on injured reserve. That leaves them with the same stable of Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Jones. Holani and Wilson have a combined four fumbles between the two of them, and two of them resulted in turnovers.
Seattle needs a spark at running back. Jones might not be the top option to provide that, but he's the third rusher for a reason. If the Seahawks are going to keep him on the roster, not sign anyone else, and the rest of their backs are struggling, it only makes sense to use all their depth.
Charbonnet will hopefully return in Week 7, but Seattle still has to get through a tough matchup against the Denver Broncos on Thursday night. A loss would give the San Francisco 49ers an even bigger lead in the NFC West standings, and that could be tough to battle back from if they don't get back on track.
At full strength, Charbonnet and Price should be the Seahawks' top two running backs. They don't have either, so Jones could be a change of pace that helps them get a win. He's a speedy runner who has returned kicks for the team this season, providing open-field upside.
It can't get much worse in the backfield. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has nothing to lose by giving Jones a few carries and seeing how he performs.

title: Final Seahawks, Broncos Injury Report Clarifies Situation On Both Sides
full_text:
It’s time for the third and final practice report of this week, this one coming complete with game statuses for players who missed some (or all) of potential practice time this week . The Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos are both staring down the barrel of a short week, so who are they going to have available? Let’s have a look at it.
Moving past the long-term, ongoing injuries to players like Jadarian Price, Anthony Bradford, and Zach Charbonnet (knee, still out), it’s not too bad. Chazz Surratt (calf) is out, a pure special teamer. The main concern is Drake Thomas (ankle), who did not practice and is out for tomorrow . The team will turn to Tyrice Knight in his absence, which isn't entirely a bad thing, but still a step down.
That's about it. No one else was listed as questionable. Beau Stephens (shoulder) and George Holani (ribs, knee) held as full participants and are ready to roll. Irv Charles (knee) was removed from the report entirely due to being put down on the practice squad in a roster switcharoo with Velus Jones Jr, but should be available for an elevation tomorrow to get his Seattle debut.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle) was listed as a full participant today, which should make people feel better about things after his (hypothetical) limited days the last two practices. Drew Lock (right forearm) and much more importantly Leonard Williams (ankle) have no game status despite limited participation today and should be available in full as needed Thursday night.
If the Seahawks can not find a way to throw the ball effectively against the Broncos in their current state of health, then there may not be much hope for them. As anticipated throughout the week, Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) are both out. That’s Denver’s best CB (and one of the best in the league) and best safety unavailable.
And the bad news doesn’t stop there either. Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable, indicative of the fact that while he’s more likely than not to play, he’s clearly not himself. Denver is highly motivated to toss him onto the field no matter what due to how helpless they’d be at boundary cornerback without him, but that doesn’t mean he’s in good shape to go.
Brandon Jones (foot), Ben Powers (biceps), and Sai’vion Jones (shoulder) are all good to go. But remember, all of this is on top of lacking Pat Bryant and Jonah Coleman, who are on IR, and Jonathan Cooper, who is suspended. It’s a Broncos team that is well below full strength no matter how you slice it. It’s up to Seattle to take advantage.
