title: 10 Urgent Issues the Seahawks Need to Fix Before Broncos Matchup
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are 3-2 coming off a disappointing 32-29 loss to their divisional rival , the San Francisco 49ers, in Week 5. What makes it worse is that the Seahawks have to turn around to go on the road to face the Denver Broncos (3-2). There have been shades of the Seahawks’ Super Bowl-winning team, but they have looked incredibly sloppy.
​From turnovers and bad decision-making to poor play from main position groups, there are several things that the Seahawks need to fix up before they face another Super Bowl contender on a tough journey. If Seattle isn’t careful and improves on some flaws, it could be facing a 3-3 record with more tough games down the road. This Broncos team is not a group to be careless about.
​1. Quarterback Sam Darnold has to stop turning over the ball . He has thrown five interceptions through the last three games played. He is on pace to throw 25 interceptions. That is unacceptable for a Super Bowl-winning quarterback, especially one who is working towards a contract extension. The Broncos have forced five interceptions this season.
​2. Darnold has to be more confident in his throws . There isn’t an indication that he hasn’t recovered from his glute injury. There are signs that he is uncomfortable with his decision-making . Darnold isn’t making the solid, tight throws he made last year; he is throwing into double or triple coverage and he is going to solid yards up the middle.
He is clearly in his own head and has to calm down and quit doubting his throws. Even if the Broncos won’t have cornerback Pat Surtain II and safety Talanoa Hufanga, Seattle has to be careful of this dangerous Broncos’ pass defense.
​3. The offense has to take risks with the running game . The Seahawks were too careful with rookie Jadarian Price before his injury and they didn’t give wide receiver Rashid Shaheed a carry. Seattle needs to be more aggressive and reliable on the ground . They need to give Robert Henry Jr., Velus Jones Jr., or another veteran a shot at running back.
​4. It is starting to feel like there is some disconnect between the new offensive coordinator Brian Fleury and the Seahawks’ players . Darnold is the most vulnerable if he feels like there isn’t a rhythm with the offense. The running back room is easily suffering and not being utilized to their best potential. Another key aspect is the lack of utilization from Shaheed , wide receiver Tory Horton and tight end Elijah Arroyo.
​5. The offensive line has to step up . This season, the experienced offensive line hasn’t seen any improvement. Seattle has allowed 11 sacks this season, including eight in the last two games. Seattle has allowed five sacks from the 49ers, who didn’t have edge rusher Nick Bosa. The offensive line has been dominated often in short-yardage and red-zone schemes. Seattle faces a much more dangerous defensive line with the Broncos on Thursday.
​6. Head coach Mike Macdonald has to admit to changes . One of the biggest problems with Super Bowl contenders or champs is believing everything will work out. Macdonald can’t be afraid to make changes. One of the biggest examples is changing coverage of cornerback Josh Jobe, who was poorly covering wide receiver Mike Evans.
​7. The run defense has to be much better . The Seahawks were one of the best run defense teams in the league last season. Through five games, they are 11th in run defense and allowed 3.7 yards per run. There are times in a game when the Dark Side Defense will be overwhelmed and allow multiple solid runs. The Broncos have an underrated running game with J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey, who might be the X-Factors along with the Broncos' offensive line.
​8. The Dark Side Defense has to shut down the short passing game . One of the reasons the Seahawks’ great defense isn’t posting elite numbers is because of the way that opposing offenses are finding ways to get the ball out fast in the short passing game. The Seahawks usually send four or more players at the line of scrimmage for a pass rush.
Offenses know there is less coverage space from the Seahawks near the middle of the zone for about five to eight yards consistently. This allows the opposing offenses to avoid the pass rush and it wears down the Seahawks’ defense.​
9. Red zone defense has to improve . The Seahawks’ defense is great at shutting down quickly. When their backs are against the wall, however, they tend to allow opponents to score. Seattle has allowed the seventh-highest red zone percentage through the first five games, 9-to-12 (75%). It should be noted that some of the opposing team’s starts in or near the red zone are due to a Seahawks turnover, but the Dark Side Defense hasn’t been great at shutting down offenses.
​10. The turnovers have to stop . It is wild that the reigning Super Bowl champions are tied for fifth in the league in turnovers with nine turnovers. This implies that Seattle is too careless with the ball. It is not just Darnold’s bad decision-making; it involves the run game. The Seahawks have lost two games this season solely based on turnovers.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 4 Questions Leading Into Broncos Game
full_text:
Losing to a non-trivally injured San Francisco 49ers team , giving them a big lead in the division to start the season, has some fans on edge. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“Will Brian Fleury make it to the end of the season?”
It’s very hard to fire a playcaller in the middle of the season. Generally speaking, any team that does it has nothing to lose. Off the top of my head, the 2012 Baltimore Ravens are the only example of doing it successfully. They fired OC Cam Cameron late in the season at 9-4, promoted Jim Caldwell, and went on to win the super bowl.
You could consider it in week 11 during the bye week, but then what? You can’t bring in someone from the outside, and everyone on the staff has no experience calling plays, so you’re just crossing your fingers. Jake Peetz, Justin Outten, or John Benton would probably be on deck, but it’s going to take some extreme incompetency to get that far.
“Should we change our scheme on offense to be as pass-heavy as possible in order to compensate for the lack of a running game?”
I really can’t see any other solution . Last year, the Seahawks were bad at running the ball most of the season, but at least their running backs didn’t fumble. Until you get to a place of trust with your backs, which may not happen for a couple more weeks when Price returns, just open up the offense and try to use short passes as a surrogate for a run game.
But more than just being pass-heavy, we need to bring back the big play. Last year, the Seahawks were inefficient offensively, but they were highly explosive. They routinely hit plays of 50 or more yards, which compensated for their shortcomings in other areas. This year, I’m not even seeing an attempt to take big shots down the field. Bring it back.
“Why is George Holani still on the team?”
The unfortunate reality is that the Seahawks are not in a position to end that particular relationship quite yet. On just about any other team in the league, I’m sure Holani would be cut for his performance on Sunday. Note that, yesterday, the Seahawks did cut ties with a back, but it was Velus Jones Jr. So they’re working on it.
When Charbonnet and Price are available again, I could definitely see Holani getting cut, especially if Robert Henry Jr makes a good impression. Just to consider the other side of the debate, however, Holani’s current struggles may be due to his injuries , and it’s possible a stint on Injured Reserve might get him back to a useful state.
“Why does Brian Fleury insist on using slow backs for outside runs?”
Fleury wants to run outside (just like Klint Kubiak did), and he doubtlessly had big plans for Jadarian Price. He lost Price very quickly , and feels compelled to use those plays regardless. It’s not the most shocking thing in the world than a first time OC doesn’t have enough put together for a Plan B and Plan C, I suppose.
But being a successful playcaller in this league is all about finding a way to use the tools that you have, and right now Fleury is failing at that. There’s a reason why every question this week dealt with him in some way, shape, or form. He’s not getting it done, and the potential solutions for producing better results are seemingly right in front of him.

title: How Brian Fleury Can Make the Seahawks Less Predictable on Offense
full_text:
Through five games, I have many criticisms of Brian Fleury as offensive coordinator and playcaller of the Seattle Seahawks. Some of them, like the zone run to George Holani with 18 seconds left in the first half last week against the San Francisco 49ers, are edge cases, unlikely to come up again. But what about one that comes up a couple dozen times a game?
Let’s toss the Patriots game, since Fleury lost his quarterback after five plays and had to put Drew Lock in cold off the bench . By my count, the Seahawks have run the ball on first down 19 of 29 opportunities against the Cardinals (65.5%), 14 of 36 against the Commanders (38.9%), 18 of 27 against the Chargers (66.7%), and 19 of 29 against the 49ers (65.5%).
Outside of the Commanders game, where Seattle fell behind and stuck their lead running back in the doghouse early, the Seahawks love running it on first down. In that game, Seattle ran it on 9 of 15 first downs (60%) in the first half, just to illustrate how circumstances dictated the change-up. I suspect the roughly 66% clip at which they do it is #1 in the league.
Here’s the thing. The Seahawks aren’t just bad at running on first down. They’re abysmal at it . They have a -0.248 Rush EPA on those runs, 30th in the league. Their overall Rush EPA is somehow even worse at -0.275 (also 30th). They don’t run the ball well in any way, shape, or form. And this data includes games where they had Jadarian Price.
Their Dropback EPA isn’t amazing, but at 0.098 and 17th in the league, it’s better than their rushing attack by a longshot. And here’s the part that’ll really blow your minds. The Seahawks Dropback EPA on first down is 0.259, 4th in the NFL. It’s not hard to put the pieces together. This team thrives on early down passing, but they rarely do it.
If the Seahawks opened things up on first downs, would there be some diminishing returns? Probably. But something has to change here. The only reason why the Seahawks don’t have one of the worst offenses in football is all the short-field scoring drives they’ve had. They’re 26th in EPA , a catastrophic -0.07 overall EPA per play. It’s not sustainable.
The current recipe is to run on first down for minimal gain, then either run again on second down for minimal gain or pass with middling effectiveness, and then pass ineffectively on third down. The recipe needs to change. Throw it more early, get into more favorable second and third downs. And maybe, eventually, we can get back to a balanced attack.

title: Seahawks vs. Broncos Could Be Jersey Game of the Year
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks will be sporting a fan favorite jersey when they take on the Denver Broncos in Week 6's edition of Thursday Night Football.
It will be the eighth time the Seahawks have worn their throwback uniforms since they were reintroduced into the rotation in 2023. The Seahawks are 4-3 when they wear their throwback jerseys, including their most recent meeting against the Broncos , where they pulled out a Week 1 win in the 2023 fourth season. The last time the Seahawks wore these jerseys was last year in Week 9, when they beat the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football.
The Broncos will also sport their throwback threads on Thursday Night Football. They are set to wear their orange jerseys with their legacy blue helmets that they wore throughout a good chunk of their history. Denver re-introduced this jersey to their uniform in 2024, and they have gone 5-0 in games where this combination is worn, which means Seattle has to reverse the curse in order to win.
An elite throwback uniform matchup Thursday night in Denver between the Seahawks and Broncos. pic.twitter.com/2s78VkNUQa
The matchup is a callback to when the Seahawks and Broncos were division rivals in the AFC West from 1976 to 2001.
The Broncos have dominated the rivalry for most of its history, winning 32 of the first 50 meetings. It wasn't until the Seahawks moved to the NFC West in 2002 that they started to open a new chapter. The Seahawks lost the first meeting as intra-conference rivals in 2002, but Seattle has won five of the last seven meetings dating back to 2006.

title: Week 6 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Slide Following Loss to 49ers
full_text:
This weekend was a gut-punch for the Seattle Seahawks as they lost 32-29 against the San Francisco 49ers.
There could be some encouragement for them, considering they had a chance to tie the game late despite multiple turnovers and a lack of an efficient ground game. Unfortunately, Jaxon Smith-Njigba was unable to haul in a pass from Sam Darnold that would have put them in field goal range. As if that wasn't heartbreaking enough, Cooper Kupp was stopped just inches short on fourth-down, ending their bid for a comeback.
Seattle has a quick turnaround with a Thursday Night Football showdown against the Denver Broncos . Before we completely turn our attention to that game, here's a Week 6 NFL Power Rankings roundup, which shows the Seahawks sliding.
Connor Orr dropped Seattle four spots and accuratley says the offense needs Zach Charbonnet back on the field. Without him, their ground game has been a mess and that has a lot to do with their struggles.
"Per friend Sheil Kapadia at The Ringer, this was the worst offensive EPA in a game coached by Mike Macdonald. This is as much a Raheem Morris note as it is a Seattle note, but I don’t think Zach Charbonnet can hit the field soon enough," Orr wrote.
Not a steep drop from ESPN, but the Seahawks are still trending in the wrong direction. Brady Henderson discussed the biggest problem for the Seattle defense this year, which he says is actually the turnovers by their offense.
"The biggest problem for the Seahawks' defense might actually be their offense; the 44 points they've given up off turnovers is tied for most in the NFL," Henderson wrote.
The Athletic also discussed the lack of a ground game in Seattle, although they also believe the return of Jadarian Price could make a difference. They also add that an improved run game would go a long way toward fixing their issues.
"The Seahawks felt the absence of Jadarian Price (chest injury) and Zach Charbonnet (PUP list) Sunday as their running woes continued. They managed just 68 yards on 24 designed rushes (2.83 yards per carry) for their backs. There are a lot of reasons to remain positive about Seattle, but the running game has to improve."
Mo Moton says the Seahawks need to regroup and while he touched on the ground game, his biggest concern is the turnovers. Since Sam Darnold returned in Week 3, Seattle's quarterback has five interceptions, something that can't happen going forward.
"The reigning champions must regroup. The Seattle Seahawks are turning the ball over at an alarming rate—nine giveaways over the last four weeks. Since Sam Darnold returned from injury, he's been part of the problem, throwing five interceptions in his last three outings," Moton wrote.
Nate Davis kept Seattle where they were, which is surprising. That said, he's not worried about a three-point loss when they weren't at their best.
"Too high you say? Sam Darnold threw two more picks on Sunday, their depleted group of running backs fumbled two more times, and even Jaxon Smith-Njigba is dropping a key pass while running wide open and free. Oh, and LB Ernest Jones IV is once again defending Darnold − literally this time. You know the champs are quality. But Sunday's loss feels similar to last year's in L.A., which set off a 12-game winning streak that only ended two weeks ago. Don't be surprised if these 'Hawks take flight soon," Davis wrote.
Davis could be right that the Seahawks are ready to take off, but that's only going to happen if they take better care of the ball and get the run game going.

title: 3 Score Predictions for Seahawks vs. Broncos
full_text:

title: 3 Matchups That Will Decide Seahawks’ Week 6 Clash vs. Broncos
full_text:
This Thursday’s clash between the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos features two teams with identical records that happen to be chasing a pair of undefeated teams in their respective divisions.
Mike Macdonald’s club comes off a frustrating 32-29 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers. Sean Payton’s club won ugly at SoFi Stadium, defeating the winless Los Angeles Chargers.
Here are three battles that could go a long way in determining which club gets its fourth victory of the season.
While Seattle’s offensive front crept into Pro Football Focus’ Top 10 last Wednesday, it’s been a rough second year so far for starting left guard Grey Zabel. The 2025 first-round pick from North Dakota State has had his struggles, and is currently PFF’s No. 42 player at the position.
On Thursday night, he figures to have his hands full with defensive end Zach Allen, who currently leads the Broncos with four sacks. He’s Pro Football Focus’ 11th-ranked interior defenders who also ranks 10th in terms of pass rush prowess.
Macdonald’s club has allowed eight sacks in their last two games—five in the loss to the 49ers—this after giving up just three sacks in the club’s first three outings.
Sam Darnold throws another interception! The Seahawks keep handing the ball right back to the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/HN2Yw0cQgX
A year ago, only the Houston Texans allowed fewer total yards per game than the Broncos. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph’s unit also finished second in the league vs. the run. Led by the league’s most productive pass rush, Denver defenders surrendered only 18 scores through the air in 17 regular-season games.
After five weeks of action, Joseph’s unit is just 22nd in the NFL in total defense, while allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per game.
Meanwhile, Seahawks’ quarterback Sam Darnold has been less-than-impressive the past three weeks. He was knocked out early in Week 1 against the Patriots and didn’t play at Arizona. In his last three games, the nine-year pro has thrown seven touchdown passes and been picked off five times.
In five games this season, the Broncos have allowed seven TD tosses and total five interceptions.
Nehemiah Pritchett diving INT! @SFvsSEA on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pvzpNYvGJF
Macdonald and defensive coordinator Aden Durde have the league’s top-ranked defense in terms of fewest total yards and fewest passing yards per game allowed. The Seahawks also lead the league with 11 takeaways. Seattle defenders have picked off seven passes, with safety Julian Lobe and cornerback Nehemiah Pritchett tied for the club lead with two interceptions. The latter is also second behind Love (5) with four passes defensed.
It’s been a very rough start in 2026 for Broncos’ third-year quarterback Bo Nix, who has nearly as many turnovers (5) as touchdown passes (6) in five outings. He’s also completing just 59.9 percent of his passes and Denver’s offense has scored only nine TDs. Pritchett may indeed add to his pick total—especially is Seattle’s pass rush gets to Nix early and often.

title: Raheem Morris is Already Proving the 49ers Right for Hiring Him
full_text:
Arguably, the best offseason addition the San Francisco 49ers made this year was hiring Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator.
The level at which he has the 49ers' defense performing is astonishing. Through five games this season, the 49ers are allowing 297.2 yards per game, the sixth-fewest in the NFL.
Most importantly, they're only allowing 18.6 points per game, the third-lowest in the league. Those numbers are impressive, but even those stats don't perfectly represent Morris' impact.
Look no further than how the 49ers' secondary is playing. They've been lights-out, which you couldn't fathom last year. They weren't remotely impressive under Robert Saleh.
That's the key difference between Saleh and Morris . It's why Morris is already proving the 49ers right for hiring him. His secondary is performing incredibly well, and they're doing it without much help from their pass rush.
The 49ers rank as the 12th-lowest-pressure-rate defense at 34.2%. And I know they balled out against the Seattle Seahawks, sacking Sam Darnold five times.
However, that can be a credit to the secondary. Darnold wasn't confident enough to throw to his receivers since they were guarded so tightly.
And when he did have confidence, he was picked off twice by Renardo Green. He's been balling out this year, along with the rest of the defensive backs, and it's thanks to Morris' scheme.
“It doesn't surprise me with Raheem. I've just been around him for too long. He's one of the best people and best coaches I've ever been around," Kyle Shanahan said. "I tried to bring him here originally when I left Atlanta. They wouldn't let him out. So, it's been a long time coming to get him here.
"He's done an unbelievable job this year, especially with the injuries, but just overall everything he's mixed up schematically. I love the confidence he's given our DBs and the way they've been playing since training camp. He's had a real huge effect on this team and we're very lucky to have him.”
Morris has the secondary playing at a different level. They're playing with a ton of fire thanks to him. It's no wonder every defensive back said they were excited to play for Morris.
And to think, it's only been five games. How much better can this defense get as they continue to ascend?
Just imagine how this secondary will look with Bosa back, and maybe another pass rusher. They will take their already sweet defense to nightmarish heights.

title: 2 Overlooked Stats Show How Elite the 49ers Offense Is
full_text:
The 49ers' offense has been on a tear this season. Brock Purdy is playing as sharp as ever, Mike Evans is dominating, George Kittle is insane, and the offensive line is elite.
All of that is contributing to the 49ers averaging 30.8 points per game, the third-most in the NFL. They also average 365 yards per game, the ninth-most in the NFL.
Those stats are nice and all, but there are a couple of overlooked ones that show how elite the 49ers' offense is. Let's dive into what those two overlooked stats are.
Negative Play % through Week 5 pic.twitter.com/Uun49NjhMS
One reason the 49ers put up a bunch of yards is that they consistently gain positive yardage. They have the second-lowest negative play percentage in the NFL at just under 4%.
You could argue that they're truly the top offense at limiting negative plays instead of the Broncos, since their quarterback, Bo Nix, loves to play it safe, as he did against the 49ers with a ton of checkdown throws.
In any case, having 96% of the plays called and executed going for a positive gain is vastly impressive. This shows that Purdy is connecting well with his receivers and kept clean on his dropbacks.
The running game is also running effectively with Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. Kyle Shanahan deserves a round of applause as well.
His game plan and feel for calling the right plays at the right time play a crucial role in their offense being ranked the second-lowest for negative plays. They're easily an unstoppable force with this depiction.
red zone touchdown rate this season: 87.5% - San Francisco 49ers 83.3% - Dallas Cowboys 81.3% - New Orleans Saints 77.3% - Detroit Lions 73.7% - Baltimore Ravens 71.4% - Buffalo Bills 69.2% - Atlanta Falcons 68.4% - Los Angeles Rams 66.7% - Indianapolis Colts 64.7% - Carolina…
The reward for having less than 4% negative plays and tallying a bunch of yards is red zone trips. And whenever the 49ers get there, they maximize their opportunity.
The 49ers are scoring a touchdown on 87.5% of their red zone trips this season, the most in the league. This is crucial to why their offense has been a problem for opposing defenses.
Anytime the 49ers get into the red zone, they're most likely going to score a touchdown. That is the difference between elite and good offenses.
They don't settle for field goals, which is a testament to Evans. He's given the 49ers a phenomenal boost in the red zone, especially when they're near the goal line.
Purdy has done an excellent job of putting it in the perfect spot for Evans. The 49ers' offense is riding high, and now that they've gotten past the Seahawks, it's unlikely any defense will slow them down in the near future.

title: How the 49ers’ Improved Defense Takes them to Another Level
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers (5-0) defeated the Seattle Seahawks (3-2) 32-29, beating their divisional foe and the defending Super Bowl champions after the 49ers' loss to Seattle in two pivotal games to end last season.
The 49ers' offense is similar to last season's, but has improved with Brock Purdy taking a step forward and the free-agent signing of Mike Evans. But what stood out in the 49ers' win in Seattle was the improvement from their defense.
In three games last season, San Francisco forced just two turnovers against the Seahawks; on Sunday, the team doubled that, with four turnovers: two interceptions and two fumbles recovered.
“I thought the D was unbelievable today. I mean to get us those four turnovers that was the difference between winning and losing today,” coach Kyle Shanahan said postgame.“To be able to get those points off those turnovers I thought they limited their explosives defended the run well.”
Seattle's offense has gotten weaker, losing running back Kenneth Walker to the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency.
But the 49ers' hiring of defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, offseason additions, and young players developing from last year have helped the unit reach a new level.
So far, Morris’ defense allows 18.6 points per game, down from 22.7 that the 49ers averaged last season.
49ers linebacker Fred Warner, who missed the last two games against Seattle last season, returned to the rivalry, forcing one fumble while leading the team with 10 tackles.
His presence alone improved the defense's outlook, along with a standout performances from rookie defensive lineman Gracen Halten who had three tackles, two tackles for loss a sack and a forced fumble in which he recovered for a touchdown.
Linebacker Jayden Dugger, who had one sack and two tackles for loss. Dugger filled in well for outside linebacker Dre Greenlaw, who was disqualified in the second quarter . This 49ers rookie class has made a meaningful impact.
Morris has also improved the team's secondary, allowing 199 passing yards per game, down from 222 passing yards in 2025.
Morris has significantly helped develop cornerback Renardo Green, who leads the team with three interceptions this season, two against Seattle. In previous seasons, Green has only had one interception in his career.
“Renardo’s ceiling is very high. I think he can be a very good corner in this league and he’s showing that,” Shanahan said. “I mean, he was big time today; it wasn’t just the two picks but stopping the slant there at the end when they were right in that field goal range.”
A big surprise has been its safeties, which are a unit many had concerns about heading into this season.
Ji'Ayir Brown has taken a step forward, already recording 34 tackles, nearly half as many as he had in any other full season (76.5).
Additionally, Morris has improved one of the 49ers' most injury-plagued units, the defensive line. Morris has been more aggressive with his pass rush than previous coordinators, getting 2.2 sacks per game. Last year, the 49ers averaged 1.2 sacks per game.
The 49ers will also get defensive end Nick Bosa back, who sustained a calf injury in Week 1. He has been limited and has struggled with injuries over the last two seasons, but anything he provides will help the unit.

title: Ranking the 49ers Players Most Likely to be Traded Before the Deadline
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers are more likely to be buying at the trade deadline than selling. However, if the right offer came their way for certain players, they could look to sell. Who could be on the move from San Francisco next month?
Jones is not a lock to get traded, but he is still the most likely. Enough teams are still in the mix, and his perception is still strong from last season. If a contender like the Minnesota Vikings had an injury and needed to make a big trade for Jones, the 49ers would struggle to say no. The 49ers have said they wanted a second-round pick. If he becomes a half-season rental, do they shift to a third?
Mustapha is starting for the injured Marques Sigle, but Sigle will be back in the lineup soon. When he returns, Mustapha will be a safety in his third NFL season with at least 23 NFL starts. However, he is currently depth in the new Raheem Morris defense. If Mustapha has another good start or two, he could net them a fourth- or fifth-round pick.
Brown is starting, and Mustapha is not. However, they might get about the same value on the trade market because Brown is in the last year of his deal, and the team acquiring Mustapha will have him in 2027 as well. The 49ers could trade Brown, and start Mustapha next to Sigle.
Greenlaw was thrown out of the 49ers' Week 5 win, and rookie Jaden Dugger excelled. Greenlaw is now suspended for Week 6 . If Dugger continues to play well, the team could invest more in the rookie by trading Greenlaw. The issue is Greenlaw appears to be more valuable to San Francisco than any other team. A Day Three pick is all they would get back.
Stick with me for a second. Let's say the 49ers trade for an edge rusher at the deadline. Nick Bosa and Mykel Williams are back, as is rookie Romello Height. White is not signed beyond this year and is not a Raheem Morris addition. San Francisco could move on if a team offers a fifth-round pick or more.
Bethune is inactive most weeks but could compete to start for some teams. A day-three pick could get him traded.
Jones has been a disappointment, but he started the past two years and is not in the starting mix in San Francisco.

title: 49ers Don’t Need to Make a Blockbuster Wide Receiver Trade
full_text:
That’s what it feels like the 49ers should put up at the wide receiver position. They have a stockpile of injuries that recently increased with Deebo Samuel , the latest to join it.
Samuel hurt his hamstring in the win against the Seahawks. The 49ers are expecting him to be out for some time, further thinning a position that’s been without Demarcus Robinson and De’Zhaun Stribling.
Mike Evans is the only trustworthy wide receiver the 49ers have right now. With all of the injuries at the position, the 49ers may be inclined to make a blockbuster trade .
Marvin Harrison Jr. was just traded to the Texans, so the market for receivers has been kickstarted. However, it makes no sense for the 49ers to make a blockbuster wide receiver trade.
They are not desperate at the position as it’s made out to be. All of their receivers who were injured during the season weren’t season-ending. Samuel, Robinson, and Stribling will be back.
You can bank on Robinson returning in Week 9 against the Raiders after nursing a high ankle sprain. Samuel will likely be back for that game as well. The only one that’ll take more time is Stribling. Christian Kirk might be back soon too.
The 49ers will be full strength at wide receiver in a matter of a few weeks. All they have to do is endure two more games without them, which are against the Commanders and the Falcons.
I’d like to think the 49ers are more than capable of beating those teams without those three receivers. Even Kyle Shanahan believes the 49ers are fine getting by with the players they have.
“I think we have enough,” Shanahan said. “We’ve got three guys on practice squad also who can help. Anytime you lose this number of guys, four guys or five guys whatever it is, it's a huge challenge. But, we do have guys in this building who can do it and we'll always look.”
Now, if the 49ers want to make a trade for Jauan Jennings, that’s sensible. It shouldn’t cost much to acquire him, and he can immediately contribute.
Those are the types of trades the 49ers should consider for receivers – bargains. A blockbuster is unnecessary when they have Evans, George Kittle, and the rest of their receivers returning.
The only blockbuster trade the 49ers should make is for a pass rusher. Otherwise, it’s unnecessary. They’re fine at wide receiver.

title: 3 Offseason Moves That are Paying Off Big for the 49ers
full_text:
Starting the season 5-0 is a dream start for the San Francisco 49ers. Everyone has been clicking on all cylinders for them to be undefeated through five games.
However, I want to take this time to recognize the offseason additions the 49ers made. Many of them have performed well, but three offseason additions are paying off the most so far, starting with hiring Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator.
It's probably safe to say now that Morris is an upgrade over Robert Saleh . I know that Saleh was given an unfair shake with Nick Bosa and Fred Warner out last year.
Saleh had nothing to work with last year. However, the secondary he had is the same that Morris has, and Morris is getting way more out of this group than Saleh did.
It's not even close. That alone has been significant for the 49ers because they had promising players in the secondary. They just needed a coach to get the potential out of him, and so far, Morris is doing it.
There's a reason every defensive back spoke highly of Morris during training camp. They knew immediately that his scheme would help them.
Plus, Morris doesn't play a straightforward defense that Saleh likes. There's more trickery afoot with his defense, which is the cherry on top of how sweet an addition and upgrade he's been.
This was the most obvious, right? After the monstrous performance he had against the Seattle Seahawks, Mike Evans is clearly one of the best offseason additions for the 49ers.
The guy is a walking first down. Of his 24 catches this season, 22 of them have gone for a first down. That's insane. Not to mention that he's a goal-line nightmare for defensive backs.
All Brock Purdy has to do if he wants a touchdown or a first down is to throw it to Evans. He's somewhere down there, right?
Thanks to Evans, the 49ers have been more of a passing offense this year. It's helping alleviate the workload for Christian McCaffrey. The impact Evans is having has been sensational.
Injuries to Alfred Collins and C.J. West have granted rookie Gracen Halton a phenomenal opportunity to be a key player. But after his performance against the Seahawks, he's more than a key player – he's an impactful one.
Halton arguably had the play of the game when he forced a fumble and recovered it in the endzone to score a touchdown near the end of the first half.
Without that, the 49ers probably lose the game. He also registered a sack on Sam Darnold. Halton has been the best rookie on the 49ers. What a draft pick.

title: Why There's No Better Time for 49ers GM John Lynch to Make a Trade
full_text:
There's no better time for San Francisco 49ers general manager John Lynch to make a trade than right now.
Following the draft, and then the schedule release, it felt inconceivable to see how these first five games have panned out.
Having the Denver Broncos, a team that made the AFC Championship last year, in addition to facing the Los Angeles Rams and the reigning Super Bowl winners, the Seattle Seahawks, in their first five games was a very tricky start on paper.
Yet here they are now, 5-0 with a 3-0 record in the NFC West. Talk about perfect starts.
Considering their perfect record, they will go up against the Washington Commanders and the Atlanta Falcons for the next two weeks. They're two games that the 49ers shouldn't underestimate by any means, but they're the more winnable games on their schedule, especially when they have some tougher tests later on.
So, wins have been more important than ever in the first half, but the thought of going 7-0 into the bye week is within touching distance.
Lynch has repeatedly stated that the 49ers must earn the right to make a trade through on-field success before he considers bringing in reinforcements.
While preserving draft capital is sensible, particularly given how previous trades have set San Francisco back, the Trey Lance fiasco being the clearest example, there comes a point when the opportunity to compete for a Super Bowl must take priority.
The 49ers are 5-0 for the third time under Kyle Shanahan. The last two times this happened, the City by the Bay went to the Super Bowl. A potential return is right there. With momentum building, this is the time for Lynch to identify an impact player who can help take the team to the next level.
Some will argue that the defense needs reinforcements, but the victory over Seattle showed that Raheem Morris' unit can still deliver despite injuries to key players, including Nick Bosa.
San Francisco desperately needs help at wide reciever. Mike Evans , who is ironically dealing with a rib injury himself, has been the last best remaining starter on offense and has made a significant difference with back-to-back impressive performances against the Broncos and Seahawks.
The 49ers are dangerously thin at wide receiver, and a trade for an established playmaker would make plenty of sense.
There is also a bigger picture to consider. This could genuinely be the final opportunity for this core to win a Super Bowl together. Trent Williams has hinted at retirement as early as next year, Kyle Juszczyk's contract expires after this season, Bosa's contract situation will need addressing, and Deebo Samuel and Dre Greenlaw are both on one-year deals following their returns this season.
Lynch has consistently shown how much this core means to the franchise. Now, he has an opportunity to reward that commitment by bringing in an impactful wide receiver while the current group works its way back from injuries.
The 49ers have earned the right to be aggressive. Now is the time for Lynch to act.

title: 49ers LT Trent Williams' Latest Performance Shouldn't Be Taken for Granted
full_text:
San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams continues to prove that age is just a number.
At 38, he's still one of the best tackles in the league, but there's even more reason to suggest he's at the top of that list so far this season.
Williams has remained all business since signing a two-year extension this offseason , and that approach has translated to the field, helping the 49ers get off to a 5-0 start through the first five games.
As a unit, the offensive line was incredible through the first four games. Brock Purdy hadn't been sacked, yet he came through and produced incredible performances worthy of an MVP award.
Williams, of course, was one of the bright spots. But in Week 5, against the reigning Super Bowl champions on their home turf, he elevated his game to even greater heights.
He was dominant in pass protection, recording 34 pass-blocking opportunities without allowing a single pressure, sack, or quarterback hit. His practically flawless performance earned him a 100.0 pass-block efficiency rating.
He's at the stage in his career where every dominant performance should serve as a reminder to appreciate what the 49ers have while they still can.
Williams is producing the goods at an elite level - something that's unprecedented for his age. He will not be around forever, so these performances against arguably superior opposition need to be savoured.
Like much of this roster, Mike Evans aside, the only thing missing from Williams' résumé is a Lombardi Trophy. The 49ers are off to a perfect 5-0 start, with Williams playing a significant role in this stretch. If this core is going to win a championship together, this could be its best, and perhaps final, opportunity to get over the line.
Undoubtedly, a place in the Hall of Fame awaits Williams, but winning a Super Bowl would add another remarkable accolade to his legacy. It is the biggest metric of success in this league for a reason. Given his journey and everything he has accomplished, a championship would make an already incredible story that much more special.
It's almost one and a half years more with Williams before he likely retires . So it's important to keep him as healthy as possible, as he will always produce excellent performances.
What the 49ers need is some luck on the injury front, but so far, going 5-0 and 3-0 in the division is about as perfect a start as they could have hoped for in their Super Bowl quest.

title: 3 Reasons the 49ers Will Be Perfectly Fine Without Dre Greenlaw
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers will be down one key player on defense in their next game, and it surprisingly won't be due to injury.
Dre Greenlaw will be out of the 49ers' Week 6 contest after t he NFL suspended him for his headbutt on a helmetless Ernest Jones in the win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Being without Greenlaw is a bummer, but the 49ers will actually be perfectly fine without him. Let's dive into the three reasons why they will be.
When Greenlaw was ejected, the 49ers used rookie Jaden Dugger in his stead on base-packages. Dugger did well in this role, so he'll be the first to look at for filling in.
He doesn't get utilized a ton in nickel packages, but I think the 49ers will work him in more there during practice this week. Garrett Wallow would've been an option, but he'll be out with a hamstring injury.
Luke Gifford will be another player they will consider, but I wouldn't call him a "capable" player. Dugger is their best option, and he's more than fine at filling in for Greenlaw.
It's also possible the 49ers look at Tatum Bethune there. He was a healthy scratch against the Seahawks, so we'll see if the 49ers think he can go out there and help.
If the linebackers aren't as capable as the 49ers think, then Raheem Morris will adapt. He's done a tremendous job this season so far, and there's no reason to doubt his ability to mask Greenlaw's absence.
The only thing he can't account for is Greenlaw's energy. That intensity is something he can't help with, but he can move his defense around to account for what Greenlaw was giving them.
It won't be perfect, but he should be able to get the defense to cover up Greenlaw's loss enough, especially since whoever fills in for him will likely be a prime target to be thrown and run at.
Whether the first two points work out or not, at the end of the day, the 49ers will be facing the lowly Washington Commanders. They are insanely mediocre.
Do the 49ers need Greenlaw to beat them? Absolutely not. If they did, they'd have a massive problem on their hands.
Defeating the Commanders should be a lock. They're coming off an embarrassing tie with the New York Giants after Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn's overtime blunder.
The Commanders are in shambles, with their defense as their only decent aspect. San Francisco's defense will be perfectly fine without Greenlaw against a terrible offense.

title: Brock Purdy Reminded Everyone of his Greatest Trait Against Seahawks
full_text:
What an incredible win the San Francisco 49ers got over the Seattle Seahawks . Entering the season, it was by far their toughest matchup on the schedule.
Winning by three points and going down to the wire proved that. The 49ers were significantly better in this game than they were in any of their three contests against Seattle last year.
Brock Purdy was one significant reason for that. He delivered dime after dime to Mike Evans , who dominated Seattle from start to finish.
However, his performance goes beyond his connection with Evans. Just in case anyone forgot, Purdy reminded everyone of his greatest trait against the Seahawks.
It's his mental toughness. That's his elite trait. I've been pointing it out for over three years . The guy has insanely strong mental fortitude. Not even a tank can measure up to it.
Purdy went into a chaotic environment at Lumen Field against the best defense in the NFL, one that has owned him and the 49ers' offense in the last two games, and was nails.
He could've easily folded under the immense pressure. He knew how big-time that game was. It wasn't just about beating a divisional opponent. The 49ers needed to stand up to their nightmare – Seattle's defense.
Purdy didn't let any of the last two matchups with the Seahawks bother him. He went into this game as cool as a cucumber. It's so impressive how he manages to remain unfazed.
But that's been evident since he became the starter in 2022. Whether it was primetime games or the playoffs, he doesn't get timid in important games.
The pressure of the game is one way he proves his mental toughness. Another way is how he responds to physical pressure in a game.
Quarterbacks who start to get sacked, hit, and pressured will likely fold over time. That could've easily happened to Purdy against the Seahawks.
He was pressured on 17 of his 34 dropbacks (50.0%), the third-highest pressure rate he has faced in a game in his career.
If he had started to struggle, no one would've blamed him. But he didn't. Not one bit. He knew what was going to happen to him in this game, despite how amazing his offensive line has been this season.
And while the 49ers' offense couldn't sustain drives for the majority of the game, Purdy helped lead the most important drive of the game, which started in the third quarter while down 26-21.
The 49ers went on a 12-play, 74-yard series that came away with a touchdown. Again, Purdy didn't get discouraged by the weight of the game, the pressure in his face, and the fact that they struggled to move the ball a lot.
Did he play a great game as he did against the Miami Dolphins and the Arizona Cardinals? No. But against the NFL's best defense on the road, he proved more in that game than against Miami and Arizona.
Purdy has raised his game this season. It's tough to deny that, but one thing that's never been debatable is his elite mental toughness, and he reminded everyone of that in the win against the Seahawks.

title: Have the Buccaneers Found Their Offensive Identity for the 2026 Season?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers got their first win of the season against the Dallas Cowboys. It was a back-and-forth game where the defense was able to do enough to help get the win, but a bigger storyline coming out of the game is the offense.
It feels like for the first time this season, the Bucs offense was in sync and able to find its footing. This was mainly due to the work of Zac Robinson, which limited what Jalon Daniels needed to do for this offense and the great running ability of back Bucky Irving.
Irving really has come back to form this season, posting 21 carries for 165 yards and a rushing touchdown against Dallas as well as two catches for ten yards and a touchdown as well. Irving already has 77 carries for 406 rushing yards and two touchdowns this season, only 182 yards away from his total last year in 2025, playing in half as many games to this point.
I believe that the Bucs' offensive identity in 2026 will literally run through Bucky Irving, something that shouldn't be too surprising when we look at Zac Robinson's history as offensive coordinator in Atlanta.
Robinson ran both Bijan Robinson and Tyler Allgeier wild in 2024 and 2025, with both backs combined having 441 carries for 2100 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns as well as 74 receptions for 519 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown in 2024. In 2025, it was 430 carries for 1992 rushing yards and 15 rushing touchdowns along with 93 receptions for 916 receiving yards and four receiving touchdowns.
I think that the team does need to see more usage from Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker going forward, but it's very clear that Robinson plans to use Irving in some type of Bijan role going forward with this team.
There are pros and cons to this type of identity, as many expected players like Baker Mayfield, Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin Jr. to lead the way for this offense this season. However, the positive is that it could help Mayfield button up some of the offensive struggles he had before his injury this season and limit turnovers overall.
Time will tell if this formula will work for Tampa Bay in the long run, but it seems like we've had a glimpse into what Robinson wants to do going forward.

title: Buccaneers Wednesday Practice Updates: Is Baker Mayfield Back?
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are set to face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday as they try to move to 2-4 on the year and turn around what is already a season on the brink.
When they do so, they're set to have undrafted free agent rookie Jalon Daniels under center for the third game in a row. Starting quarterback Baker Mayfield, whom the team signed to a three-year, $165 million extension this offseason, dislocated his thumb against the Minnesota Vikings and has been out for the last two games.
Mayfield has been trying to work his way back sooner rather than later. But did he return to practice on Wednesday to test out his thumb ahead of the Steelers matchup Sunday? We have the latest update on Mayfield and more from Wednesday's practice:
Mayfield did not return to practice on Wednesday. He appears to still be recovering from his dislocated thumb — the stitches in his thumb have reportedly been taken out, but he still needs to find the strength to grip the football, and he may not be there yet.
In other injury news, both running back Sean Tucker and cornerback Ayden Garnes were working off to the side with a trainer on Wednesday.
Tucker had just seven snaps against the Cowboys, and Garnes had just one snap on defense along with special teams duties. A Tucker injury would limit Tampa Bay's variety in the backfield, but a Garnes injury would not be too bad in the grand scheme of things — he was active to fill in for cornerback Benjamin Morrison, and he has been inactive for the rest of the year otherwise.
Morrison was back to practice after missing two games with a quad injury. So was linebacker SirVocea Dennis, who has been out with an ankle injury since Week 4. Both players provide valuable depth on the defense and are key special teams players, so that should help Tampa Bay in Week 5 if they're able to play.
The Bucs play the Steelers on Oct. 18 at 1 p.m. at Raymond James Stadium.

Tampa Bay is set to play the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 6. That game could move it to 2-4, and with the NFC South as weak as it is, the Bucs could still be in the playoff hunt if they start putting some wins together. Another loss, however, could put them out of reach depending on what happens.

"Honest question, and I suppose this is a feather in the cap of Jason Licht: How the hell wasn’t Jalon Daniels drafted? title: Buccaneers Could Get Wide Receiver Back vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers had what they considered to be quite a deep wide receivers corps heading into 2026. Unfortunately, that idea hasn't exactly shown up on the turf through Week 5.
Wideouts Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, both considered to be focal points of the offense, haven't produced relative to expectations. Jalen McMillan, expected to be a valuable weapon for the Bucs, has played just one game so far this season, and he's currently recovering from a knee injury.
Other wideouts, like rookie Ted Hurst and second-year player Tez Johnson, have had to step up in McMillan's place.
But now, the Bucs may be getting back another wide receiver they've been missing all year to help bolster that receiving corps, and he could come back as soon as Sunday when the Buccaneers play the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Bucs wideout David Sills V, who injured himself during training camp with a hamstring injury and was placed on injured reserve, opened his 21-day practice window on Monday. Sills will get his first bit of practice for the first time in a long time on Wednesday as the Bucs prepare for the Steelers.
Sills is a big-bodied wideout who could help Tampa Bay on the outside. He played with Zac Robinson last season with the Atlanta Falcons, so Robinson knows how to use him and the two understand each other's offensive goals quite well.
With McMillan still out, Sills could end up being valuable depth for the Bucs — if Tampa Bay wants to make use of him. Sills has 21 days from Oct. 12 to get back on the field and return to Tampa Bay's active roster. If he does not do so within those 21 days, he remains on IR and must remain there until the end of the season.
As it stands, Tampa Bay's 53-man roster is full. That means that if the Bucs want Sills on the active roster, they'll have to move another player off to make room — that player could go to Tampa Bay's practice squad or get released entirely.
If Sills is able to get back in time for Tampa Bay's game against the Steelers, quarterback Jalon Daniels will have another weapon to work with on offense. If not, he could shoot for the week after against the Carolina Panthers, where starting QB Baker Mayfield will likely be quarterback after he recovers from his thumb injury.
The Bucs play the Steelers on Oct. 18 in Raymond James Stadium.

title: Jalon Daniels' Advanced Metrics Trending Upward After First Career Win With Bucs
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers felt dead in the water after starting the season 0-3. And then the unthinkable happened.
They were forced to start an undrafted rookie at quarterback after Baker Mayfield went down with an injury.
Jalon Daniels was thrust into the fire early in his NFL career, but it didn't net him success in his first start. However, he and the team were able to figure out what works best, as he went on to win his second career start against the Dallas Cowboys.
In Week 4 against the Green Bay Packers, in his first start, Daniels was turbulent. He completed 19 passes for 148 yards and a touchdown, but he also threw two interceptions and took three sacks, resulting in a negative passing EPA (expected points added) of -0.194.
EPA, which measures the value of a play based on how much it increases or decreases a team's likelihood of scoring, tells a deeper story about how a player is impacting his team's success.
Daniels was able to flip his impact on the game with a positive EPA against the Cowboys on Thursday Night Football, coming away with a positive +0.229 EPA. He completed 76% of his passes for 189 yards, one touchdown, no interceptions and just one sack.
Drastically cutting down on high-risk mistakes and going turnover-free showed his improved decision-making after just one game in a primetime spot.
It wasn't just Daniels who looked sharp against Dallas. It was also the positions that offensive coordinator Zac Robinson was putting him in.
Across both games, Daniels has produced a high completion rate, but an extremely low average depth of target (4.1 yards).
While that didn't necessarily work against the Packers, it did against the Cowboys. It goes to show that Robinson is scheming up high-percentage throws that protect his young quarterback from facing heavy pressure, mitigating negative plays.
This has also allowed Daniels to get the ball out fast to his playmakers to go and make plays, rather than putting all the pressure on himself.
Daniels has also been efficient when using his legs, which will only continue to add another layer to his game as he continues trending upward in the absence of Mayfield.
While Daniels isn't pushing the ball downfield just yet, his trajectory is pointing upward, which likely means Robinson and staff will feel more comfortable opening up the offense for him.
If Daniels can continue the efficient play and growth that we have seen through his first two career starts, the Bucs could be in a good position to steal another game or two while Mayfield works his way back.
No matter what, it's great to see that an undrafted rookie is making the most of the opportunities given to him. The Bucs must make the most of this if they hope to remain in the race for the NFC South, and that might just come down to Daniels continuing to elevate his game over the next week or two.

title: The Most Surprising Group for the Buccaneers During the 2026 Season
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers defense has actually done pretty well the past couple of weeks in matchups against the Green Bay Packers and the Dallas Cowboys. The unit helped keep the Bucs in games, and if the offense were better, we would likely be talking about a Bucs team that has a better record than it does right now.
One of the biggest reasons for that is due to a group that started this season as a massive question mark, but has quickly turned into one of the great strengths of the team — the cornerback room.
Let's start off with the player who has likely looked the most impressive — cornerback Jacob Parrish.
Parrish had more pressure placed on him this off-season as he was going to move from inside corner to outside corner due to the lack of depth. So far to this point, Parrish has taken the move in stride and has made multiple plays on the football, including snagging an interception this season.
Zyon McCollum is another player who has really risen to the occasion for the Bucs.
Coming off a very disappointing 2025 season that left many fans wanting the team to move on, McCollum has stepped up against some of the best receivers in the league, CeeDee Lamb and Ja'Marr Chase, and has returned to form as the corner who earned the massive extension with the Buccaneers in the first place.
Finally, we have some surprises in Keionte Scott and Benjamin Morrison. Yes, Scott is a rookie nickel corner for the Buccaneers, but he really has done an excellent job in the short amount of time he's been on the team. He does make mistakes, but overall, it's hard to be too disappointed with how the recent fourth-round rookie has looked for the team.
When Morrison has been able to stay healthy this season, he has shown some great strides in his overall play, especially as a run defender. Yes, he is still struggling with staying healthy, but this is a far cry from the Morrison who looked completely out of place as a rookie last year and should give the Bucs some much-needed depth going forward if he is able to maintain his health.
The future seems bright for this Bucs corner room, and hopefully these players continue to grow and evolve as a strength for this team.

title: Why Baker Mayfield Shouldn’t Start for Buccaneers Against Steelers
full_text:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers starting quarterback Baker Mayfield seems to be recovering well from his dislocated thumb suffered in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings.
However, it may not be the wisest of decisions to bring him back this quickly when the Bucs face off against the Pittsburgh Steelers after a long break when they beat the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
After starting the season 0-4 with three of those losses coming with Mayfield at the helm of the offense, the Bucs were finally able to get their first victory with Jalon Daniels commanding the offense.
It wasn't the most spectacular outing for Daniels, but he was able to provide a spark that helped the offense look competent — something they haven't looked like all season.
Daniels performed admirably in his first start, a loss to the Green Bay Packers, but was able to lift the offense against the Cowboys. His charismatic energy, passion, and love for the game seemed to reverberate throughout the rest of the team. That instilled confidence in every player around him.
Everything about the offense seemed to run smoothly, sparking the Bucs to score their second-most points of the season.
Inserting Mayfield at less than 100% against the Steelers would be a disservice given the spark that Daniels has brought to this team.
Mayfield signed a massive extension this past offseason, so bringing him back and putting him in a position to further injure the same injury or worse could put the future of their franchise quarterback in jeopardy.
With the dislocation being on his throwing hand, life will be difficult for Mayfield when it comes to gripping the ball, which will lead to decreased ball security and velocity on his throws.
With further injury and heightened risk of turnover prevalent in rushing Mayfield back against the Steelers in Week 6, it would be smart for the Bucs to continue letting him rehab no matter how much he pushes to return sooner.
The season isn't a complete loss yet, with Tampa Bay still within shouting distance of the NFC South lead.
Taking one step forward after a win, only to take two steps back by playing his injury and rehab wrong, would further put pressure on the front office and coaching staff.

title: Bucs Get Surprising Odds Against Steelers With Baker Mayfield Out
full_text:
Even after the Tampa Bay Buccaneers shut down the Dallas Cowboys' prolific offense on the road last Thursday night to secure their first victory of the year, it's tough to suggest that vibes in Tampa Bay are high considering how low they were just a few days ago.
Still, the Bucs have finally found the win column, and the hope among the fanbase is that the Bucs' defense is for real and that UDFA rookie QB Jalon Daniels can continue to hold down the fort until Baker Mayfield returns.
The Buccaneers' next test will come on October 18th when Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers come to Raymond James Stadium.
Like the Bucs, the Steelers are coming off an impressive victory where they trampled the Colts. Unlike the Buccaneers, though, Pittsburgh maintains a winning record of 3-2 on the year while competing for the top spot in AFC North.
Despite how differently the seasons have gone for these two teams, it appears as though the oddsmakers in Vegas still believe the Buccaneers have what it takes to hang tight with the Steelers next Sunday. According to FanDuel , the Bucs are just a +2.5 underdog, expected to keep the final score within a field goal.
Although the Bucs defense played an extremely well-rounded game vs. the Cowboys last week, they still almost blew the game playing against arguably the worst defense in football.
Whether or not you agree with the line set for the Bucs-Steelers game, one thing is clear — the experts responsible for setting these lines clearly believe that Daniels, despite his lack of experience, is capable of running a successful offense.
Daniels doesn't need to win the game on his own. He just needs to run Zac Robinson's offense efficiently by controlling the time of possession battle and limiting turnover-worthy plays.
Daniels proved in Dallas that he is fully capable of making sound decisions, both in the pocket and on the move, which ultimately allowed his team to control the clock and limit the opportunities for Prescott and the Cowboys' explosive offense to put points on the board.
If Daniels is able to continue to build off the positive momentum he established in Week 5, there's no reason why the Buccaneers couldn't upset the Steelers at Raymond James Stadium.

title: Was Mike Evans Right to Leave Buccaneers for 49ers?
full_text:
Some players are franchise legends for their entire career and make their name with just one team. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers know what that's like — linebacker Lavonte David was one of those players, and he retired in 2025 after 14 seasons in red and pewter.
The Bucs also thought wideout Mike Evans was going to be one of those players — and so did he. When Evans re-signed with the Bucs before the start of the 2024 season, he famously declared that he was set to be a "Buc for life." Two years later, he was gone.
Evans decided to spurn the Bucs in free agency and sign with the San Francisco 49ers instead, leaving the team after 12 years of service. There's been plenty of talk about that move ever since it happened, and now that we're five weeks into the season, we're getting a clearer look at where Evans and the Bucs currently stand.
The look? Tampa Bay is 1-4 and staring at oblivion, and Evans and the 49ers are 5-0 and looking toward the Super Bowl.
So, was Evans right in leaving the Buccaneers to chase glory at the end of his career? It sure looks like it right now.
There's no doubt that being a one-franchise player would have meant a lot to Evans. But there are things that matter more, and he's on a better track to achieve those things in San Francisco than he would have been in Tampa Bay.
Evans wants to be a Hall of Famer. To do that, he needs more production, he needs to be in the public eye more often and he needs to be on a team that could potentially win him a ring in the future. There was a time with Tom Brady that the Bucs hit on all three of those requirements, but that time is far gone.
The Bucs are not a Super Bowl-caliber team. They also have multiple wide receivers on their roster to share targets with, so Evans wouldn't have gotten the share he wanted, and with Brady gone and the Bucs middling, Evans likely wouldn't have gotten the exposure required for a Hall of Fame bid.
Even worse? The Buccaneers could be staring at a rebuild next season. If head coach Todd Bowles is fired (and maybe even general manager Jason Licht), the Bucs will be starting from scratch, and Evans could have simply been on his way out regardless. Retiring as a member of the team and continuing to make his case as a Hall of Famer now seems entirely impossible, and that the gamble Evans made here was right.
Whether it was because of what happened at the end of 2025 and the infamous third-and-28 or because he simply wanted a change of scenery, Evans was certainly right to separate from Tampa Bay. And he's proved it already in Week 5 of the regular season.
The Bucs face off against the Steelers in Week 6 to try to move to 2-4 on the year. Evans and the 49ers face off against the Washington Commanders to try and move to 6-0.

title: Titans' Cam Ward Officially Hits Rock Bottom After Disastrous Start to Year 2
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans were looking for second-year quarterback Cam Ward to take a major leap in 2026, but the exact opposite has happened over the first month of the season.
Ward has been incredibly underwhelming so far this year. The Miami product has completed 63.2% of his passes for 896 passing yards, three touchdowns, and three interceptions, and hasn't led Tennessee's offense to consistent production.
Though he hasn't been given the best support from his coaches and teammates at times, Ward's struggles are mostly on him . As a result, the 2025 No. 1 overall pick officially hit rock bottom in the latest power rankings of NFL quarterbacks.
Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame released his power rankings of the NFL starting quarterbacks through five weeks, and Ward finished last. Ward was No. 25 in Verderame's preseason rankings, but fell seven spots after his lackluster start.
"The stats don’t do justice to how much Ward has struggled in Tennessee. Last week, he threw for only 70 yards over the first three quarters in a 26–3 loss to the Texans. He has yet to throw for 250 yards in a game. It’s been a disaster, and one that must have the Titans thinking about drafting his replacement in April," Verderame wrote.
Ward is still a developing signal-caller who could end up being the Titans' long-term solution at the most pivotal position in the sport. However, he's been awful this season and hasn't lived up to his top-pick status at all.
With Tennessee at 0-5 and on the road against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday , the next few weeks will be critical for Ward. If he can at least show growth and put the Titans in a position to be in competitive games, Ward will build a stronger argument to be the No. 1 quarterback in Nashville in 2027.
However, if the 24-year-old continues to turn the ball over and be a detriment to Tennessee's chances of winning, head coach Robert Saleh may begin thinking of playing Mitch Trubisky to provide his team with a possible spark. That scenario would also prompt uncomfortable conversations about Ward's future with the Titans just a year and a half after he was the first overall selection.

title: Robert Saleh Speaks on Poor Run Game, Announces Tony Pollard as Inactive for Wednesday Practice
full_text:
On Wednesday, head coach Robert Saleh announced to the media that starting RB Tony Pollard was inactive in practice with an undisclosed injury.
Pollard has time to return to practice and trend toward playing against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Last week against Houston, the Titans were held to a season-low 57 rushing yards with Pollard receiving all but three carries out of the backfield en route to a 26-3 blowout loss .
"You go to the Jets game and last game will be two games in the second half where it got a little out of hand," Saleh said. "Your run game will look like shit."
Saleh spoke candidly about the offense being withheld from running the ball consistently due to trailing in the second half, specifically against the Jets and Texans. In both of those games, the Titans were trying to come back from being down by two scores, limiting the chance to run the ball.
"Offensively, let's get a two-score lead, and then see what our run game looks like when we get to close out a game," Saleh said. "That would be freaking awesome."
Situational football is a factor in how many times an offense can run the ball. However, the truth is the Titans have a middle-of-the-road run game.
Tennessee runs the ball nearly 40% of offensive snaps for an average of 3.8 yards per rush, which ranks 17th in the NFL .
Pollard has 68 of 91 rushing attempts from the Titans, excluding QB Cam Ward, which is nearly a staggering 75% of the carries. According to PFF , Pollard's four yards per carry ranks him 23rd of 44 qualified runners despite having the 20th most carries.
If Pollard is inactive against the Colts, Daboll will have to turn to backup RB Tyjae Spears, who has primarily served as the blocking back. Spears has been a steady receiving back for Ward; he has the third most receptions on the team with 14 for 68 yards.
There's no denying the Titans offense needs change. An increase in opportunities for Spears may benefit a stagnate offense, especially against a Colts defense that allows the fifth most rushing yards per game .
Through five games, Spears has only 17 carries for 65 yards. He has the Titans only rush for more than 20 yards all season.

title: The 2 Matchups Titans Have to Win to Beat Colts in Week 6: Can Carnell Tate Bounceback?
full_text:
The Tennessee Titans travel to Indianapolis on Sunday for an AFC South showdown with the Colts.
Both teams are coming off double-digit losses in Week 5. The Colts’ defense is looking to bounce back after getting shredded by QB Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers offense.
As for the Titans, they’re just looking for any sign of improvement after an all-around beatdown by the Texans that saw them total just 187 yards of offense. Tennessee desperately needs to get in the win column this week solely to keep the panic meter from increasing more than it already has.
So, with that said, let’s take a look at which two matchups the Titans must win if they plan on flying back to Nashville with their first win of the season.
The Colts’ cornerback is in the midst of the lowest-graded season of his career, per Pro Football Focus . After not having an overall grade of less than 70 in any prior season, Gardner currently has a grade of 59.6 through five games. Even more intriguing is the fact that opposing quarterbacks have a passer rating of 120.6 when targeting the Cincinnati product, while opposing receivers are averaging more than 21 yards per reception when targeted against him.
This is an area QB Cam Ward and rookie WR Carnell Tate can try to exploit as the game unfolds. This offense desperately needs to start hitting big plays, and with Gardner showing a rare vulnerability of late, this may be the opportunity to take advantage.
Tate is coming off a one-catch, six-yard outing last Sunday and is looking to get back to the dominant performance he had in Baltimore the week prior. If Tate can consistently win this matchup (and any other he faces), Tennessee will have a chance.
If Tate is held in check once again, then that means the entire passing attack will likely be limited. And if that’s the case, it could be another long afternoon for the Titans offense.
As always, when it comes to Taylor, the Titans will have their hands full whenever he’s in the backfield. The Colts’ star RB currently ranks in the top 10 in carries (101), rushing yards (398), and rushing touchdowns (six).
This week, he gets to see an old friend he knows well: Jeffery Simmons. The Titans’ star defensive tackle is currently playing like one of the best defensive players in football regardless of position. His grade of 81.0 is the sixth-highest at his position, and even that feels low for someone as dominant as he’s been.
But in order to stop someone like Taylor, they’ll need a complete team effort from the entire group upfront. Fellow DL John Franklin Myers, Jermaine Johnson, and Jacob Martin have to join Simmons in being disciplined in the run game. You can’t press when playing someone with Taylor’s skill set. That’s how he takes advantage of you. Tennessee has to remain patient and make the plays that are there to be made.
They don’t have to make every stop, but it’s critical for their chances that they try to make the Colts one-dimensional on Sunday by limiting this ground game as much as possible.
Accomplishing that should give them a realistic shot at leaving Indianapolis with their first win of the season.

title: Titans Snap Count Analysis: Tyjae Spears Provides in Pass Game, Mitchell Trubisky is Overdue Playtime
full_text:
Sunday's blowout 26-3 home loss to the Houston Texans keeps the Tennessee Titans winless.
Tennessee is now one of three teams without a victory through five weeks. The Texans dominated Tennessee, and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers stunned the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday Night Football.
This loss marks seven consecutive losses for the Titans; their last win came against the Kansas City Chiefs without QB Patrick Mahomes in December.
Now, it's time to take a deeper look at the snap count, performances and decision-making by the Robert Saleh-led coaching staff against Houston.
In the previous two weeks, I have listed RB Tyjae Spears as a loser due to his firm role behind starter RB Tony Pollard.
However, Spears served as a reliable security blanket for QB Cam Ward in the pass game, earning him a spot as a winner. In addition to playing a season-high with 34 snaps, Spears led Tennessee in receptions with nine on nine targets for 28 yards.
Although Spears gave up a fumble on an awkward exchange from Ward, his overall performance was positive against Houston, especially because he's been relegated to pass blocking over the previous weeks.
Tennessee should look to utilize Spears as a pass catcher out of the backfield to help an underperforming Ward make easy reads.
We're at the point in the season where benching Ward should be a real option for the Titans coaching staff.
Ward had another underwhelming performance, completing 23 of 36 passes, nine of which were check-down passes to Spears, for a total of 170 yards passing. Furthermore, Ward absorbed four sacks and turned the ball over twice with one interception and a bobbled handoff to Spears.
Ward has the worst record for any quarterback in NFL history in their first 22 starts.
QB Mitchell Trubisky is yet to take a snap this season for the Titans. The former second overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft has a winning record as a starter , going 31-26 across a decade-long career.
Once the Texans took a 19-3 in the third quarter, the game felt essentially over due to Tennessee's inept offense.
In the fourth quarter, I thought there would be a chance Trubisky would get some reps. Instead, the Ward-led Titans turned the ball over on downs twice.
Unless Ward improves, expect to see Trubisky get play time soon.
For the third week in a row , RB Nick Singleton is a loser after not playing a single offensive snap against the Texans.
The rookie has only made 14 offensive snaps in three games this season. So far this season, Singleton has played primarily on special teams with 21 appearances.
Unexpectedly, the Titans handed the ball off to second-year pro RB Kalel Mullings over Singleton. In his one carry, Mullings earned a three-yard gain, only his fourth career touch. gs
Singleton's role in the offense continues to be a mystery.
Returning to the loser list is LB Cedric Gray; the Titans' leading tackler last season is yet to record more than 30 snaps in a game this season.
Against Houston, Gray has held to only 28 snaps, according to PFF . Despite the low snap count, Gray racked up six tackles and half a sack alongside DT John Franklin-Myers.
Gray has consistently played about half the snaps of rookie LB Anthony Hill Jr. and LB Cody Barton.
While Hill Jr. has emerged as one of Tennessee's best defensive players, Barton and Gray are nearly identical statistically. Barton has 26 total tackles and one pass deflection; Gray has 22 total tackles and half a sack in one less game.
It appears Gray's inactivity in Week 1 from a concussion has set him back in the depth chart in favor of Barton.
